name: 2000s_Modern_Baroque
description: A 2000s design trend that reskins Baroque opulence — damask and arabesque scrollwork, heraldic crests, blackletter type, gilded accents, crystal chandeliers, velvet and brocade — onto contemporary substrates like glossy lacquer, etched glass, chrome, satin vinyl and molded plastic. Palette runs from black-and-gold through jewel-tone magenta, purple and red to pastel lavender and pink, typically lit with saturated club light, backlit halos or chandelier sparkle. Typical subjects are nightclub lounges and boutique powder rooms, damask-printed fashion, vector crest logos, and glam merchandise such as marquee-bulb vanity mirrors and crest-emblazoned CD cases.

name: 2000s_Preppy
description: 2000s Preppy (also Girly Preppy, Preppy Y2K, Rich Girl, Popular Girl) is the mall-brand prep look of early-to-mid-2000s American teen culture: stacked pastel polo collars popped over fitted cardigans and sweater vests, hip-slung low-rise jeans and pleated tartan miniskirts, thick fabric headbands, pearl strands and oversized designer sunglasses. Its palette is light and bright — baby and bubblegum pink leading, anchored by black, white and navy, with kelly green, sunshine yellow and red plaid as support — rendered in glossy daylight, direct flash or flat catalogue studio light. Recognize it by layered collars, low-rise plaids, fuzzy handbags, flip phones and coordinated girl-clique tableaux in school, mall, campus-lawn and suburban street settings.

name: 2000s_Tuscan_Mom
description: A TikTok-born (2025–26) Y2K-revival aesthetic romanticizing early-2000s upper-middle-class Italian-American suburban glamour: warm earthy browns, terracotta, amber gold and occasional plum, animal print, low-rise flare jeans, draped halter and cowl-neck tops, chunky caramel highlights, gold bangles and slouchy logo bags, staged in Tuscan Rustic McMansions, candle-lit spas, hair salons and mall-chain interiors. Recognize it by maximalist warm-toned moodboard collages or candid digicam snaps centered on blowouts, wedge heels, jar candles, champagne and tan-leather car interiors — comfortable, attainable wealth rather than oligarch excess.

name: 2000s_Yoga_Mom
description: A retrospective 2020s TikTok/Pinterest microtrend nostalgic for the upper-middle-class American suburban wellness mom of 2001–2008: sage green and pale pink palettes, lotus flowers, rolled yoga mats, Buddha statues, bamboo, candles and green juices, set in light-wood studios, beige domestic interiors or dappled woodland light. Signature looks include Y2K athleisure (fold-over waistband flare pants, racerback tanks, knotted baby tees, wide headbands, wired headphones), period digital-camera snapshot quality, and soft pink affirmation text or lotus-clipart moodboard collages. Recognize it by the combination of pastel zen décor, disciplined wellness props, and wistful early-2000s domesticity.

name: 2010s_Bright_Kawaii
description: Mid-2010s Tumblr-born Western remix of Harajuku kawaii built on bright pastels (sakura pink, lilac, mint, baby blue), high-key natural light, and pop-culture signifiers — magical-girl anime screenshots, handheld retro consoles (Game Boy, Tamagotchi, 3DS), ramune and peach-milk bottles, holographic vinyl, pleated tennis skirts and berets. Recognizable by flat lays of kawaii charms and snacks, chibi or thin-line digital illustrations of consoles and sweets, and sarcastic slogans set in pastel bubble letters. Use for cute, crisp, pastel pop imagery with anime/gamer DNA, as distinct from softer, dreamier, or gothier pastel aesthetics.

name: 2010s_Dark_Fandom
description: An internet edit-culture aesthetic of roughly 2010–2016 (also called Insanitycore or EXEcore) built on an aggressive black / blood-red / white palette, hyperreal blood splatter thrown over flat 2D anime art, glowing or shadow-banded eyes, kitchen knives, chains, surgical masks, glitch and JPEG-artifact distress, and black-framed demotivational posters with white serif captions. It centers on the corrupted-innocence figure — yandere schoolgirls, creepypasta killers, "evil variants" of cheerful mascots — caught in a manic or dissociative trance. Recognize it by its amateur Web 2.0 edit grammar: crushed blacks, arterial red as the only warm hue, scratched text, and a lone centered figure against a splatter field.

name: 2010s_Meme_Maximalism
description: A revivalist early-2020s internet collage aesthetic (TikTok, Pinterest, Roblox; pejoratively "Retroslop"/"Rainbowslop") that stacks late-2000s-to-mid-2010s meme assets — rage comic faces, Nyan Cat, Epic Face smileys, Impact-font Advice Animals, kaomoji, sparkledogs — onto full-bleed rainbow gradients, galaxy prints, paint splatters and glitter fields with almost no negative space. Signature elements include scene/kandi-fashion anthropomorphized meme characters (choppy dyed hair, studded belts, striped stockings, huge bows), bubble-letter logos, username watermarks and year stamps like "2009," and a deliberate mix of crude MS-Paint/pixel stamps with clean thick-outlined vector art. Recognize by full-spectrum neon saturation, controlled chaos, and defiantly "cringe" random humor.

name: 2010s_Soft_Kawaii
description: 2010s Soft Kawaii is the Tumblr/Instagram-era pastel offshoot of Japanese kawaii culture: warm sepia-faded photos and thick-outlined illustrations in blush pink, cream, mint green and cocoa brown, populated by plush mascots (Pusheen, Rilakkuma, Domo), sweets given dot-eye sticker faces, decoden food charms, Peter Pan collars, Swiss-dot and English-floral prints, and knit-lace-plush textures. Recognize it by its low-contrast warm cast, tidy-cute flat lays and bedroom vignettes, and feminine Himekaji/Girly Kei/Twee layering. Use this skill to identify or generate cozy, sincerely cute imagery of food-characters, plushies, fashion coords and pink domestic objects.

name: 2010s_Summer_Nostalgia
description: Sun-bleached, filter-washed celebration of early-to-mid-2010s social-media summer (peak 2013–2016): high-exposure pool, beach and boardwalk scenes pushed into saturated teal, neon pink and golden sun flare, with rose-gold fades, blown highlights and light leaks. Signature elements include palm silhouettes against violent sunsets, flamingo and swan floaties, flat-lays of sunglasses and soda cans on bleached wood, "Keep Calm"-era text overlays, and square-crop snapshot candor native to Tumblr and early Instagram. Recognize it by the deliberate period filter cast — magenta-plum shadows, cream-gold highlights — over casual coastal leisure, never by neutral or minimalist grading.

name: 2014_Girly
description: 2014 Girly (a.k.a. Tumblr It Girl, Rosyblog) is the pale-pink Tumblr aesthetic of 2012–2016: faded, Amaro-filtered snapshots of silky striped pajamas, hair bows, fluffy pastel socks, frappuccinos and marshmallow cocoa, floral Cath Kidston bedding, vanity flat-lays and mirror selfies in baby pink, cream, beige and mint. Recognize it by lifted-black fade with a warm cream cast, amateur-intimate framing (POV feet on a bed, overhead flat-lays, grid collages, photos from behind), and overtly feminine mall-brand props (Victoria's Secret, UGG, Starbucks, Essie, ted baker); it resurfaced on TikTok 2022–2024 via "2024 is the new 2014."

name: 2020_Alt
description: 2020 Alt (Alt Kid, E-Kid, Bunny Hat Kid) is the quarantine-era TikTok youth aesthetic of the early 2020s: a black-dominant, pink-accented maximalist pastiche of Mallgoth, Scene and E-Girl fashion — plush bunny hats with dangling ears, oversized graphic tees layered over striped longsleeves, ripped fishnets, striped thigh-highs, and buckled platform boots — shot in LED-lit bedrooms and buried under sparkle filters and Sanrio/skull sticker overlays. Recognize it by nose-tip blush makeup with drawn-under-eye dots, split-dye hair, kandi beads and silver chains, Monster Energy cans, and vertical phone-native framing with dense digital sticker clusters.

name: 2020s_Preppy
description: 2020s Preppy (Gen Alpha / TikTok Preppy, "Sephora Kid") is a maximalist tween-and-teen lifestyle aesthetic of early-2020s TikTok: hot pink, cyan and neon pastels set against blown-out high-key light, oversized fleece hoodies and ribbed leggings decorated with smiley faces, lightning bolts and chenille patches, pink cowgirl hats, Stanley-style tumblers and luxury skincare hauls. Recognize it by candy-saturated color on clean white grounds, brand-forward status props, tidy maximalist arrangements, and performative cheerfulness in beach, pool, bedroom and boutique leisure settings.

name: 2_Tone
description: 2 Tone is the visual language of the late-1970s Coventry ska revival: a strict black-and-white monochrome system built on the checkerboard pattern, sharp Rude Boy suits with thin ties and pork pie hats, jagged hand-cut band logos, and block-capital gig-poster type stacks. Grainy flash-lit monochrome portraits of multiracial bands, flat hard-edged illustrated figures in skanking dance poses, and checkerboard borders or floors signal it instantly. Use when recognizing or generating ska-revival record sleeves, posters, fashion plates and band imagery rooted in anti-racist, working-class British culture of 1979–1985.

name: 50s_Suburbia
description: The idealized postwar American middle-class look, c. 1948–1960: pastel tract houses (mint, baby pink, powder blue) behind white picket fences and manicured lawns, chrome-trimmed appliances, tailfin sedans and station wagons, and apron-over-dress housewives in pearls, rendered as high-key advertising illustration, warm Kodachrome-style color photography, or bright monochrome snapshot. Signature subjects are woman-centric domestic tableaux — cooking, vacuuming, sweeping, the open stocked refrigerator — plus commuter husbands in grey suits, backyard barbecues, and streets of identical houses. The surface is seamless, cheerful order; menace, decay or uncanny stillness belongs to Suburban Gothic, not here.

name: 8-Bit
description: 8-Bit is the pixel-grid aesthetic of 1980s home consoles and early home computers (NES, Sega Master System, Game Boy, Atari, MS-DOS era): worlds built from 8×8 pixel tiles, flat unshaded color fills drawn from a tiny simultaneous palette, sprites with no outlines, and monospace HUD lettering with hard blocky dropshadows. Recognize it by large visible square pixels, flat saturated sky/grass/brick fields or black void backgrounds, cramped status strips (SCORE, TIME, LIFE), and chunky logo cards; nothing is anti-aliased, gradiented or dithered.

name: 80s-90s_Afrocentrism
description: The Black-diaspora pride aesthetic of 1980s–90s television, film, music packaging, advertising and fashion, built on flat Pan-African color blocking (red, gold-yellow, green and black, extended by orange and purple), bold African geometric prints of zigzags, triangles, dots, waves and spirals, and garments like dashikis, kufi hats and headwraps. Recognize it by cut-paper collage posters, border-framed album and movie art, color-blocked streetwear patches, petroglyph-like figures and Africa silhouettes, gold jewelry, braids and beads, Kwanzaa imagery, and bright even sitcom-or-studio lighting that centers Black subjects, families and communities. Load this skill when an image or brief involves flag-saturated Black pride design of the late 20th century rather than sci-fi, punk or boho Black aesthetics.

name: 80s_Workout
description: 80s Workout (Aerobics Fashion) is the exuberant fitness aesthetic of early-1980s aerobics culture: high-cut spandex leotards layered over shiny tights, scrunched leg warmers, terry sweatbands and white high-top sneakers, color-blocked in clashing neon pink, green, yellow and blue or candy pastels. Images center smiling, jumping, flexing bodies in seamless-paper studios, wood-floor aerobics rooms or sunlit parks, lit flat and bright with analog film grain, expressing fitness-as-fun optimism and social performance. Load this skill for activewear catalog energy, group aerobics tableaus, home-workout VHS staging, or any neon color-blocked exercise styling.

name: 90s_Cool
description: 90s Cool ("The Matrix Effect," "Bullet Time") is the action-cinema aesthetic of roughly 1994–2005: black leather trench coats, latex catsuits, wraparound Oakley-style shades and tactical harnesses, lit by a muted green-or-steel-blue digital grade with cascading code, CRT glow and bead-blasted steel weaponry. Its signature images are the frozen bullet-time arc, wire-fu suspension, hacker/espionage lone operators and coat-and-shades ensemble lineups, all in service of an overwhelming emphasis on looking cool. Recognize it by cool-toned noir lighting, black-on-black wardrobe separated by rim light, and campy early-CGI texture; it borrows from Cyberpunk and Y2K Futurism but is darker, sleeker and choreography-obsessed.

name: 92i
description: 92i is a maximalist French beauty-and-streetwear aesthetic that went viral on TikTok and Instagram in 2025, named for the Hauts-de-Seine postal code: high-coverage matte foundation, carved block-like brows, winged eyeliner, XXL false lashes, sharp bronze contour and nude-brown matte lips. Its images are vertical phone selfies, mirror shots and small collage grids set in beige domestic interiors or night cars, pairing the full-glam face with anonymous fast-fashion streetwear and small gold hardware. Recognize it by its warm bronze-brown monochrome palette, sculptural matte skin, and unapologetic banlieue confidence — the declared opposite of clean-girl minimalism and quiet luxury.

name: Abstract_Tech
description: Abstract Tech (a.k.a. FUI, High-Tech, Sci-Fi Interface, Cyber) is the visual shorthand for "technology itself": glowing blue-white lines, segmented concentric arcs, hexagons, circuit traces, binary code and node-and-line networks suspended on near-black voids. Emerging from 1980s–2000s sci-fi interfaces (TRON, Ghost in the Shell, Minority Report, Iron Man) and technology stock imagery, it depicts holographic touchscreens, heads-up displays, cyberspace tunnels and robots as self-luminous geometry. Recognize it by dark grounds, cool monochrome glow, dense non-functional interface ornament, and the total absence of nature, grime or daylight.

name: Acid_Design
description: Acid Design (Acidgrafix) is the late-2010s revival of 1990s acid-house rave flyer graphics: a black "colorful black" ground loaded with fluorescent neons (acid green, chartreuse, magenta, lavender, signal red), chrome and liquid-metal display type, wireframe globes and grids, warped Op-Art stripes and checkerboards, UI-window panels, barcodes and cynical micro-copy, plus ironic smiley citations. Recognize it in dense, modular electronic-music cover art, event flyers and label branding that fuse vector crispness with xerox/halftone decay and a dystopian, darkly humorous mood.

name: Acid_House
description: Acid House is the visual culture of mid-1980s Chicago house and the UK's 1987–92 "Second Summer of Love": the acid-yellow smiley face on ink black, neon pink/green/orange accents, and bold condensed or hand-set flyer typography listing club names, dates and addresses. It lives in two registers — flat litho-printed promo graphics (smiley emblem, psychedelic swirls, comic-book borrowings, stretched letterforms like "ACIIIIID") and grainy on-camera-flash snapshots of clubbers in baggy dungarees, bucket hats, bandanas, sunglasses and smiley badges dancing in warehouse haze. Recognize it by the smiley (often winked, distorted or repeated as an all-over badge pattern), TB-303 hardware, tie-dye, and "TRIP"/"ACID" lettering.

name: Acubi
description: Acubi (Korean Y2K, K-Grunge) is an early-2020s South Korean minimalist fashion aesthetic — a desaturated, polished evolution of Y2K built on the "slim top, baggy bottom" silhouette: cropped subversive-basics tops with asymmetrical cut-outs, mesh overlays and bolero cardigans over parachute pants, wide-leg cargos or maxi skirts. Palette of charcoal, heather grey, off-white, sage and muted earth tones, finished with sleek retro-futuristic accessories (over-ear headphones, chrome jewelry, rimless sunglasses, chunky sneakers like Adidas Sambas) and shot in clean lookbook or candid social-media light. Recognize by restrained chroma plus Y2K cut-out detail and pristine finish; never distress, never neon.

name: Adventure_Pulp
description: Adventure Pulp is the romanticized explorer aesthetic of 1930s–40s pulp magazines and film serials, recodified by 1980s adventure cinema: fedora-crowned adventurer-scholars in worn leather, khaki and olive drab amid sun-scorched desert ruins, overgrown jungle temples, and lamplit cluttered professor's studies. Its palette is earth-first — leather browns, dust khaki, desert ochre, parchment off-white — punctuated by pulp-cover accents of masthead yellow, signal red and jungle green, delivered in gouache cover paint, halftone print grain, sepia or grainy monochrome photo toning, or warm single-lamp light. Recognition hinges on period gear (fedora, leather satchel, coiled bullwhip, tall boots), scholastic props (old maps, esoteric artifacts, books, spectacles), dieselpunk-era transport (prop planes, steamships, vintage off-road vehicles), and a mood of competent, daring discovery.

name: Adventurecore
description: Adventurecore is a late-2010s Tumblr-born aesthetic of romanticized exploration — misty conifer forests, winding dirt trails, mossy creeks and fogged mountains rendered in muted earth tones (pine green, bark brown, fog off-white, dark navy) under overcast, foggy or golden-hour light. Its signature elements are practical layered hiking gear (flannel, fleece, rain shell, canvas satchel), old maps, compasses and journal sketches, and a first-person "protagonist setting off on a cross-country journey" framing, delivered through casual handheld photography, moodboard collages and garment flat-lays rather than glossy postcard views. Load this skill for images of quiet, yearning outdoor journeying, cozy readiness for any weather, and amateur-realistic nature travel with a slightly melancholic, contemplative cast.

name: Aestheticism
description: Aestheticism (the Aesthetic Movement, the "Cult of Beauty"), England c. 1860s–1900, treats every picture as a self-sufficient harmony of colour and pattern under the doctrine of "art for art's sake." Recognition hinges on two palette registers — subdued tonal arrangements of grey, sage, slate blue and ivory, and jewel-tone schemes of emerald, sapphire, ruby and peacock blue punctured with gold — deployed across idealized women lost in reverie, classical drapery, peacock feathers, lilies and sunflowers, Japanese fans, screens and blue-and-white porcelain, all in flattened, pattern-conscious compositions with enamel-smooth glazes or mist-soft nocturne scumbles.

name: Aetherpunk
description: Aetherpunk (also Arcanepunk or Magicpunk) is a utopian fantasy-tech aesthetic in which high-fantasy magic powers science-fiction-grade technology: arcane sky-ships, elemental-bound engines, construct laborers and glowing aether conduits. Its visual DNA is gilded gold and carved stone architecture with stained glass and pagan sigils, lit by one saturated aether hue — neon blue-cyan, rune violet, or undercity green — set against painterly daylight and warm brass speculars. Typical subjects are magical machines, artificer-mages, luminous artifacts and sunlit civic cityscapes that read as inherently good rather than dystopian.

name: Afrofuturism
description: Afrofuturism fuses African diasporic heritage — printed textiles, gold beadwork, regal headwraps, carved and cast sculpture — with speculative technology and cosmology: starfields, lone moons, chrome visors, sun-disc halos. Its palette grounds metallic gold and chrome in deep indigo blues and earth tones, often lifted by saturated collage accents, and its subjects are dignified Black figures as explorers, royalty, priests and hybrid beings, rendered in photomontage, airbrush illustration, editorial fashion and sculpture. Rooted in Sun Ra's late-1950s space jazz and named in 1993, it carries values of liberation, reclamation, heritage and future vision.

name: Afropunk
description: Afropunk is the visual culture of Black participation in punk and alternative subcultures, from its 1970s roots to its 200s popularization through the Afro-Punk documentary and festival: DIY-altered tartan, leather, harnesses and fishnet worn over locs, braids and afros dyed electric pink, violet or teal, shot in flash-lit club doorways, sunlit festival fields and against chainlink fences. Signature elements include hand-modified garments, band patches, zine xerox graphics, combat boots, dark lipstick and defiant group portraits; the mood is rebellious joy and Black liberation.

name: After_Hours
description: After Hours (kenopsia) is a 2010s internet aesthetic of dimly lit, empty versions of places built for crowds — night streets, parks, school corridors, parking garages, diners after closing — held in deep shadow and lit by sodium-gold streetlamps, cool fluorescent tubes or stray neon. Signature elements are practical light sources burning for no one, one-point perspectives receding into darkness, benches and tables and clocks sized for absent people, fog or snow softening the glow, and a tranquil, contemplative melancholy rather than horror. Load this skill when recognizing or generating night-empty urban and suburban scenes of stillness, absence and quiet rebellion.

name: Agejo
description: Agejo ("Ageha Lady") is a mid-2000s Shibuya gyaru substyle born from Koakuma Ageha magazine, channeling Japanese hostess-club glamour: tight black mini dresses loaded with hot pink satin bows, leopard and zebra print, rhinestones, tiered lace, garter stockings and gold chain belts. Its signature figure pairs voluminous curled light-brown hair, dolly circle lenses, thick top-and-bottom eyeliner and false doll lashes with long decorated nails. Recognize it by the black-plus-hot-pink palette, overt lingerie cues, high ornament density and glossy high-key magazine lighting.

name: Aggrotech
description: Aggrotech (Harsh EBM, Hellektro, Endzeit Elektro) is the album-art and artist-presentation aesthetic of late-1990s harsh electro: blood-red-on-black hazard signage, olive-drab military hardware, gas masks, biohazard and radiation pictograms, and medical/body-horror shock imagery rendered in distressed duotone, halftone grain and stencil or blackletter type. Recognize it by its warning-sign palette (black, blood red, acid yellow-green, olive drab), its tactical and heavy-machinery props, and its theatrical, apocalyptic misanthropy — the violent cousin of Cybergoth and the distorted child of EBM.

name: Ah_Beng
description: Ah Beng is the 1990s Singaporean and Malaysian working-class Chinese youth stereotype: rebonded bleach-blonde or copper-red hair with heavy fringes, loud Western brand logos, chunky gold jewelry, reflective sunglasses and modified cars, captured in harsh consumer-camera flash against HDB flats, tarpaulin backdrops and night parking garages. Its visual DNA fuses gang-crew posturing (bare chests, dragon and tribal tattoos, baseball bats and choppers) with Ah Lian glamour (circle lenses, gelish nails, spaghetti straps) and a persistent undercurrent of comedic parody. Palette runs cheap-bright saturated primaries and metallics over drab tropical concrete and sepia-red parody grades.

name: Airbrush_Surrealism
description: Airbrush Surrealism (aka Airbrush Kitsch) is a hand-sprayed illustration aesthetic of the late 1960s to mid-1980s built on seamless airbrush gradients in hot pink, electric blue and deep purple, mirror-chrome spheres and metallic ribbons, and impossible floating objects — planets, machines, instruments, crystals, anthropomorphic kitsch figures — staged in cosmic voids, deserts and glowing horizons with starburst glints, artificial sunbursts and X-ray cutaways. Recognize it by its photo-smooth spray finish with zero brushwork, supersaturated neon palette, glossy chrome and liquid-metal surfaces, and deadpan dream logic; it is the analog precursor that vaporwave and laser grid later sampled.

name: Akibapop
description: Akibapop (Akiba-Pop / Moe-Denpa) is the candy-saturated cover and music-video aesthetic of early-2000s Akihabara doujin denpa music: moe anime girls with star-sparkle eyes and open-mouth grins, pastel candy palettes of pink, mint, lavender and lemon, and horror-vacui clutter of sweets, hearts, sparkles, animal ears and otaku tech gadgets. Signature elements include bold diagonal bubble typography in kana and English with thick white outlines, sticker-like cel shading, halftone confetti fields, and a manic off-kilter cuteness that tips into surreal hallucination. Recognize it by maximalist pastel clutter anchored by an anime character, never by minimalism or photorealism.

name: Alay
description: Alay is the Indonesian teen subculture aesthetic of the mid-2000s to early 2010s — a deliberately tacky (norak), maximalist mash of emo fringe, band tees, neckties-over-shirts and candy-bright accessories, shot on low-megapixel camera phones and camcorder stills for Friendster, hi5 and Flickr. Recognize it by crowded goofball group poses (peace signs, duck faces, chin-on-hand), side-swept fringes covering one eye, clashing saturated green/yellow/purple/red on a black-and-white base, JPEG noise, flat on-camera flash, letterbox bars, orange date stamps and snapshot-collage grids.

name: Aliencore
description: Aliencore (Alienwave) is a 1990s-born, Y2K-filtered aesthetic of extraterrestrial kitsch and cosmic isolation, built on neon green alien skin, violet, magenta and cyan glowing against black starfields, holographic and glow-in-the-dark finishes, grey-alien icons, flying saucers and conspiracy slogans. Typical subjects are alien self-portraits and mirror reflections, UFO signage and warning signs, neon and blacklight posters, holographic fashion, plush and sticker merch, and glitched VHS broadcast frames, with moods swinging from melancholic outsider to playful kitsch. Load this skill when imagery centers the alien as a stand-in for the self and every surface reads synthetic, emissive or iridescent.

name: Aliyahcore
description: Aliyahcore is an early-2020s TikTok-born fashion microtrend created by Atlanta creator Aliyah Bah, fusing Y2K silhouettes, grunge/alt grit and Harajuku maximalism into a pink-dominant, accessory-stacked look. Its signature formula pairs a miniskirt or micro-shorts with fishnet sleeves and stockings, a garter belt, fur-trimmed platform boots, year-round earmuffs, layered rhinestone belts, fuzzy leg warmers and outfit-matched makeup, captured as candid flash snapshots in mundane everyday spaces. Recognize it by candy-pink palette anchored in black or denim, plush kawaii charms and stacked bracelets, and confident, gestural full-body outfit poses.

name: Alté
description: Alté is the mid-2010s Lagos-born counterculture look: black-grounded thrift collage punctured by green, purple and neon flashes, worn by Nigerian youth crews with bleached brows, dyed locs, retro sunglasses, stacked chains, platform boots and heels, jerseys and Ankara fragments in gender-fluid silhouettes. It reads through flash-lit phone snapshots, mirror selfies, backstage and festival candids rather than polished campaign imagery. Load this skill when an image or brief shows African youth subculture styling that mixes vintage thrift, subcultural hardware and deliberate gender play with a candid, social-native photographic texture.

name: Amekaji
description: Amekaji ("American casual," also Cocogyaru) is a late-1990s–2000s Shibuya gyaru substyle that exaggerates American West Coast surf, skate and hip-hop streetwear into candy-colored layering — oversized hoodies, puffer vests, bold-logo graphic tees, flared or banner-lettered baggy pants, jorts and mini skirts in hot pink, canary yellow, turquoise and orange over denim and khaki bases. Recognition hinges on tanned gyaru makeup with bleached straight-bang hair, baseball caps and beanies, chunky plastic jewelry, star/polka-dot Americana prints, playful peace-sign poses, and the media frames of brand-shop flash snapshots or egg/Ranzuki magazine scan pages. Expect loud color-blocking and prominent brand logos on casual sporty silhouettes — never glamour-gyaru dresses, school uniforms, or dark hip-hop streetwear.

name: American_Pioneers
description: The 19th-century US settler aesthetic of prairie migration and homestead labor — sun-bleached wheat golds, honey ambers, burlap browns and milk-paint whites, punctuated by small calico reds. Signature elements are covered wagons, sunbonnets and aprons, cast-iron pots, patchwork quilts, tinware, one-room schoolhouses and small white clapboard churches, rendered in faded daylight photography or naive folk painting. Subjects privilege domestic self-sufficiency (bread, jam, eggs, honeycomb, washday, hand-sewing) set against vast untamed grassland and the shadow of hardship on the trail.

name: American_Thanksgiving
description: The visual culture of the American harvest holiday — abundant overhead feasts of roasted turkey, pumpkin and lattice-crust pie, cornucopias, heirloom gourds and flint corn on linen-and-transferware tables, lit by candle-warm chiaroscuro, diffuse daylight or analog flash. Palette locked to the warm quadrant of pumpkin orange, brick red, golden yellow and chestnut brown, with a vintage stratum of postcard lithographs, mid-century parade snapshots and 1970s animation stills. Mood is grateful, domestic and generously cluttered: family plenitude, never minimalist coziness.

name: Analog_Horror
description: Analog Horror (VHS Horror) is an internet-born found-footage aesthetic of the mid-to-late 2010s that emulates degraded late-20th-century media — VHS tapes, CRT television broadcasts, Emergency Alert System cards, public-access idents and employee training tapes — corrupted by dread. Recognize it by tape grain and interlaced scanlines, tracking tears with cyan/magenta fringing, monochrome or desaturated imagery punctured by sparse signal red, phosphor green or deep CRT blue, bureaucratic monospace type with burn-in timestamps and late-night clocks, uncanny blackened or grinning faces, interrupted vanity plates, and sinister planets. Typical subjects are emergency alerts, channel idents, instructional pictograms, distorted children's mascots, and empty found-footage rooms rather than visible protagonists.

name: Ancient_Egypt
description: Visual language of the dynastic Nile civilization (3150 BC–30 BC): monumental sandstone and gold under hard desert sun, flat register-based tomb painting and sunken relief bounded by black contour, hieroglyph bands, papyrus- and lotus-capital column forests, pylon gates, pyramids, mummies and winged sun discs. Palette of gold, ivory, sand-brown, kohl black, lapis/faience blue and red ochre laid in unmodulated fields; human figures in composite profile with frontal eye and torso. Use for recognizing or generating pharaonic monuments, funerary art, jewellery and desert scenes, and for keeping them distinct from Egyptian Revival, Art Deco and Hellenic neighbors.

name: Angelcore
description: Angelcore (Cherubcore) is a late-2010s internet aesthetic of angelic imagery borrowed from Rococo, Baroque and Neoclassical art — cherubs and putti, feathered wings, halos, doves, heaven-like clouds — rendered in a high-key pastel palette of white, cream, pale gold, baby pink and powder blue. Its signature look is hazy sunbeam lighting with a milky low-contrast fade, glitter sparkle points, fresco ceilings and ornate columns, lace and organza drapery, and vintage-postcard or digital-collage framing. Recognize it by the pairing of divine iconography with secular softness: if the image carries wings or cherubs but reads faded, powdered and dreamlike rather than dramatic or museum-crisp, it is Angelcore.

name: Anglo_Gothic
description: Anglo Gothic (Dark Anglo) is the aesthetic of run-down British suburbs and council estates under overcast, drizzling skies — wet tarmac, crumbling terraced houses and shoddy 1960s estate blocks, telegraph poles, bare trees and parked nineties cars, all soaked in desaturated blue, grey, brown and damp green. Rooted in 1990s post-punk and Britpop melancholy and in working-class industrial decline, its images are empty, underlit, snapshot-frank views punctuated at most by a single warm window or a pair of tail lights. Recognise it by weather-first greyness, blue-hour murk, absent people and mundane British infrastructure; it is bleaker and wetter than Northerncore and far darker than After Hours.

name: Angura_Kei
description: Angura Kei is the visual language of Japan's 1960s underground theatre counterculture, later carried by Visual Kei bands and ero-guro manga — shironuri white-painted faces in modified Showa-era school uniforms and layered kimono, staged among bunka dolls, Noh masks, old wall clocks and irreverently handled imperial flags. Its palette is a muted field of ink black, paper cream and faded institutional green pierced by one saturated vermilion red, and its mood is distorted nostalgia: ominous, theatrical, anti-authoritarian. Recognize it by white face paint plus Japanese era-fusion costume plus cluttered Showa interiors plus black/white/red symbolic staging.

name: Animecore
description: Animecore (Otakucore) is a nostalgic internet aesthetic for 1990s–early 2000s otaku fan culture, built on the 2000s moe-girl render grammar — chibi-rounded proportions, enormous reflective wide-set eyes, thickened outlines, soft-gradient cel coloring — presented in pastel-pink, glitter-stamped, deliberately lo-fi frames. Its signature scenes are maximalist otaku bedrooms and character shrines: figure-crowded shelves, poster-papered walls, CRT monitors and Windows-XP-era UI chrome, plus Blingee glitter graphics, gaudy text and pixelated GIF artifacts. Recognize it by the combination of moe-archetype art, fandom-merch maximalism, and early-internet digital degradation.

name: Antwerp_Six
description: Mid-1980s Belgian avant-garde fashion aesthetic of the Antwerp Six collective — severe monochrome deconstruction (black, charcoal grey, off-white, muted earth) with exposed seams, asymmetric draping, oversized tailoring and androgynous casting, alongside a divergent wing of saturated prints and provocative color statements. Recognized in runway documentary shots, grainy black-and-white campaign portraits and stark studio editorials that privilege intellectual austerity, visible construction and anti-fashion staging over commercial polish.

name: Appalachian_Gothic
description: Regional gothic of the American Appalachian hollows — mist-veiled forested ridges, small coal-and-lumber towns, rusting trestles, abandoned mine works and chinked-corner log cabins, rendered in canopy green, mineral gray and iron-oxide rust under flat overcast or fog-bound light. Signature elements are documentary vernacular decay (dilapidated mountaintop houses, rusted cars, split-rail fences, kudzu, utility wires) plus an ambient folkloric dread of ghosts and grotesque creatures half-glimpsed in the treeline. Load this skill for haunted rural Americana where hard-work workwear, coal history and wilderness menace coexist; it is daylight-gothic as often as night-gothic.

name: Après-ski
description: Mid-century alpine resort aesthetic of post-ski socializing, born in the 1950s European Alps and revived on lifestyle blogs and Instagram in grainy, faded-film photography. Cream and snow-white chunky knits, shearling-trimmed puffers, fur-cuffed moon boots, deep red / navy / forest accents, skis and poles as at-rest props, and convivial chalet, terrace or tailgate scenes with fondue, mulled wine and firelight. Recognize by Fair Isle and cable knits, fur-trimmed hoods, snow-glare sunglasses, high-key snow light, and a casually luxurious "just off the slopes" social mood.

name: Arabfunny
description: Arabfunny is a late-2010s meme aesthetic born on r/Arabfunny that parodies early-2000s Arab and South Asian WhatsApp/Facebook chain posts: deliberately re-compressed 144p–240p JPEG and video frames, untranslated bold Arabic text, red clickbait circles and arrows, neon-green FREE DOWNLOAD buttons, 😂 emoji sprinkles, Pan-Arab red/green/white/black accents, and a clutter of Peter Griffin clips, Trollface line art, Nokia phones, camels and crude 3D animations. Recognition hinges on sensory-overload sticker clutter layered over Arab-world "boomer web" ephemera, not on deep-fry saturation alone.

name: Arabian_Nights
description: A 2020s TikTok-born celebration aesthetic of Middle Eastern and North African heritage: creators in thobes, abayas, keffiyehs and hijabs, wearing gold jewelry and dramatic kohl-lined eye makeup, set against desert dunes, arched traditional architecture and glowing pierced-brass lanterns. The palette runs candle-gold, amber and terracotta-rose dusk against garment black, or indigo-violet night with turquoise tile accents; formats range from crisp HD portraits and candlelit still-life trays to moodboard grids and flat starry-sky illustrations. It reads as self-representational cultural pride — modest, elegant, warm — never as exoticized outsider fantasy.

name: Arcadecore
description: Arcadecore (Early 80s Arcade) idealizes the golden-age video game arcade of the late 1970s–1990s: near-black rooms lit only by CRT phosphor, neon marquees and blacklight-reactive carpet. Its signature elements are arcade cabinets with glowing joysticks and buttons, pixel art and dot-matrix typography, vector wireframe glow, cosmic patterned carpets, tokens and tickets, in a palette of black, navy and fluorescent pink, cyan and green. Subjects range from cabinet-lined aisles and control-panel close-ups to arcade fashion portraits and UV pattern fields, all carrying nostalgia, competition and communal fun.

name: Archive_Fashion
description: Archive Fashion is a collector-driven street aesthetic of the late 2010s–2020s (Japan, US) built on vintage avant-garde runway pieces — Raf Simons, Helmut Lang, Rick Owens, Undercover, Carol Christian Poell — worn as deconstructed black-and-grey layers: raw hems, slashed asymmetric zippers, bondage straps and tactical pockets over oversized or low-rise flare pants stacked on chunky boots. Signature cues are deliberate decay (torn woolens, unraveled seams, distressed denim), muted macabre motifs (skeletons, spiderwebs, punk-text patchwork), fur trims, ushankas, masks and sunglasses, captured in unpolished snapshot light. Recognize it by worn designer hardware plus anti-fashion distress; it is neither emo's skinny band-tee silhouette, sleek Hedi Boy rock glamour, nor glossy futuristic techwear.

name: Aristocrat
description: Aristocrat (Gothic Aristocrat, EGA) is a mid-1990s Japanese street fashion of mature, androgynous gothic elegance modeled on 19th-century European aristocracy: ankle-length black skirts and tailored long coats, waistcoats, jabots and cravats, top hats and veils, roses, crosses and fleurs-de-lis on a near-black palette with crimson, midnight blue and antique brass accents. Recognize it by long structured silhouettes with no petticoat volume, pale poised androgynous figures, period boots, and funereal lookbook staging; it deliberately rejects Lolita cuteness, prints and petticoats.

name: Art_Academia
description: Art Academia is the academic internet aesthetic of visual-art making and viewing — plaster cast rooms, oil-crusted wooden palettes, charcoal sketchbooks, salon-hung museum walls and sunlit atelier easels — rendered in warm neutrals (plaster white, oat, taupe, umber) punctuated by saturated pigment accents led by cadmium yellow. Figures appear from behind admiring statues, or as paint-stained hands at work, bathed in soft north-window daylight with a quiet, filmic grain. Load this skill when an image must read as classical art-school devotion — tactile, curious, reverent toward antiquity — rather than literary academia, productivity culture or DIY art-girl irony.

name: Art_Deco
description: Art Deco (Paris, 1910s–1930s) is the machine-age luxury style: bilateral symmetry, stepped ziggurat silhouettes, sunburst–chevron–zigzag ornament, and high-contrast black/ivory/gold/chrome palettes enriched by jewel tones or powder pastels. Signature subjects include skyscraper crowns and theater façades, lacquered salon interiors, macassar-ebony cabinets and onyx mantel clocks, flat-plane lithographic posters with geometric capitals, slender pochoir fashion plates, frosted-glass and bakelite objects, and streamlined trains, liners and cars. Load this skill when imagery must evoke Roaring-Twenties glamour, verticality, exotic veneers and faith in technology.

name: Art_Hoe
description: Art Hoe is a mid-2010s Tumblr-born aesthetic and movement created by and for young creatives of color, fusing saturated primary colors — mustard yellow above all — with nature greens and soft pastels like lavender and peach. Recognize it by the "modified selfie" collaged or doodled over with famous paintings, halos and flowers; sunflowers, succulents and ivy beside well-used sketchbooks, paint tubes and palettes; Fjällräven Kånken backpacks, cuffed mom jeans, mustard cardigans, Dr. Martens or platform sneakers with painting-print statement socks; and collage-covered bedroom-studio walls lit by warm window light and yellow fairy lights.

name: Art_Nouveau
description: Art Nouveau (1890s–1910s, Western Europe) is the Belle Époque total-design style built on asymmetrical "whiplash" S-curves and stylized nature — vines, orchids, dragonflies, peacocks, flowing-haired female figures — rendered in muted olive, mustard, brown, lilac and sage with gold and brass accents. It appears in flat-color hand-lettered posters, exposed iron-and-glass architecture, curvilinear stairwells and facades, jewelry, lamps and art glass. Recognize it by sinuous organic line fused with structure itself, faded earthy palette, and ornament that grows out of the object rather than sitting on it.

name: Art_Singulier
description: Art Singulier — the French outsider art current of the 1970s (art hors-les-normes, création franche, heir to Art Brut) — paints personal mythology in bright saturated fields of turquoise, vermilion, marigold and cobalt, with naïve-cubist split faces, totemic figures, visionary houses and gardens, obsessive hand-drawn pattern, encrusted collage-assemblage surfaces and wobbly hand-lettered inscriptions. Recognize it by untrained frontality, either horror-vacui density or a single icon on a flat color field, non-naturalistic even light, and everywhere the evidence of the hand; it absorbs Cubism and Surrealism but never academic finish, pop gloss or digital cleanness.

name: Artcore
description: Artcore is the album-cover and rhythm-game key-art aesthetic of the Japanese dōjin electronic music genre (early 2000s onward): anime-styled angels, fairies and cyborgs in Gothic-Lolita-inflected dress, set amid cathedral vaults, shimmering crystals, shattered glass, angel feathers and flourishing flowers. Its palette is cool and high-contrast — blues, purples and whites, either as luminous high-key watercolor washes or abyssal indigo darkness pierced by a radiant bloom — usually finished with letterspaced serif titles. Recognize it by the fusion of Gothic/Baroque grandeur, crystalline shard geometry and melancholy classical elegance over an electronic-modern skeleton.

name: Arte_Povera
description: Italian avant-garde of the late 1960s–70s whose visual DNA is the "poor" material itself — earth, stones, raw wood, burlap, rope, newspaper, rags, water, living plants — staged as sculpture or installation with documentary neutrality in white cubes, classical Italian rooms or open ground. Expect earthy, material-derived palettes (tan, stone grey, umber, rust, plaster white) punctuated by industrial or organic accents (dyed-water blue, lettuce green, chaotic multicolour textile heaps); forms of pile, stack, mound, floor grid, lean-to and suspended hang; perishable process elements; and an austere, anti-spectacular mood of conceptual juxtaposition between natural and artificial, old and new.

name: Arts_and_Crafts
description: British-led decorative style of the 1880s–1920s (William Morris, John Ruskin) built on dense, flat repeating patterns of stylized garden flora — acanthus, tulip, rose, daisy, scrolling vines — and birds such as thrushes, in natural-dye colors of indigo, madder red, ochre and olive green on deep or oatmeal grounds, alongside honest hand-made objects of quarter-sawn oak with exposed joinery, hammered copper and silver, matte-glazed stoneware and block-printed paper. Recognize it by symmetrical scrolling-stem repeats, matte earthy palette, medieval flatness, and visible handwork; the mood is pastoral, earnest and anti-industrial.

name: Asian_Baby_Girl
description: Asian Baby Girl (ABG) is a 1990s-born Asian American subculture aesthetic built on full-glam makeup (filled brows, dramatic false lashes, colored contacts), bleached/ombré or contrast-streaked hair, black form-fitting tops with baggy pants or jerseys, hoop earrings, coffin nails and dragon/flower/Chinese-character tattoos. It is photographed as digital snapshot culture — harsh on-camera flash against night blackness, magenta-violet club neon, car interiors, arm's-length selfies — with boba cups, plush toys and streetwear-luxury logos as props. Palette anchors on black with saturated neon pink, red and gold accents; mood is playful, confident defiance of the "model minority" stereotype.

name: Athleisure
description: Athleisure ("athletic streetwear") is a casual style of the late 2010s–early 2020s that fuses performance gymwear — track jackets, joggers, leggings, compression tops — with streetwear volume and tailored pieces. Recognize it by tech fleece, ribbed knits and spandex in either tonal neutrals (cream, black, heather grey, olive) or flat color-blocked panels of red, blue and green on a white or black ground; oversized hoodies and jackets over slim bases or baggy, stripe-taped track pants; and chunky retro trainers kept deliberately in frame. The mood is confident, casual ease — workout gear elevated for city life, never costume sportswear.

name: Atompunk
description: Atompunk is the 1950s–60s vision of the future replayed as dystopia, satire or cold-war dread: finned rockets, ringed space stations, hover cars and Googie needle-spires in saturated pulp-magazine color (atomic orange, teal, mustard, magenta over chrome and starfield indigo) with gouache, airbrush and offset-print texture. Recognize it by analog dials and cathode-ray consoles, bubble-helmet astronauts, starburst atomic motifs, Populuxe pastel suburbia or post-nuclear wastelands — a bright retrofuturist surface with irony, decay or pessimism underneath. Distinguish from sincere Raygun Gothic and Space Age design by that countercultural twist.

name: Australiana
description: Australiana is the irony-soaked revival of 20th-century Australian popular culture, born in the 1980s (Ken Done, Coogi, Expo '88, Flamingo Park) and resurrected as "Australiana 2.0": clashing primaries and neons splashed on stark white, or maximalist all-over prints of koalas, kangaroos, galahs, waratahs and gum leaves, alongside Aboriginal-derived dashed-line painting fields, cream-brick suburbia, stilted Queenslanders, mosaic highway murals and tourist-postcard display type. Recognize it by deliberate "colours that don't go together," terry towelling and acrylic knits, fairy-bread kitsch, hard midday sun, and a larrikin, self-aware nostalgia that homages the past while winking at it.

name: Austurbane
description: Austurbane (Austere-Urbane) is a late-2010s product-photography and brand-design aesthetic that pairs stark minimalism with earthy, upscale sophistication: editorial serif type set in vast whitespace, hard directional light casting branch and seed-head shadows across the frame, and highly staged still lifes of marble, rough stone, organic ceramics and matte paper in muted beige, cream, brown, copper, bronze and black. Its typical subjects are premium packaging, stationery and branding suites, and editorial spreads, arranged in geometric isometric angles or strict top-down flat lays with a zen, curated, "classy minimalism" mood. Load this skill when recognizing or generating refined earth-tone brand imagery defined by dramatic natural light, raw natural materials and restrained serif typography.

name: Autumn_Aesthetic
description: Autumn Aesthetic (aka Fallcore, Romanticized Autumn, Cozy Autumn) is a 2010s social-media lifestyle style that idealizes the fall season through a warm earth-tone palette of burnt orange, rust, mustard yellow, rich brown, cream and beige. Its signature elements are falling leaves and foliage-canopied streets, pumpkin spice lattes and apple cider, chunky knits and plaid flannel, candles, classic books, cozy blankets, pumpkin patches, misty mornings and candlelit interiors, rendered in soft diffuse or low golden light with a matte, film-like warm grade. Recognize it by cozy domestic or leaf-strewn outdoor scenes that radiate nostalgia, slowness and domestic comfort — distinct from Halloween's spookiness and Dark Academia's austerity.

name: Avant_Apocalypse
description: Avant Apocalypse is a 2020s fashion aesthetic of neutral maximalism — deconstructed, asymmetrically layered garments in earth tones, bone, ash grey and soot black, cut with cut-outs, sheer panels and raw edges so the body is revealed and armored at once. Signature reads: stacked layering of distressed knits and sheers, off-kilter silhouettes with trailing panels, strap-and-O-ring harnesses and sculptural wire, chunky platform boots under stacked leg warmers, hooded or masked faces against austere seamless, concrete or dust-toned grounds. Use when recognizing or generating runway-grade dystopian styling that is distressed-by-design yet body-conscious, as opposed to literal survivalist post-apocalypse costuming.

name: Avant_Basic
description: Avant Basic is a 2020s, social-media-born soft maximalism: candy pastels (blush pink, lilac, pistachio, peach, baby blue) layered over cream or white grounds, clashing retro-psychedelic patterns — checkerboard, wavy swirls, abstract florals, gingham — with curvy Memphis-descended shapes like wiggly mirrors, bubbly candles and rounded furniture. Typical subjects are sunlit pastel interiors, intarsia-knit lookbook fashion, garment flat-lays and collage lookbooks. Recognize it by pattern-mixing held in pastel harmony, kitsch sincerity, curved silhouettes, and bright, soft, even daylight.

name: Avantropop
description: Avantropop (aka Avant Garde Prefuse) is the late-2000s/early-2010s broadcast-and-electropop graphic style: asymmetrical vector geometry, warped black-and-white optical stripes and checkers, CMYK process neons (magenta, cyan, yellow, lime) fired across black or white fields, halftone dot screens, photo-cutout collage, soft prism gradients and chunky geometric sans type in the ITC Avant Garde Gothic family. Typical subjects are TV network bumpers and idents, electropop music-video frames, festival posters and flyers, youth-tech advertising, type specimens and colorblocked streetwear looks. Recognize it by diagonal, high-energy, collage-layered composition that fuses avant-garde op-art instinct with glossy digital pop crispness.

name: B-Movie_Horror
description: The visual language of cheaply made American horror cinema from the 1930s–1980s and its promotional art — grainy or washed-out film frames, visible foam-latex prosthetics and glossy too-red fake blood, and lurid hand-lettered one-sheet posters in clashing signal red, acid yellow, poison green or duotone salmon-on-ink. Signature elements are caps-lock taglines, billing blocks, floating-head montages, screaming faces, rubber monsters, brains in jars, flying saucers, and fog used to hide nonexistent sets. Typical subjects are mad scientists, alien invasions, giant mutated creatures, vampires, possessed nuns and video-era slashers, all rendered with earnest, visible cheapness.

name: Babycore
description: Babycore is a 2010s Tumblr-born internet aesthetic of infancy and toddlerhood nostalgia: milk-faded pastel pink, baby blue, mint and cream applied to plush toys, pacifiers, baby bottles, alphabet blocks, frills and maximalist nursery clutter. Its images are overexposed and soft-focus, full of plush fur, crochet, tulle and frilly socks, and its mood is strictly non-sexual comfort, innocence and gentleness. Recognize it by washed-out pastels with milky shadows, childlike details like Peter Pan collars and rattles, and hazy high-key light.

name: Babygirl
description: Babygirl is a 2010s Tumblr-born feminine aesthetic of reclaimed girlhood: milky pastel pink, lavender and baby blue fields, frills, lace, satin bows, Peter Pan collars, pigtails, plush piles and pacifier charms, rendered in hazy high-key light with star-sparkle overlays. Typical subjects are plush-stacked bedrooms, detail crops of frilled garments and bead accessories, and moodboard collages carrying cursive "babygirl" or "crybaby" text. It is a non-sexual comfort aesthetic; recognize it by its infantile-comfort motifs plus soft digital bloom, and separate it from Babycore, Nymphet, Puppygirl and DDLG-coded imagery.

name: Baddie
description: Baddie is the 2010s Instagram-model and YouTube beauty-guru aesthetic of confident, heavily made-up women: thick sculpted brows, cut-crease shadow, dark liner, false lashes and clear gloss over contoured, dewy skin, paired with long acrylic nails, wigs or laid edges, and a streetwear-meets-glam wardrobe of crop tops, hoodies, tracksuits, ripped jeans, camo pants and name-brand sneakers. Its palette anchors on black, red, camo, beige, white and pink, shot in harsh phone-flash night interiors, hard daylight on concrete, or soft pink studio glow, with hoop earrings, chains, designer logos and stacks of cash as flex props.

name: Bakala
description: Bakala (Makinero, Ruta Destroy) is the Spanish club subculture of late-1980s to early-2000s Valencia, built around 72-hour macro-discotheque rituals on the CV-500 road and expressed in two registers: avant-garde "Diseño Destroy" flyer art (flat neon blocks of safety orange, yellow, magenta and cyan over black ink, halftone comic faces, crosshairs, bat/rocket/oval club logos, modernist typography) and a hard tribal uniform of reversed MA-1 bombers flashing orange lining, shaved "Cenicero" cuts bleached platinum or butane-orange, gold chains, bell-bottoms and platform boots, all captured in grainy on-camera-flash snapshots of parking lots, club façades and dawn dancefloors. Recognize it by the orange-on-black palette, print-grain collage language, Spanish club logotypes and endurance-party subject matter; load this skill for Spanish ruta / mákina nostalgia imagery and its graphic canon.

name: Balearic_Aesthetic
description: Late-1980s Ibiza-born visual style of sun-bleached euphoria — Mediterranean sunsets over open water, soft-focus film light, flowing white linen, canvas shade-sails and whitewashed terraces, in a palette of golden yellow, sunset orange, soft pink, azure and bleached white. Subjects range from seated silhouette crowds watching the sun drop, to minimalist sea-facing villas and pools, aerial rocky coastlines, hammock postcards and lo-fi club-night snapshots, all unified by horizon-anchored, unhurried composition. Recognize it by natural backlight, a sea horizon, linen and haze — never neon, never strobe.

name: Ballet
description: Ballet is the visual aesthetic of classical dance, spanning Renaissance court origins, 19th-century Romantic spectacle and modern rehearsal-room editorial photography. Its DNA is the duality of practice and spectacle: leotards, pink tights and satin pointe shoes at the barre versus bell-shaped Romantic or stiff classical tutus under stage light, in a palette of white, blush pink, cream and black threaded with gold and silver. Recognize it by technical dance posture, tulle and satin textures, barre-mirror-studio interiors, spotlit corps de ballet, and supernatural story-ballet figures (swans, sylphs, sugarplum fairies), rendered anywhere from hand-tinted lithograph and pastel painterliness to grainy monochrome and desaturated contemporary photo.

name: Balletcore
description: Balletcore is an early-2020s, TikTok-born fashion aesthetic that dresses everyday life in ballet practice and performance wear: blush pink, milk white, cool gray, nude and accent black, carried by satin bow flats, slouched leg warmers, tulle skirts, leotards, wrap tops and bolero knits, ribbon lacing and scattered bows. Recognize it by dancerly body language (turnout, port de bras, floor stretches), dance-studio framing with mirrored walls and barres, sheer-versus-knit texture layering, and soft, low-contrast, faded phone-or-film light. It differs from plain coquette frill by its athletic practice-wear register and studio/stage settings, and from classical ballet imagery by its garment-first, lifestyle framing.

name: Ballroom_Culture
description: Ballroom Culture is the competitive underground aesthetic of Black and Latino LGBTQ+ houses in New York City, from 1960s–70s Harlem balls through their late-80s/90s documentary exposure and contemporary cinematic revival. Its visual DNA: a walker frozen mid-stride or mid-vogue on a borrowed hall floor — checkered vinyl, mirror ball, exposed pipes, crowd packed behind barriers — wearing sequins, lamé, feathers, long gloves or sculptural metallic costume in jewel reds, golds, fuchsias and purples, lit either by harsh direct-flash snapshot or saturated gel glamour. Signature elements include angular vogue hand performance and dips, category costumes embodying archetypes ("realness"), trophies, emcee microphones, and chosen-family group portraits with layered gesturing hands.

name: Barber_Beats
description: Barber Beats is the album-art aesthetic of the late-2010s Vaporwave subgenre of the same name: minimalist, sincerely elegant sleeves built from heavily edited classical sculptures, mythological figures and baroque painting fragments, set against solid ink fields or simple patterns with vinyl-and-cassette packaging furniture. Its palette is a strict two-to-four ink print scheme — paper neutrals, matte black, vermilion, ochre, tangerine, cobalt, violet — applied as duotone, halftone or woodcut reproduction, with vertical Japanese type, cropped oversized lettering and restrained Acid Graphics grid devices. The mood is luxurious, melancholy and relaxed, like a late-night lounge; there is no neon, no glitch and no irony.

name: Barbiecore
description: Barbiecore is a hyperfeminine, pink-monochrome aesthetic descended from Mattel's Barbie doll and early-2000s McBling tween culture, built on hot pink, pastel pink, lavender, violet and holographic sparkle. Signature elements include mini dresses in satin, sequin, patent or plush; plastic jewelry, tiny handbags and heart-shaped sunglasses; vanity and self-care props; pink cars, mansions and horses; and groups of friends in coordinated pink, all lit with glossy, high-key brightness. Use this skill for sincere, kid-friendly pink glam — as opposed to the jaded adult irony of Bimbocore and Bubblegum Bitch or the beachy palette of Coconut Girl.

name: Bardcore
description: Bardcore (Tavernwave) is a 2020s internet aesthetic born from medieval-style covers of modern pop songs: parchment creams and sepia washes, muted madder reds, dusty blues and ochre golds; lutes, harps, flutes and frame drums; peasant and ren-faire garb; blackletter cover type and manuscript- or woodcut-style illustration laced with knowing anachronistic humor. Recognize it by aged-paper grounds, candlelit minstrel scenes, costume flat-lays and collages, and the wink of a modern subject rendered in a medieval idiom.

name: Baroque
description: Baroque (c. 1600–1750, born in Rome) is the Counter-Reformation style of orchestrated spectacle: chiaroscuro light falling like a spotlight on ecstatic figures, swirling diagonals and peak-moment action, monumental domes, curved façades and trompe-l'œil ceilings, and interiors upholstered in gilded bronze, crimson damask, marquetry and veined marble. Signature elements include tenebrist light-and-dark contrast, heavy gilt ornament (putti, acanthus rinceaux, cartouches, mascarons, festoons), baldachin beds and state portraits in satin and velvet, and axial palace-garden grandeur. Load this skill for religious ecstasy and martyrdom, classical mythology, absolutist courts, ornate furniture and candlelit dramatic tableau imagery.

name: Basque_Radical_Rock
description: Rock Radikal Vasco (RRV), the 1980s Basque Country punk movement, looks like a photocopied fanzine page or hand-assembled record sleeve: stark black, off-white newsprint and flag red, with Ikurriña green used only as a citation of the Basque flag. Signature elements are the Ikurriña and the red star, cut-and-paste collage, stencil/ransom-note/hand-scrawled typography with deliberate "K" spellings, thresholded duotone protest photography, and crude spiky ink drawings. Typical subjects are street protest, industrial decay, ordinary working-class people, and punk iconography fused with local separatist and leftist symbols.

name: Bastardcore
description: Bastardcore is a late-2010s Tumblr-born "cursed image" aesthetic of petty delinquency: grainy, high-flash night photos of shopping-cart riders, traffic-cone heads, burning skateboards and bullet-holed signs in underpasses, parking lots and badly lit rooms. Its palette is explicitly any color, bound by one rule — murky low-light surroundings pierced by a single harsh bright source (camera flash, fire, sodium streetlamp, headlights). Signature elements include novelty slogan shirts, skeleton masks and cone-or-box heads, grotesque food and vermin, deadpan handwritten statements, and anonymous amateurs caught mid-mischief.

name: Bauhaus
description: Bauhaus (1919–1933; Weimar, Dessau, Berlin) is the German modernist school's total-design aesthetic — primitive geometry (circle, square, triangle), clean unornamented lines, sans-serif type, and functional objects in tubular steel, glass, and lacquered wood. Its palette anchors on the primaries red, yellow, and blue plus black, white, and gray, warming to cream paper and small textile accents of teal, pink, and orange in weaving-workshop pieces. Typical subjects: cantilever and slat chairs, nesting tables, glass-and-metal lamps and tea services, fringed geometric rugs, abstract lithograph posters, and white cubic architecture with ribbon windows.

name: Beach_Goth
description: Beach Goth (also Aloha Goth, Surf Goth) stages classic goth signifiers — skulls and bones, bats, black lace, coffin hardware — inside bright tropical summer settings of sand, palms, shoreline and pool floats. Its palette locks matte black and bone white against sun-bleached sand, sea-glass teal and palm green, rendered in faded sun-bleached film or saturated daylight with deep black masses. Coined by the band The Growlers and circulated on TikTok and Instagram, it reads as deadpan macabre leisure: black swimwear, lace parasols, bat-print towels and skeleton props under a noon sun.

name: Belgian_Popcorn
description: Belgian Popcorn is the visual culture of the late-1960s-to-1970s Belgian underground slow-swing dance scene: dark, opulent provincial dance halls where formally dressed couples turn controlled whirls to obscure 1950s–60s American R&B played at drowsy speed, beer glasses in hand under neon club signs and wood panelling. Its surviving image record is grainy direct-flash monochrome and faded colour snapshot film; its lived palette is deep amber, oxblood, beer-gold and velvet brown. Recognize it by formal vintage attire (minidresses, headbands, narrow ties, cardigans, patterned shirts), coupled slow-swing posture, crowded beer-sodden floors, and 45 rpm vinyl as talisman.

name: Berlin_Techno_Fashion
description: Berlin Techno Fashion ("Berghain aesthetic", Berlin clubwear) is the dress of Berlin's post-reunification techno club scene: head-to-toe black leather, vinyl, mesh and rubber built for twelve hours of dancing, carrying fetish harnesses, chains, chokers, thick platform boots and narrow dark sunglasses, set against concrete walls and overcast grey light. Beside the monochrome core sits a theatrical queer-club pole of costume, body paint, glitter and one loud statement element, and both are rendered with snapshot flash, film grain or deadpan editorial flatness. Load this skill for club-functional black minimalism with fetish hardware, industrial Berlin settings, and an anti-display, anti-fashion attitude.

name: Big_Pop
description: Big Pop is the loud, clean, high-impact pop-culture design of the late 1980s to mid-1990s: huge slanted, stretched or jumbled typography crashing across flat saturated color-blocks in yellow, purple, green, orange and magenta. Signature elements are high-energy dancers and supermodels in leather, spandex and bodycon silhouettes, stark hard-flash shadows, white-void or single-color grounds, and promotional layouts such as CD sleeves, posters, flyers, game box art and dimensional mall signage. Recognize it by its core value of boldness — maximalist shout energy executed with crisp, untextured print cleanliness.

name: Biker
description: Outlaw motorcycle subculture aesthetic born in post-WWII America (1950s onward): black leather jackets and patch-covered vests, tattoos, beards, ripped denim, studs and chrome, anchored by cruisers, choppers, bobbers and sport bikes on desert highways, urban alleys, garages and night streets. Palette of black, gray and red warmed by rust/amber dusk light or cut by hard flash and high-contrast monochrome; motifs of smoke, dust, revving machines and posed intimidation or sex appeal. Reads as toughness, danger and open-road freedom — an attitude, not merely a person on a bike.

name: Bills
description: The Bills (also Yankees, Kinshasa Cowboys, Billism) were a late-1950s youth subculture of Léopoldville, Belgian Congo (now Kinshasa), that restaged the American movie cowboy in segregated Congolese communes — wide-brimmed Stetson-type hats, checkered neck kerchiefs, plaid flannel shirts, denim and high-heeled leather boots, worn with deliberate trail-worn ruggedness and confrontational bravado. The documented visual record is silver-gelatin monochrome portrait photography: solo and crew tableaux posed against reed-mat screens, sun-baked brick and packed-dirt yards; colour embodiments stay inside an earthy triad of leather brown, denim indigo and plaid red.

name: Bimbocore
description: Bimbocore is an early-2020s TikTok-born aesthetic of reclaimed hyperfemininity: frames drenched in hot pink, baby pink and magenta, loaded with glitter, rhinestones, faux fur, velour and patent vinyl, styled after 2000s McBling (Juicy Couture tracksuits, platform heels, flip phones, Playboy and Barbie logos). Signature elements include glossy oversaturated flash lighting, digital sparkle overlays, slogan and affirmation text in curly Y2K fonts, and heavy makeup with black liner and gloss lips. Typical subjects are mirror selfies, accessory flat-lays, dense pink scrapbook collages and doll-like posed figures carrying ironic or political captions.

name: Biopunk
description: Biopunk is cyberpunk's fleshy offshoot — dystopian biotechnology rendered as living architecture, wet specimen labs, and mutated or engineered bodies rather than chrome cyberware. Its palette is shadowy grays, sickly greens, bile yellows and rust browns pierced by bioluminescent cyan, violet and magenta; signature elements include Giger-esque biomechanical forms, glass culture vats and petri-dish fluorescence, skinless flesh interiors, hazard-stenciled containment, and figures in black techwear, lab coats and respirators. Typical subjects are underground DIY labs, corporate clone nurseries, body-horror mutations, and machines that look grown rather than manufactured.

name: Black_Dandyism
description: Black dandyism is the sartorial movement in which Black subjects wield the tailored grammar of the European dandy — constructed suits, waistcoats, hats, neckwear, canes — as self-expression and dignified resistance. Visually it pairs strict tailoring discipline (pressed creases, built shoulders, pinstripes, chalkstripes, plaids, candy stripes in cocoa, charcoal and ivory) with assertive saturation (signal scarlet, emerald, coral, tangerine, petrol teal) and a dense accessory code (flat caps, fedoras, boaters, round spectacles, pocket squares, accent socks, spectator shoes, canes), presented by composed, self-possessed subjects from archival monochrome to glossy red carpet. Recognize it by the fusion of formal European cut, bold chromatic or pattern play, and poised Black self-presentation.

name: Black_Ivy
description: Black Ivy is the African American subversion of WASP preppy dress, crystallized in the Civil Rights and Black Power decades (1950s–1970s) on HBCU campuses and in Black urban professional life, and revived in contemporary editorial fashion. Its visual DNA is a tailored prep skeleton — navy blazers, oxford cloth, tweed, khaki trousers — crossed with Black cultural markers: all-black sunglasses, black turtlenecks, denim, gold chains, natural afros and taper fades, HBCU lettering, sneakers under suiting. Palette runs deep earth tones (maroon, olive, camel, gold, plum, navy, black) with restrained pastel accents, rendered either as archival black-and-white/sepia snapshot or faded analog color film.

name: Black_Metal
description: Black Metal (Trve Kvlt) is the visual language of the early-1990s Norwegian second wave: grainy, high-contrast black-and-white photography, corpse-painted figures in all-black leather, spikes and bullet belts, snowbound conifer forest, candlelight, inverted crosses and pentagrams, and blackletter/Old English type with spiky illegible band logos. The palette is strictly black and white, with a secondary range of muted medieval-manuscript earth tones; the mood is cold, misanthropic and deliberately lo-fi. Recognize it by monochrome grain, corpse paint, occult sigils and winter forest; separate it from Death Metal's fleshy color gore and Dungeon Synth's cozy fantasy illustration.

name: Black_Nouveau
description: Black Nouveau is the 1990s–early-2000s Afro-Asian fusion interior aesthetic of Black American homes: black lacquer and gold anchored in saturated magenta, oxblood, plum or olive rooms, layered with zebra/leopard/tiger prints, Chinoiserie wall fans, folding screens, bamboo and porcelain, and Afrocentric artwork portraying Black figures. Signature look is a maximalist, warmly lamplit domestic room where Orientalist (Japonisme/Chinoiserie) and Afrocentric motifs coexist on every surface, reading as worldly, sensual, aspirational luxury. Recognize by the fusion rule plus animal print plus low golden glow; it is neither pure Art Deco nor pure Orientalism nor Tuscan/boho beige.

name: Bling_Era
description: Bling Era is the late-1990s-to-mid-2000s Dirty South hip-hop aesthetic of conspicuous wealth — tunic-scale throwback jerseys, iced-out platinum chains and grillz, chrome and diamond-encrusted graphics, saturated reds, electric cyans and jersey blues on white or black. Recognize it by harsh flash or neon-club lighting, star-flare sparkles keyed to metal, sneakers worn over the shoulder like necklaces, spinning rims, McMansion and megaclub sets, and a triumphant flex-culture mood. It separates from McBling's pink rhinestone femininity, Y2K Futurism's tech chrome, and golden-age hip-hop's gritty street realism.

name: Blob_World
description: Blob World (aka mushbuhcore) is a mid-2010s 3D-render aesthetic of inflated, melted, gelatinous organic forms in matte clay, glossy jelly, translucent resin and fuzzy flock, colored in powdered pastels, saturated candy gradients or single-hue saturation with sparse neon accents. Signature elements include limbless hyper-flexible mascots, floating rings and checkerboard floors, squiggle furniture, balloon-inflated typography, and a cheerful-surreal mood with an uncanny body-horror undertow. Recognize it by soft-body deformation, candy shader vocabulary and soft studio-render lighting.

name: Bloghouse
description: Bloghouse is the flash-blown, neon-soaked visual language of the mid-to-late-2000s electro-house blogosphere: direct on-camera flash, overexposed glossy skin, acid pink/green/metallic-silver neons against club black, skinny jeans, cheap leather jackets, shutter shades and American Apparel basics caught mid-movement in cramped party frames. Its graphic layer is sticker-bomb flyers, blog headers and album art with distorted MS Paint typography. Recognize it by cheap-digital-camera glare, glowsticks, plastic cups, DJ booths and reckless posed confidence — messy but confident, trashy yet stylish, sitting between rave, electroclash and Y2K digital grime.

name: Blogspot_Scene
description: Blogspot Scene is the xerox-collage packaging aesthetic of the early-2000s US hypnagogic drone/ambient cassette and CDR underground: grainy photocopied cut-and-paste montages in black, white and toner-tinted greys, stocked with aliens, cryptids, pyramids, obelisks, armillary spheres and murky landscape fragments. Its signature elements are third-generation photocopy decay (halftone dots, toner speckle, cassette J-card fold creases), tiny typewritten or label-maker caption strips, and surrealist juxtaposition with no narrative explanation. Typical subjects are esoteric archival ephemera — UFO snapshots, Victorian engravings, mid-century press photos, tropical foliage, starfields over water — reassembled on paper and scanned flat.

name: Blokecore
description: Blokecore (also Ladcore) is a 2020s TikTok-born aesthetic built on British football-fan dress: vintage 1980s–90s club jerseys — obscure Second Division shirts prized — worn over basic light-wash jeans and old Adidas sneakers such as the Samba, posed deadpan in mundane domestic, street or terrace settings. Its palette is whatever team colours the kit carries, anchored by denim blue and white gum-soled trainers; its register is amateur phone-camera, often vertical with plain caption overlays. Recognize it by the visible replica shirt worn as fashion, the crossed-arms stare, and the unpolished working-class British backdrop.

name: Blokette
description: Blokette is a 2020s TikTok-born micro-aesthetic that stages a deliberate collision between masculine football culture and hyper-feminine coquette dressing: numbered football shirts, striped track jackets and Adidas Sambas paired with pleated mini skirts, satin hair ribbons, leg warmers, knee-high socks and ballet flats. Its palette blocks saturated team colours (navy, red, yellow, kit-white) against blush pastels and cream, and its imagery reads as casual, flash-lit snapshot photography of everyday places. The recognition anchor is the gender-contrast pairing itself — at least one blokecore sportswear piece and at least one coquette-delicate piece in the same frame.

name: Bloomcore
description: Bloomcore (also Flowercore or the Floral Aesthetic) is a late-2010s social-media aesthetic in which flowers are the protagonist: wildflower meadows, rose-clad cottage windows, poppy and tulip fields, chintz and botanical prints, and gardens carried into the home. Its palette runs from sunlit naturalistic greens, creams and petal pastels to a text-sanctioned dark-floral pole of deep indigo, black and rich red, all rendered in golden, dappled, film-soft light. Recognize it by bloom-dense frames with no empty negative space, domestic objects nestled in grass, floral garments on cropped anonymous figures, and a nostalgic, biophilic, quiet-life mood.

name: Blueberry_Girl
description: Blueberry Girl is a 2020s TikTok/Pinterest "fruit girl" microtrend built as a moodboard identity around a cool blue palette — milky "blueberry milk" powder blue through chambray denim to deep navy — set against white, cream, silver and sparse black. Signature elements include blueberries and pale blue manicures, stacks of books and reading nooks, cozy patterned interiors (gingham, ditsy florals, toile, eyelet), cable knits, denim, satin hair bows, delicate silver jewelry, tea cups, headphones, cats and ocean horizons, all rendered in soft diffused cool light with intimate, often faceless snapshot framing. The mood is calm, introspective, studious and nostalgically comfortable.

name: Bobby-Soxer
description: American teen-girl subculture aesthetic of the mid-to-late 1940s, built on folded-down white ankle socks worn with black-and-white saddle shoes or penny loafers, pleated skirts, and Shetland sweaters over white blouses. Palette centers on structural white, pastel or bright knit solids, and two-tone shoe leather, surviving mostly as grainy black-and-white press and newsprint photography. Typical subjects are groups of adolescent girls at soda fountains, sock hops, theatre queues, and swooning crooner-idol crowds, expressing peer conformity and giddy emotional release.

name: Bodikon
description: Bodikon (body-con) is the Japanese Bubble-Economy club and street fashion of late 1985–1994: body-hugging neon mini dresses and shoulder-padded power suits worn with long one-length black "wanren" hair, rooster-comb bangs, chunky gold jewellery and logo luxury bags. Visually it reads as flash-lit 35mm film and offset magazine print — saturated reds, yellows, hot pinks and sequin blues against black, cream and gold, with animal prints, fur boas and feathered Juli fans from the disco otachidai platform. Confident, sexy, loudly affluent: the office lady gone dancing at Juliana's Tokyo.

name: Bogan
description: Bogan is the proudly lowbrow working-class aesthetic of 1980s-onwards Australia and New Zealand: mullet haircuts, red-and-black flannelette shirts worn open over cracked-print band or beer-logo singlets, denim cutoffs, ugg boots and country hats, captured with flat on-camera flash in sun-bleached suburban backyards, driveways, caravan parks and poker-machine clubs. Its palette anchors on red, black and orange against faded denim, grey marle and corrugated-iron grey, with fluro workwear as an accent; signature props include stubbies in stubby holders, Holden/Ford muscle cars and utes, and Bali souvenir singlets. The mood is larrikin, anti-authoritarian and self-deprecating — unrefined by conviction, never glossy.

name: Boho-Chic
description: Boho-Chic is the early-2000s festival-fashion aesthetic of flowing peasant blouses, tiered maxi skirts and caftans in cream, beige, rust and warm brown, cinched with wide studded belts and stacked with layered pendant necklaces, bangles, slouchy suede boots and slouchy hobo bags. Recognize it by sun-faded earthy palettes, paisley and floral prints, fringe, crochet and embroidery, golden-hour or soft overcast light, and a curated undone-ness in candid street, roadside, field and flat-lay imagery. It differs from historical Bohemian by its polished, designer, aspirational finish.

name: Bombardier
description: Romanian-Balkan flex subculture of the mid-2010s to early 2020s, native to phone cameras and TikTok verticals: near-black molded athletic wear or fake-luxury logo tees and baroque kitsch prints, thick gold Cuban-link chains, tinted designer sunglasses, tattooed high fades, sneakers only, posed with or inside older black BMW, Audi and Mercedes sedans. Values ostentatious flexing and sincere kitsch — "lack of taste" worn as a badge rather than a flaw.

name: Bon_Chic,_Bon_Genre
