Signature elements include heart/star/flower scatter, glitter and translucent pink plastic, faux fur and feather boas, makeover-salon and sleepover scenes, big-eyed cartoon tween characters, and high-key studio promo photography. Recognize it by its ornate, playful, kid-scale "diva" femininity — mall retail, toy boxes, scented cosmetics, tween pop marketing — as distinct from adult glamour or tech-futurist Y2K.

name: Cutecore
description: Cutecore is a 2020s internet aesthetic (Tumblr-born, TikTok-spread) that juxtaposes Heisei-era kawaii — Sanrio mascots, frills, pastel pink/yellow/blue, pudding and strawberry stickers, pink Nintendo DS props, cluttered pink bedroom shrines — with signifiers of somatic horror and distress: photorealistic blood splatters, bandages, gauze, anxious kaomoji, and lo-fi JPEG decay. Recognize it by pink-dominant pastel maximalism punctured by red blood accents, compression artifacts, and claustrophobic clutter; a sanitized non-gory variant ("Kawaii Kei") keeps the clutter, decay and melancholy but drops the blood.

name: Cyber_Angel
description: Cyber Angel (also Frutiger Angelic, Digital Angel, Internet Angel) is an early-2020s Tumblr/Pinterest aesthetic that fuses 90s–2000s sci-fi anime, outdated internet technology and Y2K retrofuturism with angelic iconography. Recognize it by a high-key white–ice-blue–silver palette, overexposed "angel glow" blooms and lens flares, VHS scanlines and dithered anime halftone, old OS windows and media-player UI chrome, white-haired anime girls, feathered wings and halos, and curved white utopian architecture. The mood is tender, escapist and hopefully nostalgic — a digital heaven rendered in baby blue.

name: Cyber_Doll
description: Cyber Doll is a mid-2020s TikTok-born aesthetic of deliberately uncanny porcelain-doll self-portraits: faces digitally reconstructed (enlarged glassy eyes, shrunken nose and mouth, tiny V-line jaw, poreless pale skin) under muted, gloomy dark-pastel or near-monochrome filters. Signature elements include schoolgirl-coded sailor uniforms and gym wear or frilled white doll dresses, hair ribbons, plush props, cursive lowercase text overlays, and vertical phone-camera framing in plain domestic interiors. Recognize it by the tension between doll prettiness and obvious digital artificiality — the uncanny valley is the goal, not a flaw.

name: Cyber_Ghetto
description: Cyber Ghetto is a mid-2010s Tumblr-born fusion aesthetic, coined by Belgian artist Ruth Laveau, that welds late-90s/early-2000s hip-hop streetwear and bling to kawaii cute, seapunk teal, grunge distress and lo-fi digital graphics. Recognize it in flash-lit fit pics and accessory close-ups: neon-colored braids, rhinestone pendants and blackletter chrome script, holographic vinyl, mesh and baggy airbrushed denim, Japanese writing, smileys and aliens, camcorder timestamps and galaxy borders, in magenta, acid green, aqua and pastel pink anchored by black. Its mood is defiantly playful self-invention — a cyberspace refuge for the marginalized, nostalgic for a future that already looks dated.

name: Cyber_Grunge
description: Cyber Grunge (a.k.a. Y2K Grunge or Military Y2K) is a 2020s streetwear aesthetic fusing 90s grunge earthiness with Y2K futurism: distressed, layered, androgynous outfits in black, gray, olive, khaki and washed blue, built on low-rise flared cargo pants, "subversive basics" with cut-outs and mesh, chunky platform boots, bucket hats or beanies, and tech accessories like oversized headphones and goggles. Recognize it by deadpan full-body lookbook or street-snap framing, utilitarian straps and pockets, star motifs and pearl necklaces, and a matte, faded grade — often rendered as grainy digicam photos, zine collages, or muted cel-shaded anime illustration. The mood is urban, utilitarian, nostalgically disillusioned.

name: Cyber_Stylin’
description: Cyber Stylin’ is the umbrella aesthetic of mid-2000s to early-2010s browser dress-up games, pixel Dollz and glossy fashion-girl illustration: vector-cel or airbrushed doll figures in Y2K wardrobes (low-rise jeans, mini skirts, crop tops, newsboy caps, waist chains, layered bling) set on flat pastel or boldly saturated pink-purple-white-brown-blue-black grounds. Signature reads are doll-asset compositions (full-body outfit displays, squad lineups, avatar busts), hard specular gloss on hair and lips, sparkle glints and script or bubble-font wordmarks. Load this skill when an image looks like customizable paper-doll art from the Flash-game web — feminine, playful, self-expressive — rather than photography, anime, or modern flat design.

name: Cyber_Swag
description: Cyber Swag (a.k.a. Night Swag, Snow Swag, Alt Swag) is an early-2020s TikTok/SoundCloud aesthetic that fuses Y2K-revival streetwear — baggy stacked jeans, shark hoodies, robbery masks, Hello Kitty/Sonic/Spiderman plush — with cybersigilism chrome stars, neon glow icons on black voids, and lo-fi digicam photography washed in a single oversaturated tint (violet, acid green, hot pink, deep blue, red). Signature elements: digital stars and sigil hearts, liquid-chrome Metalheart emblems, pixel dither and halftone textures, black gradient borders, foggy winter forests and after-hours urban flash snapshots, "Ghastly Panic"-style font captions. Typical subjects: masked teens in color-matched hoodies, glowing flat icons, pixelated cartoon characters, money piles and lighters under translucent color washes.

name: Cybercore
description: Cybercore is a 2020s Pinterest/TikTok revivalist aesthetic that remixes Y2K-era retro-futurism into a melancholic, ethereal edit: saturated electric blues, chrome silvers and harsh whites over CRT scanlines, Windows-95-style dialogue boxes, pixel cursors, flip phones and CRT hardware, late-90s anime girls and virtual idols, planets, angels, butterflies and four-point star sparkles, softened by pastel pink accents and tiny lyric text. Recognition hinges on cold blue-monochrome tinting, halftone/pixel textures, self-emissive screen glow, and legacy-software UI layers fused with organic or celestial symbolism. Mood is nostalgic, lonely, dreamlike — anemoia for an early internet the viewer never lived.

name: Cyberdelia
description: Cyberdelia (cyberdelic) is the utopian techno-psychedelic aesthetic of the late 1980s to mid-1990s: primitive early CGI, fractal tunnels and kaleidoscopic mandalas rendered in fluorescent acid colors — magenta, cyan, acid green, hot orange, electric violet — glowing against black or deep-violet voids. Signature elements include chrome and oil-slick marbled 3D blobs, glossy orbs, radial starbursts, 3D metallic or iridescent typography, warped checker grids, and rave or hacking iconography carried on flyers, album covers and software ads. Recognize it by its euphoric, transcendent mood and deliberate early-90s digital primitivism, as opposed to cyberpunk's dystopian grit or vaporwave's muted irony.

name: Cybergoth
description: Cybergoth is the late-1990s electronic-industrial club style built on a black PVC/vinyl base cut with a single stark UV-reactive neon accent (green, pink, blue, orange). Its signature silhouette stacks synthetic dreadfalls ("cyberlox"), forehead-pushed goggles or respirator/gas masks, biohazard and circuit motifs, faux-fur "fluffies" and massive platform boots onto androgynous club dancers. Load this skill for neon-on-black rave-goth fashion, industrial-dance club scenes, and festival looks defined by lox, goggles, masks and platforms rather than by gothic-rock romanticism.

name: Cyberminimalism
description: Cyberminimalism (also called Cyberbougie) is a hyper-reductive digital-design aesthetic of the late 2010s tech web: a near-black or paper-white canvas holding little beyond grotesque sans-serif type, a strict module grid (often Apple-style bento tiling), and one luminous color gradient — smooth or grainy — glowing like a self-lit orb in the void. Typical subjects are landing pages, app UIs, product feature grids, brand identity boards and event posters, all rendered with premium sleekness, monochrome typography and vast negative space. Recognize it by black backgrounds, bento grids, black-or-white sans type, and gradients doing the only color work in the frame.

name: Cyberpop
description: Cyberpop (also called "cyber") is a 1990s Japanese retro-futuristic street and rave aesthetic that imagines the future as bright, neon and fun: hot pink, electric cyan, lime and holographic silver rendered in patent vinyl, faux fur and laser-cut acrylic. Signature elements are orbit rings and shoulder puffs on garments, wide-leg UFO pants, platform boots with fluffy leg warmers, cyberlox dread falls, chunky goggles or futuristic headphones, and space-motif jewelry (aliens, rockets, stars, shooting stars). Recognize it in Harajuku street fashion shots, club flyers, accessory display walls and Y2K-flavored game key art — always optimistic and party-leaning, never dystopian or dark.

name: Cyberprep
description: Cyberprep (post-cyberpunk) is the utopian mirror of cyberpunk: clean white and light-blue futurism of a leisure-driven society where cybernetics serve sport, pleasure and self-improvement. Expect high-key daylight or orderly neon, glossy white parametric architecture, glass-and-steel lattices, monorails and flying transit, holographic interfaces, friendly robotics and elegant prosthetics, rendered as polished digital paint or clean renders. Signature DNA: white/pale-ice-blue dominance with cyan and orchid accents, optimistic "high tech/high life" mood, and cityscape, cyberspace, technology and robotics as core motifs.

name: Cyberpunk
description: Cyberpunk is the 1980s-born dystopian near-future aesthetic of "high tech, low life": night-time megacities drenched in neon cyan, magenta and violet, rain-slick streets mirroring kanji signage and holographic ads, chrome prosthetics and tactical techwear worn by marginalized outsiders. Recognize it by black-dominant frames lit by practical neon and screen glow, layered vertical density of megastructures and cable runs, smog haze, and machinic augmentation; subjects range from sublime city vistas and street-level crowds to studio-lit helmet studies and monochrome techwear lookbooks.

name: Cybersigilism
description: Cybersigilism (aka Neo-Tribal / Gen Z Tribal) is a late-2010s Berlin club-born blackwork tattoo and graphic-design aesthetic built from needle-thin, blade-sharp spiky linework: bilateral sigils that fuse biomechanical circuitry, "vamped" hearts, stars and crosses, and illegible extreme-metal logotypes into cursed chrome-and-black glyphs. Its palette is black, charcoal and silver/chrome on void-black or paper-white fields, corrupted by deep-fried scan grain, airbrushed metal bevels and rave-flyer type blocks; typical subjects are tattoos on skin, band and rapper logos, album covers, streetwear prints and sigil-creatures.

name: Cybertwee
description: Cybertwee is a 2014 feminist net-art aesthetic that rewrites cyberpunk in pastel: pink and lilac washes, glitter, holographic film and kawaii emojis fused with LEDs, microchips and Y2K-era consumer tech like flip phones and GameCube controllers. Look for lace, ruffles, crystals, iced cookies, gentle selfies and soft low-poly 3D dreamscapes lit by LED glow — technology rendered tender, sincere and deliberately girly.

name: DIY_Punk
description: DIY Punk (Xerox Punk, punk zine) is the cut-and-paste graphic language of the late-1970s British punk scene: threshold-black photocopied imagery, ransom-note cut-out lettering, marker-scrawled gig details and slapdash amateur collage on cheap off-white paper, in black ink with at most one flat spot color. Recognize it by halftone dot degradation, torn cut edges, typewriter type colliding with hand lettering, defaced official portraits and flags, and hand-annotated prices and dates on flyers, fanzine spreads and record sleeves.

name: DORFic
description: DORFic (also called PolySunk) is the corporate-industrial futurism of the mid-2000s to mid-2010s: stark white minimalist architecture, interfaces and cityscapes flooded with daylight and structured by saturated orange and yellow panels, hexagonal tech patterns and low-poly geometry. Signature elements include glossy reflective floors, glass curtain walls, halftone-dot and vector-swoosh graphics, near-monochrome techwear or business-casual figures with visors, gloves and protective gear, and a sanitized dark alternate mode of black rooms lit by glowing orange panels. Typical subjects are office interiors and congress halls, game and console dashboards, feature-phone and robot product shots, and athletic figures in motion through sterile white space.

name: Dadcore
description: Dadcore is a late-2010s fashion aesthetic built on the deliberate adoption of the middle-aged suburban father's wardrobe: stonewashed denim, jorts, pleated trousers, faded promotional t-shirts, polar-fleece half-zips, windbreakers, washed baseball caps and chunky white "ugly" sneakers worn with visible athletic ankle socks. Its palette is heather grey, stonewashed blue, khaki, navy and faded primary tones; its register is unposed, comfort-first and anti-aspirational, captured as candid street snaps, domestic interiors, flat studio lookbooks or faded family-album portraits. Recognize it by the neither-oversized-nor-slim fit, honest laundered wear, mundane suburban props and deadpan mood; separate it from Normcore's blank anonymity, Gorpcore's technical gear, Eclectic Grandpa's curated vintage and Vacation Dadcore's resort context.

name: Dandy
description: Dandy is the late 18th–19th century British and French aesthetic of studied, effortless masculine elegance: impeccably tailored dark wool coats in black, midnight blue and charcoal, starched white linen cravats, top hats, walking canes, gloves and mirror-polished boots, carried with an air of cool nonchalance (sprezzatura). Its visual record runs through Regency fashion plates, lithographed portraits and early monochrome or sepia photography, all governed by a subdued palette where cut and fabric quality replace color and ornament. Recognize it by restraint: a sharp precise silhouette, white linen as the single bright note against sober darks, and a bored, detached, self-possessed pose.

name: Danish_Pastel
description: Danish Pastel (also Pastel Scandi, Dopamine Decor) is a 2020s Gen-Z interior and graphic aesthetic of bright candy pastels — pink, lilac, baby blue, soft yellow, pistachio — layered over naturally lit white rooms with simple Scandinavian furniture. Signature elements include wavy and scalloped mirrors, twist and bubble-cube novelty candles, wavy checkerboard rugs, pastel milk crate bins, blob-shaped ceramics, flat cut-out motivational posters, and tulips or houseplants in ribbed glass vases. Use when recognizing or generating airy, playfully cluttered domestic vignettes, product flat-lays, or flat vector graphics that feel optimistic, childlike and comforting rather than rustic, moody or neon-loud.

name: Dark_Academia
description: Dark Academia is a mid-2010s internet aesthetic that romanticizes elite 19th-century European and Ivy-League schooling — candlelit libraries, Gothic and Neoclassical architecture, white marble busts, gilded-frame Old Master paintings, and prep wardrobes of tweed, sweater vests and pleated skirts. Its palette is black, deep brown, forest green, burgundy, tan and cream under chiaroscuro or sunless overcast light, carrying moods of melancholy intellectualism, mystery and decadence. Recognize it by annotated books, mahogany paneling, pointed arches, autumn-to-winter light, and a composed, reverent stillness.

name: Dark_Aero
description: Dark Aero (aka Mata Nero / Frutiger Ego) is the sleek dark-mode offshoot of Frutiger Aero, c. 2001–2015: near-black graphite voids lit by aero glass, piano-black lacquer, chrome speculars and neon spectral accents (electric blue, teal, magenta, amber). Signature subjects are premium consumer and enterprise electronics — smartphones, consoles, media-player UIs, game menus, promo ads — plus equalizer pulses, spectrum columns, bokeh, auroras and holographic flares. Recognize it by glossy skeuomorphic realism floating in black; distinguish it from Frutiger Aero (no nature), Flat Design (gloss present), Hexatron (no hex grids) and Metalheart (no industrial metal).

name: Dark_Cabaret
description: Dark Cabaret (aka Punk Cabaret, Cabaret Noir, Brechtian Punk Cabaret) is the theatrical, music-born aesthetic that fuses Weimar-era cabaret, Victorian/Edwardian tailoring and burlesque costuming with punk and goth darkness: stark white mime-or-clown face paint with heavy dark-rimmed eyes and bold lips, bowler hats, pinstripe suits, corsets, candy-stripe stockings and fishnets, staged against red curtains, checkered floors, fairground machinery or bare studio voids. Its palette is soot black, bone white and oxblood red with muted sepia or slate intermediates and stark value contrast; its lighting is spotlight, candleflare or harsh flash falling off into black. Mood is grotesque elegance, dark humor and unsettling theatricality — performer portraits, double acts and revue tableaux with canes, parasols, teacups, pianos and accordions.

name: Dark_Circus
description: Dark Circus (aka Dark Carnival, Haunted Circus, Creepy Clown) is the horror inversion of the vintage circus: soot-black and bone-white striped tents, oxblood crimson, tarnished gold and sepia fog, lit by wan Edison bulbs, candles and failing string lights. Signature elements are hand-lettered freak show banners, distressed ringmaster tailcoats and crushed top hats, cracked clown and pierrot greasepaint, harlequin diamonds, iron cages, marionettes and abandoned carousel rides. Rooted in Victorian sideshow iconography and codified by 1980s killer-clown horror plus The Night Circus's monochrome tents; expect low-key foggy lighting, decayed carnival architecture and menace lurking behind the spectacle.

name: Dark_Fantasy
description: Dark Fantasy (Fantasy Horror) is a cinematic, pre-modern fantasy aesthetic inflected by horror — desaturated grades of black, midnight blue, deep forest green and dull silver, punctured only by small accents of blood crimson or candle-flame amber. Signature elements are crumbling stone castles and ruins, fog-choked spindly forests, corvids, bone and iron props, dripping candles, bloodied blades, and figures in heavy wool, leather and velvet (hooded cloaks, corsets, crowns, masks, blank pallid makeup) lit by a single dim source under overcast twilight. The mood is foreboding, melancholic and macabrely beautiful, privileging moral ambiguity and tragic fate over heroic triumph.

name: Dark_Girly_and_Sweet_Girly
description: Japanese boutique-kawaii fashion (2019–present) built on ultra-feminine blouses with Peter Pan or sailor collars, ribbon bows, raschel lace and high-waisted mini skirts, deliberately counterpointed by edgy hardware — heart-shaped buckles, eyelets, chains, cross charms, fishnets — and sad "pien" makeup. Coordinates obey a strict two-color law on a black or white base with muted pink, grey plaid or rare pastel accents, finished with platform loafers or multi-strap mary janes, lace stockings, twin tails with hime bangs, and mini backpacks or totes hung with plush keychains. Spans a "dark" pole (black, silver/gold hardware, garters) and a "sweet" pole (white and pink, rectangle headdresses, heart charms, also called Ryousangata), overlapping but not identical to Jirai Kei.

name: Dark_Naturalism
description: Dark Naturalism is a 2020s Tumblr aesthetic that fuses Dark Academia's scholarly props with Naturecore's outdoors, relocating study to fogged conifer woods, damp field paths and the naturalist's desk. Its palette is sage and forest green, charcoal, bone cream and oxblood maroon; its signature elements are forest fog at liminal hours, pressed flowers and tea-stained field notes, open windows, linen-and-plaid layering, and respectfully kept bones, beetles and spiders. Recognize it by mist-softened trail light, specimen-and-notebook still lifes, weather-worn boot-and-skirt fashion, and a mood of quiet mystery and diligent curiosity.

name: Dark_Nautical
description: Dark Nautical (also Lighthousecore, Sailorcore) is a 2020s internet aesthetic of melancholic Atlantic maritime life: fog-swallowed lighthouses, storm seas, weathered rope, stone harbor cottages and lantern-lit windows, rendered in desaturated slate blues, sea greens, fog greys and sandy browns with film-grain muting. Recognize it by solitary sentinels against vast water, salt-worn materials, overcast or single-amber-point lighting, and an undercurrent of dread and isolation beneath a serene surface. It is the working-coast, grieving-coast counterpart to crisp prep Nautical, theatrical Pirate and sunny Coastal leisure imagery.

name: Dark_Nymphet
description: Dark Nymphet is a 2010s Tumblr-born photo aesthetic of gloomy, grainy adolescence: a washed grey-blue film haze over black, bone white and oxblood red, with red lips, red nails and red props as the only saturated accents in frame. Signature elements include lace camisoles and ribbon corsets, mini skirts with Mary Janes or scuffed Converse and frilled socks, pearls and heart lockets, cigarettes in heart-shaped ashtrays, lollipops, cherries and ballet shoes, all rendered in analog grain, dust specks and melancholic stillness. Recognize it by its undone vintage-girl melancholy — Nabokov via Lana Del Rey — darker and grungier than Nymphet, romantic where Kinderwhore is punk.

name: Dark_Romanticism
description: Pessimistic branch of the Romantic movement (late 18th–19th century, American and European), visualized as chiaroscuro scenes of psychological dread: ink-black and umber darkness pierced by one moon, candle, or phosphorescent apparition-glow, with bone-white shrouds, sickly greens and storm teals. Signature elements are sublime hostile nature (fog, thunderstorms, deep water, dark forests), ruined and funerary architecture, demons, ghosts, doppelgangers and witches, and emblems of death (skulls, biers, shrouds) staged around a small, guilty, obsessed or trance-bound human figure. Reads as literary illustration or visionary painting — matte, washed, etched or glazed — never glossy, never brightly lit, never hopeful.

name: Dark_Triad
description: A monochrome, short-video-edit aesthetic born on TikTok around 2023 from looksmaxxing and blackpill culture, built on crushed-black, blown-white high-contrast portraits of sharp-jawed men in tailored suits or leather, classical statues, and gym steel. Its signature marks are the glowing triangular "Dark Triad" pyramid logo watermarked or flashing over footage, harsh chiaroscuro sidelight carving jawlines and "hunter eyes," a chrome-and-grey palette occasionally skewed by a cold teal, green or violet cast or a single red accent, and vertical 9:16 framing with condensed all-caps captions. Recognize it by templated aggression: digital grain, posterized thresholds, cigarette smoke, and emotional detachment performed as dominance.

name: Darksynth
description: Darksynth (also Dark Synthwave, Dreadwave, Slasher Synth) is the aggressive early-2010s offshoot of synthwave whose artwork fuses neon-noir cyberpunk dystopia with occult and satanic symbolism — pentagrams, inverted crosses, chrome skulls, masked killers — over near-black grounds flooded with magenta, deep red, electric blue and violet. Signature look: airbrushed comic-book illustration degraded by VHS grain and scanlines, chrome metal-style logotypes, glowing eyes and visors, neon perspective grids, and John Carpenter-esque 80s horror menace. Load this skill to recognize or generate "retro-noir / cyber-doom" imagery that is deliberately darker and heavier than outrun synthwave.

name: Dau_al_Set
description: Visual language of the post-Civil-War Catalan avant-garde (Barcelona, 1948–1956): dreamlike Surrealist-Dada imagery rendered as trembling calligraphic ink lines, esoteric sign-scatter (stars, crescents, sun-discs, open eyes, crosses, alchemical glyphs), and fantastic horned or masked creatures on bone-white paper or dark earthy ochre grounds pierced by isolated vermilion, cadmium-yellow and cobalt accents. Recognize it by distorted portraits annotated with astral symbols, checkered harlequin bodies, spindly insect limbs, handwritten Catalan text and dice/seven numerals, and by scratched, scrubbed matter textures that bridge toward Art Informel.

name: De_Stijl
description: De Stijl (Neoplasticism), the Dutch movement of 1917–1931, builds every image from straight horizontal and vertical black bars and flat rectangular planes of red, blue and yellow plus the non-colors white, black and gray, balanced asymmetrically into a "dynamic equilibrium." Recognizable in orthogonal grid paintings, color-blocked architecture and furniture (Rietveld's Schröder House, Red and Blue Chair), and revival fashion and product design; absolutely no curves, diagonals, shading or naturalistic representation. Mood is austere, utopian calm: reduction to essentials as a spiritual and social program.

name: Dead_Inside
description: Dead Inside (zxc ghoul) is a post-Soviet 2010s teen subculture aesthetic built on a strict black-and-white monochrome punctured by a single blood-red accent — glowing red irises, red slashes, red duotone bursts. Its signature look pairs Tokyo Ghoul-derived manga art (screentone halftone, pencil crosshatch, inverted negative space, white hair over obscured faces) with lo-fi phone photos of teens in oversized black hoodies, checkered trousers and face-covering bangs. Recognize it by the black/white/red-only palette, halftone and ink-blot texture, hidden or manically grinning ghoul faces, and a numb, nihilistic phonk-avatar mood.

name: Death_Metal
description: Death Metal is the album-art and subculture aesthetic of the extreme metal subgenre born from early-1980s thrash: hand-painted gore tableaus, anatomical and skull iconography, dripping blood-red or chrome logos, and a lived uniform of long hair, beards, battle vests and camo pants. Its palette anchors on blood red, rust orange, bone white and void black, lit by theatrical single-source glow, with crafted painterly macabre (crypts, altars, corpses, écorché figures) fused to near-illegible metal typography. Recognize it against black metal's monochrome rawness, gorecore's photographic shock collage, and generic horror's cinematic polish.

name: Deathrock
description: Deathrock is the early-1980s punk–goth hybrid born in Los Angeles clubs and London's Batcave, recognizable by the deathhawk (a teased, backcombed mohawk with long side pieces), corpse-white foundation with smudged black eyeliner and dark lipstick on all genders, ripped fishnets worn as tights, shirts or spiderweb sleeves, and hand-painted black leather covered in occult and B-movie horror lettering. Its palette is black-dominant with bone-white skin and sparse accents of blood red, purple or cold blue, typically delivered through grainy high-contrast monochrome or faded, flash-blown color snapshots. The mood is campy macabre theatre fused with DIY punk scruff: bats, spider webs, skeletons and cemetery motifs applied with safety pins, studs and uneven brushwork.

name: Decadence
description: Decadence is the fin-de-siècle (1880s–1890s) aesthetic of artificiality and morbid beauty, an extreme offshoot of Aestheticism and Symbolism embodied by Beardsley's ink plates, Wilde's Salomé and The Yellow Book. It reads in two registers: high-contrast black ink on ivory paper with flat black masses, lace-like stipple and thin ruled borders, or jewel-tone painting in deep purple, emerald, ruby, sapphire, old gold and sickly absinthe green. Signature content: cut orchids and lilies, absinthe and opium paraphernalia, femmes fatales and androgynous youths, peacock feathers, brocade and lacquer interiors, languid reclining poses carrying an erotic-macabre undertow.

name: Deco-Luxe
description: Deco-Luxe is the mid-1970s-to-early-1990s luxury revival of Art Deco and Streamline Moderne — lacquered jewel-tone or black-and-white interiors, chrome, polished brass, mirror and etched glass, sunbursts, chevrons and ziggurat steps held in symmetrical, low-key light. Typical subjects are hotel lobbies, lounges and restaurants, setback skyscrapers, airbrushed event posters and monogram-like corporate identities that broadcast 1980s materialism and status. Recognize it by gloss-plus-metal sheen, stepped symmetry and nocturnal glamor, as distinct from period Art Deco patina, Disco Deco club kitsch and Memphis Lite pastels.

name: Decon-dustrial
description: Decon-dustrial (Deconstructivist Industrial) is a late-1980s-to-early-2000s aesthetic of factory adaptive reuse in which skewed, intersecting steel and timber structures are left raw and exposed beside ductwork, raw cables, bolted plates and visible welds, in a palette of brown, black, white, yellow and orange punctuated by signal red. Signature elements include cage lights and halogen worklights, corrugated metal, OSB plywood, cinderblock, translucent polycarbonate sheet, exaggerated joints, and vintage commercial signage vernacular, composing rooms that read as frozen mid-construction or mid-collapse. Typical subjects are alternative clothing stores, trendy urban coffee shops, industrial loft conversions, jagged metal retail racks, open steel stairs, and early-digital-era heavy-tech graphic design.

name: Deconstructivism
description: Late-20th-century architectural movement, catalyzed by the 1988 MoMA "Deconstructivist Architecture" exhibition, whose buildings fragment, tilt and collide — skewed non-rectilinear volumes, cantilevers that deny their supports, and collage-like assembly held in controlled chaos. Palette of muted metallics (titanium, stainless steel, zinc), exposed or painted concrete, curtain-wall glass and white enamel, punctuated at most by a single accent system such as folly red, pastel enamel paneling or patinated green. Recognize by destabilized massing that looks about to collapse, visible standing-seam or shingle cladding, sliced voids and abstract follies; subjects run from museums, concert halls and memorials to bridges, metro stations, fire stations and leaning towers.

name: Decoplex
description: Decoplex (90s Deco Revival) is the 1990s–2000s third wave of Art Deco, built from neon-traced movie-multiplex architecture, chrome-edged diners and zigzag transit halls in vibrant neon red, yellow and blue over black or deep jewel grounds. Its signatures are towering vertical blade signs and fins, parallel speed lines, sunbursts and swoops, and thick center-extruded geometric type with polished metallic faces or neon edging. Typical subjects are theater entryways and lobbies, concession stands, aero-poster heroes, and deco-revival logos and title cards, all carrying a playful, cinematic nostalgia for Hollywood's golden age seen through a 1990s lens.

name: Decopunk
description: Decopunk (Ottensian Dieselpunk) is the sleek, utopian half of dieselpunk — retrofuturism built on 1910s–1940s Art Deco and Streamline Moderne: stepped-setback ziggurat skyscrapers, sunburst ray fans, chevron and zigzag ornament, polished chrome and brass, zoot suits and bias-cut dresses. Its palette runs from vermilion/black/cream poster triads and gold-with-teal metallics to sepia monochrome and pastel painted cityscapes; subjects range from counterfactual "world of tomorrow" metropolises with airships and monorails to glamorous period figures and Deco-framed poster graphics, often with one anachronistic touch such as VHS in a lacquered cabinet. Recognize it by gleam: surfaces are polished, light is theatrical, and even its shadows keep their shine — grit and soot belong to dieselpunk, not here.

name: Decora
description: Decora (Decora Kei) is a maximalist Japanese street fashion from late-1990s Harajuku whose visual DNA is accessory overload: rows of plastic hair clips, face stickers and band-aids, stacked bead bracelets, plush charms, tulle tutus and layered socks over leg warmers, all in a clashing neon-or-pastel rainbow palette. Recognize it by accessory density that obscures the base clothing, child-like character motifs (Sanrio, magical girls, Western cartoons), unnatural wig colors, and head-to-toe snapshot framing; subgenres stretch from pastel rainbow to black-based Dark Decora with horror kitsch.

name: Deep_Fried_Meme
description: Deep Fried Meme is a mid-to-late 2010s internet aesthetic of deliberate image degradation — extreme saturation, HDR over-sharpening and repeated JPEG recompression that melt skin into batter-yellow and crush backgrounds into saturated red, acid green or laser blue. Its signature marks are lens-flare starbursts over the eyes, the 🅱️ emoji swapped into words, 😂/👌 stickers, and warped glow-haloed captions layered over low-poly cartoon characters or portrait faces. Recognize it by crunchy macroblock texture, posterized color bands and flare bloom: a loud, ironic, "cursed" anti-glossy look.

name: Dekotora
description: Dekotora ("decoration truck") is the Japanese art-truck aesthetic of the 1970s: working trucks rebuilt into rolling light-shrines of neon tubes, LED arrays, ultraviolet lamps and polished stainless, chrome and gold metalwork. Recognition hinges on tiered light towers and cantilevered light racks above the cab, elaborate grille guards and oversized bumpers, illuminated kanji name signage, airbrushed murals of dragons, gods and pop icons, and brocade-upholstered cabs with crystal chandeliers — all glowing neon teal, hot pink and electric green against night black.

name: Delicate_Sweet
description: Delicate Sweet (also Pinkcore, Softette) is a mid-2010s Tumblr aesthetic of washed-out baby pink, cream and beige rendered in hazy, overexposed soft focus — lace trims, satin bows, doilies, vintage nightgowns, stuffed animals, pillows and soft sweets arranged in sleepy domestic interiors. Its signature elements are handmade textile detail (eyelet, scalloped lace, quilted cotton), faceless resting figures, overhead flat lays of comfort objects, and a mood of safety, innocence and self-care. Load this skill to recognize or generate faded-pink domestic tenderness and to separate it from Babycore, Morute, Cult Party Kei, Ethereal and Soft Girl.

name: Demoscene
description: Visual language of underground real-time computer demos born in 1980s Europe: procedurally generated geometry and raster effects — starfields, copper-bar horizon gradients, interference rings, checkerboard grid floors — in electric blue, neon green and RGB primaries on high-contrast black, plus dithered pixel art, PETSCII/teletext character mosaics, chrome bevel logos and scrolling ticker text. Recognize it by visible computation: pixel grids, ordered dither, mathematically repeating patterns, and demo-screen grammar that flaunts technical virtuosity under file-size constraints.

name: Denpa
description: Japanese psychological-horror aesthetic of 1990s–2000s visual-novel culture, built on the collision of mundane urban Japan (tangled utility wires against overcast skies, rooftops, empty classrooms, CRT-lit rooms, liminal street corners) with intrusions of delusion: semi-transparent sketch figures, glitched monospace text, static, fleshy hallucination. Palette commits to one register at a time — static grey and ink black, deep night blue, desaturated teal-green, deceptively bright summer pastels, or hyper-saturated magenta moe façade. Recognize it by lo-fi grain, scanlines and dither, high-contrast chiaroscuro, isolated figures, and an undercurrent of paranoia and derealization humming beneath ordinary surfaces.

name: Devilcore
description: Devilcore (also Demoncore) is a 2010s internet aesthetic of seductive occult transgression: red–black–grey duotones, horned and tailed silhouettes, inverted pentagrams and demonic sigils, blood, blades, candles, and fetish hardware (chains, harnesses, fishnet, stiletto heels). Its images are grainy, low-key and moodboard-like — backlit figures reduced to black shapes against blood-red fields, blasphemous religious icons, cropped legs and hands, lowercase caption boxes. Recognize it by the triad of red field + black silhouette + occult or dominance glyph; it flirts where Catholic Horror fears, and stylizes where Gorecore mutilates.

name: Dieselpunk
description: Dieselpunk is the retrofuturism of the interwar-to-1950s machine age: riveted steel tanks, armored trains, zeppelins, biplanes and walker mechs set beneath soot-stained Art Deco and Streamline Moderne skylines. Its palette is black, gunmetal grey, olive drab and rust, punctuated by brass, bone-cream and poster vermilion; its mood swings between wartime grit, film-noir shadow and Jazz-Age Deco optimism. Recognize it by rivet rows and engine-turned aluminum, vacuum-tube electronics, propaganda-poster graphics, and period dress — trench coats, fedoras, aviator caps and goggles, mechanic overalls.

name: Digital_Horror
description: Digital Horror (also Internet Horror or Flash Horror) is the horror of the early web, roughly late 1990s to early/mid 2010s: lo-fi game captures, corrupted Flash cartoons, cursed web pages and haunted home-video edits rendered with pixelation, JPEG smear and period software chrome such as Bandicam watermarks, Windows Movie Maker title cards and Comic Sans. Its palette swings between black-and-blood-red monochrome, desaturated olive-gray murk, bone-white on black, and garish early-web pastels invaded by darkness, always organized around a nostalgic children's-media object twisted wrong. Recognize it by compression artifacts plus obsolete interface typography plus a single uncanny deviation inside an otherwise innocent digital frame.

name: Diner
description: Diner is the aesthetic of the 1950s American roadside diner: vinyl booths, checkered floors, chrome counters, neon "OPEN 24 HOURS" signage, and hearty comfort food — pancakes and eggs, burgers and fries, pie, milkshakes, Coca-Cola in glass. Its palette runs from warm, sun-faded cream, cherry red and turquoise in the traditional mode to saturated candy pink and neon glow in the modern mode, always carried by analog snapshot warmth and period service culture (uniformed waitresses, jukeboxes, napkin dispensers, memorabilia-covered walls). Recognize it by the combination of a working restaurant interior, plated American comfort food, and homey mid-century commercial decor.

name: Diner_Kitsch
description: Diner Kitsch is the 1970s-onward nostalgic revival of 1940s–50s American diner, drive-in and malt-shop culture — black-and-white checkerboard floors, chrome-trimmed counters, channel-tufted vinyl booths, neon signage, jukeboxes and carhop waitresses, rendered in mint, turquoise, hot pink and cherry red. Recognize it by its revival-media lens: airbrushed album covers and movie posters, menu and business-card graphics with tail-fin script type, and blue-hour photography of glowing roadside neon, all staging an idealized, carefree mid-century roadside America rather than documenting it.

name: Dionysism
description: Dionysism is a two-strain hedonistic aesthetic descended from the ancient Greek cult of Dionysus: dilapidated marble statues, ivy and grape clusters, and metal goblets brim-full of wine on one side; grainy night rooftop parties, red-washed smoky basements, and toga-clad friends on the other. Its palette anchors on wine red, black, earthy brown and linen cream, punctured by saturated party-color light washes; its signatures are spilled wine, draped linen, garlanded skin, and disorderly feasting. Recognize it by the marriage of classical antiquity with intoxicated night euphoria — never orderly, never sober, never glossy.

name: Disco
description: Disco is the nightclub-born visual culture of 1970s New York and Philadelphia: mirrored disco balls scattering pinpoints of light across dark rooms, pulsing light-up dance floors, and bodies in sequins, Lurex and metallic polyester cut for movement. Its palette is metallic chrome and gold plus saturated neon magenta, violet, cyan, red, orange and yellow firing against near-black night interiors, rendered in grainy saturated film with halation and strobe echo-trails. Recognize it by mirror-sphere light scatter, platform shoes and bell-bottoms, androgynous glitter glamour, and euphoric communal dance-floor energy.

name: Disco_Deco
description: Disco Deco (also called Psyche-Deco) is the mid-1960s-to-1970s revival of Art Deco geometry fused with disco-nightclub hedonism: bilaterally symmetric supergraphics, heavy geometric display typefaces, concentric rainbow arches, stepped ziggurats and stylized sunbursts in saturated yellow, red, orange, magenta, electric blue and teal, set on cream or black grounds or inside mirrored club interiors glowing with amber, purple and electric-blue light. Recognition hinges on the marriage of sleek jazz-age symmetry with party energy — disco balls, silver foil, sequins and lamé, medallion portraits, tunnel-like receding arches, and arced geometric lettering. Load this skill when an image or brief shows deco structure pushed into acid-bright, nightlife-saturated color.

name: Disco_Polo
description: Polish post-communist dance-pop kitsch of the late 1980s to mid-1990s — cassette-stall compilation covers and low-budget music videos built on clashing neon saturation, chrome- and rainbow-gradient 3D beveled lettering, sunburst rays, starburst badges, halftone dots and cutout sticker photos of gel-haired performers in shiny suits and gold chains. Recognize it by primitive green-screen compositing, rented-limo and hotel-pool aspiration, wedding-hall party scenes and cheap offset-print gloss, all delivered with sincere provincial joy rather than irony or minimalism.

name: Divine_Machinery
description: Divine Machinery is a 2020s techno-sacral aesthetic that fuses CRT-era hardware — cable bundles, motherboards, monitor walls, transmission towers, e-waste assemblage — with Christian, especially Catholic, iconography: crucifixes, sacred hearts, angels, neon-lit cathedrals. Its ground is near-black, lit only by machine emission in phosphor green, BSOD blue and alarm red, with glitch, scanlines and pixel/terminal text functioning as liturgy. Recognize it when hardware is arranged as relic, altar or angel — the machine as divine messenger, the human as creator-god.

name: Dizelaši
description: Sanctions-era 1990s Serbian (Belgrade) street subculture look — bold color-blocked nylon tracksuits with trouser legs tucked into socks, black bomber jackets, baggy Diesel jeans, Nike Air Max sneakers, thick gold chains, shaved heads and aviator sunglasses worn even indoors at night. Saturated teal, magenta, purple, red and neon panel blocks set against concrete, brick arches and flash-lit club darkness, photographed as dense crew group portraits. Signals turbo-folk toughness, scarcity-era materialism and street credibility; also covers the cleaner Neo-Dizelaši revival variant.

name: Dokukawaii
description: Dokukawaii ("poison cute", aka Dokukawa or Neon Gore) is a 2010s Japanese aesthetic of maximum-saturation neon rainbow clashing with sickly medical-toxic motifs — gas masks, pill capsules, slime, bleeding void-eyes, keep-out tape. It renders cute girls, creature mascots and dolls in flat graphic poster or maximalist-clutter treatments with bold outlines, halftone dots and ironic Japanese/English slogans. Recognize it by its "eye poison" effect: candy-kawaii substrate pushed to acid saturation with a morbid, toxic sting.

name: Dollar_Store_Vernacular
description: Dollar Store Vernacular is the cheap-commercial design language of 1990s–2000s local advertising: WordArt bevel-and-emboss logos, hard-edged photo cutouts pasted over starfield or sky gradients, clashing red/yellow/orange/blue/green on black, and overstuffed flyers, pop-up ads, infomercial frames and knock-off packaging loaded with prices, toll-free numbers and fine print. Recognize it by information overload, unaliased pasted edges, starburst price bursts, skeuomorphic clipart and sincere bargain hype; it lives on local TV commercials, small-business catalogues, shareware boxes, fairfood signs and convenience-store windows.

name: Dollcore
description: Dollcore (ドーリー系) is a 2010s Japanese aesthetic built around ball-jointed and porcelain dolls: poofy empire-waist Lolita-derived dresses, peter pan collars, satin ribbons, ball-jointed tights, chunky platform Mary Janes and faceted gemstone hearts, all sunk in soft-focus, low-contrast haze. Recognize it by doll stillness — posed joint angles, masked or face-hidden figures, porcelain matte makeup — across a two-register palette of dusty porcelain pastels (blush, lavender, mint, cream) and mourning black against porcelain white. Typical subjects are the dolls themselves, "living doll" masked models, headless coordinate detail studies, accessory flat lays and dreamy collage edits with script captions.

name: Dollette
description: Dollette — the name adopted in the early 2020s for the delicate wing of Coquette — is a hyperfeminine soft aesthetic of the 2010s Tumblr lineage: dusty blush pink, ivory and beige in faded, low-contrast light, built on bows and ribbons, lace-trimmed milkmaid and babydoll tops, ditsy florals and gingham, pearls, lip gloss and perfume bottles, pointe shoes and romance ephemera arranged on floral patchwork quilts. Typical images are flat lays, hanger and dress-form garment shots, mirror selfies, shabby-chic pink bedrooms, and still lifes of love letters, vintage cakes and tea cups. Recognize it against Balletcore (dancewear-first), Bubblegum Coquette (saturated candy pink), Dollcore (porcelain-doll artificiality), Dark Nymphet and Waif (grunge, despair, sexualized narrative).

name: Dolly_Girl
description: Dolly Girl is the mid-1960s London Mod-born fashion aesthetic of exaggerated childlike femininity: shapeless babydoll A-line mini dresses with Peter Pan collars, puffed sleeves, lace and ribbon trim, in nursery pastels (baby pink, powder blue, mint, lemon) plus gingham and daisy prints, worn with white tights, knee socks and flat Mary Janes. Signature cues are doll-eye makeup (heavy lower-lash mascara, drawn crease, pale lips), teased hair with blunt fringe or a pixie cut, satin bows and plush-toy props, and high-key studio or magazine-print presentation with halftone grain. Recognize it by the trio of above-knee hemlines, pastel nursery palette and gamine doll posing — not by any single garment.

name: Dolly_Kei
description: Dolly Kei (also Antique Kei) is a 2010s Japanese fashion aesthetic built on dark antique layering — black and deep jewel-tone velvets, distressed lace and embroidery, faux fur, and large creepy-fairytale accessories like lace chokers and skulls, drawn from Grimm and Andersen rather than Disney. Its images are candlelit, horror-vacui antique-shop interiors and thrifted vintage coordinates with braids, worn hems and clashing patterns, all soaked in amber lamplight. Recognize it by low-key warm lighting, maximalist clutter of taxidermy, bones, dried herbs and glass-front cabinets, and a battered, uncanny storybook mood.

name: Doomer
description: Doomer (Doomerwave) is a late-2010s internet aesthetic of pessimistic urban desolation: Soviet-era Khrushchyovka panel blocks, Brutalist concrete and post-industrial streets photographed at night, in winter snow, or under fog and overcast, all pulled toward a muted cold palette of grey, navy blue, black and dim purple. Signature elements include VHS/glitch media degradation, sparse warm window lights in vast dark facades, empty snowbound courtyards and tram lines, and optionally the crude beanie-and-hoodie Wojak figure or a nihilistic caption line. Recognize it by gloom-filtered low contrast, absent or tiny human presence, and a mood of resigned alienation rather than ruin spectacle or cozy nostalgia.

name: Dopamine_Dressing
description: Dopamine Dressing (多巴胺风) is an early-2020s, China-born fashion and interior aesthetic built on flat planes of highly saturated color blocking — hot pink, tangerine, sun yellow, neon green — with simple fruit, candy, smiley and rainbow motifs, glossy plastics and jelly accessories against plush maximalist silhouettes. Recognize it by coordinated contrasting chroma in every dominant surface, high-key shadowless lighting, lustrous light-reflecting materials, and an overtly optimistic, playful mood across lookbooks, open-plan interiors, product flat-lays and bilingual poster graphics.

name: Downtown_Girl
description: Downtown Girl (NYC Girl) is a 2022-born TikTok/Pinterest aesthetic romanticizing downtown city life through a 1970s–2000s lens: overcast or dusk-lit streets, subway windows, fire escapes and scaffolding, bookstores, record shops and cafés, all shot like a grainy digicam or film snapshot. Its palette is black, off-white, beige, coffee brown and denim with oxblood-red punctuation; its signature objects are oversized thrifted sweaters and band tees, combat boots and Doc Martens, canvas ecobags, over-ear headphones, vinyl and CDs, electric guitars, annotated books, cats and grids of ceramic coffee mugs. Recognize it by cozy autumnal urban intimacy and soft-grunge nonchalance, never glossy wealth or hyper-feminine polish.

name: Dragoncore
description: Dragoncore is a 2010s Tumblr-born aesthetic of draconic elegance and curated hoards — painterly dragons and still-lifes of coins, gemstones, crystals, pearls and fine jewelry in dark jewel tones (black, oxblood red, deep green, brown, grey) lifted by gold and silver glint. Signature elements include guardian dragons coiled over treasure, elemental palette families (fire, earth-crystal, water, air, ice), dim refined lighting, serpentine graceful creature design, and an opulent-but-tasteful, well-kept mood descended from Tolkien, Pern, Eragon, Wings of Fire and Dungeons & Dragons.

name: Draincore
description: Draincore is a late-2010s/early-2020s fan-born internet aesthetic from Drain Gang's SoundCloud/Tumblr/TikTok communities: maximalist, trashy-glossy digital collages fusing Y2K chrome, excessive sparkles and lens flare, glitch and chroma damage, low-resolution anime and distorted clip art, black-metal lettering, and kawaii fairy/flower motifs over blown-out white or acid-neon fields. Recognize it by noisy layered overlays, fake digital decay, "cute-plus-decay" juxtapositions, and a parallel earth-toned 90s-hip-hop streetwear fit-pic branch (baggy jeans, trucker caps, bling belts, androgynous layering). Mood is hyper-ironic, vulnerably nihilistic, Y2K-nostalgic.

name: Dreamcore
description: Dreamcore is the surreal early-2020s internet aesthetic of dream-logic space: low-poly 3D suburbia, domestic interiors and poolrooms washed in hazy pastel lavender-pink-peach light over saturated CGI lawns, with rainbows, solid clouds, floating eyes, winged angels, mushrooms and sparse cryptic red text. It pairs comforting nostalgic emptiness with one quietly wrong element, rendered in kitschy early-CGI or soft-grain photo-edit texture. Load this skill to recognize or generate dreamlike liminal suburbia, eye/mushroom/angel dream motifs, or pastel-haze dreamscapes that comfort and unsettle at once.

name: Dreampunk
description: Dreampunk is a mid-2010s internet aesthetic born from sample-free, ambient offshoots of vaporwave and from cyberpunk's night-city mythology: rain-soaked megacityscapes at night, lit by magenta, violet and cyan neon, populated by isolated figures or no one at all, and veiled in fog, film grain and light glitch corruption. Recognize it by deep blue–purple–black palettes with small-area neon accents, wet reflective asphalt, dense vertical CJK signage, dreamlike haze and album-cover typography. The mood is lonely, introspective and cinematic — a city experienced as a dream, never as an action scene.

name: Dreamy_Indie_Girlhood
description: Early-2010s Tumblr photographic aesthetic of teenage girlhood shot on hazy analog film — washed pastel rainbow, overexposed highlights, light leaks, glitter and sticker overlays, cluttered suburban bedrooms, flower crowns, tulle skirts and Mary Janes. Born from Rookie Magazine and Petra Collins's "female gaze," it favors moody, inward, unpolished intimacy: still lifes of girly totems, melancholy childhood mementos, sun-flared fields and water. Recognize it by film grain plus pastel fade plus DIY collage hand plus adolescent interiority, never by glossy polish.

name: Dresiarz
description: Polish working-class youth subculture of the late-1980s–1990s post-communist transition, defined by the full tracksuit uniform — frequently bootleg Adidas/Nike/Puma polyester with three-stripe piping — paired with athletic sneakers, shaved or buzzed heads, and concrete housing-estate (blokowiska) backdrops. The palette splits into a saturated sportswear layer (navy, black, heather grey, optic white, color-block panels of brick red, teal, bottle green, cream) set against a desaturated environment of concrete, peeling plaster and overcast sky, captured in flat daylight or harsh compact-camera flash. Recognize by crew group poses with deadpan stares, older BMWs and Fiats, pit bull-type dogs, and an amateur snapshot medium; mood is street bravado, group loyalty and materialist swagger, often filtered through satirical Polish media parody.

name: Drift_Phonk
description: Drift Phonk is the TikTok-era visual language of Russian-born aggressive phonk and drift-car culture (late 2010s onward): night-time JDM-style drift cars and skulls rendered in purple-magenta duotone with acid-green neon accents, crushed blacks, and VHS scanline/glitch degradation. Its signature carrier is square cover art pairing cars and/or skulls with jagged all-caps metal-style lettering, underglow neon, tire smoke, and meme-internet stickers. Recognize it by its cool purple/green/white/blue/gray palette, nocturnal emissive lighting, and degraded broadcast texture — never daylight, never clean.

name: Dungeon_Synth
description: Dungeon Synth is the cassette-trading visual language of early-1990s black metal's ambient offshoot: xerox-degraded monochrome, candlelit corpsepaint portraits, chainmail coifs, and naive medieval-fantasy paintings of castles, ruined towers, misty conifer forests and winter mountains. Its palette is muted black, grey, moss green, brown and parchment, sometimes washed in a single cold blue or violet duotone, framed by blackletter or typewriter typography and tape-insert layouts. The mood is escapist, melancholic, archaic and deliberately lo-fi — photocopy grain, scan noise and hand-dubbed cassette artifacts are marks of authenticity, not flaws.

name: Dunhuang_Feng
description: Dunhuang Feng is the Chinese aesthetic descended from the Silk Road Buddhist art of the Mogao Caves (4th–14th c.), built on saturated matte mineral pigments — malachite teal, azurite blue, lead-red terracotta, earth ochre, kaolin white — applied in fluid contour linework with soft gradient shading. Its signature elements are ribbon-trailing flying apsaras (feitian), concentric lotus zaojing ceiling medallions, mild-featured Buddhas and Bodhisattvas with halo rings, dense orderly narrative mural bands, and desert-oasis frontier landscapes; its modern branch recycles these into a warm-toned guochao design system for fashion, packaging, interiors, games and stage. Recognize it by the cool-teal/warm-red mineral tension, ordered decorative abundance, and sacred flight-without-wings.

name: Dutch_Golden_Age
description: Seventeenth-century painting of the Dutch Republic — intimate, meticulously observed scenes of domestic life, civic and individual portraiture, still life and low-country landscape, built on somber earthy browns, ochres and greys with reserved accents of ultramarine, vermilion and lemon yellow. Signature elements are chiaroscuro light from a single window or source, luminous linen whites and pearl highlights emerging from warm shadow, and jewel-precise rendering of textures such as wool, satin, glass, wood and feather. Typical subjects are letter-readers and servants at their tasks, merry companies, guild and anatomy group portraits, vanitas and banquet tables, dune flats under cloud-heavy skies, and costumed character heads.

name: E-Boy
description: E-Boy ("electronic boy") is the late-2010s TikTok-born youth aesthetic of young men in layered black streetwear — oversized graphic tees over striped long-sleeves, ripped skinny jeans, platform combat boots — hung with silver chains, padlock pendants and cross jewelry, topped by middle-parted curtained hair, often dyed, with chipped black nail polish. Its palette is strictly black-white-silver over concrete gray, shot in lo-fi phone-native frames (mirror selfies, wall fit-checks, grainy liminal candids) with cool desaturated grading and a performatively sad, deadpan pout. Recognize it by the combination of chain hardware, center-parted hair and online-selfie framing; it differs from emo and scene by its monochrome restraint and from E-Girl by its absence of makeup grammar.

name: E-Girl
description: E-Girl is a late-2010s TikTok-born online-persona aesthetic mixing dark alternative fashion — oversized band tees, pleated plaid skirts, fishnets, chain belts, spiked chokers — with kawaii softness: plushies, hot-pink accents, anime and gaming props. Its face signature is heavy winged eyeliner, blush swept horizontally across the nose bridge, and drawn-on hearts or tears under the eyes, framed by blunt bangs and split-dye or streaked pink/pastel hair. Recognize it by phone-native vertical framing (high-angle selfies, headless outfit checks), bedroom sets lit by ring light or pink/purple LED strips, and a black-dominant palette with pink, red or lilac accents in either desaturated fade or neon-saturated treatment.

name: Early_Cyber
description: Early Cyber is the raster-shock graphic language of the first desktop-publishing wave, peaking mid-1980s to mid-1990s: thermographic false-color portraits, heavy pixelation and dot-matrix fields, fractal swirls and warped display type collaged against flat geometric vector blocks. Its palette is rainbow-as-data — heat-map ramps, neon-on-black, pastel airbrush — applied to album sleeves, magazine covers and poster prints carrying cyberpunk-era optimism and dread. Recognize it by pixel-sorted faces, posterization, glow halos, head-up-display grids and panelled collage layouts with bitmap or stretched serif typography.

name: Earth_Tones
description: Earth Tones (Fall Tones) is the American commercial and interior design aesthetic of roughly 1973–1984, built on chocolate brown, burnt orange and harvest yellow, rounded supergraphic circles and concentric arcs, wood veneer paneling, shag carpet and soft serif or rounded lowercase logotypes. Recognize it in faded-film photos of paneled dens, hotel rooms and camper interiors, in storefront signage and print ads where concentric color bands carry the composition, and in its 21st-century nostalgia revival with softened green-and-blue palettes. It reads as cozy, pragmatic post-oil-crisis warmth — never neon, never chrome, never hand-made folk.

name: Earthy_Black_Girl
description: Earthy Black Girl (aka Black Girl Boho) is a 2020s TikTok-born Afrocentric Neo Soul revival aesthetic centered on Black women: earthy terracotta, olive and cocoa browns lifted by Pan-African gold, red and green; waist beads, cowrie shells and layered gold jewelry over bare skin; headwraps and heat-free textured hair; crochet, linen and Kente/Ankara/bogolan prints; Kemetic and Adinkra symbols worn beside moon phases and lotus glyphs. Typical images are warm, faded, intimate mirror selfies, garden portraits, outfit collages and flat-lays. Recognize it by the triad of beaded adornment, diaspora spiritual symbols and soft analog warmth — never by one fixed scene.

name: Easter
description: Seasonal holiday aesthetic of Christian Resurrection Sunday, built on a bright pastel palette — mint, baby pink, butter yellow, lavender, white and fresh green — and folk symbols of renewal: dyed eggs in straw nests and wicker baskets, bunnies, chicks and lambs among spring grass, tulips and blossom sprigs. Soft high-key daylight, matte natural textures (hay, wicker, eggshell, ceramic, kraft paper) and a tender, playful, hopeful mood carry it across registers from rustic lifestyle photography to flat vector clipart and watercolor greeting art. Recognize it by the egg-and-bunny symbol set plus pastel eggshell color logic; separate it from plain spring imagery by its holiday symbols, and from Christmas or Halloween by its light-valued palette and daylight.

name: Eclectic_Grandpa
description: Eclectic Grandpa (Grandpacore) is a 2020s TikTok/Pinterest microtrend of curated vintage menswear — oversized topcoats, shaggy cardigans, cricket vests, corduroy and quilted jackets, high-waisted wide trousers, sensible loafers or retro sneakers — in earthy neutrals punctuated by sparing bright accents. Recognize it by slouchy layered silhouettes, quietly clashing heritage patterns (houndstooth, pinstripe, gingham, cable knit), baseball caps and tinted glasses, and a nonchalant comfort-first mood captured in candid daylight or collage flat-lays.

name: Eco-Beige
description: Eco-Beige (also Eco-Rustic) is a late-1980s-to-mid-1990s commercial aesthetic of performed naturalism: unbleached linen, kraft paper, twigs, raffia straw, exposed wood and brick, in a beige-cream field accented by sage green, bark brown and dusty blue. Recognize it by hand-tied twine and cloth-wrapped packaging, pressed botanicals and tree-or-leaf brand marks, stripped-down boutique, spa and wellness interiors, and soft, grainy, low-contrast light that reads homespun and authentic. It is the brand-facing, rustic subsect of Zen-X, born from 1990s environmental consciousness and often deployed as greenwashing.

name: Edwardian
description: Edwardian (1901–1910, Britain and its global echo) is the aesthetic of the pre-WWI "long summer": ivory lace, silk satin and chiffon in pale pastels with gold and jewel-tone accents, the S-bend "pouter pigeon" silhouette crowned by enormous feather-and-flower hats, tailor-made walking suits, morning coats and Homburgs, tennis lawns, parasols and tea tables. Recognise it by formal upright portraiture in soft diffused light or in sepia and silver photographic registers, airier Baroque Revival and Queen Anne interiors carrying Art Nouveau ornament, and a mood of optimistic, class-coded leisure. It sits between Victorian gloom and 1920s modernism, lighter in palette and posture than the first and far more formal than the second.

name: Egyptian_Revival
description: Egyptian Revival is the Western monumental and decorative design language of c. 1800–1850 (with a Victorian afterlife) that recasts ancient Egyptian mass into crisp nineteenth-century masonry and objects: battered pylon gateways, cavetto cornices, lotus-bud and palm-leaf columns, obelisks, winged sun disks and paired sphinxes, in sandy beige, ochre and terracotta stone or in black marble and patinated bronze picked out with ormolu gold. Recognize it by strict bilateral symmetry, sloping trapezoidal silhouettes, cemetery/memorial programs, hieroglyph banding, and a solemn, geometric stillness.

name: Electro_Swing
description: Electro Swing is the visual arm of the swing-house music scene: a 2010s internet-born "anachronism stew" that remixes 1920s–1950s archive material — sepia paper, halftone photo cutouts, flappers, tin robots, gramophone horns — with modern intrusions like neon signage, headphones and flat vector bounce. Recognize it by a desaturated sepia/grayscale/cream base spiked with electric blue or magenta neon, rubber-hose characters caught mid-dance, sunburst poster layouts, distressed film grain, and stacked Art Deco, circus or letterpress typography. The mood is always celebratory: a party where the archive and the dance floor collide.

name: Electroclash
description: Electroclash is the ironic late-1990s/early-2000s revival of 1980s new wave and electro, filtered through techno-era graphic design: jet black, metallic silver and stark neon (hot magenta, signal red, electric yellow, cyan) deployed as xerox duotones or airbrushed vector gradients. Signature elements include analog synthesizers and vocoders held as props, Liquid Sky-derived androgynous glam with clashing makeup, fishnet, sequins and plastic visors, deadpan robotic performance poses, and DIY cut-and-paste collage set with ransom, stencil or thin outline-script type. Typical subjects are monotone performers, staged club tableaux, flash-burned fashion portraits, and flat graphic covers built from hard-edged color fields.

name: Electronic_Body_Music
description: Electronic Body Music (EBM) is the stark visual language of the early-1980s Düsseldorf–Brussels post-industrial electronic scene: a monochrome uniform of black, grey, white, signal red and olive drab; military surplus, leather harnesses, ribbed tank tops and fresh-cut crops; Socialist-Realist hammer-and-cog emblems, stencil capitals and constructivist poster geometry; grainy analog video and high-contrast photography of anonymous, disciplined bodies posed as workers and commanders. Load this skill to recognize or generate EBM album sleeves, club posters, band portraits and video stills, and to keep them separate from Aggrotech horror, Cybergoth neon, Rivethead gear-clutter and New Beat psychedelia.

name: Emo
description: Mid-2000s MySpace-era subculture look and its DeviantArt illustration twin — jet-black straightened hair with a long side-swept fringe over the eyes, skinny jeans, tight band tees, studded belts, Converse, heavy eyeliner on all genders, in a black-dominant palette pierced by blood red, paper white, or a single neon "coontail" streak. Signature content runs from flash-blown mirror selfies and suburban outfit shots to sketchy pencil-textured chibi line art with broken hearts, skulls, stitches and huge empty eyes. Confessional, melodramatic, tender-angst in mood; distinct from goth, scene, and the later e-kid and emo-rap styles.

name: Emo_Rap
description: Visual language of mid-2010s SoundCloud emo rap — black-dominant frames cut with white line-work and blood-red or violet-magenta accents, dyed dreadlocks and face tattoos, silver chains over ASSC/Thrasher/Vlone/FTP hoodies, withered roses, broken hearts, skulls, barbed wire and weeping nostalgic-cartoon edits. Rendered through lo-fi processes: direct-flash snapshots, xerox paper grain, glitch/datamosh smears, red or purple duotone washes, scrapbook collages of handwritten notes and Polaroids. Subjects are lone melancholic figures, masked hooded avatars, object still-lifes and minimal icon-on-black album graphics expressing grief, numbness and confessional vulnerability; peak era 2016–2020.

name: Equestrian
description: Equestrian is the aesthetic of horseback riding as a practiced craft: horses, tack (saddles, bridles, bits, stirrups) and the disciplined partnership between rider and animal, dressed in English or Western riding attire. Its palette is earth colors, white, tan and muted blue — dappled grey coats, tan breeches, black velvet helmets, oiled brown leather — lit by soft overcast arena light, high-key noon sun, or moody stable shadow with breath steaming in cold air. Recognize it by tack close-ups, braided manes, tucked-in show shirts, sand footing, and quiet moments of connection in stables, show rings and paddocks.

name: Erokawa
description: Erokawa is the Japanese cute-erotic aesthetic coined by Kumi Kōda in 2005, fusing kawaii sweetness with lingerie-level eroticism under a pink-and-white pastel regime. Signature elements: kawaii lingerie (frilled bralettes, bloomers, lace trim), fashion harnesses and garter straps, lace chokers and collars hung with heart padlocks, cat ears, and maid-style frills, rendered in high-key soft light across photo lookbooks, pastel anime illustration, and pink-duotone manga panels. Subjects are sexy-cute women or anime girls — solo or in yuri pairs — posing with playful, female-gaze confidence rather than explicit exposure.

name: Eshay
description: Australian youth-subculture aesthetic (Sydney, late 1990s–2000s) built on a uniform of designer sportswear — polo shirts, puffer vests, athletic shorts — anchored by Nike Air Max Plus "TN" sneakers, a bumbag slung across the chest, branded caps and gold jewellery, over a black/white/grey/navy palette with single saturated brand accents. Images read as amateur phone snapshots or drill-video stills: harsh on-camera flash or flat overcast daylight, crews packed shoulder-to-shoulder against brick-veneer walls, train platforms, rail yards and suburban backyards, faces sometimes hidden by balaclavas or check scarves. Recognise by piqué polo knits with chest logos, glossy quilted nylon puffers, tan check trim at accessory scale, and mundane Australian suburbia as stage.

name: Ethereal
description: Ethereal is a 2010s–2020s internet aesthetic of otherworldly delicacy: high-key pastel imagery in pink, white, blue and soft green, soaked in soft focus, luminous bloom and drifting sparkle. Its signature elements are weightless subjects — flowing lace gowns, veils, swans, fairies, angels, princesses and classical dancers — staged in dreamy gardens, ponds, ballrooms and fairy-tale castles with sincere, irony-free romanticism. Load this skill when an image feels heavenly, blurred, luminous and wholesome rather than sharp, saturated, opulent or ironic.

name: Ethno-Chic
description: Ethno-Chic (Ethnic Chic) is a travel-collected global-craft aesthetic born from 1960s hippie-traveler souvenir culture and refined with modern clean-lined design: neutral plaster, linen and wood shells layered with saturated geometric textiles (kilim flatweaves, African wax prints, ikat, embroidered bands), woven-basket gallery walls, rattan, jute, terracotta and dark wood. Its palette spans warm earth tones and jewel tones grounded by black and white, and its subjects range from eclectic interiors and sun-baked terraces to fashion in handcrafted embroidery, headwraps and beaded jewelry. Recognize it by visible handwork, mixed cultural provenances, storytelling objects and abundant warm natural light.

name: Ethnogoth
description: Ethnogoth is a mid-2010s European Goth substyle that fuses loose Middle Eastern, North African and Central Asian folk robes — black kaftans and kandooras — with an 80s-derived Goth face of matte pallor, smoky black eyes and near-black lips. Its signature is a silhouette-concealing garment buried under hammered Kuchi silver and gold: stacked bib necklaces, coin chains, filigree crescent or horned crowns, turbans and sheer veils, often over shaved or partially shaved heads. Recognize it by hieratic, frontal portraits where metal glints against matte black cloth, icon-like solemnity, and folk embroidery meeting dramatic Goth makeup.

name: Euphoric
description: Euphoric (Euphoria Aesthetic / Euphoriacore) is a late-2010s Gen Z style born from HBO's Euphoria: moody saturated cinematography in deep purple, indigo, magenta and hot pink, glitter-tear and rhinestone makeup used as emotional storytelling, neon gel lighting, and Y2K cut-out, sheer-mesh, skater-grunge and vamp fashion registers. Recognize it by rhinestone tear tracks on glossy skin under colored light, fairy-light bokeh and starburst flares, tinsel and sequin night interiors, and a dreamlike haze that fuses euphoric high with vulnerable ache. Use it for teen-interiority portraits, club and bedroom night scenes, expressive makeup imagery and social-native collage edits.

name: Expressionism
description: Early-20th-century modernist mode (Germany and Austria, c. 1905–1920s) that trades objective reality for inner state: distorted or elongated figures, mask-like faces, and intense, arbitrary, symbolic color set in dissonant chords. Signature elements include agitated or swirling brushwork, woodcut-derived blunt black contours, tilted and compressed space, and subjects of urban alienation, psychological turmoil, embraces, animals and spiritual yearning. Recognize it by emotional dissonance — acid blue against vermilion, pale flesh against rust — and by anatomy and perspective bent to feeling rather than fact.

name: Factory_Pomo
description: Factory Pomo is the late-1980s-to-mid-1990s postmodern machine aesthetic: gears, cogs and metal ridging drawn with early-CAD precision, fused with Art Deco sunbursts, Constructivist type bars and Bauhaus primaries in clashing, color-inverted combinations. It lives on theme-park gates, arcade interiors, kids' science-show title cards, video-game box art, sports logos, soda cans and trade-show booths — symmetric, hard-edged, airbrushed and speckle-textured, lit either flat-graphic or by festive magenta-and-green neon at dusk. Recognize it by pristine painted industrialism played for fun: gear portals, beveled chrome type, granite-speckle fills, and simple shapes inverted against black, white or grayscale metal.

name: Fairground_Baroque
description: The ornate artisan aesthetic of the European travelling fair at its Belle Époque peak (c. 1850–1914) — hand-carved, gilded softwood carousels, booth facades and fairground organs dressed in polychrome allegorical painting, bevelled mirrors, twisted brass poles and bulb-traced scrollwork. Palette of deep red, gold leaf, ivory, forest green and royal blue with high-contrast polychrome accents; signature subjects are carved carousel horses and exotic animals, rocaille bas-reliefs, painted medallions, pipe-organ cases and lithograph posters. Recognize it by the tension of monumental, hand-worn decoration on temporary modular structures: warm gilded spectacle, never factory gloss.

name: Fairy_Grunge
description: Fairy Grunge (also Grunge Fairycore / Grunge Fairy) is an early-2020s, pandemic-born internet fashion aesthetic that fuses fairycore whimsy — translucent insect wings, elf ears, moss, crystals, woodland settings — with the distressed, thrifted layering of 1990s grunge and kinderwhore. Recognize it by a muted earth palette (moss green, bark brown, black, bone cream), fishnets and torn knits worn in foggy forests, overgrown ruins and cloudy or night light, rendered in grainy soft-focus photography, digital collage or painterly folklore illustration. The mood is dreamlike, dark and escapist: whimsy deliberately weighed down by imperfection.

name: Fairy_Kei
description: Fairy Kei (フェアリー系, "fancy") is a Harajuku retro-fashion aesthetic built entirely from 1980s children's pop culture — My Little Pony-era toys, Care Bears, Rainbow Brite, magical-girl anime and early shoujo manga — rendered in a fluffy, floaty palette of pastel pink, baby blue, lavender, lemon and mint. Recognize it by unicorn-and-rainbow motifs, plush and tulle textures, oversized sweatshirts over fluttery petticoats, stuffed animals worn as clothing or bags, and high-key candy maximalism; typical subjects are pastel fashion coords, vintage toy collections, plush-cluttered rooms and shelves, and die-cut fancy-goods illustration.

name: Fairycore
description: Fairycore is a late-2010s/early-2020s internet aesthetic of romanticized fairy mythology: soft-focus, glowing imagery in pastels and earth tones (blush pink, cream, butter yellow, moss green, lavender) dusted with glitter, sparkles and lens flares. Signature elements are translucent fairy wings, elf ears, mushrooms, moss, butterflies, flower crowns and sheer tulle or lace dresses, set in enchanted forests, streams and wildflower glades with gentle animals like fawns, bunnies and cats. Recognize it by its dreamy bloom, tiny-figure-in-vast-nature scale play, and optimistic "accessible magic" mood — distinct from Cottagecore's rustic domesticity and Fairy Grunge's decay.

name: Fallen_Angel
description: Fallen Angel (Dark Angelcore) is a 2020s Tumblr/Pinterest aesthetic of the exiled, rebellious angel: solitary winged figures with black, grey, or tattered wings, rendered in stark monochrome or desaturated storm-light palettes with chiaroscuro shadow, classical ruins, overcast skies, scattered feathers, and small fire or gold accents. Recognition hinges on tragic high contrast and a mood of sorrow, pride, and fall from grace — the deliberate inverse of heavenly Angelcore purity.

name: FantasY2K
description: FantasY2K (Medieval Y2K) is a kitsch late-1990s-to-2000s aesthetic that recuts Medieval Fantasy costume — lace-up corsets and stays, flare and puff sleeves, long skirts, hip belts, crochet, brocade and sheer layering — into Y2K silhouettes with deliberately anachronistic modern hair, makeup and cuts. Recognize it by highly saturated jewel and earth tones (burgundy, rust, teal, royal purple, orange), metallic beading and heraldic or Art Nouveau ornament, gaudy cluttered compositions, and early-2000s surface artifacts such as over-edited glow, holographic sheen, awkward 3D-render smoothness and flat book-cover illustration. Typical subjects are runway models in medieval-revival couture, film and TV court scenes and heroes, stylized castle-and-unicorn landscapes, and camp, self-aware knight-and-princess tableaux.

name: Fantasy
description: Fantasy is the aesthetic of imagined pre-industrial worlds: mist-wrapped forests, cliff-top castles, moss-eaten ruins and sunbeam-lit glades inhabited by dragons, stags, wolves and cloaked travellers. Its palette runs from deep moss green and stone grey through parchment cream to sunrise amber, lit by volumetric mist, forest god-rays and golden-hour backlight, with signature props of potion bottles, brass keys, leather-bound books, scrolls, crystals and swords. The mood is wonder, adventure and companionship — escapism that stays hopeful rather than horrific.

name: Fantasy_Astronomy
description: Fantasy Astronomy depicts the study of the heavens in fictional, magical worlds, borrowing the look of Scientific Revolution and Victorian observatory culture: midnight-navy and bluish-purple night fields, gold and silver line-work, parchment star charts and engraved moon plates, brass telescopes, astrolabes and armillary spheres, candlelit observatories with whimsical architecture, and star-embroidered Victorian-to-midcentury dress. Signature elements are constellation line-work over deep blue, circular celestial medallions framed by scholarly marginalia, gilt instruments, and a quiet blend of research and divination. Use this skill when an image fuses antique astronomical science with overt magic, night-blue palettes and hand-made (engraved, painted, stitched) cosmos imagery.

name: Farmer's_Daughter
description: Late-2010s/early-2020s lo-fi rural-Americana snapshot aesthetic that pairs nymphet-coded suggestiveness with farm-domestic iconography — braids tied with ribbons, denim overalls and daisy dukes, eyelet and crocheted milkmaid tops, cowgirl boots and ruffled socks set in dirt yards, hay fields, cow pastures, trailers and roadside groceries. Palette of milk cream, dry-grass tan, soil brown and faded denim, punctured by cherry red and light pastels, shot like amateur flash or overcast film snapshots. Reads as a carefree farm idyll with a faint Southern-Gothic undercurrent of menace.

name: Fashioncore
description: Fashioncore (FXC) is the early-2000s youth style born in Southern California metalcore and hardcore circles, recognizable by jet-black flat-ironed hair with a side-swept swoop fringe and bleached "skunk" sections, white studded belts over fitted band tees and black skinny jeans, and skull, diamond and bone iconography in a black–bleached-blonde–red palette. Portraits carry a vain, confrontational, mosh-pit-ready posture and a mid-2000s compact-digital photo treatment of direct flash, color casts and blown highlights.
