Recognize it by translucent X-ray anatomy, electrograph traces, holographic data overlays, glassy cell membranes, and editorial wrappers such as magazine mastheads or supplement cartons; green is absent outside plant biology and pink/magenta stays confined to gradients.

name: Medicalcore
description: Medicalcore (also Hospitalcore, Nursecore) is an internet aesthetic that stages clinical paraphernalia — syringes, pills, IV bags, bandages, hospital beds, red-cross emblems — inside a sedative palette of white, pink, lavender, mint and baby blue, with red held back as a small emblematic accent. Its images (still-life photos, flat lays, macro shots, faded room snapshots, doll portraits, anime edits, collage grids) favor high-key haze, low contrast and shallow depth of field, treating sickness with tender, coping-oriented care rather than glamour or horror.

name: Medieval
description: European Middle Ages (5th–15th century) visual culture: flat tempera-and-gold-leaf picture planes on vellum, wool tapestry fields, frescoed arcades and gem-set goldsmith work, all organized by Christian devotion and feudal hierarchy. Signature elements include burnished gold grounds, a lapis-and-vermilion jewel palette, inscribed banderoles, heraldic beasts and fleurs-de-lis, millefleurs pattern fills, vielle-playing courtiers, plated knights and cloisonné reliquary crosses. Load this skill to recognize or generate manuscript illuminations, tapestries, wall paintings or reliquary metalwork in the pre-Renaissance European idiom.

name: Medieval_Fantasy
description: Medieval Fantasy stages a fantastical European Middle Ages (5th–15th century, England-flavoured) of knights, castles, crowns, swords and working magic. Its palette spans earthy wool-and-leather umbers, tans and grey-greens up to concentrated jewel accents of crimson, emerald, royal blue and purple on heraldry, gowns and cloaks, lit by overcast daylight, tall window light or candle glow. Read chainmail, tooled leather, frayed wool cloaks, velvet gowns, parchment and rough stone, carrying moods of chivalric devotion, quest and escapist pageantry.

name: Medievalcore
description: Medievalcore (2020s Medieval Revival, Castlecore, Weirdieval) is a maximalist fashion-and-design aesthetic that recuts Middle Ages archetypes — the Joan-of-Arc warrior, the dark-fairytale princess, the witch — into modern garments: chainmail and metallic-mesh dresses, rigid breastplate corsets, conical hennins, knitted bonnets, cloaks, tapestry prints and cross pendants. Its palette anchors metallic silver and gold against deep red, black, forest green and earthy brown, lit anywhere from candlelit chiaroscuro to runway flash and stage gel. Recognize it by armor treated as clothing, Gothic/Catholic ornament, distressed leather and cabochon jewels, and deliberately anachronistic, "weird girl" staging.

name: Melodycore
description: Melodycore (MyMelodycore) is an early-2020s Sanrio-fandom aesthetic organized around the character My Melody: high-key pastel pink, white and cream imagery washed in soft bloom and glitter overlays, saturated with bows, ribbons, lace, hearts and character merchandise. Typical subjects are flat lays of character goods, frilled Girly Kei and Ryousangata outfits, decorated nail and makeup close-ups, and shrine-like pink room displays. Recognize it by its monochrome-pink devotion, dreamlike overexposed glow and kawaii innocence — the light twin of Kuromicore.

name: Meme_Rap
description: Meme Rap is the visual language of 2010s ironic internet rap: lo-fi paste-up collages that crash sanitized childhood mascots, moe anime girls and early-2000s convenience-store products into mid-1990s gangsta-rap signifiers. Expect bubblegum pink and saturated primary clipart colors with neon accents, aliased WordArt typography, JPEG compression artifacts, hard-edged green-screen cutouts, and absurd wealth props like pink sports cars, cash stacks and Parental Advisory badges. Recognize it by deliberate amateurism — mismatched layer resolutions, webcam-flash photos dropped onto flat cartoon backgrounds, sticker-scatter borders — never by polished design.

name: Memphis_Design
description: Memphis Design is the flamboyant postmodern style of the Milan-based Memphis Group (founded by Ettore Sottsass, 1980–1987): bright white or pastel grounds plastered with saturated geometric primitives, black zig-zag and squiggly lines, and clashing plastic-laminate patterns in pink, yellow, blue, red, purple and teal. Signature subjects are totemic, asymmetrical furniture, lamps and ceramics presented as sculptures, plus flat color-plane interiors, TV-studio sets and graphic layouts that sit deliberately between kitsch and elegance. Load this skill when an image shows anti-minimalist clash of hard geometry, printed pattern and candy color — not restrained modernism, not neon-on-black retrowave.

name: Memphis_Jr.
description: Memphis Jr. (alias Playskool PoMo) is the children's offshoot of 1980s Memphis–Milano design — candy-saturated reds, oranges, yellows, blues, pinks and purples deployed as hard-edged geometric patches (circles, triangles, checkerboards, polka dots, confetti sprinkles, Bacterio squiggles) on white or bright solid fields. It lives on late-80s-to-mid-90s play-center storefronts, toy packaging, mascot and logo lockups, paper-craft dioramas, preschool TV sets and early low-poly CGI playfields, always pairing rigid geometry with freeform squiggles and oversized multicolor lettering. Recognize it by patchwork pattern-on-pattern, primitive-solid assemblages (cones, spheres, zigzag slabs) and sincere childlike cheer rather than adult irony.

name: Memphis_Lite
description: Memphis Lite is the corporatized, consumer-grade evolution of Memphis Design that saturated popular culture from roughly 1984 to 1997 — pastel CMYK fields built on teal/aqua, pink/magenta and purple (or bright primaries spiked with those hues), dry-brush squiggles and scribbles, stippled gradients, misaligned geometric assemblages with solid drop shadows, and outlined brush-script type. It lives on album covers, TV title cards and game-show sets, mall and store interiors, cartoon key art, patterned upholstery and airport carpet, fashion, and paper cups. Recognize it by cut-paper shape groups separated by blank space, airbrush-and-stipple modulation of otherwise flat color, and playful Art Deco/Cubist figurative accents — never earth tones, never dark neon perspective grids.

name: Mermaidcore
description: Mermaidcore is an early-2020s internet-native fashion and lifestyle aesthetic that stages subjects as if just emerged from the sea: iridescent fish-scale sequins and paillettes, seashells, pearls and coral set in a palette of aquamarine, seafoam, lilac and coral pink over pearl-white and deep-sea jewel blues. Recognize it by wet-look sheen, scale textures in fabric or makeup, sheer water-like fabrics and netting, and aqueous lighting ranging from high-key pastel to sapphire gloom pierced by light rays.

name: Messy_French_Girl
description: Early-2020s, TikTok-born nightlife twist on Parisian chic — black leather jackets and oversized blazers thrown over slip dresses, smudged eyeliner under a bold matte red lip, bedhead hair with curtain bangs, and a cigarette held as an accessory. Palette of black, oxide red, cream and beige, shot on grainy, flash-lit film in cafés, bar counters, party sofas and rumpled bedrooms. Recognize it by candid snapshot framing, warm underexposed grain, one quiet luxury cue (quilted handbag, silk, pump) amid deliberate dishevelment, and a "put together but never perfect" attitude.

name: Metal
description: Visual language of the heavy metal subculture, from its c. 1970 UK/US crystallization through its 1980s–90s extreme offshoots: a black-dominant palette punctured by blood red, bone sepia and rot green, illegible spiky band logotypes, battle jackets sewn with patches and studs, long hair and plain black clothing, corpse paint in the black-metal lineage, and morbid occult, skeletal and anatomical iconography rendered in grainy analog monochrome or low-key studio light. Typical subjects are band group portraits against void-black backgrounds, illustrated album-cover tableaus of skulls, skeletons, robed figures and decayed flesh, patch-vest still lifes, and the horns-hand gesture.

name: Metalhead
description: Visual style of the heavy metal subculture from the 1970s onward — black leather with pyramid studs, sleeveless denim or leather battle jackets densely sewn with band patches and pins, long hair (or shaved head), black band T-shirts, and the corna hand gesture. Palette is black, worn indigo denim, silver hardware, white logo print and sparse blood-red, captured in faded analog snapshot, harsh on-camera flash, or haze-and-gel stage light against working-class backdrops of brick, parking lots and backstage rooms. Use when recognizing or generating images of metal fans, battle jackets, concerts, and biker-derived defiance iconography.

name: Metalheart
description: Metalheart (also called Depthcore or Trendwhore) is the dark, edgy offshoot of Y2K Futurism that ran from 1998 to 2005: deformed 3D abstract shapes in polished chrome and bead-blasted metal, futuristic HUD-like UIs with minimalist icons, grids, coding text and technical sans-serif fonts, all floating on blurry near-black backgrounds pierced by lens flares and light streaks. Its palette is gray, black and white charged by a single saturated accent of blue, green, red or yellow, and its native habitats are album covers, website and console skins, and early-2000s game key art in the wake of The Matrix.

name: Metrosexual
description: Metrosexual is the groomed, consumer-polished masculinity of late-1990s and 2000s urban centers — men in carefully fitted neutral tailoring (light grey blazers, khakis, pale blue poplin shirts, fine-gauge knits) punctuated by a single confident accent such as ochre trousers, an oxblood knit or coral socks, plus considered accessories like silk scarves and man bags. Its signature is meticulous grooming (product-styled hair, shaped brows, manicured hands, tidy stubble or clean shave), trim coordinated outfits with deliberate footwear, and glossy editorial, street-style, runway or paparazzi photography in soft daylight or even studio light. Typical subjects are fashion-conscious metropolitan men posing or walking in city streets, solid-color studio backdrops, runways and press walls.

name: Mexican_Muralism
description: Mexican Muralism (Muralismo Mexicano, 1920s–1950s) is the post-Revolution Mexican public-wall painting movement: monumental frescoes and industrial-enamel murals bound to stairwells, vaults, lunettes and courtyard walls, in an earth-mineral palette of ochre, terracotta and volcanic gray ignited by flame orange, mineral turquoise and gold. Signature elements are dense multi-episode narrative friezes of indigenous warriors, peasants, workers and revolutionary soldiers, pre-Hispanic vocabulary (feather headdresses, stepped-fret temples, serpents, maize), muscular allegorical nudes, and painted fire-light on matte plaster at architectural scale. Load this skill when an image or prompt involves didactic public wall painting, collective historical narrative, or mestizo national iconography rather than easel painting.

name: Mid-Century_Medieval
description: Mid-Century Medieval (Medieval Revival) is a 1950s–1970s kitsch reinterpretation of Middle Ages iconography — castles, knights, heraldic shields, tarot figures, lutes and herald's trumpets — rendered in bright heraldic reds, yellows, blues and greens on cream paper stock or saturated analog film. Signature elements include embroidered tunics, velvet cloaks and trumpet sleeves fused with 1960s mod hemlines, flat storybook poster illustration, crest-and-shield commercial branding, and pageant-like studio or garden tableaus. Typical subjects are costumed models in lush gardens or against plain studio backdrops, fairy-tale album sleeves and film posters, and kitschy themed-restaurant heraldry.

name: Mid-Century_Modern
description: Mid-Century Modern (MCM, c. 1945–1969) is the post-war American design language of clean lines, organic-and-geometric forms and functionality over ornament: low-slung post-and-beam houses with walls of glass, warm walnut-and-teak interiors punctuated by mustard, burnt orange and turquoise pops, and flat- or triangle-roofed commercial storefronts with glass-panel fronts and period neon pylons. Recognize it by indoor–outdoor openness, molded plywood and fiberglass furniture on tapered legs, exposed wood beams, honest materials and an optimistic, uncluttered mood; subjects range from residential exteriors and living rooms to franchise signage and angular period product design.

name: Mid-Century_Nursery_Kitsch
description: Mid-Century Nursery Kitsch is the pastel toy aesthetic of the 1950s–early 1970s American nursery: rubber-faced plush animals and matte ceramic figurines with oversized glossy painted eyes, airbrushed rosy cheeks, and tiny bow-shaped mouths, dressed in satin bows, party hats, and lace-trimmed clothing. Its palette is locked to baby pink, powder blue, butter yellow, mint green, cream, and white, arranged in maximalist collector clusters among die-cut paper ephemera, pennant garlands, and chalky gouache greeting-card illustration. Recognize it by the infant-schema animal face, fuzzy vintage plush pile, lightly glazed ceramic, satin ribbon, and soft, faded, shadowless snapshot lighting.

name: Midwest_Emo
description: Midwest Emo is the faded-snapshot visual language of the 1990s Midwestern emo scene and its 2010s revival — earth-tone suburbia, plaid flannel over plain tees, cuffed jeans and canvas sneakers, twinkly guitars and basement flyer walls, dusk skies over vinyl-sided houses. Recognize it by amateur point-and-shoot grain, overcast or on-camera-flash light, desaturated khaki–teal–brick palettes, group hangs or solitary melancholy, and styling that is deliberately unfashionable and sincere. It is emo without the black eyeliner and studs: sad, but warm, suburban and communal.

name: Midwest_Gothic
description: Midwest Gothic is a mid-2010s Tumblr-born regional gothic aesthetic that frames ordinary rural American Midwestern life — weathered farmhouses, sale barns, grain bins, rail yards, mobile homes, cornfields, small-town street grids — in a macabre, desaturated light of overcast skies, mud seasons and snow fields. Its visual DNA is vernacular snapshot realism: flat shadowless daylight or weak night flash, bone-gray and taupe palettes with rust as the only accent, vast empty skies, absent people, and a faint folkloric wrongness at the edge of the frame. Recognize it by its dread of emptiness and indifferent nature rather than by ruins, grandeur, or monsters.

name: Milipili
description: Milipili is an early-2020s Argentine youth-fashion aesthetic of affluent, trend-conscious "it girls": a maximalist, revealing Y2K/McBling revival built on total-black outfits, low-rise pants, belly-baring crop tops, micro skirts, cargo pants and platform or knee-high boots, finished with glitter, rhinestones, chains and small designer handbags. Its palette is black, white and denim punctured by single saturated pops (hot pink, acid yellow, cherry red, electric blue), rendered in glossy vinyl, leather, holographics and matte cotton baby tees, and photographed in harsh direct-flash snapshots, mirror selfies and festival or concert candids. Typical subjects are young women posing cheekily solo, in tight friend groups, or performing on stage; the male variant is called Tincho.

name: Military_Chic
description: Military Chic is a civilian fashion aesthetic, originating in Napoleonic-era uniform borrowing and modernized by 20th-century combat gear, that fuses masculine military grammar — army jackets, camouflage print, cargo pockets, epaulettes, brass buttons, combat boots — with feminine styling in a khaki, olive drab, tan, brown and black palette. Recognize it by disciplined earth-tone or monochrome-olive ensembles, brass hardware, cinched utilitarian silhouettes, and a poised mood spanning ornate dress-uniform glamour to rugged field practicality.

name: Military_Goth
description: Military Goth is a social-media-era fashion aesthetic (2010s Tumblr, 2020s TikTok/Pinterest) that overlays goth theatricality — powdered pale base, smoked-out eyes, black or oxblood lips — onto a military uniform silhouette of peaked officer caps with occult insignia, structured epaulette coats, decorative ammunition belts and leather harnesses. Its imagery is portrait-format and overwhelmingly black, with olive drab or charcoal confined to outerwear, frequently rendered monochrome or heavily desaturated, lit either high-key against plain white or low-key with studio vignette. Recognize it by the co-presence of uniform headgear and heavy goth makeup; neither element alone defines the style.

name: Military_Lolita
description: Military Lolita is a Japanese Lolita substyle that fuses the petticoat-held bell or A-line skirt silhouette with ornate 18th–19th century European dress-uniform tailoring: structured double-breasted jackets, epaulettes, gold buttons and braid, medals, and peaked military caps over knee-length voluminous skirts. Its palette is dark and formal — black, navy, deep green, khaki, burgundy — lifted by brass-gold trim and ceremonial props such as sabres and antique rifles. Recognize it by poised, disciplined full-body coordinate photography in soft lookbook light, where cute Lolita volume meets commanding regimental formality.

name: Millennial_Feng
description: Qianxi Feng (Millennial Feng, "00s China") is the mainstream street-fashion and snapshot aesthetic of 2000s China — bright pink, yellow and denim-blue casualwear (low-rise flared jeans, platform shoes, sequined mini bags, colored knee socks) caught on early consumer digital cameras against white-tile buildings with blue glass windows, continental-European plaza facades, UFO-shaped roofs and sign-dense pedestrian malls. Its mood is boom-era optimism, abundance and playful self-expression, often framed today as curated "Beauty of the Boom Years" nostalgia with vintage magazine-scan gloss.

name: Millennium_Disco
description: Millennium Disco is the glossy 1995–2005 disco-revival aesthetic in which 1970s dancefloor code — mirrorballs, platform shoes, flared trousers, afro wigs, halter leotards — is rebuilt with Y2K space-age polish: chainmail and lamé metallics, velour, rhinestone bedazzle, supergraphic starbursts and rounded geometric logotypes. Its palette runs oxblood red, gold, silver, purple and white through hot magenta and electric cyan, lit either by strobe-warm club glow or by airbrushed periwinkle-to-pink gradients. Recognise it in diva portraits, roller-rink and nightclub interiors, glitter-set display type, checkered dancefloors, and playful camp glamour that treats nostalgia as party fuel.

name: Millennium_Orientalism
description: Millennium Orientalism (also called Eastern Exoticism or Corporate Eastern) is a 1990s–2000s commercial fantasy aesthetic that stitches pan-Asian and Middle Eastern motifs — genie lamps, lanterns, dragons, lotus flowers, bindis, camels, pseudo-Arabic and pseudo-Chinese script — into glossy mall-kitch packaging, advertising and interiors. Its palette is plum, magenta and purple against metallic gold, saffron orange, hot pink and lacquer red, usually laid over airbrushed radial gradients scattered with white sparkle starbursts. Typical subjects are beauty campaigns with "Eastern" product names, toy and doll tie-in art, teen bedroom and bedding spreads, lantern-lit lounge interiors, and pop single covers.

name: Minet
description: Minet is the look of affluent Parisian teenagers of the early-to-mid 1960s who gathered at the Drugstore Publicis on the Champs-Élysées: androgynous, deliberately worn-in Anglophile tailoring — crest blazers with gold buttons, houndstooth tweed, gabardine trenches, cropped corduroy trousers, Clarks and JM Weston loafers — punctuated by canary yellow, candy pink and pale blue Shetland sweaters. Visually it survives as grainy silver-gelatin street reportage of coiffed youth gangs lounging under lit DRUGSTORE signage, and as flat pop poster graphics on canary yellow with silhouetted figures. Recognize it by the fusion of 1960s Parisian streetscape, Mod-inflected schoolboy elegance, and an aloof, being-seen pose.

name: Minimal_Wave
description: Minimal Wave is the visual language of obscure late-1970s-to-mid-1980s pre-MIDI cassette electronics and its 2000s archival revival: black-white-and-grey xerox-grade imagery, heavy film grain and tape noise, stark stacked sans-serif or hand-scrawled typography, severe geometry, architectural one-point perspectives, tape machines and oscilloscope-style technical diagrams, and letterboxed Cold War-era film stills, at most broken by a single pale or saturated accent. Typical subjects are deadpan faces, cropped eyes and hands, subway tunnels, wireframe grids and amateur costumed figures, all carrying melancholy, detachment and lo-fi cassette-culture nostalgia.

name: Minimalism
description: Minimalism is the reductive aesthetic of post-WWII Western art (peak 1960s–early 1970s, lifestyle revival since 2010), defined by decluttered frames, solid muted color fields and honest matte materials. Recognize it by white/neutral/pastel palettes, a single isolated subject held in generous negative space, unadorned cubic architecture, quiet solid-color clothing, museum-style object photography, and occasional flat De Stijl primary-color blocks used as geometry rather than decoration. The mood is calm, intentional, anti-consumerist order.

name: Mission_School
description: Mission School (aka Urban Folk, Lowbrow Folk, New Folk) is the hand-painted bohemian street aesthetic of 1990s San Francisco's Mission District: muted earthy-urban house-paint colors, faux-weathered textures, folk sign-painting lettering, UPA-revival cartoon figures, graffiti softened into folk motifs, and cluster-hung assemblages on found boards and cardboard. Typical subjects are skaters, coffeeshop murals and packaging, row houses, fire escapes, quirky ordinary people, painted skate decks and wooden folk figures; the mood is DIY, deadpan-warm and deliberately amateur. Mainstream from roughly 1998–2008 as the "more authentic" successor to Global Village Coffeehouse branding.

name: Mizuiro
description: Mizuiro (水色, "water color") is a 2010s Japanese youth aesthetic of cool-toned, blue-gray graded photos and wobbly minimal illustrations built on a mandatory triad of light blue, cyan and white, with slouchy aqua tracksuits and hoodies, flared leg warmers, piles of white-and-blue plush mascots (Cinnamoroll above all), concealed faces under sticker overlays, and Web 1.0/webcore accents. Its mood is kawaii but pessimistic and fragile — otaku melancholy staged in arcades, parking garages, concrete streets and high-key white rooms. Recognize it by the ubiquitous cold aqua filter, matte plush-and-fleece textures, silver/black micro-accents and blush-pink leakage; note that "Tenshi Kaiwai" is a Western misnomer for its 2020s revival, not a separate angelic style.

name: Mob_Wife
description: Mob Wife is a 2020s TikTok-born fashion aesthetic (c. 2023–2025) that costumes the romanticized Mafia wife of Goodfellas, Casino and The Sopranos: leopard and animal prints, vintage-coded fur and faux fur coats, black leather, knee-high black boots, chunky gold jewelry, oversized dark sunglasses, designer handbags and bright red lipstick over a black-dominant palette punctured by gold and red. Maximalist, loud-luxury and unapologetically materialist, it is the deliberate antithesis of Clean Girl minimalism. Recognize it by stacked fur and print textures, blown-out hair or silk headscarves, stone-stoop and gilded-interior settings, and warm golden-hour or direct-flash lighting with a filmic grain.

name: Mochette
description: Mochette (also Forgottencore, Grosscore, Ugly Cute, Nauseous Nostalgia) is a 2010s Tumblr aesthetic that welds tender feminine cuteness — pale pink lace, dolls and doll parts, ballet ribbons, babydoll dresses, floral quilts — to revulsive rot: mold, fungi, snails and worms, stained and torn textiles, peeling pastel rooms, raw and decaying matter. Its look is faded analog snapshot or washed-out film, in a sickly palette of blush pink, cream, sage-olive green, rust brown and gray, aiming for queasy tenderness and nausea rather than gothic fear. Load this skill when an image or prompt pairs dollish femininity with deliberate taint, decay, disease or vermin.

name: Mod
description: Mod is the British youth-subculture aesthetic of late-1950s to mid-1960s London: razor-sharp tailored suits with narrow lapels, miniskirts and geometric A-line shift dresses, polo shirts buttoned to the top, and chrome-laden Vespa or Lambretta scooters. Its palette is black-and-white contrast punched with bold primaries (red, blue, yellow), orange and turquoise, arranged as flat color-blocks, polka dots, stripes and Union Jack or RAF-roundel emblems. Recognize it by androgynous boyish silhouettes, geometric Sassoon-style bobs, opaque tights and go-go boots, fishtail parkas, and deadpan graphic poses under flat studio light or grainy black-and-white press photography.

name: Modernism
description: Modernism (c. 1890s–1945, Western Europe) is the umbrella aesthetic of the radical break: fragmented Cubist planes, reduced geometric abstraction, machine-age precision, and white functionalist architecture on pilotis with ribbon windows. Its palette alternates between doctrinal De Stijl primaries, desaturated ochre-umber-grey Cubist earth, and machine-white plaster and steel; its signature moves are asymmetry, flattened or fractured space, stripped ornament, and function-first structure. Subjects range from papier-collé still lifes and deadpan dreamscapes to steel-and-glass villas, photomontage, and austere typographic book jackets.

name: Modernisme
description: Modernisme (Catalan Modernism, c. 1888–1911) is the Catalan branch of Art Nouveau — architecture, design and painting in which structure melts into organic, curvilinear form (bone-like balconies, parabolic arches, undulating stone walls) and is skinned in trencadís broken-tile mosaic, stained glass and wrought-iron stemwork over earthy exposed brick and honey stone. Its palette spans vibrant ceramic polychromy (cobalt, turquoise, emerald, saffron, cream) and natural earth tones, with a parallel muted grey-beige plein-air painting branch and flat olive/ochre poster art with hand-lettering. Recognize it by nature-derived structural curves, fragmented ceramic colour, craft-integrated Gesamtkunstwerk richness, and a fin-de-siècle Barcelona bourgeois mood mixing vitality with Symbolist melancholy.

name: Moe
description: Japanese character-design aesthetic codified in the 2000s from 1980s–90s bishōjo anime and otaku forum slang, built on neotenous proportions — oversized glossy round eyes with star-shaped or layered specular highlights, kitten-rounded skulls, minimized mouths and noses, and soft compressed body silhouettes. Palette runs pastel pinks, lavenders, mints and sky blues, or bold saturated hues reserved for hair, eyes and costume; signature markers are maid dresses, sailor or blazer school uniforms, kemonomimi (cat ears foremost), ribbons, twintails and chibi registers. Subjects are endearing youthful characters — solo busts, ensemble casts, chibi vignettes, gijinka mascots — rendered in flat cel paint or smooth airbrushed digital color under even, shadowless light.

name: Moe_Swag
description: Moe Swag ("Gangstas with Waifus") is a 2010s meme aesthetic that collages flat, cel-shaded moe anime girls into photographs, spray-paint murals and album covers of real-world "tough" figures — rappers, gangsters, masked militants, politicians, gopniks — posed in affectionate two-shots. Recognition hinges on the seam: a muted, warm-filtered or flash-lit photographic layer against saturated candy-colour anime inserts, deadpan or grinning embraces, dakimakura props, and casual JPEG grain. Humor, irony and cultural blending are the payload; finishes range from rough cutout edits to painted murals and meme-rap cover art.

name: Monochrome_Luxe
description: Monochrome Luxe is a semi-minimalist interior-design aesthetic of the 1980s–90s built on a black-and-white two-tone armature punctuated by at most one or two blocked saturated accents (cherry red, magenta, sunflower yellow, cobalt, teal-mint, tangerine). Signature elements are white square ceramic tile with dark grout, color-blocked laminate cabinets, matte or painted black metal, clear and frosted glass, articulated track and desk-arm spotlights, strict stripe/checker geometry, and — in its early-80s phase — exposed steel trusses and embossed sheet steel. Typical subjects are kitchens, bathrooms, bedrooms, dining rooms, cafes, bars and retail interiors rendered with catalogue-plate evenness.

name: Mori_Kei
description: Mori Kei (Mori Girl / Mori Boy) is a Japanese street fashion of the late 2000s that dresses as if the wearer lived in the woods: many loose, body-hiding layers of off-white and earth-toned cotton, linen, wool knit and lace — the "yurufuwa" fluffy-soft look — stacked with cardigans, vests, knit shawls, tights, lace-up leather boots and baskets. Its palette is cream, beige, moss green and bark brown with small floral accents of soft pink or dusty blue; its motifs are forests, deer, moss, flowers, hanging herbs, cottages and fairy tales, lit in soft overcast or dappled shade. Recognize it by the erased silhouette of stacked loose layers, natural minimal makeup with high round blush, and a quiet, slow-life woodland mood.

name: Morute
description: Morute ("morbid" + "cute") is an early-2010s Tumblr aesthetic that frames macabre subjects — kitchen knives, rifles, extracted teeth, gas masks, decaying small-town houses — inside hyper-feminine girlhood settings of blush pink, milk white, lace, vintage dolls and Catholic kitsch. Its images fade like overexposed film or dim like vintage snapshots, and its signature move is the tender framing of dread: crucifix shrines on pink satin, doll-like figures in nightgowns holding weapons, empty pink rooms that feel unsafe. Recognize it by the pink/white/gray milk-faded palette, obsessive accumulations of religious paraphernalia, Kinderwhore-derived babydoll fashion, and an atmosphere of vulnerable, guilt-laden nostalgia.

name: Mote_Kei
description: Mote Kei (モテ系) is a late-2000s Japanese feminine fashion aesthetic built around mass-appeal charm: quiet, ladylike coordinates in neutrals (ivory, beige, taupe, navy) with a single soft pastel accent, knee-to-midi pleated or tulle skirts, soft knits and puff-sleeve blouses, groomed brown wavy hair, and small ladylike accessories like structured bags, pearl headbands and thin heels. Its imagery is catalog- and magazine-born — full-body coordinate shots on white cycloramas, pale studio sets or sunlit streets, plus coordinate spreads and hair-tutorial pages with Japanese captions — lit high-key, even and shadowless. Recognize it by its balance rule: cute but not childish, softly sexy but modest, trendy but never loud, flashy or overly sexual.

name: Moto_Boho
description: Moto Boho (also Moto Bohemian or Greaser Boho) is a mid-2010s-to-mid-2020s fashion aesthetic from US and Australian street and runway culture that fuses motorcycle hardness with bohemian softness — cropped or oversized black leather and distressed olive suede thrown over ruffled chiffon, prairie white, lace and crochet. Its palette grounds itself in black, oxblood, deep brown and forest green, lightened by sun-washed creams and faded pastels, with chunky studded belts, chains, fringed suede bags and heavy buckled boots as the hardware counterweight. Recognize it by the deliberate soft-vs-hard layering in a single silhouette: a delicate hem under heavy leather, fringe over lace, a combat boot beneath a tiered maxi skirt.

name: Motomami
description: Motomami is a 2020s Spanish internet-born aesthetic launched by ROSALÍA's 2022 album, fusing hard biker culture (black leather jackets, racing pants, cat-ear cyberpunk helmets, thigh-high moto boots) with soft feminine vulnerability (sheer fabric, pink nails, butterflies, handwritten confessions) on stark white paper voids. Its palette is black, lipstick red, paper white and soft pink, organized through torn-collage zine layouts, ballpoint scribbles, liquid-gothic red logotypes and Y2K sunglasses. Recognize it by the deliberate hard/soft duality: moto hardware and racing leather framed by minimalist art direction, scribbled marginalia and avant-garde helmets rather than garage or club realism.

name: Movida_Madrileña
description: Post-Franco Madrid counterculture (late 1970s–1980s) whose visual DNA is stark black leather, fishnets and DIY studs collided with fuchsia, electric blue and signal red, worn by androgynous, heavily made-up crews in bars, clubs and concert halls. Two coexisting registers define it — grainy direct-flash black-and-white nightlife documentary, and hyper-saturated comic-poster painting with hand-lettered Spanish type and subverted Catholic kitsch. Recognize by teased quiffs and mohawks, camp theatrical posing, flat pastel or clashing polychrome backdrops, fanzine xerox grain, and collective euphoria rather than gloom.

name: Mudéjar
description: Mudéjar is the hybrid architectural and decorative style of medieval Iberia (12th–16th c.), in which Christian Romanesque and Gothic building structures are clothed in the ornamental vocabulary of Al-Andalus: intricate laid brick, blind arcades, sawtooth friezes, glazed azulejo insets in cobalt, green and white, carved yesería stucco, horseshoe and multi-lobed arches, and gilded artesonado wooden ceilings. Recognize it by terracotta brick masses under hard Mediterranean sun, tiered bell towers studded with lozenge tilework, arcaded patios on slender columns, coffered timber ceilings, and all-over aniconic geometric pattern extending even to lusterware ceramics. Typical subjects are church apses and towers, courtyards, portals, ceilings treated as full-frame pattern fields, and Hispano-Moresque dishes.

name: Mushroomcore
description: Mushroomcore (Mushcore) is an early-2020s internet aesthetic that romanticizes fungi and the forest floor: earthy browns, soft creams and moss greens punctuated by the scarlet-and-white Amanita muscaria toadstool, rendered in moist macro close-ups, misty woodland scenes, foraging wear, mushroom embroidery, ceramic mushroom lamps and fairy-ring folklore. Recognition hinges on fungal centrality plus an earthy, damp, enchanted-understory mood — wonder and tender decay rather than general nature prettiness. Load this skill when images or prompts center mushrooms, toadstools, mossy forest floors, mycological craft or mushroom-motif fashion and decor.

name: Mythpunk
description: Mythpunk is the postmodern makeover of folklore — fairy tales and myth retold dark, poetic and surreal, dressed in baroque multicultural fashion with punk-goth fey twists. Its palette is aged organic (moss green, bark brown, parchment cream, dusty blue-grey) punctured by oxblood red or antique gold, rendered in painterly book-cover illustration, folk-naive panel painting, overcast woodland photography or dreamlike low-fi renders. Signature content: subverted fairy-tale tableaus, beast-and-maiden entanglements, thorn-choked woods, gloomy gothic stone, and non-linear, symbol-laden composition carrying morbidity, sensuality and a twisted tenderness.

name: Naarmcore
description: Naarmcore is an early-2020s Melbourne-born streetwear aesthetic: utilitarian, anti-fashion layering of puffer jackets, cargo and parachute pants, technical hiking shoes and beanies in a neutral earth palette of black, khaki, grey and beige. It reads as deadpan phone-camera snapshots of oversized, slouchy silhouettes against graffiti laneways, corrugated-iron backlots, overcast rooftops and festival shade-sail crowds. Recognize it by technical outdoor gear worn strictly in inner-city settings, baggy proportion play, white crew socks, and lo-fi flash-lit candid framing.

name: Nanchatte_Seifuku
description: Japanese 2000s "pretend school uniform" aesthetic (aka High School Fantasy) that romanticizes female high-school life through mix-and-match uniform pieces — blazers or sailor tops, pleated plaid skirts, ties and ribbon bows, loose socks, uwabaki indoor shoes, loafers — worn casually and photographed in faded pastel washes or muted film-snapshot tones. Signature subjects are school-calendar motifs: classrooms with wooden desks and blown-out window light, cherry blossoms over concrete schoolyards, bicycles with front baskets, decorated bags and plush charms, group outings shot from behind or in playful cropped angles. Mood is wholesome, nostalgic and friendship-centered, distinct from luxury Preppy, tanned Gyaru/Kogal and menacing Yandere school imagery.

name: Naturecore
description: Naturecore is the 2020s umbrella aesthetic of romanticized wild nature — misty mossed forests, tree-covered mountains, lakes, streams, swamps, wildflower meadows and quiet fauna, rendered in a green-dominant palette of moss, fern, bark brown and bone white under diffuse, dappled or mist-softened light. Its images read as serene escapes from urban screen life: photographic and texture-forward (moss velvet, lichen crust, duckweed, fern fractals), with humans absent, tiny, or reduced to reverent hands. The range runs from sunlit meadow calm to quietly mysterious deep woods, never to horror.

name: Nautical
description: Crisp maritime aesthetic descended from sailors' workwear and navy tradition, built on a structural white-and-navy pair with small loud signal-red accents, weathered wood, brass and bold Breton stripes. Signature subjects are the sea and rocky coastline, lighthouses, boats and docks, ship wheels, anchors and life rings, seagulls and sea life, shingled beach houses, and sailor-collared dress from Victorian seaside walking suits to resort wear and sailor Lolita. Mood is serene, orderly and sun-bleached — yacht-club elegance or rugged fisherman charm — never murky, gothic or piratical.

name: Nazi_Chic
description: Countercultural appropriation of Third Reich uniform tailoring and insignia for shock value — black structured wool and leather uniforms, peaked caps, red brassards, Iron Cross / Totenkopf / party-eagle motifs and German blackletter type over a black-red-white palette with silver hardware glints. Born in mid-1970s London punk, it spread into metal, glam, industrial/EBM and fetish scenes and later into depoliticized East Asian pop spectacle. Recognize it by cold authoritarian discipline worn ironically: confrontational frontal poses, grainy monochrome or clinical desaturated lighting, crisp uniform geometry crossed with bondage gear.

name: Neko
description: Neko is the kawaii aesthetic built on the anime cat-person trope: human figures given cat ears, tails and paw mittens, dressed in high-key pastels (pink, lilac, cream, rose gold) with optional black accents. Signature elements are fluffy faux-fur and chunky-knit textures, bell chokers and heart-ring collars, satin bows, frilled maid and Lolita touches, paw-print motifs, and blush-pink sparkle effects. Typical subjects are catgirls and feminized catboys in cosplay or avatar form, plush paw-mitten close-ups, dressed-up real cats, and pink duotone manga illustrations.

name: Neo-Aero
description: Neo-Aero (Frutiger Aero Revival, early 2020s) is a nostalgia-maximalist digital aesthetic of wet-glass and liquid skeuomorphism, exaggerated lens flare, and floating bubbles or translucent spheres drifting over saturated grass-green hills beneath brilliant sky-blue "Windows" skies with wispy clouds. Recognize it by chrome-and-glass 3D typography, dewy manicured nature, rippling turquoise water, fictional glossy UI windows, and a washed-out heavenly white glow applied to album covers, posters, collages and renders; the mood is retrospective technological optimism and hyper-clean comfort.

name: Neo-Chinese_Style
description: Neo-Chinese Style (Xinzhongshi, 新中式) is a contemporary Chinese aesthetic that distills traditional signifiers — Mandarin collars, frog closures, Chinese knots, Qipao/Hanfu-derived silhouettes, flower-bird-dragon embroidery — into modern tailoring, and quotes low-key Hui/Su architectural vocabulary in new concrete-and-glass buildings. Its palette runs from ink black and rice-paper neutrals through earthy tones and pastels to controlled flashes of vermilion, indigo and gilt; its staging spans clean lookbook/OOTD photography, saturated-backdrop avant-garde editorials, and symmetric blue-hour architecture with reflecting pools. Read it as poised Guochao cultural confidence: classical elegance simplified for daily wear, never period costume.

name: Neo-Pop
description: Neo-Pop (New Pop) is the post-1980s postmodern successor to Pop Art: bright saturated commercial color, bold black contours enclosing hard-edged planes filled with polka dots, hearts, stars and stripes, glossy inflated or polished commodity forms, and dense appropriation collage of celebrities, cartoon characters, brand logos and advertising. Typical subjects include balloon animals, serial spot grids, anime-flavored figures, kitsch domestic objects and trademark parody, all delivered with playful irony and an industrial, gallery-polished sheen. Load this skill when an image must read as a celebration-cum-critique of consumer culture — maximal, candy-bright and glossy — rather than vintage comic-strip Pop, underground Lowbrow or otaku Superflat.

name: Neo-Tokyo
description: Neo-Tokyo is the 1980s Japanese branch of cyberpunk — vertical canyons of megastructures and neon-lit skyscrapers stacked with kanji and katakana signage, holographic advertisements, and rain-slicked streets that mirror saturated magenta, cyan and violet light against deep blacks and cool grays. Codified by Akira and Ghost in the Shell, it pairs gleaming technological overreach with gritty urban decay, lone pedestrians, biker gangs and flying vehicles under a polluted night sky. Recognize it by signage-saturated vertical density, wet reflective asphalt, foggy atmospheric depth, and 1980s cel-anime or painterly concept-art rendering.

name: Neo-Vectorheart
description: Neo-Vectorheart (Vectorheart Revival) is a late-2010s Neo-Y2K revival of the Y2K-era Vectorheart look: hard-edged vector emblems chamfered at 45/60-degree angles, cryptic futuristic glyph typography, and hairline technical HUD scaffolding set on monochrome black-and-white fields with at most one saturated accent (signal red, acid lime, electric cyan, violet). It appears chiefly as logo and wordmark lockups, bass-music single covers, esports and game UI, and exploded machine schematics, ranging from sleek minimal lockups to maximalist "gamer-grunge" detail. Recognize it by notched angular shield marks, micro-monospace data readouts, glitch grain over matte black, and diagonal slash bands.

name: Neo-Y2K
description: Neo-Y2K (Y2K Revival) is the late-2010s/early-2020s resurrection of turn-of-the-millennium retrofuturism: liquid chrome and Metalheart metal forms, highly saturated blues, pinks and greens on clean minimalist grounds, dynamic techno typography and Japanese-ad collage logic. Typical subjects are studio fashion editorials (cargo pants, oval sunglasses, chunky sneakers), glossy CGI blobs and inflatable vinyl objects, chrome icon and logo sets, and playful sticker-collage posters. Recognize it by crisp modern render quality paired with affectionate, energetic nostalgia — glossy and playful, never melancholic, grungy or dystopian.

name: Neoclassical_Pomo
description: Postmodern architectural and graphic style of the late 1970s–1990s that double-codes classical Roman and Greek grammar — pediments, colossal columns, exaggerated arches, obelisks, axial symmetry — with ironic, playful intent, setting marble and stone against curved glass curtain walls, neon tubing, synthetic finishes and bright pastels. Typical subjects are corporate and civic facades with oversized or freestanding classical fragments, dramatic empty lobbies and rotundas with stylized colonnades and faux-ruin props beside modern furniture, public plazas, and early airbrush/CGI advertisements and posters of floating digital columns and statues over gradient sunset skies. Recognize it by a white-dominant palette, factory-new stone, scale irony, sterile theatrical light, and the constant collision of antique form with late-century commercial material.

name: Neoclassicism
description: Neoclassicism (c. 1760–1830, born in Rome, spread across Europe and North America) is the Enlightenment's return to Greco-Roman antiquity: symmetrical temple fronts, domes and coffered ceilings in pale limestone and plaster white; interiors of garlands, medallions and Pompeian grotesques on ochre, verdigris or crimson silk; history paintings of togas, oaths and civic sacrifice rendered with smooth surfaces and stage-clear light; engraved visionary spheres and fashion plates of high-waisted gowns and black-coated pantaloons. Recognize it by archaeological correctness, bilateral symmetry, a somber restrained palette with strong clear light, and an air of moral solemnity posed against Rococo frivolity.

name: Neofolk
description: Neofolk (apocalyptic folk, folk noir) is the visual language of the early-1980s London post-industrial scene: high-contrast monochrome photography and xerox-degraded collage carrying runes (Algiz, Sowilo), medieval heraldry, Totenkopf and camouflage over war memorials, classical statues and military graveyards. Its palette is olive drab, field grey, black, charcoal and parchment white; its surfaces carry grain and film artifacts reminiscent of 1920s German Expressionist cinema; its figures wear disciplined military surplus and 1930s intellectual dress; its printed matter speaks in blackletter, woodcut linework and engraved seals. Recognize it by mournful archival solemnity and coded, deliberately ambiguous insignia — not by Goth theatricality or martial industrial's monumental propaganda polish.

name: Neon_Noir
description: Neon Noir is the night-side of 1970s–80s neo-noir cinema re-saturated with 1980s neon: near-black streets lit only by magenta, purple, cyan and red signage, thickened by fog and rain-slick reflections, populated by silhouetted lone figures and morally ambiguous antiheroes. Recognize it by chiaroscuro darkness pierced by vibrant diegetic neon glow, wet asphalt mirroring signs and tail lights, motel-and-storefront signage or pixel-font text, and an overriding air of existential isolation. Typical subjects include night streets, parked period cars, motels and overpasses, top-down pixel game screens, and rim-lit portraits of criminals and drifters.

name: Neon_Ooze
description: Neon Ooze (also called Oozepunk) is the gross-out marketing aesthetic of 1980s–1990s kids' culture, built on viscous day-glo fluids — slime, goop, toxic waste — dripping across toy blister packs, comic and VHS covers, game art and print ads. Its visual DNA is radioactive green ooze with wet specular highlights splatted over electric purple, hot pink and acid yellow fields, populated by mutant creatures, waste drums, radiation trefoils and creepy-crawlies, with dripping jagged lettering and starburst callouts, all played for laughs rather than horror.

name: Neoperreo
description: Neoperreo is the mid-2010s internet-born, Latin American and Spanish underground alternative to mainstream reggaetón, visually defined by net.art flyer collages, chrome Y2K consumer tech (flip phones, desktop OS icons), hyper-glossy lips and stiletto nails, doll-like 3D-rendered avatars, and harsh-flash club snapshots. Its palette swings between candy-neon magenta/lavender/acid green with chrome neutrals and a dark gothic lacquer mode, often captioned in blackletter or death-metal logotypes. Queer, feminist, DIY and sexually liberated, it reads as "cute turned menacing" — twisted Lolita meets cultura de barrio.

name: Nerd
description: Nerd is the aesthetic of academic devotion and unfashionable enthusiasm, pairing a mid-century stereotype wardrobe — thick prescribed glasses, bowties, suspenders, button-down shirts, high white socks, slacks — with knowledge signage: chalkboards dense with equations, stacks of library books, chessboards and twist puzzles, lab glassware, beige retro computers, and sci-fi fandom posters and collectibles. Its palette is hue-open but anchors in red, green, brown, blue and grey, ranging from saturated plastic primaries to chalk-white on slate and muted institutional neutrals, lit flat and honest by studio, fluorescent or domestic light. Mood is earnest, comically awkward, collector-obsessive; subjects run from stereotype portraits and library/lab interiors to maximalist fandom bedrooms and isolated object still lifes.

name: Nerdcore
description: Nerdcore is the album-cover aesthetic of nerdy hip-hop, coined by MC Frontalot in the late 1990s and crystallized in the 2000s–2010s: drawn or photo-collaged rapper portraits in bold glasses and ties, dropped into 8-bit–2000s video-game worlds, circuit-board backdrops and CRT/cartridge clutter, in saturated comic primaries or vaporwave-shifted pastels. Look for the mashup of hip-hop braggadocio (mics, poses, cash-as-parody, label stamps) with nerd matter (pixels, sprites, dice, pixel fonts, meme type), proud self-mocking wit, and bold display typography over screen-native color.

name: Net.art
description: Net.art is the critical art of the 1990s web, using browsers, raw HTML, hyperlinks, online forms, ASCII character renders and terminal green-on-black as both medium and subject, alongside the default palettes of early websites (system gray chrome, link blue, naive pixel neon). Recognize it by screen-literal compositions — window chrome as frame, text and code as image material, deliberately shredded or glitched layouts — and by deadpan documentation of CRTs, phone-in flyers and sparse gallery walls. It reads conceptual and anti-commercial, never decorative, which separates it from glitch art, weirdcore and demoscene polish.

name: Neubrutalism
description: Neubrutalism (Neo Brutalism, Neo Memphis) is a late-2010s digital design aesthetic that breaks design conventions on purpose: flat, clashing rainbow color fields, thick dark outlines, hard 45° offset shadows, grotesque stretched uppercase type, oversized UI chrome, pseudo-3D blocks, graph-paper grids and 1930s rubber-hose cartoon mascots, all filtered through 1990s Webcore and Memphis Design nostalgia. Load this skill when an image or prompt shows sticker-like outlined cards with solid drop shadows, browser-window frames, deliberately "off-putting" color pairings, or loud anti-polish web/poster graphics.

name: Neue_Slowenische_Kunst
description: Neue Slowenische Kunst (NSK) is the retro-avant-garde visual language of the 1980s Ljubljana collective (Laibach, IRWIN, New Collectivism): red-black-white silkscreen posters and paintings that quote Socialist Realism, Suprematism, Constructivism and totalitarian pageantry through "over-identification." Recognize it by black Malevich-derived crosses, hammer-swinging worker silhouettes, cog-and-antler emblems, heraldic symmetry, grotesque caps locked into text borders, gold-leaf icon panels, and deadpan monochrome ritual stagings — always ambiguous, never sincere.

name: Neumorphism
description: Neumorphism ("Soft UI", late 2019–2021) is a low-contrast interface aesthetic in which buttons, cards, tiles and widgets appear extruded from or dented into a background of the exact same matte color — off-white, light gray, soft blue or pastel, with a charcoal dark-mode variant. Its signature is the paired shadow rule: one soft light shadow top-left, one soft dark shadow bottom-right, inverted to inner shadows for pressed states, with rounded corners and no borders anywhere. Typical subjects are app screens, widget panels, icon tile grids, toggles/sliders/clocks and soft plastic hardware renders such as keyboards and remotes.

name: New_Beat
description: New Beat is the visual language of the Belgian late-1980s club subculture (1987–89): overwhelming black clothing and graphics punctured by Belgian-flag yellow and red, the yellow smiley weaponized as a defacement over politicians' and military faces, oval gravestone-portrait "bomma badges," layered rosaries, bowler hats and BDSM leather on androgynous, pale-faced clubbers. Expect halftone black-and-white photography, flat Pop-Art collage flyers and record sleeves, analog VHS color casts, and a deadpan macabre-camp mood that mixes menace with a wink.

name: New_England_Gothic
description: New England Gothic ("Northern Gothic") is a regional Gothic aesthetic of Puritan haunting and colonial memory — witch trials, old burying grounds, weathered-shingle houses, run-down harbor and mill towns — descended from Hawthorne's 1835 Dark Romantic fiction and revived through 2010s Tumblr liminal-space photography. Its palette is dry and sadd: overcast grays, bone white, near-black, dried-grass ochre, leaf-rust, oxblood and candle-amber, rendered in tempera-dry paint, desaturated film or archival print registers. Signature elements include slate headstones, bare branch lace, fieldstone walls, white meetinghouse steeples, a single lit window at dusk, aged sermon and trial paper, and empty off-season roads.

name: New_Figuration
description: New Figuration (Nueva Figuración) is the post-WWII return to the human figure in 1950s–60s Argentina, Mexico, Venezuela, Colombia and Spain, in which bodies are distorted, smeared, inflated or monstrified as social critique. Recognize it by damaged but legible figures set against colliding flat saturated color planes (cobalt, leaf green, signal red, violet) or mournful black-brown-purple fields punctured by raw flesh pink, with informalist scribble, washes, smudged mask-faces and collage seams over any polished finish. Masked or skull-like portraits, caged or seated isolated figures, satirical officials, eerie family groups and chaotic crowd friezes are its signature subjects.

name: New_Look
description: New Look is the post-WWII Parisian couture aesthetic launched by Christian Dior in 1947: an architectural hourglass silhouette with rounded shoulders, a nipped-in waist and a voluminous mid-calf skirt, rendered in beige, navy and monochrome black-and-cream. Recognize it by Bar-style peplum jackets, pleated circle skirts, wide-brim or straw hats, opera gloves, pearls, and mannequin-poised figures lit in silver-gelatin editorial light. It values hyperfemininity, opulence and sensuality-through-tailoring as a deliberate rejection of wartime utility dress.

name: New_Money
description: New Money is the conspicuous-display aesthetic of recently acquired wealth: legible luxury brand logos and monogram canvas, gold and silver metal, fur coats, sequins, private jets, yachts, luxury cars, marble floors and stacked designer shopping bags, in a palette of gold, silver, black, cream and a loud red accent. It spans a maximalist Gold/Jet-Set branch (plunging metallic gowns, oversized mirrored sunglasses, gold-plated objects, contoured tan and coffin nails) and quieter Minimalist and Bourgeois-Bohemian branches that still signal purchase rather than inheritance. Recognize it by advertising-gloss lighting, current-season products, accumulation of status objects in multiples, and a performative, triumphantly materialist mood.

name: New_Partisans
description: New Partisans (Novi Partizani) is the mid-1980s Sarajevo rock-movement aesthetic that re-appropriates Yugoslav WWII Partisan iconography — titovka side caps with the red petokraka star, olive JNA-style tunics with gold epaulettes, knitted partizanke socks, grainy archival Partisan photographs — inside commercial album-sleeve montage. Its palette is muted military olive, wool grey and khaki punctured by dominant flag red, layered with torn-paper historical collage, condensed uppercase slogans ("Bratstvo i jedinstvo"), Romanticist painting quotations and deliberate collisions of socialist-heroic and Western pop-stardom registers. Recognize it by square sleeve formats, halftone and duotone print grain, group portraits in stylized uniform, and the red star used as both badge and punctuation.

name: New_Primitivism
description: New Primitivism (Novi primitivizam) is the deliberately démodé, "smart yet trashy" visual language of 1983–87 Sarajevo: xerox cut-and-paste collage, hand-lettered cursive script and street-slang captions over halftone photos, naive comic-strip illustration, and the flat, washed lighting of early-1980s Yugoslav TV studios. Signature elements include the 1970s leisure-suit uniform (plaid jackets, waist-tight bell-bottoms, thin gold chain, pointy špicoke shoes), marker-yellow and signal-red blocks on xerox black, crowded mahala rooftops, and affectionate caricatures of coalminers, taxi drivers, petty thugs and pensioners. Load this skill for late-socialist Balkan subculture, DIY zine and vinyl-sleeve collage, sketch-comedy studio staging, or camp mock-official Yugoslav rock imagery.

name: New_Rave
description: New Rave (Nu-Rave, Neu-Rave) is the mid-2000s British indie-dance subculture (c. 2006–2008) whose visuals weld 1990s rave signifiers — glowsticks, neon face paint, whistles — onto skinny-jeans indie fashion, all rendered in fluorescent CMYK neons with crushed blacks and blown-out highlights. Signature elements include direct-flash club snapshots, chroma-keyed flat color fields, 8-bit sprites and vector psychedelia (Vectordelia), kaleidoscopic lattices, oversized slogan tees, lamé leggings, and neon-acetate Wayfarers or shutter shades. Recognize it by hedonistic DIY maximalism, solarized skin tones, and bold sans-serif type with neon-glow outer strokes.

name: New_Romantic
description: New Romantic (Blitz Kids) is the flamboyant London club subculture of 1978–1983: androgynous youths wearing theatrical clown-white makeup, graphic color-block eyeshadow and spiked or teased hair, dressed in DIY hybrids of pirate/rococo historicism (poet shirts, sashes, hussar jackets, brocade, tricorn-style hats) and synth-pop futurism (sharp suits in odd colors, gold lamé, geometric haircuts). Its palette sets black and stark white against unmuted primaries, hot magenta and metallic gold/silver, captured in hard-flash club snapshots, flat studio portraits and airbrushed poster graphics on grainy analog film. Recognize it by gender-ambiguous glamour, escapist theatricality, and the deliberate collision of historical costume with electronic-era cool.

name: New_Wave
description: Late-1970s to mid-1980s music and graphic-design aesthetic of "synthetic modernity": fluorescent hot pink, electric yellow, cyan and tertiary purple/orange/green fired against black voids or flat paper grounds; dysfunctional modernist grids, photocopier grain, moiré and airbrush smoothness; atomic-age retro-futurist kitsch, floating triangles and orbit discs, angular big-shoulder suits, skinny ties, wedge haircuts and thick-rimmed glasses. Ironic, robotic, art-school camp delivered through vinyl sleeves, concert posters and early-MTV framing. Load when an image mixes 1950s atomic kitsch with 1980s plastic color and broken Swiss-grid typography.

name: New_Wave_Tropical
description: New Wave Tropical is a mid-1980s to mid-1990s commercial-leisure aesthetic of electric-saturated rainforest and beach imagery rendered as Matisse-style construction-paper cutouts — chunky palm fronds, toucans, hibiscus-type blooms, elephants and folk-geometric zigzag borders in hot pink, turquoise, lime green and sun yellow on white or black grounds. Recognize it in resort signage, allover apparel prints, beverage packaging, ceramics and promo posters that fuse African, Caribbean and Latin motifs with retro-punk freeform playfulness and a kitschy vacation optimism.

name: Newlyn_School
description: Late-Victorian to Edwardian plein-air painting of the Cornish fishing colony at Newlyn (c. 1880s–1910s), blending French Realist social conscience with Impressionist atmosphere. Silvery grays, cool blues and earthy ochres under overcast or rain-washed light; mirror-wet beaches, harbor walls, beached pilchard boats, and working figures — net-menders, fish sellers, seaweed gatherers, women in headscarves — absorbed in their tasks. Recognize it by its silver-and-earth palette, reflective wet foregrounds, solid drawing under broken water-strokes, and its quiet documentary mood.

name: Nightcore_(aesthetic)
description: A mid-2000s to early-2010s internet aesthetic of moonlit digital fantasy: 2000s moe-style anime characters — angels, vampires, magical girls, lone girls with wind-blown hair — staged in saturated navy and electric-blue nightscapes beneath oversized full moons, with falling white petals or feathers, violet mid-tones and pale pink accents. Born as the uniform thumbnail look of YouTube nightcore remixes and desktop-wallpaper culture, it pairs high-contrast celestial backlight with melancholic romanticism and airbrushed visual-novel polish. Recognize it by the blue-only night palette, the giant glowing moon, drifting particle atmospheres and bittersweet solitude.

name: Normcore
description: Normcore is the 2010s anti-trend aesthetic of deliberately average, brand-less dress — plain cotton tees, logo-free hoodies, stone-washed straight-leg "dad" jeans, chinos and chunky New Balance-type sneakers in navy, gray, white, beige, washed denim and black. Its imagery mimics stock photography, 1990s catalog spreads, retail banners and deadpan flash snapshots: flat clinical lighting, pedestrian backdrops (brick walls, parking lots, bedrooms, store aisles), unisex relaxed silhouettes and a "perfect boring" affect. Recognize it by anonymity: no loud logos, no skinny fits, no aspirational styling, no golden-hour romance.

name: Northern_Soul
description: Northern Soul is the visual culture of the working-class all-nighter dance scene of late-1960s to 1970s Northern England and the Midlands: grainy, flash-lit greyscale dance-floor photography of athletic solo dancers in high-waisted wide-leg trousers and patch-covered knit vests, plus a screen-printed ephemera vernacular of circular sew-on badges, the raised clenched fist emblem, 45 rpm vinyl, record bags and club flyers in cream, rust, mustard and teal. Recognize it by the black fist logo, embroidered club patches (Wigan Casino, Blackpool Mecca, The Torch), sprung wooden dance floors, turntable-and-vinyl motifs and "Keep the Faith" flyer typography.

name: Northerness
description: Northerness is a 2010s Nordic/Scandinavian aesthetic fusing deep conifer wilderness, Norse pagan ritual, and hygge hearth-warmth in a muted palette of charcoal black, spruce green, fog gray, snow white, oxblood red, navy wool-blue and candle gold. Signature elements include lusekofte knit sweaters, cloaks and flower crowns, silver hammer pendants and drinking horns, longship prows, candles and cinnamon buns, wolves and bears in mist, and National Romantic painterly illustration. Recognize it by hushed fog or single-candle lighting, wool–birch–parchment textures, and a calm, reverent mood that balances cold vastness with communal warmth.

name: Nostalgiacore
description: Nostalgiacore is a late-2010s/early-2020s internet aesthetic of remembered 1990s–2000s childhood, rendered as faded amateur digicam snapshots and hazy video stills: empty playgrounds and classrooms, childhood bedrooms, glowing CRT TVs, beige family computers, inflatable pools and molded-plastic play equipment. Its palette is washed-out warm vintage or flash-flattened pastel with primary-color plastic accents, veiled in grain, soft blur and orange LCD date stamps, often captioned with a melancholic lowercase line of longing. Recognize it by the triple lock of childhood liminal space, obsolete consumer tech, and memory-degraded photography — bittersweet and tender, never surreal, horror-tinged or crisp.

name: Noucentisme
description: Noucentisme is the Catalan classicist movement of c. 1906–1923, recognizable by matte ochre-cream-soft-blue palettes, axially balanced compositions built from columns, arches, balustrades and rose garlands, and serene Mediterranean landscapes, pastoral nudes and sculpturally calm portraits. Its visual DNA is "Mediterraneanism": diffuse southern daylight, earthy low-chroma colour, and a Greco-Roman and Renaissance vernacular fused with early-twentieth-century civic order, appearing in oil painting, gouache, lithographic posters and stucco-and-stone architecture. Load this skill when an image shows restrained classical order, warm earth tones and a quiet civic or pastoral mood, rather than Art Nouveau flourish or Art Deco glamour.

name: Nouveau_Réalisme
description: French avant-garde of 1960–1970 (Restany, Klein, Arman, Villeglé, Rotella, César, Tinguely, Spoerri, Raysse) that appropriates consumer reality directly instead of depicting it: lacerated street-poster stratigraphy (décollage) with fragmented advertising type and halftone cinema faces, accumulations and compressions of identical manufactured objects, fixed meal remains, kinetic scrap machines, plastic assemblages, and deep ultramarine International Klein Blue monochromes. Palette swings between weathered cream paper grounds shredded with vermilion, cobalt, cadmium yellow and magenta printer's ink, matte raw-pigment blue, pastel plastic consumer colors, and neutral white-cube documentation light. Recognize it by physical indexical traces — torn paper fibers, crushed metal, glued layers, halftone dots, serial repetition — presented deadpan, never painted illusion.

name: Nu-Goth
description: Nu-Goth is the sleek 2010s Tumblr-and-Instagram evolution of Goth: strictly monochrome black-white-grey streetwear-minimalist outfits carrying flat white occult screen-prints (pentagrams, triangles, moons, inverted crosses, Ouija lettering), silver moon-and-pentagram jewelry, wide-brim hats, round sunglasses, strap harnesses and platform boots. Recognize it by deadpan pale faces with black lipstick, hime-cut bobs or silver-lilac dyed hair, leather biker jackets over maxi skirts and ripped tights, and flat, desaturated lookbook, mirror-selfie or digital-illustration framing. It reads as fashion-forward minimalism with an occult graphic language — streamlined and internet-native, never theatrical vintage Goth.

name: Nu-Metal
description: Nu-Metal is the visual language of mid-1990s to early-2000s American alternative metal: baggy JNCO-width denim, oversized band hoodies and basketball jerseys, wallet chains, spiky hair, dreadlocks and facial piercings, set against rusted industrial decay, cinderblock walls and warehouse voids. Its palette is black, concrete grey and photocopy bone sickened by a single video-grade cast — piss-yellow, acid green or cold cyan — with VHS grain, lomo blur, fish-eye distortion, strobe freezes and halftone poster cutouts. Recognize it by the hybrid of hip-hop streetwear volume and metal aggression, scribbled or stenciled band logos, and aggro-cool suburban angst.

name: Nu-Punk
description: Nu-Punk (aka Chicago Punk) is the low-fashion visual language of late-1990s and early-2000s American punk — thrift-store denim, black skinny jeans, studded belts, cut-off band tees and muted beanies, photographed in grainy desaturated or sepia monochrome against decaying rust-belt city backdrops. Signature elements include punk-show crowd communion, flat screen-printed gig posters and marker-scrawl DIY logos, parodied civic sports badges, and a single deep blood red as the only saturated accent. Subjects are working-class bands, crowds and punk houses just getting through the day: personal struggle and communal good times, never political spectacle or glam bombast.

name: Nyashka
description: Nyashka (Няшка, drain-nyashka) is a 2020s Russian–Ukrainian alt aesthetic built on a porcelain-white doll face — black scleral or enlarging circle lenses, heavy outward-winged eyeliner, thin flat horizontal brows, deep burgundy or black lips — set against oversized black Drain streetwear (hoodies, Adidas tracksuits, wide-leg trousers) in lo-fi vertical phone selfies. Its signature is the tension between kawaii cuteness (blunt-fringed straight hair, lace trim, bows, pink sticker accents, silver cross chains) and bleak post-Soviet mundanity (panel-block stairwells, underpasses, night streets, cluttered bedrooms). Recognize it by the blank unblinking stare, matte white base, and doll makeup over mundane sportswear; separate it from E-Girl, Jirai Kei and Dead Inside by the paler base, flatter brows and Slavic street context.

name: Nymphet
description: Nymphet (also Vintage Americana Coquette, American Lolita, Lolitacore) is a Tumblr-era (c. 2012–2014) aesthetic descended from Nabokov's Lolita and its 1962/1997 film adaptations: cherry red, cream, baby pink and baby blue rendered in faded 35mm or Polaroid film, pairing schoolgirl innocence (lace ankle socks, gingham, milkmaid braids, teddy bears, lollipops) with grown-up flirtation (glossy red lips, bralettes, thigh-highs, flash-lit confidence). Recognize it by heart-shaped sunglasses, red lollipops and cherries, saddle shoes and Mary Janes, 1950s–70s Americana settings (motels, diners, suburbia, grassy yards), bedroom shrine corners of paper ephemera, and a bittersweet, nostalgic mood held inside sun-bleached, pink-cast analog texture.

name: Ocean_Grunge
description: Ocean Grunge is a music-centric internet aesthetic from circa 2014 that reads as Seapunk's depressive twin: open ocean, deep-sea fauna and drowned classical statuary rendered in blacks, greys and muted blues, pierced only by bioluminescent or glitch intrusions of mint, magenta or sickly yellow. Signature elements include murky underwater light, foam and basalt, oil-rig and submarine industrialism, datamosh smears and compression corruption, mirrored symmetry and corrupted glyph typography, all carrying nihilism, emptiness and drowning dread. Load this skill when sea or deep-water imagery feels cold, drained, degraded and hopeless rather than vibrant, tropical or heritage-nautical.

name: Oceanpunk
description: Oceanpunk is the speculative aesthetic of sea-borne technology — wooden-and-brass ships, lashed-together flotilla cities, stilt harbors, submarines and underwater habitats built to explore, colonise and traverse the ocean, often in a post-apocalyptic world. Its palette is aqueous teal and sea-green over hull grey and weathered wood, warmed by bronze, brass and pinpoint lamp amber, rendered in painterly concept-art washes or clean ink-lined cel color. Signature subjects are stacked ship-cities, salvaged vessels, pirates and sailors, and anachronistic machinery that mixes Victorian, modern and sci-fi technology on one salt-worn hull.

name: Office_Siren
description: Office Siren (aka Bayonettacore, Corporate Girlie) is a 2020s TikTok-born microtrend that restyles 1990s–2000s corporate fashion as sensual role-play: narrow rectangular "Bayonetta" glasses, form-fitting tailoring (pencil skirts, fitted button-downs, tight knits), stilettos and sleek buns, in a strictly muted palette of grey, black, cream and sandy brown with occasional oxblood-red or leopard accents. Recognize it by flash-lit candid or clean editorial framing, office-coded settings and props, and a cool, competent, knowingly alluring mood.

name: Oi!_Skinhead
description: Oi! Skinhead (Second Wave / Street Punk Skin, UK late 1970s–80s, globally revived from the 2010s) is a working-class street aesthetic built on shaven heads, olive-drab nylon MA-1 bomber jackets, bleached "snowflake" drainpipe jeans cuffed over polished 10-to-20-hole oxblood or black Dr. Martens, and thin scarlet braces slung over Fred Perry-style polos or band-logo T-shirts. Its palette is oxblood, black, bleached denim white-on-indigo and olive drab, punctured by red tartan and vinyl accents, shot in flat overcast snapshot light against brick, concrete, council-estate yards and terrace steps. Recognize it by the utilitarian workwear-plus-military silhouette, the cuffed hem that always exposes the boot shaft, and arms-around-shoulders gang solidarity poses.

name: Oktoberfest
description: Oktoberfest (d'Wiesn) is the Bavarian folk-festival aesthetic: blue-and-white lozenge checks, beer-gold Maßkrugs with foam crowns, pretzel-crust and gingerbread browns, and Tracht costume (Lederhosen, Dirndl, Tyrolean hats) staged on rustic wood, in marching parades, or under night fairground lights. Born from the 1810 Munich royal wedding and celebrated each autumn, it prizes convivial abundance, brass music and Bavarian folk pride. Recognize it by checkered ribbons and napkins, icing-script gingerbread hearts, wheat and hops, brass bands, beer tents and Ferris-wheel skylines.

name: Old_Hollywood
description: Old Hollywood is the glamour of the American studio system's Golden Age (c. 1930s–1960s): silver-gelatin monochrome or saturated Technicolor, diffused glamour lighting with halation blooming around the face, finger-waved hair, bias-cut gowns, fur stoles, opera gloves and tuxedos. Signature objects include velvet stage curtains, glittering marquees, film reels, studio cameras, rotary phones, cigarette smoke caught in a spotlight, and art deco interiors. The mood is elegant, nostalgic and faintly melancholic — manufactured stardom at its most polished.

name: Old_Money
description: Old Money is the visual language of inherited wealth — understated, tailored elegance in a muted palette of cream, beige, camel, navy, black and dusty pastels, staged among estates, wood-paneled rooms, country clubs, courts and equestrian grounds. Signature elements include navy blazers, tweed skirt-and-jacket sets, turtlenecks, pearls, logo-less leather bags, wide-brim hats, antique cars, horses, ancestor portraits and fresh flowers, rendered with film-grain daylight or dim tungsten formality. Recognize it by discretion: wealth signaled through cut, patina and lineage rather than logos, with an emotional reserve that runs from serene leisure to melancholy drama.

name: Old_Web
description: Old Web (Web 1.0 / GeoCities aesthetic) is the amateur-homepage and desktop-interface look of the 1990s–early 2000s web: web-safe primaries and neon text on tiled starfield or teal grounds, beveled gray Windows chrome with blue title bars, 88×31 badge strips, glitter GIFs, rainbow bevel-emboss word art, underlined blue hyperlinks, visitor counters and "under construction" banners inside rigid table layouts. Recognize it by mismatched-resolution elements (pixel art, compressed JPEGs, clip art, system fonts) assembled with sincere maximalism rather than designed harmony. Use for personal homepage shrines, period desktop screenshots, badge walls, media-player windows, and dial-up-era interface artifacts.

name: Olderbrothercore
description: Olderbrothercore is a 2020s nostalgia aesthetic that recreates the lived-in bedroom and entertainment center of a rebellious suburban teen boy of the late 1990s–mid 2000s, rendered like a lo-fi point-and-shoot snapshot with harsh direct flash. Its visual DNA is black plastic plus translucent lime/Xbox green, cluttered shelves of CDs, DVDs and game cases, CRT televisions, band and game posters, and energy-drink junk food, all framed by deliberate suburban averageness — drab carpet, plain wooden furniture, tangled cables. Recognize it by flash falloff into dark corners, branded green-black palette, physical-media clutter, and a relaxed, mischievous mood.

name: Onii_Kei
description: Onii Kei ("elder brother style") is a Japanese men's street fashion of the 1990s–2000s that fuses American casual, Italian casual and rocker influences into a slick, host-club-confident look: black leather jackets and sharp blazers over low-necked tanks, imported slim distressed jeans, pointed boots, and the teased "wolf hair" shag. Its palette is grounded in black and brown with washed denim blues, cream tees and tan chinos, punctuated by branded watches, luxury belts, statement sunglasses and subtle pendants. Recognize it by the slim vertical silhouette, groomed shaggy hair in chestnut/copper/ash-blonde tones, and sleek dark layering with a rock edge.

name: Opium
description: Opium (also Vamp, 00, Opiumcore) is a 2020s Atlanta-born fashion-and-music aesthetic built on monochromatic black avant-garde darkwear (Rick Owens, Balenciaga, Vetements), brutalist platform boots, wrap-around sunglasses and chrome cross jewelry, shot with harsh on-camera flash, thermal/infrared false color or deep-fried editing. Signature marks are inverted crosses, anarchy symbols, bats, "00" branding, spiky illegible black-metal typography and blood-red accents on stark black-and-white. Typical subjects are face-obscured figures in extreme-proportion silhouettes, nocturnal gothic architecture, red-hazed stages and occult poster graphics.

name: Org-Nouveau
description: Org-Nouveau (Organic-Nouveau) is a late-1980s-to-1990s organic-postmodern style of interiors, architecture and object design that revives Art Nouveau and Catalan Modernisme as melting plaster caves, whiplash ironwork and shell-, bone- and coral-derived forms. Recognize it by amber-ochre and peach plaster vaults against teal, plum and iridescent blue accents, nautilus-spiral chair backs, pod-cluster blobby furniture, gourd- and petal-shaped lanterns, mosaic-terrazzo blob floors, and warm cove or pinpoint "cave starlight" lighting. Typical subjects are restaurant, bar and club interiors, sculptural shell houses and storefront canopies, organic lamps, vessels and furniture objects.

name: Oshare_Kei
description: Oshare Kei is the bright, pop-leaning outlier of Japan's Visual Kei rock scene, coined around 2001 by the band BAROQUE: band costumes that fuse punk hardware (biker chains, studs, buckles, ripped skinny jeans) with Decora-like candy excess — hot pink, cobalt, lime and lemon yellow set against a black or white anchor, polka dots and animal print, striped or bow-tied knee socks, and towering teased hair in unnatural colors under tons of hairclips. Recognize it in group band promo shots with dramatic black eyeliner over otherwise light makeup, brightly colored contacts, piled-on bracelets and character bags, playful poses, and high-key white or saturated graphic pop backdrops. The mood is upbeat, kawaii-punk and defiantly cheerful.

name: Oshi_Culture
description: Oshi culture (wota / oshikatsu) is the Japanese idol-devotion aesthetic from the 2000s onward: pastel-pink maximalist shrines of merchandise — ita bags, deco uchiwa fans, cheki photo cards, chibi plushies — assembled around a single beloved idol, plus the concert ritual of glow sticks, happi coats and synchronized fan dance. Recognize it by repeated idol faces multiplied across badges, cards and cutouts, handmade ribbon-and-lace decoration, member-color coordination, ryousangata frilly pink event fashion, and night scenes pierced by penlight neon trails. Typical subjects range from flat-lay craft arrangements and shelf shrines to crowd shots from behind and light-trail wotagei dances.

name: Ostalgie
description: Ostalgie (GDR nostalgia / Eastalgia) is the post-1990 East German retrospective aesthetic built from the vernacular design of the DDR: Ampelmännchen traffic-light figures, Trabant cars, Dederon fabrics, Spreewald pickles and offset-printed Ostprodukt packaging with EVP price marks.
