Its visual DNA is faded pastel blues, browns, oranges and muted greens, mustard-patterned wallpaper, wood-veneer furniture, FDJ blue shirts, signal-red/green glow and bold German grotesque label typography. The mood is gemütlich, affectionate-ironic domestic nostalgia — consumer objects and lived-in rooms, never state-heroic propaganda.

name: Ouji
description: Ouji (the youthful branch of Japanese Boystyle) is a Victorian- and Rococo-inspired "prince" fashion of the late 1990s/early 2000s, built on knee-gathered knickerbockers (pumpkin pants), a fitted blouse–vest–jacket stack with jabots and lace, top hats or crowns, and knee- or mid-calf laced or platform boots over visible socks. Its palette runs from black and jewel tones (bordeaux, navy) through earthy Classic browns to pastel Sweet tints, rendered in silk, velvet, brocade and tartan prints with silver and antique-gold hardware. Androgynous, youthful and meticulously coordinated, it reads as the boyish sibling of Lolita rather than as historical reenactment or stage costume.

name: PC-98
description: PC-98 is the 1990s Japanese microcomputer game aesthetic of the NEC PC-9800 series: detailed anime pixel art at up to 640×400 on a quantized 16–256 color palette, with checkerboard dithering standing in for gradients, and game chrome such as thick decorative borders, kanji bitmap dialogue bands, portrait insets and custom menus. Recognize it by countable square pixels, teal-cyan machine interiors or magenta-pink romance sets, 90s anime faces with large glossy multi-highlight eyes, and a black bottom band of Japanese dialogue; typical subjects are visual-novel close-ups, cockpit and office interiors, schoolrooms and fantasy fields.

name: PC_Music
description: PC Music (the Hyperpop visual world) is the glossy, hyper-saturated digital aesthetic of the 2013 London label collective around A. G. Cook: hyper-real CGI product shots, corporate-advertisement parody, early-2000s web design clutter, and doll-like retouched pop personas, all anchored to #0000ff hyperlink blue, neon pink and lime, and holographic chrome silver. Signature elements are sterile seamless-backdrop product staging (drink cans, CDs, chrome icons), frozen liquid and metal material studies, mirror-symmetric vector emblems, and maximalist collage typography over saturated monochrome fields. Mood is ironic euphoria — consumerism celebrated and critiqued at once, perfection that advertises its own fakeness.

name: PEEPS
description: PEEPS (Gengarcore) is a late-2010s Ura-Harajuku street fashion that reads as sporty goth for ghost Pokémon trainers: mostly black casual sportswear electrified by neon purple, checker and zebra prints, tribal flame embroidery, chain belts and silver hardware, plus Gengar plush and 3D kanji graphics. Typical images are thrifted coord flat lays, wall-snap outfits with cut-out layered tops and chain-hung short bottoms, purple-duotone zine collages, and chibi character art on black voids. Recognize it by the black-plus-neon-purple casualness, sock-based sporty legs (never fishnets), and ghost-Pokémon playfulness fused with goth hardware.

name: PMC_Ryodan
description: PMC Ryodan is a 2020s Russian–Ukrainian teenage subculture aesthetic: crews of long-black-haired anime fans in oversized black hoodies screen-printed with a white twelve-legged spider and the number 4, grey-black checkered trousers and chunky sneakers, photographed deadpan in post-Soviet malls, park paths and overcast waterfronts, or rendered as flat black VK/Telegram meme graphics with white line-art spiders and handwritten Cyrillic. A near-monochrome black-and-white palette, faceless hair-curtain portraits, back-view crew lineups and an ironic "PMC" pseudo-military framing distinguish it from Dead Inside, E-Boy and the Adidas-clad gopnik/offnik rivals.

name: PRL_Nostalgia
description: PRL Nostalgia is the Polish post-1989 aesthetic of longing for the Polish People's Republic (1947–1989): concrete greys and muted pastels punctured by saturated communist-branding red, analog consumer artifacts (Polo-Cockta bottles, warm ice cream cones, Junak motorcycles, Syrena and Polonez cars), restored neon signs, cooperative signage and reconstructed period interiors such as Pijalnia bars and museum living rooms. Recognize it by Polish-language script logos and hand-painted shop lettering, veneer-bakelite-chrome materiality, overcast daylight or neon-against-night lighting, faded film grain, and a tender, kitschy mood that sanitizes the era into a "gentle past".

name: Pacific_Punk_Wave
description: Pacific Punk Wave is a late-1970s-to-1980s Los Angeles-born postmodern design mode fusing new wave album art, punk collage defiance, Italian radical design objects and sabotaged Swiss typography. Recognize it by horror-vacui cut-paper layering, airbrushed/stippled/striped fills instead of flat color, hot magenta–electric yellow–teal on cream (or neon airbrush on black), zigzag and starburst kitsch citations, leopard print, classical statue fragments, and hand-drawn lettering crashing over duotone photos. Typical subjects are gig posters, album covers, sculptural laminate furniture and eyewear assemblages, flash-lit postmodern interiors, and ghosted multiple-exposure portraits with spiky hair and heavy makeup.

name: Palewave
description: Palewave is a mid-2010s internet-born minimalist menswear aesthetic (Reddit r/streetwear, Tumblr, peak ~2015) defined by a strictly pale, washed-out palette — cream, sand, stone grey, light-wash denim, blush pink — worn in loose layered fits and anchored by minimal white leather sneakers. Recognize it in full-body street "fit pics" shot in flat overcast light against mundane urban backdrops, entirely free of black, logos and saturation. Use this skill to generate or identify quiet, comfort-first pale casual outfits and their documentary-style photography.

name: Paninaro
description: Paninaro is the flashy, brand-obsessed youth style of early-1980s Milan: glossy brightly coloured down puffer jackets, rolled Levi's 501s over thick white socks and wheat-nubuck Timberland boots, conspicuous designer badges, Ray-Ban sunglasses, and fast-food trays, small motorcycles and comic magazine mastheads in saturated primaries on yellow. Daylight 35mm snapshot or halftone newsprint rendering; consumerist, apolitical, playfully showy. Use when identifying or generating images of 1980s Italian label-driven teen sportswear culture, paninoteca hangouts, or Il Paninaro-style magazine graphics.

name: Paperback_Chic
description: Paperback Chic (also Chobanicore / Chobani Chic) is a late-2010s-to-present branding and packaging aesthetic that makes labels, book covers, posters and cafe graphics read like friendly artistic paperbacks: matte paper fields in cream, sage-mint, blush pink and peach, oversized retro serif or Didone display type set in one or two inks, airy open layouts, and simple flat or hand-drawn fruit, botanical and animal marks. Recognize it on wellness drinks, organic food packs, swing tags and literary covers carrying soft matte color, generous whitespace and wholesome, playful nostalgia.

name: Parisian_Apaches
description: Belle Époque Parisian street-gang aesthetic (1890s–1914) as preserved in staged gelatin-silver photographs and sensationalist press lithographs: casquette caps, red flannel sashes and neck scarves, striped jerseys, flared Bénard trousers, surin knives and brass-knuckle Apache revolvers. Palette of worker red, blue and white over aged cream paper or sepia emulsion, with theatrical swagger, brawl diagonals and valse chaloupée dance poses. Use for Belle Époque underworld subjects, pulp crime poster art, or period street-gang portraiture.

name: Parisian_Girly
description: Parisian Girly is a late-2000s/early-2010s tween interior-and-fashion aesthetic built on a romanticized, cliché-loaded Paris: a strict pink-black-white palette, Eiffel Tower silhouettes, Breton stripes, poodles, fleurs-de-lis, mannequins and ornate mirrors, delivered with McBling-era glitter and bright commercial polish. Recognize it by bold pattern blocking (polka dots, zebra, stripes), cursive French phrases as decor, and sweet childlike glamour in bedrooms, party tableaus, desserts, garment flat-lays and vector shopping-girl illustrations.

name: Partille-Johnny
description: Partille-Johnny (PJ) is the late-2000s Swedish teen-boy snapshot aesthetic: gravity-defying hair-wax spikes or back-slicks, orange self-tanner skin set against pale white-coated lips, rubber bands stacked up the calves over pant hems, and hi-vis reflex vests thrown over logo tees and big-logo Evisu denim. Images read as flash-blown compact-camera uploads from Bilddagboken-era domestic interiors, bathroom mirror selfies and crammed group poses, radiating conformity, meticulous grooming and loud attention-seeking. Recognize it by the bronze-orange / stark-white / denim-blue triad with neon accents, low-megapixel flash blowouts, and packs of teenage boys groomed to an identical, deliberately artificial standard.

name: Party_Rock
description: Party Rock is the maximalist club-kid aesthetic of LMFAO's late-2000s/early-2010s "club boom": neon pink, electric blue and highlighter-yellow spandex clashed against zebra and leopard print, shutter shades or lensless nerd glasses, cardboard robot heads, gold rope chains and confetti-choked house parties. It is shot in harsh point-and-shoot flash or saturated club LED light, full of grinning, mid-shuffle subjects performing aggressive, ironic joy. Recognize it when an image reads as a deliberately tacky, costumed 2010s party rather than cool, composed or angsty youth culture.

name: Pastel_Gore
description: Pastel Gore is a late-2010s internet-art aesthetic that paints explicit gore — exposed organs, bones, stitches, dripping blood, dismemberment — in soft pastel color and cartoonish kawaii stylization, frequently substituting candy, slime, sprinkles or fruit flesh for bodily matter. Recognize it by pink/lavender/baby-blue blood, rainbow-soft innards, disembodied eyeballs with heart- or star-shaped pupils, bows paired with knives, flat cel-shaded digital illustration, and sticker-sheet, OC-portrait or all-over-pattern formats born in Tumblr/DeviantArt fandom circles.

name: Pastel_Goth
description: Pastel Goth (a.k.a. Kawaii Goth, Spooky Kawaii) is an early-2010s Tumblr-born fashion and graphic aesthetic that welds goth iconography — inverted crosses, bats, eyeballs, bones, pentagrams, dripping fonts — onto milky pastel pink, lavender, mint and baby blue, anchored by black hardware like studded collars, fishnets and platform boots. Recognize it by constant double-coding: macabre symbols rendered in candy colors, high-key or flash-flat washed lighting with sparkle and gradient-filter overlays, and creepy-cute chibi, pixel or meme-edit graphics. Typical subjects are outfit coord shots, makeup and dip-dye hair close-ups, accessory flat lays, and pastel cloud-sky edit backgrounds.

name: Pastel_Southwestern
description: Pastel Southwestern is a late-1980s to early-1990s American design aesthetic that bleaches classic desert-Southwest motifs into a serene palette of pale turquoise, clay pink, apricot, sage green and sand, accented with light lilac and light pink. Recognize it by stucco and adobe volumes with rounded edges and arched niches, stepped geometric bands derived from Indigenous-peoples art, saguaro cactus silhouettes, banded desert-horizon murals, plush pastel upholstery and bleached oak, appearing in homes, fast-food and hotel interiors, pueblo-style chain architecture and product packaging. The mood is breezy, sun-washed and sincerely kitschy, defined by its rejection of the dark rust tones and heavy iron of rustic Santa Fe design.

name: Pastoral_Whimsy
description: Pastoral Whimsy is a storybook-rural aesthetic descended from 19th-century children's book illustration and idealized farm life, rendered in cream, beige, pale yellow, soft blue, mint and sage green with hand-drawn pen linework and soft watercolor washes. Its signature subjects are farm and woodland animals (ducks, fluffy sheep, rabbits, deer, hedgehogs), often gently clothed or anthropomorphized, plus ditsy floral prints, cottages, cottage gardens, rolling hills, still ponds, aprons, flowy linen dresses, straw hats and tea in mismatched mugs. Recognize it by its low-chroma pastel palette on paper-white or beige grounds, visible handmade mark (ink hatch, watercolor bloom, printed cotton weave), diffuse shadowless light, and a playful, serene, nostalgic mood that favors storybook fantasy over strict realism.

name: Paty_de_SP
description: Brazilian teen-girl mirror-selfie aesthetic born on São Paulo TikTok in the early 2020s out of the 1990s–2000s "patricinha" rich-girl slang: black leather, sequins and satin shine anchored by white, silver and light-wash denim, punctured by candy-pink or neon accents. Signature elements are vertical phone mirror selfies in bedrooms, closets and shopping malls, crop tops paired with mini skirts or high-waisted denim, silver trinket jewelry, long decorated nails and chunky sneakers (Nike Air Force, Air Jordan, V10). Elegance-aspiration with a funk/trap undercurrent.

name: Peach_Girl
description: Peach Girl (aka Peachy Beachy) is a summer-2024 TikTok beauty-and-fashion microtrend, popularized by Hailey Bieber, built on a warm sun-kissed glow in peach, coral, apricot and cream with dewy skin, glossy "juicy" lips, generous peachy blush and simple casual clothing. Recognize it by high-key soft lighting, peach fruit appearing as print, intarsia knit, sticker or flavored snack-and-cosmetic prop, and an effortless, fresh, youthful warmth. It sits between Soft Girl's cool pastels and Tomato Girl's savory reds, and drops Coquette's bows and lace for relaxed everyday staples.

name: Peacock_Revolution
description: Mid-1960s Swinging London menswear rebellion in which slim, Edwardian-cut suits of paisley, brocade, corduroy and velvet, frilly shirts, cravats, kipper ties, Nehru collars and winklepicker boots were worn by mop-haired young men in clashing jewel-and-candy colours. Typical subjects are British Invasion band group portraits, Carnaby Street street snaps and boutique interiors, captured on warm, slightly faded analogue film. Recognise it by tailored silhouettes loaded with feminine-coded print, frill and embroidery — dandyish and urban, never hippie-loose.

name: Pearlcore
description: Pearlcore is an early-2020s fashion, beauty and decor aesthetic that makes pearls the protagonist — single strands, chain-layered necklaces, pavé-encrusted garments and accessories, and tiny scatter-beads on faces and nails — set in a luminous palette of white, cream, blush and iridescent nacre sheen. Soft diffuse lighting, satin and lace textures, shell and porcelain props, and deliberately gender-neutral styling modernize the gem away from its formal heritage codes. Recognize it by pinpoint specular highlights on rounded beads, draped pearl lines across skin or fabric, and still lifes staged on cream satin, warm beige studio backdrops or blush walls.

name: Pen_&_Pixel
description: Pen & Pixel (aka Bling Era Graphics, Dirty South Style, No Limit Style) is the maximalist Southern hip-hop album-cover design language of the mid-1990s to early 2000s: diamond- and gold-encrusted 3D logotypes acting as the compositional hero, hard-edged Photoshop cutout collages of rappers surrounded by luxury cars, mansions, jets, exotic animals and explosions, all drenched in lens flares and starburst sparkles over saturated jewel-tone skies. Recognize it by bevelled metallic type treated as jewelry, ignored scale and physics, sticker-banner packaging furniture, and a "hood rich" surreal abundance in gold, chrome silver, diamond blue and fire orange.

name: Peoplehood
description: Peoplehood (Tumblr, c. 2021) is a slice-of-life aesthetic of ordinary mutual care — hands braiding hair, shared soup ladled from one pot, a forehead kiss on a bus, an elderly couple crossing a street with a bouquet. Its palette is beige wool, olive green and tangerine orange, rendered either as grainy 35mm candid snapshots or flat Fauvist gouache illustration. Recognize it by gesture-led composition, communal food, apartment windows, and bustling, multi-ethnic public space treated with reverence.

name: Phonk
description: OG Phonk (Rare Phonk) is the early-2010s SoundCloud hip-hop aesthetic of the Memphis-rap revival: purple/magenta "lean"-tinted imagery run through bootleg VHS degradation (grain, tracking tears, camcorder OSD), chrome Pen & Pixel-style bling lettering, gothic and dripping horror fonts, skull and grim-reaper iconography, parked 1990s luxury sedans, cassette-bootleg layouts and Parental Advisory stickers. Recognize it by violet-black grounds, degraded flash photography or foggy "cloudy" haze, collage cutouts and faux-vintage tape dating; it is deliberately slow, murky and nostalgic, unlike drift phonk's racing cars or cyber ghetto's Y2K gloss.

name: Photo_Playground
description: Photo Playground is the mixed-media children's-screen aesthetic of the Y2K era (roughly 1996–2015): photographic background plates and photo-puppeted animals collaged with flat Flash-era vector cutouts that wear obvious drop shadows. Bright grass green, sky blue and lavender purple dominate idyllic backyards, parks, farms and cozy cluttered rooms, lit by even midday sun or warm window light. Recognize it by the legible seam between real photo texture (fur, leaves, gingham, wood grain) and obvious cartoon shape, and by its quiet, liminal, comfort-first staging of play.

name: Photorealism
description: American painting mode of the late 1960s–1970s (also Super-Realism, Hyperrealism, Sharp-Focus Realism) that hand-reproduces a photograph with invisible brushwork, razor-sharp focus and documentary color fidelity. Palette is dictated by the source photograph, spanning saturated candy-and-chrome commercial color, muted diner and street tones, and full grayscale; subjects are mundane American life — reflective storefronts, cars and chrome, diners, signage, everyday still lifes, deadpan portraits and worker figures. Recognize it by mirror/glass reflections, specular highlights on glossy curves, snapshot cropping, even diffuse light, and a smooth airbrushed surface with no painterly hand.

name: Pianocore
description: Pianocore is a monochrome, music-notation aesthetic rooted in 2000s Japanese Lolita fashion with 1990s Moschino precursors, defined by the literal application of piano keyboards and sheet music as surface pattern on clothing, accessories and graphic edits. Look for piano-key hem borders, music-note tights, flowing staves and treble-clef charms in black, white, cream and sepia, framed by lace, bows and Mary Janes. Recognize it by high-contrast notation-as-decoration on hyper-feminine coordinates, accessory flat-lays and scrapbook-style digital collages — never by instruments alone as props.

name: Picniccore
description: Picniccore (alias Picnic Jamcore) is a pastoral internet aesthetic of outdoor meals and home preserves — gingham blankets, woven baskets, glass jam jars, strawberries and cherries, thumbprint cookies and lattice pies. Its palette anchors saturated berry reds on blush-pink, cream, butter-yellow and sage-green grounds, lit by bright warm daylight with crisp summer shadows. Typical subjects are preserve still-lifes, picnic spreads on grass, and puffy-sleeved strawberry-print dresses or frilled aprons.

name: Pijo
description: Spanish upper-class youth aesthetic from the 1970s onward — polished, preppy-adjacent leisurewear (piqué polos, wool sweaters knotted over the shoulders, striped shirts, loafers, silk scarves, gold jewelry) in a palette of beige-white-navy neutrals, pastels, and saturated pops including Spanish flag red and yellow. Typical images show groomed young people, alone or in arms-over-shoulders groups, in marinas, club terraces, brick plazas, or glossy color-block studio sets, radiating cheerful smugness and conspicuous consumption. Recognize it by pressed, gel-set grooming, brand-legible status cues, and clean advertising-grade brightness rather than heritage restraint.

name: Pin-up
description: Mid-20th-century American glamour aesthetic of mass-printed "cheesecake" (and "beefcake") images: a single coiffed model — victory rolls or Bettie bangs, sharp winged eyeliner, hunter's-bow red lipstick — posed playfully against a seamless studio backdrop, an airbrushed painted gradient, or a poster layout. Palette runs red, black, white, navy and pastels across silver-gelatin monochrome, sepia, hand-tinted prints and gouache illustration; signature motifs include high-waisted shorts, polka-dots, cherries, leopard print, stockings, garter belts, corsets and sailor styling. Mood is wink-and-nudge confidence: wholesome yet alluring, nostalgic, empowering.

name: Pink_Parisian
description: Pink Parisian (also Vintage Parisian) is a Tumblr-curated nostalgic aesthetic of mid-twentieth-century Paris and Old Hollywood: blush pink, cream, muted gold and silver-gelatin black-and-white laid over Belle Époque façades, Rococo salons and café terraces. Signature elements include faceted French perfume bottles on vanity trays, macarons and champagne, roses and peonies, 1930s–1960s lace-tweed-satin fashion, handwritten love notes, bows on poodles, and soft-focus couples in love. Recognize it by faded vintage-film color or grainy monochrome, heritage-maison luxury treated as longing rather than flex, and a wistful, hyperfeminine, escapist romance.

name: Pink_Pilates_Princess
description: Pink Pilates Princess is an early-2020s wellness-feminine aesthetic of hyper-feminine athleisure in blush, ballet pink and cream — ribbed knits, seamless leggings, leg warmers, plush oversized pullovers, silky pink pyjamas — shot as mirror selfies, paparazzi errand candids and soft sheer-curtain studio light. Signature props are the rolled pink yoga mat, an iced drink or matcha in a clear cup, a bow spa headband with face mask, wired earphones, pink tumbler and duffel bag. It reads as model-off-duty self-care ritual: pilates and barre stretches, skincare in bed, tidy pink-and-white interiors.

name: Pink_Princess
description: Pink Princess (also called Rocococore or Modern Rococo) is a luxury-feminine aesthetic fusing 18th-century Rococo ornament with 1950s–60s French-chic vintage: a pink-white-gold palette of blush satin, cream lace and gilt brass, populated by hair bows, white Persian cats, swans, ballerinas, pearls, macarons and pink-frosted cake in canopy-bed bedrooms and clawfoot-tub bathrooms. Its subjects are pampered upper-class leisure — tea parties, petal baths, vanity rituals, ballet, rose-strewn picnics — rendered in soft diffused light with a filmic pastel grade. Recognize it by pink-dominant color, ornate groomed staging and dollhouse tidiness rather than castle regalia.

name: Pirate
description: Pirate (Piratecore, Piratewave) is the seafaring-raider aesthetic of the 16th–18th century Golden Age of Piracy filtered through a modern collector's boho lens: sea-green and turquoise water, weathered brown timber, ivory linen and antique gold, populated by ships, treasure trinkets, shells, bones, charts and flintlock steel. Typical subjects are cabinet-of-curiosity shelves and labelled specimen jars, corseted boho-layered fashion on coastal cliffs and dunes, aged ink sketches and star charts, and painterly maritime vistas under storm or grotto light. Recognize it by weathered, thrifted material culture plus curiosity-cabinet display logic and a mood of curious freedom — distinct from crisp Nautical, horror-tinged Dark Nautical, and land-bound Adventurecore.

name: Pissikset
description: Pissikset (pissis) is the Finnish teen-girl subculture of the late 1990s–early 2010s, the Nordic branch of Mcbling: low-rise jeans and tight branded tops, short denim skirts, furry boots and fur-trimmed jackets, animal-print accents, sequins and patent vinyl in a candy palette of pink, baby blue, mint, lilac, white and black over orange-tanned skin. Signature cues are bleached or straightened blonde hair, heavy makeup with pale lips, sunglasses worn indoors, maximalist status accessories (hoop earrings, bangle stacks, logo handbags), visible thong straps above the waistband, and mall or city-center snapshot-flash photography, often finished with Y2K collage graphics and cursive logotypes. The mood is loud, defiant, glossy and self-awarely satirical — glamour assembled on a teen budget and worn as group identity.

name: Pixel_UI
description: Pixel UI is the pixelated interface aesthetic of 1980s-to-early-2000s graphical operating systems and application software — Classic Mac OS, Windows 3.x/9x/NT, AmigaOS, OS/2 and DOS shells — built from unaliased bitmap type, sprite-like icons, bevelled grey/teal/blue windows, dither patterns and cascading dialogs. Recognize it by hard single-pixel outlines, inverted menu-highlight bars, hard offset drop shadows, strictly budgeted palettes and the grammar of title bars, menus and forms; it is the work-and-software counterpart to the gaming-focused 8-Bit aesthetic.

name: Pixelscape
description: Pixelscape is the mid-2000s browser-game aesthetic of elaborate isometric pixel art — candy-saturated dioramas of busy streets, cutaway rooms and everyday social life, populated by chunky simplified avatars and often trimmed with brand marks or chat-bubble UI. Recognize it by a fine, uniform pixel grid, 2:1 dimetric projection, flat per-plane shading, dense prop clutter, and a high-saturation palette set against flat color fields or a dark void. It descends from Habbo Hotel-era advergames, Java mobile titles and pixel-based web design.

name: Pițipoancă
description: Late-2000s Romanian subculture aesthetic of hyper-feminine, McBling-derived glamour: orange spray tan, bleached blonde extensions, heavy 2000s "bad" makeup, rhinestone-studded corset tops, animal prints and hot-pink bodycon minis on very high platform heels. Typically captured in amateur direct-flash snapshots inside clubs, boutiques and domestic rooms with satin curtains and glossy white interiors. Mood is boastful, unapologetic confidence and status display.

name: Plaguecore
description: Plaguecore is a late-2010s Tumblr-born aesthetic built on the 17th-century plague doctor persona: beaked bird masks, wide-brim hats, long shapeless cloaks, and antiquarian medical paraphernalia (syringes, forceps, corked vials, leech jars, leather-bound books) rendered in black, grey, bone white, silver and brass. Its images favor candlelit or overcast low-key light, aged paper and woodcut inserts, corvids, rats and dry macabre humor, expressing scholarly curiosity rather than horror gore.

name: Plakatstil
description: Plakatstil (Sachplakat, the German "object poster", c. 1905–1920s) reduces an advertisement to a single isolated product or simplified figure drawn in flat lithographic colour planes against an unmodulated field, paired only with a bold, integrated brand name. Its palette is two to four high-contrast hues — vermilion red, deep teal-blue, olive-mustard, ink black, warm paper cream — with crisp hand-drawn silhouettes, matte print grain and generous negative space. Recognise it by what is absent: no ornament, no scenery, no slogan, and no modelling beyond a step or two of flat tone.

name: Plant_Mom
description: Plant Mom (Plant Parent) is a mid-2010s Instagram/Pinterest lifestyle aesthetic of domestic houseplant cultivation: interiors packed with clustered potted greenery — Monstera, fiddle leaf fig, snake plant, succulents, cacti — in terracotta, white ceramic, macramé and glass propagation vessels, lit by warm bright indirect window light. Its palette is verdant green plus earth tones, soft white, terracotta and mustard yellow, rendered either as casual phone snapshots of care rituals (watering, misting, propagating) or as Pinterest-style cut-out collages with affectionate lowercase captions and indie/hipster gardening fashion. Look for biological maximalism, nurturing props (watering cans, misting bottles, roots in water jars) and a cozy, mindful, gently humorous mood.

name: Playboy
description: Mid-20th-century jet-set aesthetic of the charismatic hedonist — tailored dark suits and tuxedos, expensive watches and gold accents, staged beside sports cars, yachts, private jets and casino tables. Palette of black, navy and crisp shirt-white with gold or silver accents, lit by night neon bokeh, blue-hour maritime light, or tungsten casino glow. Recognize it by leisure-as-identity: wealth displayed through poise, machines and companions rather than logos, with an undercurrent of charm, seduction and optional menace.

name: Plazacore
description: Plazacore is an early-2020s TikTok/Instagram fashion aesthetic that restyles Upper-East-Side preppy as a playful hotel-heiress fantasy: cropped tweed jacket-and-skirt sets, babydoll dresses with oversized Peter Pan collars, hair bows and padded headbands, pearl strands, tights and Mary Janes. Its palette oscillates between powder pink and baby blue pastels and black-white or grey houndstooth neutrals, punctuated by bright red or royal blue, and its settings are grand hotel interiors, gilded rooms and classical city façades. Recognize it by structured tweed plus deliberately childlike-girlish accessories executed with a polished, luxurious finish.

name: Pokemón
description: Chilean youth-subculture aesthetic (2006–c. 2012, aka HxCitos/Hardcoritos) fusing Emo, Otaku, Hip-Hop and Punk into black anime-shag "piña" haircuts with long side-swept bangs, black eyeliner, glitter, striped or polka-dot polos, skinny decayed jeans, Converse, stacked decora bracelets, and candy fuchsia/lime/purple/red accents over a black-and-white base. Visually it survives as mid-2000s Fotolog/MSN-era snapshots: low-megapixel sensor noise, harsh on-camera flash at night, blown-out flat daylight, pixel-font watermarks and meme overlays. Mood is extroverted melancholy — pacifist, playful, childlike fantasy posed in plazas, graffiti walls and club corners.

name: Political_'Wave'_Aesthetics
description: Umbrella term for internet propaganda aesthetics (Laborwave, Fashwave, NATOwave, Militarywave, Tradwave, Monarchowave, Anarchowave, Faragewave, Serbwave, Libertywave, Terrorwave) that re-skin 1980s–90s Vaporwave/Synthwave retrofuturism — neon perspective grids, sunset roundels, VHS grain, chromatic aberration, vertical Japanese captions, pixel-font slogan boxes — with explicit ideological emblems such as red stars, hammer and sickle, circled-A, NATO compass rose, national flags, religious icons or royal portraiture. Base layers are found media: archival photographs, news stills, classical busts, religious processions, combat footage or hardware photos, unified under a magenta/pink wash, a single-hue monochrome field, or a black-and-white duotone with red/green fringe. Recognize by the collision of overt political symbol-portraiture with degraded retro-digital kit and meme-grade slogan typography.

name: Polychrome
description: Polychrome is an early-2010s graphic-design aesthetic in which saturated color behaves as physical matter — powder bursts, ink-in-water clouds, smoke plumes, paint smears and oil-slick marbles — exploding across plain white or black studio grounds. Born in electronic-music cover art (Koan Sound's album of the same name) and consumer-tech advertising (Vaio, Bravia, Windows, Nintendo, Costco), it pairs high-contrast blue, red, orange, yellow and turquoise gradients with grayscale portraits, products or thin sans-serif logo lockups held in generous negative space. Recognize it by volumetric, particulate, studio-lit color events; never flat vector gradients, geometric pattern, neon grids or brushed metal.

name: Pomo_Faux_Ruins
description: Postmodern architectural and interior aesthetic of the late 1970s through 1990s built on intentionally fragmented classical motifs — columns truncated mid-air, cracked pediments, detached capitals, broken arches — rendered in pristine, hyper-sterile modern materials such as fiberglass, pastel-painted drywall, smooth concrete, chrome and neon tubing. The palette anchors on white, brown and black, punctured by saturated theatrical up-lighting, neon highlights and simulated open-sky ceilings rather than by pigmented surfaces. Typical subjects are mall courts, hotel and office atriums, cafe and nightclub interiors, plaza or lawn folly "ruins," and studio installations of plaster fragments posed as stage sets.

name: Pont-Aven_School
description: Synthetist–Cloisonnist manner of the late-1880s Breton artist colony around Gauguin and Émile Bernard: large flat planes of bold, non-naturalistic color — vermilion earth, apple-green meadows, chrome-yellow skies — sealed by strong dark outlines, with tilted ground planes, compressed depth and matte, enamel-like paint. Signature subjects are Breton peasant life: women in winged white coifs and black costumes at pardons, processions, dances and harvests, thatched cottages, water mills and church spires, plus moonlit folklore night scenes. Reads as solemn, devotional, deliberately "primitive" simplification rather than optical observation.

name: Poolcore
description: Poolcore is the 2010s liminal-space aesthetic of empty indoor poolrooms: still teal-to-blue water, grids of small white square ceramic tile, and caustic light-refraction patterns rippling across submerged surfaces. Photographs and 3D renders alike, it trades in eerie serenity — municipal pool halls, tiled corridors half given over to water, close-ups of sunlight netting on a pool bottom — with a palette of blues, teals and whites and a total absence of people. Recognize it by the invariant triad of contained water + tile grid + refracted light, held in a quiet, dream-familiar emptiness.

name: Pop_Art
description: Pop Art is the mid-1950s–1960s Anglo-American movement that recasts advertising, comic strips, product packaging and celebrity publicity as fine art: flat saturated primaries and secondaries, uniform black outlines, Ben-Day/halftone dot fields, silkscreen repetition and deadpan speech-balloon text. Recognize it by mechanical print mimicry (regular dots, misregistered passes, tape-crisp flat planes), consumer-goods and mass-media subjects, and an ironic, celebratory cool. Load this skill for images that must read as commercial-print-derived art of the 1950s–60s, not painterly, photoreal or surreal work.

name: Poppare
description: Poppare is the Swedish indie-pop subculture of the late 1990s to mid-2000s that restyles 1960s Mod through a melancholic Scandinavian lens — teased voluminous A-line bobs with blunt bangs, heavy black eyeliner with a star sticker under one eye, Peter Pan collar blouses, miniskirts, skinny trousers, opaque tights and Dr. Martens or Mary Janes. It runs in three registers: strict black-and-white "Panda" monochrome, candy-bright Decora-flavoured "Glitter" pastels with tiaras and hair clips, and navy-red Breton-stripe nautical "Håkan". Recognition hinges on lo-fi blog-era snapshot photography, pale androgynous subjects, Mod silhouette discipline, and a "looking good but feeling sad" wistfulness.

name: Poppers
description: Poppers (German "Die Popper," Austrian "Snobs") were a West German youth subculture of roughly 1979–1984, born in Hamburg high schools: affluent teenagers performing brand-fetishist preppy luxury as street style — cashmere V-necks and argyle, polo shirts with knitted ties, Fiorucci carrot pants, white jeans, tassel loafers over Burlington socks, trench coats, and the signature "Poppertolle" quiff with an asymmetrical fringe sweeping over one eye above a shaved nape. The visual DNA is muted cashmere solids (powder blue, cream, camel, oxblood) against black, white tapered trousers, visible designer logos worn as status, and a smug, posed, see-and-be-seen coolness staged in front of ice-cream parlors, café awnings, schoolyards, mopeds and disco entrances, captured either as faded warm-cast early-1980s color snapshots or grainy black-and-white press reportage.

name: Positivity_Kawaii
description: Positivity Kawaii (also Wellness Kawaii or Western Kawaii) is a 2010s Western marketing aesthetic built on pastel pink, mint, lavender and cream fields carrying chunky rounded or bubble-letter affirmations, puns, and simple blush-cheeked mascots — cats, unicorns, fruit slices, sushi, teacups, rainbows, smiling clouds — printed across stationery, mugs, socks, plushies and loungewear campaigns. Recognize it by high-key shadowless pastel backdrops, sticker-like sparkles and rainbow arcs, four-panel motivational comic grids, seamless fruit-character repeat patterns, and a wholesome, wellness-flavored wink. It is slogan-forward and commercially graphic, unlike Japanese Kawaii, and playful-modern rather than rustic-saccharine, unlike Live Laugh Love.

name: Post-Apocalyptic
description: Post-Apocalyptic depicts civilization after collapse: ruined city canyons, barren wastelands, looted interiors and reclaimed monuments rendered in earth tones, concrete greys and dull desaturated color under overcast or dust-charged skies. Its signature elements are weathered concrete, rust, dead or overgrown foliage, abandoned and modified vehicles, makeshift survival gear, and absent or tiny human figures; the mood is desolate, survivalist, melancholy. The visual language spans painterly concept-art matte paintings and desaturated documentary-style photography of places like Pripyat.

name: Post-Grunge_Maximalism
description: Post-Grunge Maximalism (Affliction-core, Ed Hardy-core, Rock Revival) is the mid-to-late-2000s fashion and graphic-design aesthetic of tattoo-flash heraldry — skulls, crosses, angel wings, eagles, daggers and blackletter script stacked into dense symmetrical crests on faded black, brown and bone-white tees and baggy premium denim, amplified by foil prints, rhinestones, embroidery and heavy distressing. Recognize it by ornate banner-ribbon crest logos, thick contrasting topstitching on jeans, metallic and splattered print textures, and harsh flash-lit night snapshots of wearers; the mood is hypermasculine rock-and-roll luxury from the MMA, nu-metal and nightclub scenes of the 2000s.

name: Post-Impressionism
description: Post-Impressionism (France, c. 1886–1905) is the umbrella term for the generation after Impressionism — Cézanne, Van Gogh, Gauguin, Seurat, Signac, Denis, Toulouse-Lautrec — that kept Impressionism's bright color and real-life subjects but rejected its fleeting optical snapshot in favor of structure, outline and symbolic meaning. Recognize it by visible constructive mark-making (pointillist dots, ridged comma-stroke impasto, parallel hatched patches, or flat cloisonnist color planes edged in dark contour), arbitrary symbolic color (red vision-fields, violet shadows, yellow flesh), flattened decorative space, and subjects of rural labor, ritual and religious vision, park and cabaret leisure, still life, portraiture and analyzed landscape.

name: Post-Punk
description: Post-Punk is the late-1970s UK/US aesthetic of austere monochrome minimalism — black and grey second-hand tailoring, trench coats, button-up shirts, slim trousers and Dr. Martens, captured in flat flash or overcast analog grain against brick, plaster and concrete. Its visual language fuses working-class "Eastern Bloc chic" deadpan with Bauhaus, Dada and German Expressionist geometry (Factory Records-style album art: stark line plots, diagrams, black fields). Recognize it by restrained androgynous silhouettes, a drab black-grey-sepia palette, anti-rockstar candor, and architectural linearity; a late theatrical variant adds black eyeliner, dark lipstick and teased hair as the bridge to Goth.

name: Poster_Gal
description: Poster Gal (a.k.a. Y2K Chibi, deviantARTcore) is the amateur fan-art and flash-photo aesthetic of US teen deviantART culture, c. 2002–2013: heavily stylized chibi figures hybridizing anime with Western cartoons — oversized heads, large feet, connected simplified fingers, fangs, exaggerated expressions — rendered with low-quality airbrush smudge shading, visible pixels and scanned-paper grain. Its palette runs black, Matrix terminal green, cobalt blue, marker red, grape purple and hot pink over paper white; its subjects are era fandoms (The Matrix, Lord of the Rings, InuYasha, Hetalia, pop-punk and nu-metal bands), self-made ID cards, and poster-plastered bedrooms shot with harsh on-camera flash. Recognize it by its constitutive datedness: pixelation, pencil-on-scan texture, handwritten dedications and green monospace captions, and an earnest angst-kawaii mood.

name: Poverty_Chic
description: Poverty Chic (Homeless Chic, Derelicte, Recession Dressing) is a luxury-fashion aesthetic of artificially destitute dressing — factory-distressed fabric torn to structural failure, mud and oil soiling, trash-bag and duct-tape improvisation, and oversized multi-layer silhouettes in mud brown, faded grey, olive drab and bone. Born from the 1990s commodification of grunge and pushed by Galliano's Dior, Vivienne Westwood and Demna's Balenciaga, it reads as deadpan irony: couture constructed to look scavenged, priced to look obscene. Recognize it by head-to-toe layered incongruity, deliberate filth on expensive garments, one recontextualized "trash" object, and theatrical-dim or flat-campaign lighting.

name: Power_Dressing
description: Power Dressing is the late-1970s-to-1980s corporate armor of wide padded shoulders, sharp double-breasted tailoring, pencil skirts and pleated trousers in navy, charcoal, black and grey pinstripe, punctuated by a single bold accent such as scarlet red. It reads like glossy 1980s print advertising — seamless studio backdrops or marble-and-checkerboard status interiors, assertive full-body poses, coiffed voluminous hair, statement gold jewelry, leather gloves and heels — projecting authority, ambition and workplace equality. Recognize it by the inverted-triangle silhouette: shoulders deliberately wider than hips, nipped or belted waist, severe polished grooming.

name: Prairiecore
description: Prairiecore is a 1970s-born pastoral aesthetic romanticizing American pioneer life on the grasslands — open prairie horizons, wheat and tall dry grass, horses and cattle behind wooden rail fences, and figures in calico prairie dresses, straw hats, bonnets and parasols. Its palette is light brown, sun-bleached cream and cool meadow green under pale sky blue, lit by hazy golden-hour or soft overcast daylight with a faded analog-film softness. Recognize it by horizontal grassland vistas with small homestead structures on the horizon, ruffled midi-length dresses, wind-moving grain fields, and a mood of free, hard-working, gently eccentric nostalgia.

name: Pre-Raphaelite
description: Victorian English painting style (from 1848) of jewel-toned color — cobalt, ruby, emerald against luminous ivory whites — rendered with botanical precision and crisp, shadowless light. Signature subjects are medieval and Arthurian narrative, biblical and mythological scenes, literary heroines, and idealized women with abundant flowing hair, pale skin and melancholic or languid gazes, set against pattern-saturated grounds of damask, tapestry, roses or river weeds. Reads as enamel-glazed oil paint, hard contours, concealed brushwork, and morally serious, emotionally charged staging.

name: Preacher's_Daughter
description: A 2020s Tumblr-born American aesthetic built from Ethel Cain's album visuals — the hushed domestic world of a Protestant preacher's teenage daughter, photographed like faded 1970s–2000s snapshots. Look for wood-paneled rooms, cream cable-knit sweaters and long skirts, crosses, Bibles and hymnbooks, stained glass, American flags and old pickup trucks, in a palette of wood brown, cream, ghost white and moss green, with a bleak-beautiful undercurrent of religious trauma beneath small-town respectability.

name: Precisionism
description: Precisionism is the American interwar painting mode (late 1910s to early 1930s) that renders factories, skyscrapers, bridges, water towers, silos and machine parts as immaculate, brushless geometric planes in muted grays, greiges and oxide reds. Its signatures are hard-edged simplified volumes, totally depopulated scenes, banded or wedge-cut skies, crisp flat cast shadows, and a cool desaturated palette punctuated by at most one accent family such as brick red or gold. Recognize it by matte flat planes, cylindrical industrial forms, absence of any human figure, and a silent, monumental, orderly mood.

name: Preppy
description: American Old Money leisure aesthetic born from Ivy League and preparatory-school dress codes (c. 1910s–1950s, Northeastern US): navy blazers with brass buttons, oxford button-downs, madras and khaki chinos, crested cable-knit sweaters, repp ties, boat shoes. Palette splits between New England naturals (navy, khaki, hunter green, burgundy, cream) and Southern Prep saturated contrasts (hot pink, kelly green, turquoise, bright yellow), bridged by pastel summer tones. Sunlit porches, sailboats, tennis courts, manicured lawns, nautical and collegiate motifs, monograms, golden retrievers; mood is cheerful, orderly, effortlessly inherited class.

name: Preschool_Pop
description: Preschool Pop is the late-1990s/early-2000s children's-media aesthetic of classroom mark-making — crayon and chalk hand-lettering, stick-figure and "tadpole" child drawings, oversized alphabet blocks, pencils, teddy bears and school gear set on paper-cream, chalkboard-black, or flat matte primary fields. Its palette anchors on matte red, blue and yellow with orange, green and purple accents, and its surfaces carry wax-crayon grain, felt, clay and paper tooth rather than gloss. Recognize it by wobbly hand-drawn outlines, suns/houses/trees, handprints, and child art applied at architectural scale as murals, banners and storefront supergraphics.

name: Pridecore
description: Pridecore is a late-2010s Tumblr aesthetic that recolors art, moodboards, pixel graphics and character edits into the exact stripe palettes of LGBTQ+ pride flags — bisexual magenta-purple-blue, transgender pastel blue-pink-white, pansexual pink-yellow-blue, aro/ace greens and greys, and niche custom flags. Its signature outputs are 3×3 moodboard and stimboard grids with a central color-swatch tile, glitter and sparkle overlays, neon signage in flag hues, symmetrical flat-lays of hue-matched objects, and fan-art recolors of characters' hair and clothing. Recognize it by a disciplined multi-hue flag palette applied transformatively to any subject, with a celebratory, identity-declarative mood.

name: Princecore
description: Princecore is a Royalcore micro-aesthetic of youthful, masculine-or-androgynous royalty — heirs, pages and ballet princes in poet shirts, cravats, capes and ceremonial armor, wearing delicate coronets rather than heavy state crowns. Its palette is light-first: ivory, duck-egg blue, gilt gold and silver, puncted by heraldic blue, crimson, violet and garden green, staged in gilded Rococo interiors, ornate arbor gardens and storybook castles. Recognize it by tailored court dress, quills and love letters, mirror-polished (never battle-worn) armor, and a courtly, boyish romanticism seated between Princesscore's gowns and Kingcore's sovereignty.

name: Princesscore
description: Princesscore is a late-2010s internet aesthetic, mainstreamed by Bridgerton, that romanticizes the princess fantasy through hyper-feminine, period-inspired dress: puff-sleeve and ball gowns, corsets, tulle, lace, tiaras, pearls and opera gloves in pastel pink, cream, white and gold. Recognize it by voluminous romantic silhouettes, opulent delicate fabrics catching candlelight or dappled garden light, courtly and fairy-tale settings (ballrooms, staircases, rose gardens, enchanted woods), and a soft, graceful, escapist mood.

name: Psychedelia
description: Psychedelia is the 1960s countercultural aesthetic of altered consciousness, born in the San Francisco and London rock-poster and album-cover scene. It recognizes itself through day-glo complementary color vibration, melting Art Nouveau line, hand-drawn illegible lettering, horror-vacui pattern density, and surreal cosmic iconography such as mandalas, zodiacs, wings and eyes. Typical subjects are concert posters, album sleeves, tie-dye and boldly printed fashion, light-show stages, and distorted or symmetrized portraits.

name: Psychobilly
description: Psychobilly is the visual culture of the early-1980s British punk–rockabilly fusion scene: towering quiffs and dyed mohawks, sleeveless leather vests and brothel creepers, 1950s pin-up silhouettes crossed with zombies, skeletons, coffin-shaped double basses and B-movie monsters, all delivered with a campy grin-over-gore wink. Its palette is black and bone white spiked with blood red, hot pink, poison green and electric purple, appearing in flash-lit club snapshots, studio pin-up portraits on flat saturated backdrops, and screen-printed gig posters. Recognize it by the three-way fusion of rockabilly tailoring, punk damage and tongue-in-cheek horror kitsch.

name: Pulp_Fantasy
description: Pulp Fantasy is the 1960s–70s science-fantasy cover-art aesthetic of oil-painted and airbrushed imagery: hyper-muscular heroes, sorceresses and monstrous foes beneath blood-red twin moons, monolithic citadels, primordial jungles and glowing caverns, all lit in dramatic chiaroscuro with lurid red-teal and orange-violet complements. It carries the physical print DNA of cheap pulp magazines, paperbacks, prog-rock album sleeves and cinema one-sheets — distressed bold display typography, sensational taglines, paper grain, smoky atmospheric depth. Recognize it by visceral action, primal mythic stakes and kitsch sincerity rather than by any single subject or framing.

name: Punk
description: Punk is the DIY anti-fashion and graphic language of mid-1970s New York and London: thrifted clothing aggressively modified with rips, safety pins, studs and hand-painted slogans, studded leather or denim battle jackets patched into wearable billboards, mohawks, tartan and combat boots, in a palette of black, worn denim/leather naturals and shock red. Its print branch is Xerox-degraded collage — ransom-note cut lettering, stencils, defaced official portraits and flags. Recognize it by visible handmade modification, confrontational snapshot photography, anarchy symbols, and a raw, anti-commercial mood.

name: Puppycore
description: Puppycore (also Wancore) is a kawaii aesthetic of photo-manipulated puppies and small pets rendered in hazy soft pastels — pink, baby blue, lavender, cream — with digital sparkles, cheek blush, ear bows, and paw/bone/heart motifs, descended from 2000s Japanese stationery and merchandise (San-X, Artlist) and the Heisei Retro nostalgia wave. Recognize it by high-key diffuse light, soft-focus bloom, die-cut photo collages and sticker-sheet layouts on gingham or candy-stripe grounds, bubble-letter or cursive-script pun typography, and printed halftone/scan artifacts. It is the pet-centric facet of Heisei Retro, adjacent to but distinct from Cutecore, Kawaii and Sanriocore.

name: Puppygirl
description: Puppygirl is a 2020s internet kemonomimi aesthetic in which a human subject wears dog signifiers — clip-on fluffy or floppy ears, tails, collars with bone tags, leashes, paw-print socks and mitts, kennels and dog beds — layered over an e-girl/alternative wardrobe of pastels, fishnets and oversized knits. It is staged at floor level in carpeted bedrooms and den-like domestic interiors, or rendered as soft anime illustration, in a palette of blush pink, lavender, cream and heather grey anchored by black or punched with turquoise and magenta, carrying a goofy, submissive ":3" playfulness. Recognize it by the combination of pet-play gear (dog ears + collar + paws/bones) with floor-level domestic staging; it is distinct from Neko (cat signs), Furry (full animal body), and plain E-Girl (no pet signifiers).

name: Purism
description: Purism (Paris, c. 1918–1925, Amédée Ozenfant and Le Corbusier) renders everyday objects — bottles, glasses, pipes, pitchers, guitars, machine parts — as purified, whole geometric types with clean contours, flat matte color and architectonic, stacked compositions. Its palette is subdued and earthy (ochre, brown, gray, olive green, bone white), occasionally anchored by a single saturated ground plane of oxide red or deep green; light is diffuse, modeling curved forms with smooth lathe-like gradations instead of cast shadows. Recognize it by its solemn, anonymous order: recognizable silhouettes, frontal shallow space, machine precision, and total rejection of ornament and expressive brushwork.

name: Qin_and_Han_Dynasties
description: Imperial Chinese aesthetic of 221 BCE–220 CE built on the cinnabar-red and lacquer-black palette of wuxing color symbolism, with spiraling yunqi cloud scrolls, the four Sishen direction-creatures, and liubo TLV square-in-circle geometry across lacquer, bronze, terracotta, silk brocade and pictorial brick. Typical subjects are burial goods (terracotta soldiers, painted silk banners, lacquer vessels), wadang eaves tiles, bronze mirrors, cross-collared shenyi robes in quju and zhiju cuts, and rank-ordered horse-and-chariot processions in flat narrative registers. Recognize it by coiled S-curve ornament filling circular medallions, central-axis symmetry, and matte clay, patinated bronze and glossy red-black lacquer surfaces.

name: Qingleng_Feng
description: Qingleng Feng ("clear-cold style") is the Chinese Wuxia/Xianxia aesthetic of aloof restraint: a solitary pale figure in matte snow-white or ice-blue hanfu — or minimalist modern commuter wear — framed by falling snow, morning mist, moonlit night or overcast rain. Its palette runs from snow white through silver grey and muted blue to anchoring ink black, with clean draping lines, high collars, plain jade or slim silver, and props such as the straight sword, guqin, scroll or oil-paper umbrella. The mood is calmness, detachment and otherworldly elegance — never warmth, coziness or romance.

name: Quality_Tumblr
description: Quality Tumblr is the circa-2012 Tumblr-dashboard aesthetic of hyper-filtered, brighter-than-life product and lifestyle photos made by and for teenage girls: a single mall-brand object (soda can, sphere lip balm, home-button iPhone, Polaroid, John Green paperback) held up to camera against a blurred bedroom, or laid flat on rumpled white sheets. Its palette is neon pastels — bubblegum pink, mint, lilac, baby blue pushed past real-life saturation or blown out to a milky high-key — anchored by pink and punctuated with black galaxy prints, wayfarer frames and dark room backgrounds. Square crops with thin white borders, faceless wrist-and-torso crops, stacked friendship bracelets, fairy-light bokeh and sincere consumer sweetness are its signature grammar.

name: Queencore
description: Queencore is the mature, reigning-monarch branch of Royalcore: jewel-toned regality of thrones, crowns, scepters, brocade ballgowns and palace interiors in dark reds, deep purples, royal blue, emerald, gold, silver and stark black-and-white. Its images carry state-portrait gravity — chiaroscuro candlelight, macro regalia detail, axial throne-room vistas, crowned silhouettes — expressing power, duty and elegance under burden rather than princess romance.

name: Queercore
description: Queercore (homocore / queerpunk) is the visual language of the queer punk subculture that emerged from mid-1980s Toronto zine culture: xerox-degraded black and white, newsprint off-white and hot pink as a political accent, with leather and the pink triangle as core motifs. Its signature artifacts are cut-and-paste photocopy zines, flash-blown snapshots of basement and community-hall shows, pride protest photographs, drag makeup, and bodies used as billboards with marker slogans. Recognize it by deliberate amateurism — photocopy grain, on-camera flash, crowd-pressed bodies, ransom-note typography — fused with explicit, sex-positive queer signage and an anti-respectability stance.

name: RGB_Gamer
description: RGB Gamer is the late-2010s/2020s aesthetic of the domestic gaming battlestation — matte-black or appliance-white desks, racing-style bucket chairs and tempered-glass PC towers saturated in addressable LED light, dominated by magenta, violet and cyan washes. Signature elements are rainbow case fans, per-key RGB keyboards, geometric light panels, neon wall signs and streaming gear, photographed at night in bedrooms and streamer corners. Recognize it by emissive neon acting as the room's only light source, sleek consumer gaming hardware, and purple-soaked walls.

name: Racaille
description: French banlieue street aesthetic of the 1990s–2000s, still lived today as "Lacoste TN" or "les gars de cité": black or navy tracksuits, Lacoste caps and bucket hats, Nike TN sneakers over pulled-up white socks, checkerboard or monogram crossbody bags, photographed in flash-lit cité courtyards, stairwells and concrete ledges. Recognize it by monochrome sportswear plus exactly one luxury accent, crew poses on housing-estate architecture, and lo-fi phone-snapshot grading with direct night flash. Distinct from MDLR's drill masks, 92i's glossy luxury-rap flex and Baddie's beige glam.

name: Racing
description: The Racing aesthetic (racecore, motorsports) is the visual culture of competitive automobile and motorcycle racing, from 1900s Grands Prix to the modern Formula 1 paddock: rosso-corsa red, black, optic white and metallic silver liveries stacked with sponsor logotypes, checkered flags, branded helmets and quilted Nomex race suits. Signature subjects are aerodynamic machines at speed, pit-lane and paddock glamour, and racewear worn as fashion, rendered in hard daylight or faded warm film. Load this skill for circuits, liveries, race gear, checkered motifs, or motorsport-derived editorial fashion.

name: Rad_Dog
description: Rad Dog (aka Neon Surf / Neon Surf Shack) is a late-1980s to early-1990s surf-skate commercial aesthetic built on hand-drawn tribal zigzag and confetti patterns, paint splatters and ooze blobs in lime, hot pink, electric blue and vibrant yellow stacked over black or cream grounds. Signature carriers are sun-faded caps, bold tees, sneakers, cassette and box-art covers, cartoon sharks and dogs, tiki-Hawaiian kitsch sunbursts, and scribbled multi-colour typography, occasionally extending into neon-lit mall retail interiors. Recognize it by the simultaneous chord of three-plus neons, wobbly ink line work, and all-over pattern density applied to youth-marketed product.

name: Radical_Design
description: Italian anti-design movement (1966–c.1972, Florence/Pistoia) of ironic, oversized soft-sculpture furniture — lip sofas, grass-blade seating fields, giant glove chairs, glowing wavy-edged mirrors — rendered in saturated jewel tones, vinyl gloss and plush fur against seamless studio grounds or theatrical colour-plane interiors. Recognise it by biomorphic polyurethane forms, pop-surreal scale shifts, clashing flat colour blocks, manifesto-style playfulness and utopian future-city speculation; it sits between Pop Art's print flatness and Memphis's laminate confetti but is softer, sculptural and politically ironic.

name: Raggare
description: Swedish working-class youth subculture aesthetic, born in the 1950s and still alive today, built around big V8 American cars (or black-painted Volvo stand-ins) used as social stages, greased pompadours, blue denim, leather vests and kitsch Confederate-flag Americana transplanted into Nordic small-town and midsummer settings. Core palette of chrome silver, denim indigo and leather/primer black, punctured by one loud accent — flame orange, magenta paint or flag red — over rust, dust and hand-painted club lettering. Recognizable in candid snapshot-style scenes of groups perched on cruising sedans, gravel-lot car meets, and patched club members posing with beer cans under pale Scandinavian light.

name: Rainforest_Chic
description: Rainforest Chic (the 90s Eco-Theme / Radical Nature) is a late-1980s-to-1990s consumer aesthetic of hyper-saturated, airbrushed jungle maximalism — misty waterfalls, split-level marine ecologies, neon macaws and morpho butterflies, carved-log typography and zigzag "global tribal" bands over midnight indigo, canopy green and sunset orange. Recognize it by its earnest save-the-rainforest didacticism, laminated gloss and wet, horror-vacui foliage density on posters, VHS boxes, product packaging, album art and themed retail interiors.

name: Rave
description: Rave is the lived aesthetic of electronic dance parties from the late 1980s onward — neon and fluorescent colour burning against black, fog-cut laser beams and strobes, baggy phat pants, bucket hats, round sunglasses, pacifiers, glowsticks and kandi beads, smiley-face acid house emblems and DIY info-line flyers. Typical subjects are euphoric crowds and costumed dancers in warehouses, hangars, squats and open fields, captured as grainy on-camera-flash snapshots or long-exposure light trails, with a strictly all-black Berlin techno counter-pole. Load this skill for dance-party culture, light-show interiors, kandi/PLUR accessories, 1990s clubwear, and flyer or poster graphics in the acid-house-to-festival lineage.

name: Raw_Industrial
description: Raw Industrial (also Industrial Style or Industrial Chic) is the loft-interior aesthetic of the late 2000s–2010s that treats the bones of converted factories as the decoration: exposed brick, bare concrete, black steel pipes and beams, weathered wood, and metal factory lighting inside open warehouse volumes. Its palette is neutral — grays, browns, blacks and metallic tones — with color arriving only through focal furniture, textiles and plants. Recognize it by unfinished structural surfaces left visible, open shelving and metal racks, reclaimed-wood islands and large sectionals zoning open plans, and Edison bulbs or metal dome pendants hanging from high ceilings.

name: Raxet
description: Raxet is a late-2010s Spanish trap-fashion aesthetic that reclaims choni street style through bold maximal accessories and bootleg-luxury glamour. Look for tracksuits styled with elegant or provocative pieces, XL gold hoop earrings, fanny packs, fishnet, faux fur, platform shoes, high hair, and elaborate embellished nails. Its palette centers black and gold with bright saturated accents and animal prints.

name: Raygun_Gothic
description: Raygun Gothic is the optimistic American retrofuturism of circa 1945–1970 — pulp-comic space adventure in saturated primaries, chrome and neon: finned rockets, bubble-canopy flying saucers, starburst atom graphics, helpful robots, and diner-chrome utopias projected onto alien planets and moon cities. Recognize it by bright comic-book color, streamlined chrome machines with aircraft fins and bubble glass, glowing energy beams, period poster lettering, and wholesome heroic optimism; it is the light-hearted cousin of Atompunk and the narrative, science-fiction extension of Googie architecture.

name: Realism
description: Mid-19th-century French movement (Courbet, Millet, Daumier, Manet) that paints ordinary modern life — field laborers, workshop and domestic interiors, plain nudes, unromanticized fields and forests — in earthy umber, ochre, moss-green and linen-white under faithful natural light. Signature traits: monumental seriousness given to mundane subjects, solid modeled bodies absorbed in work, matte oil surfaces with disciplined brushwork, and a complete absence of idealization, allegory or Romantic drama. Recognize by the somber earth palette, the dignity of laboring hands, and light that behaves like weather rather than theater.

name: Recession_Pop
description: Recession Pop (Electropop 08) is the maximalist club-pop aesthetic of 2008–2013: vibrant neon magenta, electric blue and lime green fired against black and mirror chrome, excessive glitter, asymmetrical haircuts and graphics, shutter shades and sci-fi visor sunglasses, deliberate lens flare and packed party scenes. Recognize it by glossy hyper-produced flash or strobe lighting, faceted futuristic garments, color-blocked neon sets and bold geometric sans typography; it packages hedonistic, relentlessly optimistic escapism from the Great Recession.

name: Regencycore
description: Regencycore is a 2020s fantasy-fashion aesthetic that reimagines British Regency dress (early 1800s) through a glossy, deliberately anachronistic lens: empire-waist gowns with puffed cap sleeves and low square or sweetheart necklines, in white and candy pastels, embellished with glitter, gemstone appliqués and floral brocade far beyond period accuracy. Typical subjects are social-season tableaux — garden parties, drawing-room teas, candlelit tables, promenades, ensemble casts on neoclassical steps — plus runway and street-style interpretations of the same silhouette, all shaped by the heightened look of Bridgerton. Recognize it by the under-bust waistline, sheer ruffled organza overlays, pearls, long gloves and feather hair ornaments, and a saturated pastel palette that reads confection rather than museum.

name: Reggae
description: Reggae is the visual culture of Jamaican roots music from the late 1960s onward — the Rastafari tricolor of red, gold and green anchored in black, deployed as flag bands, gradients and sunbursts behind stencil or silhouette portraits, dreadlocked figures in knitted tams, peace signs, Lions of Judah, ganja leaves and maps of Africa. Posters, murals and record sleeves carry bold hand-painted or distressed lettering on worn paper, canvas and sun-faded walls, alongside handmade bead, wood and leather accessories. Recognize it by saturated flag-bright color plus black, embodied Rasta dress, and a laid-back but defiant mood of peace, love and resistance.

name: Reggaetonero
description: Visual culture of the mid-2000s Latin Caribbean reggaeton subculture (roots in the late-1990s Puerto Rican and Panamanian underground): high-contrast black-and-white streetwear loaded with gold and silver-platinum chains, diamond-set watches, baseball caps and designer sunglasses worn indoors. Signature subjects are shaved-head or short-tufted men in jerseys, baggy denim or suits over bare chests posed in confrontational crew clusters, women in tight fitted party wear, perreo couples, and club, beach and money-flex scenes. The mood is loud flexing, eroticism and street authenticity — studio promo gloss laid over barrio grit.

name: Renaissance_Revival
description: Renaissance Revival is a 1990s reinterpretation of Renaissance, medieval and Elizabethan imagery — corsets, bodices, Elizabethan ruffs and long dresses photographed through a soft sepia veil of gold, brown and black. Signature elements are parchment grain and sepia filters, arched niches and illuminated-manuscript borders, renaissance script typography, candlelit amber glow, and backlit fairy wings. Typical subjects are solitary costumed women, winged fairies, manuscript pages, oracle-card borders and period-drama film stills.

name: Renovador_Movement
description: Galician avant-garde of the 1920s–1930s (Os Renovadores / Movemento Renovador) — regional subjects such as Atlantic coasts, rías, peasants, fisherfolk, gaiteiros, romarías and intellectual portraits, rendered with borrowed Cubist plane-simplification, Expressionist texture and Surrealist dream-logic, plus ink-line graphic satire (retranca) and stone-carved, Celtic-flavoured "Gallaecia" lettering on posters, mastheads and book covers. Palette of granite grey, earth ochre, Atlantic teal, parchment paper and vermilion accents; dignified working figures, religious symbols repurposed for civic meaning, polychrome sculpture and architectural murals.

name: Retro_Gamer
description: Retro Gamer is the nostalgia aesthetic of physical video-game culture from the 1980s–2000s: grey-and-black consoles, chunky multi-pronged controllers, CRT televisions, cartridge shells, arcade cabinets and densely packed collector rooms. Its palette anchors in machine grey, black and beige carpet, punctured by pea-green Game Boy glow, pastel handheld candy colors and neon marquee magenta-cyan emitted by the machines themselves. Mood is comfort, contentment and euphoric nostalgia — lived-in cable tangles and glowing screens, never pristine modern product gloss.

name: Retrofuturism
description: Retrofuturism visualizes the future as imagined from a past era — an 1890s chromolithograph of a video-call boudoir, a 1930s sepia print of ziggurat skyscrapers, a 1950s–60s chrome-and-pastel rocket lounge, a porthole-studded pod house, a dial-and-vacuum-tube computer. Its DNA is the friction between two layers: a period style layer (lithograph stipple, halftone newsprint, etching hatch, Art Deco chrome, molded Space Age plastic) and a speculative machine layer (flying trains, finned rayguns, clunky robots, domed megastructures, "advanced" versions of obsolete technology). Palette ranges from sepia ink and lithographic pastels to atomic-age teal, coral and chrome; mood swings from naïve utopian wonder to ironic nostalgia for a future that never arrived.

name: Riot_Grrrl
description: Early-1990s feminist punk DIY aesthetic from Olympia, Washington and Washington D.C., built on photocopied zine collage — handwritten manifestos, typewritten blocks and cut-out ransom letters in black, ivory, hot pink and protest red, with tape, smudges and scissor lines left visible. Signature elements include defaced mass-media cutouts, slogans reclaimed on skin and clothing, babydoll dresses over combat boots, smudged eyeliner and smeared lipstick, and flash-lit snapshots of female-fronted bands in small venues. Recognize it by paper-as-battleground composition, monochrome-plus-one-hot-accent color, and agitational first-person text.

name: Rivethead
description: Rivethead is the utilitarian dress code of the late-1980s/90s EBM and electro-industrial club scene — military surplus, factory workwear, combat boots, goggles and gas masks, hardware-store jewelry, locked into a monochrome of black, charcoal, olive drab, grey and rusted steel. It is recognized by its documentary register (grainy club photos, band press shots, magazine scans) and by silhouettes that read as soldier or assembly-line worker rather than vampire or rave dancer. Load this skill when identifying or generating industrial-music subculture fashion, EBM club nights, or post-industrial dystopian utility wear.

name: Roadman
description: Roadman is the mid-2010s London youth-subculture aesthetic: a monochrome black-grey-white streetwear uniform of glossy black puffed jackets, tech-fleece hoodies and joggers, black balaclavas or masks, diagonal crossbody belly-bag straps and clean white sneakers, shot in harsh phone-flash night snapshots on UK estates, in open car doorways and in face-hiding mirror selfies. Recognise it by concealed or deadpan faces, crew clusters against brick-and-concrete street vernacular, drill/grime adjacency and lo-fi vertical phone framing; in US circulation it appears as "Nike Tech".

name: Roaring_Twenties
description: The visual culture of the 1920s Jazz Age — flapper silhouettes (cloche hats, bobbed hair, beaded drop-waist dresses at knee hem), Art Deco geometry, and machine-age emblems like cabinet radios and early automobiles, staged in cabarets, ballrooms and city canyons. Palette runs from silver-gelatin monochrome and sepia to black lacquer loaded with gold, silver and deep jewel tones (emerald, sapphire, ruby), plus flat vermilion-and-midnight poster graphics. Look for kick lines, balloons and streamers mid-air, brass jazz bands, stiff-collared tuxedos and kinetically posed women rather than static formal portraiture.

name: Robotcore
description: Robotcore (aka Codingcore, AI.core, Androidcore) is an underground internet aesthetic of machine sentience: androids, robotsonas and anthropomorphized AI rendered in a cool monochrome world of blues, cyans, teals and violet tints over black voids, lit from within by neon signs, holograms and glowing circuit traces. Its signature elements are circuit boards and exposed robot parts, lines of code and terminal text treated as poetry, machined hardware macro studies, futuristic machine cities, and glitch/CRT screen artifacts. Recognize it by its cold emissive lighting, chrome-and-porcelain machine bodies, declarative machine-identity typography, and its mood of yearning identification with the robot rather than fear of it.

name: Rockabilly
description: Rockabilly is the visual language of 1950s American rock 'n' roll and its revival subculture: a cherry-red, jet-black and cream palette seasoned with bright pastels, laid over polka dots, checkerboard tile and leopard print, staged among vintage cars, gas pumps, diners, jukeboxes and barber poles. Its figures are rockabellas with victory rolls or Bettie bangs, winged liner and deep red lips, and pompadoured rockabillys in white tees, cuffed jeans and leather — both proudly tattooed, posed in pin-up body language. It reads as exaggerated, sun-saturated 1950s Americana with a deliberate alternative edge, never as wholesome preppy retro.

name: Rocketpunk
description: Rocketpunk is the retro-futuristic and hard-science-fiction aesthetic of spaceflight, spanning 1950s Space Age pulp to modern "NASApunk" realism: vehicles assembled from legible engineering parts — cylindrical and spherical tanks, truss spines, flat radiator and solar-panel wings, torus centrifuges, cone-and-fin rockets descended from the V-2 — set against void black or a planetary limb. Its palette is matte hull white, bare aluminum, ochre and rust panel accents over black space and Earth blue, lit by a single hard sun or by floodlit night launch pads. Recognize it by dedicated propulsion-and-payload sections, checkerboard bands, circular portholes, nixie-tube consoles, and a competent, documentary optimism about human expansion into space.

name: Rockstar_GF
description: Lo-fi, flash-lit snapshot aesthetic emulating the girlfriends of rock musicians from the 1970s through the early 2000s — long leather jackets and shaggy fur coats over slip dresses, fishnets and flare pants, set in a black-white-red palette with silver glints. Grainy backstage corridors, dive bars, car windows and night stairwells filled with cigarettes, band tees, cross jewelry and guitars, mixing grunge grit with romantic femininity. Recognize it by harsh on-camera flash or tungsten bar light, crushed blacks, lived-in mess, and a single saturated red accent against monochrome surroundings.

name: Rococo
description: Rococo is the ornamental style of Louis XV's France (Paris, 1720s–1760s): pastel fields of powder blue, rose, mint, cream and lavender charged with ivory stucco and gold leaf, structured by asymmetrical C- and S-scrolls, rocaille shellwork, acanthus, garlands, putti and mascarons. Its subjects are intimate pleasure — fêtes galantes, courtship, pastoral idylls, mythological love, powdered-wig portraiture, porcelain figures and mirrored salon interiors — rendered in hazy light at domestic rather than monumental scale. Load this skill to recognize or generate 18th-century French-derived courtly ornament, pastel boiserie rooms, scroll-driven decorative design, Sèvres/Meissen porcelain, and period fashion with panniers, ribbons and lace.

name: Rococopunk
description: Early-2010s DIY costuming aesthetic fusing 18th-century Rococo opulence — powdered wigs, corseted court silhouettes, frills, lace, pastel brocade — with punk rebellion: mohawks and feather crests, studs, clownish rouge, anachronistic denim and sneakers. Palette runs powder pink, mint and ivory against fuchsia, turquoise and brocade gold, captured as flash-lit party snapshots, warm stage tableaux, or crowded baroque-group portraits. Recognize it by handmade excess, camp aristocratic parody, and the deliberate clash of courtly silhouette with anti-authoritarian garnish.

name: Rokku
description: Rokku (Rock Gal / Rokku Gal) is a mid-to-late 2000s Japanese gyaru substyle that fuses goth, punk and visual kei into a black-grounded street coordinate: pale luminous skin, heavy smoky circle-lens eyes, bleached or dyed teased hair, studded faux leather, chains, skulls, crosses, red-black plaid, leopard print, ripped denim and ruffled mini skirts over platform or combat boots. It lives in flash-lit blog snapshots, brand-shop snaps and gyaru magazine scans, often finished with hand-drawn deco overlays, and it deliberately rejects the classic gyaru tan in favour of rebellious, cute-aggressive darkness.

name: Rolinga
description: Rolinga ("Stone") is the working-class Argentine rock subculture of the late 1980s–1990s built on devotion to The Rolling Stones — shaggy mullet with thick straight fringe (flequillo), tongue-and-lips and band t-shirts, flared torn jeans, frayed neck scarf, choker, worn platform sneakers. Its palette is denim blue, black, off-white cotton and logo red, captured as amateur snapshots against brick barrio walls, curbs and concert pits. Recognize it by loud logo allegiance, androgynous long-fringe hair and barrio-football authenticity, not by grunge flannel, bohemian craft or cumbia sportswear.

name: Romantic_Academia
description: Romantic Academia (aka Coquette Academia) is a 2010s literary aesthetic that fuses the cream-and-tan daylight classicism of Light Academia with the visual language of romantic love: kiss-marked pages, embracing couples, lace blouses, pearls, pressed roses, ornate vanity mirrors and handwritten letters. Recognize it by an ivory-blush-gold palette warmed by dappled or window-pane sunlight, film-grain softness, aged paper and antique remnants (lockets, frescoes, Greek busts, vintage photographs), all arranged around reading, writing and tenderness.

name: Romantic_Goth
description: Romantic Goth is the 1990s goth substyle that dresses 19th-century Romantic melancholy in flowing velvet, lace and corsetry — a black ground lit by deep jewel tones (burgundy, forest green, sapphire), ivory and silver. Signature elements are flowing gowns and poet shirts, lace chokers and dark-stoned jewellery, moonlit graveyards, ruined castles, black roses, candelabras and ravens, all carried by soft silhouettes and dark dramatic elegance rather than strict period recreation. Typical subjects are solitary mourners, lovers, allegorical angels and faeries, candlelit interiors and night gardens, appearing across fashion photography, digital painting and figurine work.

name: Romantic_Italian
description: Romantic Italian is a sun-faded, pastel-and-neutral aesthetic that romanticizes Italy's cities, countryside and classical art heritage — white marble sculpture, blush stucco facades, Venetian canals, citrus and fig still lifes, linen and silk fashion — all bathed in soft Mediterranean summer light. Recognize it by dusty rose/cream palettes, Classical and Renaissance art markers (busts, cast galleries, domes, ruins), quiet leisure-class props (straw baskets, wine, scarves, gondolas), and romance implied obliquely through shadows, embracing statues or turned-away figures. It separates from Pink Parisian by its Italian regional anchors and Classicism, and from Cottagecore by its Mediterranean grandeur and haute-couture fashion.

name: Romanticism
description: European movement of c. 1790–1850 whose visual art paints the sublime — untamed nature, storms, mists, mountains, ruins and shipwrecks — through dynamic compositions, heightened atmospheric color and expressive, visibly worked paint, from molten Turnerian gold to Friedrich's cold grey-blues.
