Tiny or solitary figures dwarfed by vast landscape, nocturnes, ghostly apparitions, revolution and execution scenes, medieval ruins and Byronic heroes carry its core emotions of awe, terror and melancholy.

name: Route_66
description: Mid-century American roadside kitsch of the 1950s–60s Mother Road — garish neon signage, Googie and programmatic mimetic architecture, giant fiberglass statues and teepee motels set against the vast dusty Southwest plain. The palette juxtaposes dusty earth browns and rust reds with neon turquoise, hot pink, chrome silver and pastel mint/pink, lit either by harsh noon sun or by neon against black desert night. Use for roadside Americana, autotourism nostalgia, linen-postcard graphics, and desert-highway kitsch.

name: Royalcore
description: Royalcore romanticizes Western European court life of the Baroque, Rococo and Regency eras through ball gowns, corsets, opera gloves, tiaras, pearl jewelry, gilded palace interiors and elaborate tea sets. Its palette runs from porcelain cream, blush pink, powder blue and sage with gold-leaf accents to a candlelit register of royal blue, emerald and deep red velvet. Recognize it by structured historical silhouettes, maximalist gilded ornament, regalia still lifes, and soft painterly or amber candlelight staging.

name: Russian_2K17
description: Russian 2K17 ("Vernite Moy 2017 / Bring Back My 2017") is a 2016–2018 VK-born teen aesthetic of post-Soviet urban everyday life: grainy, compressed cheap-phone snapshots of panel-block yards, podyezd entrance halls, rooftops and teenage bedrooms, lit by sodium-yellow streetlight against cold blue shadow or raspberry-magenta dusk skies. Signature elements are worn-in Thrasher/Adidas/Vans streetwear, hidden or averted faces, garland-lit rooms with Soviet wall carpets, and sincere-yet-self-aware Cyrillic caption and lyric overlays. Recognize it by low-res flash photography texture, post-Soviet residential scenery, and a melancholy filtered through post-irony.

name: Rustic
description: Rustic is a romanticized rural-labor aesthetic built on unfinished wood, fieldstone, brick and organic materials in a browns-and-reds earth palette, openly embracing the grit, rust, soot and wear of farm life. Its signature subjects are farmhouses, barns and cabins, hearths and cast-iron stoves, old or rusty tools, taxidermy, farm animals, stacked firewood and hay, and wide rural landscapes lit by firelight, lamplight or low golden sun. Load this skill when imagery or prompts feature weathered timber vernacular architecture, harvest fields, workwear-coded warmth, or lived-in clutter rather than polished, pastel or minimalist interiors.

name: Sad_Beige
description: Sad Beige is a 2020s domestic-and-wardrobe microtrend of near-total colorlessness: nurseries, living rooms, toys and clothing rendered in beige, cream, oat, taupe and blond wood, with matte linen, bouclé, rattan, crochet and sheepskin textures under soft diffused daylight. Signature elements are uncluttered minimalist rooms, muted children's goods (cloud-shaped rugs, geometric star cushions, spray-muted play trees), dried pampas, fairy lights and ribbed vases, inhabited by millennial parents and toddlers in neutral knits. Recognize it by its drained palette, serene under-furnished emptiness and faintly satirical calm; it lacks Clean Girl's grooming gloss, Boujee's gold-and-marble shine and Light Academia's scholarly browns.

name: Sadboi
description: Sadboi is the early-2010s Tumblr/SoundCloud aesthetic of performed male melancholy: lo-fi degraded photography and anime edits (VHS tracking, pixelation, chromatic aberration), monochrome streetwear and bucket hats, wilted roses, Japanese lettering and frown emoticons over near-black grid backgrounds. Its palette is desaturated blue-purple and grey-black punctured by a single saturated accent (rose red, neon glitch fringe), and faces are routinely hidden by hands, black censor bars or scribbles. Recognize it when depressive one-liners, broken-heart emojis and eye-censoring collide with streetwear, ironic consumer-brand appropriation (Arizona Iced Tea, Fiji Water) or Bart Simpson edits.

name: Sadgirl
description: Sadgirl is a 2010s Tumblr feminine-melancholy aesthetic built from desaturated black, gray, and dull blue lo-fi imagery, VHS grain, rain, smeared mascara, cigarettes, and introspective or self-deprecating text. Its signature subjects are isolated feminine figures, tragic literary archetypes, bedroom interiors, and small symbols of self-destruction, treated as poetic rather than polished. Use this skill for images that should feel vulnerable, low-fidelity, and romantically sad without becoming glossy, cute, or explicitly harmful.

name: Safari_Chic
description: Safari Chic is the "elegant adventurer" fashion aesthetic — khaki, beige and camel cotton/linen safari jackets (the saharienne) with four bellows pockets and belted waists, Bermuda shorts, wide-brim sun hats, leather straps and animal-print accents, codified by Yves Saint Laurent in 1967–68 from British colonial khaki-drill expedition wear. Recognize it by monochrome earth-tone ensembles, utility pocketing, straw and leather accessories, and warm savanna, canvas-tent or soft studio settings in golden or diffused light.

name: Sandalpunk
description: Sandalpunk (also Bronzepunk) is a retro-futurist antiquity aesthetic: Greco-Roman marble architecture, crested bronze armor and colonnaded halls fused with hand-crafted impossible technology — gear-driven automata, Antikythera-style dial mechanisms, watermill dynamos, fan- and sail-rigged flying barges. Its palette is white marble, gold/bronze, metal gray and Aegean blue, lit by Mediterranean sunshafts or forge-dark chiaroscuro. Typical subjects are armored hoplites and legionaries with machined details, sunlit marble interiors, colossal bronze automatons, and processional Roman monumentalism.

name: Scandi_Girl_Winter
description: Late-2010s Scandinavian winter fashion microtrend (peaked 2022–23) built on warm-neutral layering — off-white, oatmeal, camel, heather grey — in chunky cable knits, slouchy turtlenecks, oversized puffers and shearling coats, wide-leg trousers, thick wool scarves, fuzzy earmuffs and giant totes. Shot as candid, overcast street-style snapshots in snowy Nordic cities or soft window-lit interiors, with hygge-derived coziness, practical comfort and small playful pops of powder blue, moss or mint over a minimalist base. Recognize by bulky natural-fiber layering, snow or slush underfoot, stone and stucco facades, and an unposed, scarf-bundled ease.

name: Scandinavian_Design
description: Nordic design movement popularized in the 1950s, defined by functional clean-lined furniture in light woods, pale neutral envelopes of white, beige and gray, and rooms flooded with daylight from bare or sheer-dressed windows. Signature elements include organic biomorphic forms (bent-plywood shells, wishbone- and egg-type silhouettes, wavy-edged glass vases), warm low lamplight and candles, sparse curated decor of plants, ceramics and simple-patterned linen/wool textiles, plus a documented dark variant of charcoal walls warmed by sheepskin and brass glow. Typical subjects are airy interiors, standalone furniture and glassware object shots, bold two-color folk-botanical textile prints, and white sculptural modernist architecture.

name: Scene
description: Scene is the mid-2000s to early-2010s US youth-subculture aesthetic born from emo and hardcore punk on MySpace: solid black clothing punched with hot pink, electric blue and lime neon, heavily teased straightened hair with side-swept fringes and "raccoon tail" streaks, thick raccoon eyeliner, skinny jeans, band tees, studded belts and checkerboard or animal-print accents. Recognize it by lo-fi snapshot flash photography, glitter-and-splatter MySpace/Blingee graphics, chibi big-eyed cartoon avatars with sketchy line art, and playful "rawr" kitsch (Hello Kitty, skulls, hearts, bows) over an androgynous, party-optimistic mood.

name: Scene_Tween
description: Scene Tween is the early-2010s tween merchandise aesthetic that repackaged the teen Scene subculture for children: neon rainbow animal prints (leopard spots, zebra and tiger stripes) laid over black or white grounds, saturated hot pink, lime green, electric blue and violet, heavy glitter, peace signs, hearts and friendship slogans. Signature subjects are oversized glitter-eyed plush toys, robotic pet toys, backpacks, folders, craft kits, sneakers, color-blocked tween bedrooms and sassy cartoon character promos in the Justice / Claire's / Lisa Frank orbit. Recognize it by pattern-on-pattern maximalism, rainbow-dyed (never naturalistic) animal print, and a cheerful "diva/sassy" positivity that sanitizes Scene's edge into kid-friendly sparkle.

name: Scenecore
description: Scenecore (aka Colorpuke) is an early-2020s internet aesthetic and hyperpop offshoot that revives 2000s Scene-kid culture as a maximalist digital pastiche: rainbow checkerboard fields, Blingee/PicMix glitter graphics, stacked kandi bead bracelets, and full-spectrum neon on black, populated by mascots like GIR, Hello Kitty, Hatsune Miku and Nyan Cat. Recognize it by horror-vacui collage layouts, flash-lit outfit snaps with split-dye hair, platform boots and tutu-over-skinny-jeans layering, pixel-glitch seasoning, and an unironic "cringe culture is dead" exuberance.

name: Seapunk
description: Seapunk is a 2011 Tumblr/Twitter-born internet aesthetic that fuses aquatic fantasy with 1990s cyberculture — early-3D CGI dolphins, pyramids, palm trees and mirror-flat water planes rendered in aquamarine, cyan, turquoise, seafoam, lilac and pastel pink. Recognize it by its utopian glossy sheen over low-poly chrome shaders, dithered gradient skies, yin-yang and smiley iconography, GIF-loop rotating geometry, and rave-surfer fashion in dyed turquoise hair and transparent plastic. Use for oceanic Y2K-net nostalgia, aquatic digital collage, or 90s-CGI-flavored tropical scenes.

name: Seiz_Breur
description: Seiz Breur is the Breton modernist-revival style of 1923–1947: high-contrast woodcut and wood-engraving graphics in black on cream paper, lifted by at most one or two muted spot inks (ochre gold, brick red, sage green), with hand-carved blocky Breton-language lettering. Its signature elements are Celtic emblematics — triskelion, ermine spots, spirals, saw-tooth borders, knotwork — and linear sacred light: radiating white or gold rays around saints, folk heroes, open books and gnarled trees. Typical subjects are Breton peasants and sailors in coiffes and embroidered vests, pardons and pilgrimages, marine life, forests, and typographic slogan posters, all rendered as flat cut planes crossed by white gouge lines.

name: Sextrance
description: Sextrance is the 2020s SoundCloud hard-trance microgenre's visual language: deliberately corrupted 2000s–2010s digital nostalgia built from low-poly racing/rhythm/FPS game imagery, anime stills, trading-card frames, jewel cases and figure-box scans, all run through bitcrush, datamosh and JPEG-scale compression. Its palette is purple, black, electric blue, hot pink and white shot through with holographic, color-shifting CD-foil iridescence. Recognize it by chaotic collage layering, vertical Japanese game-menu text, pixel or chrome graffiti logotypes, game HUD fragments, and either neon-on-black glow or blown-out scanner white.

name: Shabby_Chic
description: Shabby Chic is the 1980s interior aesthetic codified by Rachel Ashwell, built on furniture and fabric that look lovingly worn — chipped white-painted wood, rose-sprig chintz, lace and ruffled slipcovers under a crystal chandelier. Its palette is sun-faded cream, blush pink, sage and sky blue; its mood romantic, feminine, comfortably nostalgic. Recognize it by distressed painted furniture, small-scale rose florals, skirted and ruffled textiles, pearl-and-crochet trinket layering, and high-key diffused light over matte, aged surfaces.

name: Shamate
description: Shamate is the Chinese migrant-worker subculture of the late 2000s–early 2010s whose visual signature is enormous spray-dyed spike hair — crimson, gold, electric blue, violet, platinum — towering over pale, foundation-lightened faces rimmed with black eyeliner. Cheap bright streetwear, studded dog collars and chains, group snapshots in grey industrial plazas, and hyper-saturated QQ-album photo editing (glow, lens flares, stickers, decorative borders) complete the look. Recognize it by the hair-first silhouette: backcombed radial volume that dominates the frame while clothing and setting stay deliberately mundane.

name: Sharpies
description: Australian working-class youth-gang aesthetic of 1960s–1970s Melbourne — ultra-tight striped "Conny" cardigans worn several sizes too small, high-waisted flared jeans, mullets, platform shoes, homemade tattoos and pierced ears, captured in faded amateur snapshots on brick-veneer streets, train trains and town-hall dance floors. Palette of denim indigo, oxblood red, mustard and black knit against sun-bleached concrete; mood of territorial, peacock working-class bravado. Recognize it by the constricted knit-over-flare silhouette and the suburban Australian snapshot finish.

name: Shenxian-fu
description: Shenxian-fu ("immortal garb") is a 2020s Chinese Han-yuansu fashion aesthetic that dresses women as the female Taoist xian of ancestral imagination, built on Wei-Jin-derived layered ruqun silhouettes in cinnabar red contrasted against turquoise and malachite blue-green on ivory silk. Its signatures are draping looped ribbons and wide sleeves, skirts with hanging sash tails (zaju chuishao fu), half-arm jackets with pleated facing (banbi), embroidered waist-hung panels (bixi), and high coiled topknots or gold crowns, rendered either as mineral pigment on aged silk and mural gold or as saturated modern reconstruction photography. Typical subjects are solitary nymphs, moon goddesses and celestial court dancers posed in temple corridors, gardens, mist sets or plain studio backdrops.

name: Shibuya-Kei
description: Shibuya-kei is the sleeve-design and fashion aesthetic of the mid-to-late 1990s Shibuya, Tokyo pop scene: flat, saturated print colors (tangerine, mustard, lime, magenta, cyan) on cream and jet black, bold black-and-white Op Art patterns such as polka dots, tartan and concentric circles, and a cut-and-paste quotation of 1960s Mod, French yé-yé and Space Age kitsch. Expect bob-haired figures in mini-skirts and tailored suits, silkscreen duotones and Warhol-style repetition grids, lowercase geometric sans-serif type with catalog-number microtype, and clean modernist layouts on square album sleeves. The mood is chic, witty, nostalgic and cosmopolitan — consumerism practiced as curation.

name: Shibuya_Punk
description: Shibuya Punk (aka Grind Fiction / Animemo) is an early-2000s Japanese urban aesthetic born from Jet Set Radio-era game art direction: cel-shaded rendering, graffiti-layered Shibuya/Shinjuku cityscapes, baggy Y2K streetwear, and clashing high-saturation palettes of lime green, hot pink, orange and electric blue. Signature elements include inline skates and grind rails, spray tags and kanji sticker graphics, chain-link fences and stacked neon signage, and angular characters frozen in kinetic mid-grind poses. Recognize it by flat toon-shaded color planes with hard-edged shadow shapes over dense neon city grit and defiant street-crew energy.

name: Shoe_Diva
description: Shoe Diva (aka Pink Parisian Chic) is a late-1990s-through-2000s commercial illustration aesthetic built on thin, loopy, sketchy pen linework over flat candy fills of pink, yellow, lavender, mint and periwinkle, depicting elongated fashionable women with stiletto pumps, luxury shopping bags, cosmopolitans and Eiffel-Tower Parisiana. Recognize it by its hand-drawn wobble, fashion-croquis proportions, confetti-scattered fetish objects on flat pastel or paper-white grounds, and script-plus-serif typography with crowns and sparkles; it lives on chick-lit book covers, cosmetics branding, logos, murals and apparel prints.

name: Signalism
description: Signalism is the Yugoslav neo-avant-garde of the late 1960s–1970s (Novi Sad, around Miroljub Todorović and the journal Signal), which treats language itself as raw material: visual poetry, mathematical formulas, punctuation glyphs, arrows and machine diagrams collaged in xerox-halftone black and white with a single saturated red accent. Expect serially repeated modules, dense "text labyrinths," found engraving and newsprint specimens, rubber-stamp red gears and symbols, and flat scanned-page lighting. Load this skill to recognize or generate work that reads as a scientific diagram of poetry rather than a painting, a poster, or a clean modernist layout.

name: Signalwave
description: Signalwave (Broken Transmission) is the visual arm of the early-2010s vaporwave subgenre built from VHS-recorded television: degraded screencaps of 1980s–90s broadcasts — weather maps, news desks, station idents and sign-off slides, commercial sets — softened by tape grain, chroma bleed and lifted purple-indigo blacks. Recognize it by mundane institutional broadcast content frozen mid-transmission, dusty teal-and-blue palettes leaking magenta chroma and amber dusk flare, pixel-dithered graphics, on-screen banner text and static. The mood is nostalgic, liminal and eerily calm — lost media remembered fondly, never horror.

name: Silicon_Dreams
description: Silicon Dreams is the uncanny, dreamlike look of early 3D computer graphics from the mid-1980s to early 2000s — sparse surreal landscapes and floating primitives rendered in Bryce 3D, Pov-Ray and Terragen, with low-poly faceted geometry, dithered pastel gradient skies (periwinkle, lavender, cyan), mirror-calm reflective seas, chrome and glass spheres, and naive "janky" CGI creatures. Recognize it by primitive single-light shading, low-resolution dithered textures, horizon-centered emptiness, and a sterile utopian sci-fi mood; typical carriers are demo reels, TV bumpers, game stills, and drum-'n'-bass album covers, often with VHS or 8-bit print degradation.

name: Silkpunk
description: Silkpunk (Sino-punk) is a 2010s speculative aesthetic, coined by Ken Liu, that builds technology from the organic materials of late imperial and early-20th-century East Asia — bamboo, paper, silk, timber, bronze — instead of iron and steam. Recognize it by pagodas and upturned eaves, wooden automata and silk-skinned flying machines, lantern-glowing timber interiors, and gold-and-vermilion regalia with tassels, knots and seal stamps, set against ink black, parchment, or misty jade. Typical subjects are handcrafted machines in daily life, courtly figures in silk, terraced mountain cities, and parchment schematics; neon, chrome and coal smoke are absent.

name: Simpsonwave
description: Simpsonwave is a mid-2010s Vaporwave subgenre that re-grades classic-era Simpsons cel animation into melancholic VHS memories: washed-out purple-pink "codeine" color grading, tracking errors, static and chromatic aberration over flat 90s broadcast cartoon flats, with lone characters (Sad Bart, Lisa at empty desks, Homer driving) held in dreamy suburban stillness. Recognize it by the collision of sitcom cel line-work with worn-tape degradation, pastel violet haze, optional fullwidth melancholic text and vaporwave geometry. It is nostalgic, sorrowful and surreal rather than cozy, fried or abstract.

name: Sinofuturism
description: Sinofuturism (Chinese Sci-Fi Futurism, Socialist Cyberpunk) is the 2010s aesthetic of future visions tied to Chinese cultural identity: state-scale infrastructure (dams, viaducts, pylons, warehouse logistics), space programs, AI and smart-city surveillance rendered in slogan red, space-program blue, concrete beige and metallic silver, often veiled in mist or lit by neon and LED signage. Recognize it by Chinese-character banner and LED typography on socialist-modernist concrete, collectivist scale contrasts of tiny figures against megastructures, and a mood swinging between accelerationist optimism and rustbelt melancholy.

name: Sizz
description: Sizz is a 2010s internet-born aesthetic (named circa 2017 out of Tumblr/Instagram currents, community centered on r/sizz) that degrades photographs of real subjects with noise, blur, scan and printer artifacting, and subtle deformation to reach "abstracted realism." Its spine is high-contrast black and white or fog-dissolved gray, occasionally muted desaturated color or a single ember-orange accent; typical subjects are solitary blurred figures, liminal streets, graveyards and fields, hanging cloth, and machine-glitch mark-fields. Recognize it by a sibilant grainy surface, soft or smeared focus, mundane reality made strange, and composition-first framing.

name: Skater
description: Skater is the visual culture of skateboarding, from 1950s California sidewalk surfing to the 1990s street-era uniform of baggy denim, skate-brand graphic tees and scuffed cupsole shoes, shot on fisheye lenses, on-camera flash or sun-faded film against concrete plazas, brick walls and graffiti. Its palette anchors on concrete grey, asphalt black and sun-bleached tan, punctured by deck-graphic pops of pink, fire red and cobalt; its motifs rank skateboards and skate terrain first, then worn grip tape, prohibited signs and slouched crew lineups. The mood is casual, communal and anti-authoritarian — mid-trick tension or sunburned hanging-out, never polished.

name: Skeuomorphism
description: Skeuomorphism is the digital-design aesthetic of the 1980s–early 2010s in which interface elements, icons and products imitate real-world materials and objects — stitched leather, wood grain, brushed metal, paper, glass panes — rendered with bevels, drop shadows, gradients and specular gloss so depth reads as physical. Expect warm wood-and-paper neutrals or charcoal instrument panels, analog dials, knobs and sliders, stitched seams, rivets and page corners, and a single consistent light source. Load this skill to recognize or generate UI screens, app icons, control panels, product mockups and texture studies that answer the question "what physical object is this pretending to be?"

name: Skhothane
description: Skhothane (Izikhothane) is a mid-2000s township youth subculture from Ekurhuleni, Gauteng, South Africa, whose visual DNA is maximalist clashing designer fashion — glossy silk print shirts, DMD-style jackets, Italian Carvela/Rossimoda loafers — worn by crews in boastful dance-battle poses on township streets, parks and roadside verges. Look for bright clashing prints (fuchsia, turquoise, acid yellow, violet, orange) against black skinny trousers and mundane asphalt or painted-wall backdrops, crouches and crew clusters captured in saturated compact-camera flash snapshots, and optional wealth-theater props such as trampled clothes, poured whisky and dangling price tags.

name: Skinhead
description: British working-class subculture aesthetic born in late-1960s London, defined by shaved or closely cropped heads, polished Dr. Martens lace-up boots, braces over tucked-in button-down or Fred Perry polo shirts, straight-leg Levi's or Sta-Prest trousers with rolled hems, and Harrington or satin bomber jackets, in a solid palette of black, oxblood, navy, white and grey punctuated by tartan and houndstooth checks. Photographically it reads as flash-lit snapshot or grainy black-and-white documentary realism set in vernacular urban space — brick walls, graffiti, football terraces, club interiors — carrying a hard-but-smart, crew-loyal working-class posture. Spans 1960s traditional skins, 70s suedehead and 2 Tone-adjacent crossovers and 80s Oi! waves, and includes female, queer and anti-racist subjects alongside the far-right segment the subculture is often misread as being.

name: Slavic_Doll
description: Early-2000s high-fashion aesthetic built on the Eastern European supermodel ideal — extremely slender, pale, doll-faced young women with high cheekbones, almond eyes and long straight blonde or "Slavic hair," wearing fur coats, miniskirts and knee-high boots in muted neutrals of black, white and beige. It reads as runway and backstage flash photography, painterly editorial portraiture, or glossy magazine covers, all carrying an aloof, inaccessible elegance; its 2020s revival adds faux-fur hats and a Winter Bimbo inflection.

name: Slavic_Violence_Tumblr
description: Mid-2010s Tumblr aesthetic of post-Soviet grimness — grainy, lo-fi photographs of balaclava-clad youths and shaved-head conscripts in army-green camouflage, set against Russian Orthodox icons, brass crosses, weapon flat-lays, chains and rope, snow yards and panel-flat interiors. Palette of black, olive drab, concrete grey and tarnished icon-gold, with crushed shadows, sensor grain and compression artifacts; mood of nihilistic intimidation, grim piety and cold tenderness-in-brutality. Load this skill when an image fuses Eastern European paramilitary dress, Orthodox Christian symbols, restraint motifs and amateur lo-fi menace.

name: Slavic_Winter
description: Slavic Winter is a photography-based internet aesthetic of post-Soviet residential courtyards in snow, shot at blue hour or after dark: flat panel-block facades (khrushchevka, brezhnevka) with scattered amber lit windows against deep indigo skies, snow-buried cars, bare trees, haloed streetlamps and mundane courtyard clutter. Its palette is a narrow field of cold blues, near-blacks and sky-tinted snow, punctured only by small warm points of artificial light, rendered with unstaged phone-camera low-light realism. Recognize it by inhabited-but-empty winter micro-district exteriors carrying melancholy, quietude and cozy isolation; never by people, fashion, ruins or daylight travel scenery.

name: Sleepcore
description: Sleepcore (sleepycore, drowsycore) is a therapeutic late-2010s internet aesthetic of sleep and dreams: hazy pastel fields of soft pink, light blue, lavender and pale yellow anchored by deep night blue, populated by stuffed animals, pajamas, bedding, nightlights and star/moon/cloud motifs. Its imagery — faded photos, old children's-show stills, soft illustrations, empty dreamlike nurseries — carries low-contrast haze, gentle melancholy and ASMR calm. Recognize it by bedtime stillness and half-asleep fuzziness rather than by warm rustic comfort (that is Cozycore).

name: Slimepunk
description: Slimepunk is an early-2010s Tumblr-born music and visual microgenre built on toxic neon-green slime dripping over black — biohazard and radiation trefoils, syringes and IV drips, gas masks and rubber gloves, mallgoth-rave fashion, and DIY web-collage grammar like checkerboard transparency, clip-art grids and dripping fonts. Recognize it by viscous acid-green ooze with phosphorescent glow, hazard graphics, Mountain Dew / Nickelodeon slime nostalgia and corrosive teen irony; it emerged from seapunk as its self-declared "villain."

name: Sloanie
description: Sloanie (Sloane Ranger) is the English upper-class country-and-city uniform codified by The Official Sloane Ranger Handbook (1982): waxed Barbour jackets, tweed, Hunter wellington boots, pie-crust collars and pearls, set in earthy olive-brown-navy tones with pastel blouses and scarlet hunting accents. Recognise it by overcast English light, muddy hemlines, Land Rovers and hunting-breed dogs, family tartans, country-house interiors with ancestor portraits, and an air of understated inherited wealth — from Diana-esque young women at point-to-points to tweeded men with shooting sticks and flat caps.

name: Snackwave
description: Snackwave is a mid-2010s Tumblr-born fashion and object aesthetic that wears fast food as pattern: hyper-real or cartoonish pepperoni pizza, burgers, ramen cups and fries printed all-over on leggings, tees, onesies and accessories, or parodied as fast-food logotypes and packaging. Its palette is the condiment triad — ketchup red, mustard yellow, cheese orange — on bun cream or pitch black, deployed maximally and with deadpan, anti-wellness humor. Recognize it by snack-print garments, logo-parody quilting and cup-label graphics, novelty plush and phone cases, and a celebratory, self-deprecating attitude toward processed food.

name: Social_Realism
description: Interwar (1920s–30s) political figuration of working people — matte earth-tone and ash-gray palettes, worn clothing and laboring hands, frontal or processional compositions of workers, breadlines, picket lines, tenements, fields and factories, rendered in oil, tempera, lithograph or documentary photograph with unflinching, dignified clarity. Recognize by muted umber/gray color held to a descriptive legibility, collective groupings of the "masses," and an explicit critique of power; separate it from state-heroic Socialist Realism, apolitical 19th-century Realism and monumental Mexican Muralism.

name: Socialist_Realism
description: The state-mandated heroic art of the USSR and allied communist states (1920s–1980s): academic oil painting and flat poster lithography that stages idealized workers, peasants, soldiers, scientists, youth and leaders in film-still tableaus of collective triumph. Palette of signal red, wheat gold and earth brown laid over muted naturalistic tones; recurring red flags, hammer-and-sickle emblems, machinery, sheaves, spires and open optimistic skies. Earnest, irony-free collectivist optimism — recognition hinges on painterly academic realism fused with unambiguous communist iconography.

name: Soft_Apocalypse
description: Soft Apocalypse (a.k.a. Apocalypsecore) depicts the slow, gentle collapse of urban society — brutalist concrete, skyscrapers, subway halls and bridges reclaimed by moss, ferns, ivy and rooftop forests, in a palette of green, grey, weathered white and light brown. Light is soft and diffuse; the mood is melancholy yet hopeful, and human figures, when present, forage, tend and travel calmly instead of fighting. Recognize it by living vegetation actively interrupting bland man-made geometry, with rust streaks and standing water as accents — and never fire, combat, gore or horror grading.

name: Soft_Boy
description: Soft Boy is a late-2010s Gen Z masculine aesthetic of gentle emotional openness — oversized layered knits, cardigans and overshirts over collared shirts, baggy cuffed light-wash jeans with white tube socks and beat-up classic sneakers, artfully tousled curtain or shaggy hair, round wire-rimmed glasses, and books, vinyl records or film cameras as props. Its palette is muted and matte: faded blues, dusty pinks, lavender, moss green and rust orange over cream, beige and warm gray, photographed in diffused natural light with a faded, grainy film grade. Recognize it by the slouched vintage menswear silhouette, tender unposed gestures (hugging a plush, holding a picked flower, hand at the cheek), and a dreamy, approachable, introspective mood.

name: Soft_Colonial_Wanderlust
description: Soft Colonial Wanderlust (aka Cheeky Victorian Revival) is an ironic Victorian-to-pre-WWII expedition fantasy, born in the late 1980s and peaked with the early-2010s hipster wave: sepia and muted browns on aged paper, engraved illustrations, cut-out collage figures, circus typography, and motifs of compasses, maps, binoculars, hot air balloons, mail art and carnivals. Recognize it by sun-faded paper-grain palettes, whimsical explorer subjects (mustached dandies, aeronauts, naturalists, circus performers), and a cheeky, wonder-struck tone that treats vintage technology as affectionate joke rather than steampunk machinery.

name: Soft_Countriana
description: Soft Countriana is the late-1970s-to-1980s suburban country-romantic aesthetic: cream and ivory grounds washed with milk-diluted pastels (dusty blue, blush rose, lavender, peach, sage) arranged as gingham checks, polka dots and hand-painted folk sprigs of geese, hearts, cherries and tulips. Signature elements are frilled nightgowns and Gunne Sax/Laura Ashley-style dresses, quilted bedspreads and quilt skirts, ceramic canister sets, wicker furniture, dollhouses, teddy bears and rocking horses, lace-trimmed windows and Victorian-revival trim, all under diffuse, shadowless daylight. Recognize it in cozy bedrooms, nurseries, country kitchens, pastel tea tables and catalog-style fashion shots that read as a suburban memory of farm life rather than farm life itself.

name: Soft_Girl
description: Soft Girl is the late-2010s TikTok-born aesthetic (peak 2019) of exaggerated, doll-like hyper-femininity: high-chroma pastel pink, lavender, peach and baby blue rendered in bright, overexposed, low-contrast "airy" photography. Signature elements are childlike accessories (butterfly and pearl hair clips, scrunchies, beaded necklaces), pleated skirts, oversized hoodies and fluffy cardigans, sun-flushed blush makeup with faux freckles and hand-drawn cheek motifs, and props like strawberry milk cartons, plush animals and Sanrio-style stickers. Recognize it by candy-pastel palette plus maximalist cutesy styling on young feminine subjects, selfie/flat-lay/collage formats.

name: Soft_Grunge
description: Soft Grunge (Pale Grunge) is a mid-2010s Tumblr photographic aesthetic of desaturated black-white-grey snapshots — urban concrete and crosswalks, minimalist white interiors, houseplants, case-less iPhones, classical busts and mall-bought grunge-lite fashion — punctuated by muted green or blue accents and sardonic Arial text or Japanese kanji. Recognize it by faded low-contrast filters with lifted blacks, monochrome grids (tile, crosswalk, grid print), fishnets and tennis skirts, and an apathetic, lovesick, minimalist mood. It differs from Sadgirl's warm vintage melancholy and E-Girl's neon makeup by its cool grey minimalism and streetwear status symbols.

name: Solarpunk
description: Solarpunk is a hopeful eco-futurist aesthetic coined in late-2000s Brazil and mainstreamed in the 2010s: sunlit settlements where buildings are wrapped in vertical gardens and vine-draped terraces, stained-glass solar panels and small wind turbines wear their energy on their skin, and Art Nouveau curves meet hand-mended workwear and cluttered community rooftops. Its palette is leaf green, sky and water blue, sunlight yellow and plaster white; subjects range from painterly vistas of sprawling green cities to greenhouse atriums, edible landscapes, repair-cafe street life and vegetated towers. Recognize it by lived-in, DIY lushness at human scale — never the glossy corporate "green" of stock imagery.

name: Song_Dynasty
description: Court and literati aesthetic of Song China (960–1279): ink-first painting on aged silk or paper, tianqing and celadon glaze tones, composed negative space, and quiet scholarly subjects. Signature elements include monumental misty landscapes or one-corner diagonal compositions, Ru/Guan/Ge/Ding/Jun ceramics, bird-and-flower studies (plum, orchid, bamboo, chrysanthemum), the moon, and slender restrained Hanfu such as the beizi coat and wing-flapped futou cap. Reads as clean, quiet and elegant — muted mineral colour subordinate to ink, matte jade-like glaze surfaces, diffuse shadowless light, and emptiness treated as a designed element.

name: Sots_Art
description: Sots Art is the ironic Soviet underground style of 1970s–80s Moscow that fuses the heroic grammar of Socialist Realism — leader portraits, red stars, hammer and sickle, bold propaganda slogans — with Western consumer logos and pop icons (Coca-Cola, McDonald's, Mickey Mouse, comic heroes) in a deadpan satirical collision. Visually it alternates between flat agitprop poster fields of signal red, black and paper white carrying heavy sans-serif text, and glazed academic oil tableaus in candlelit umber, ochre and gold that mimic state-propaganda finish. Recognition hinges on double-coding: official Soviet symbols rendered faithfully but placed in absurd, consumerist or self-subverting contexts, with the political figure — never the consumer icon — at the center.

name: Southern_French_Gothic
description: Southern French Gothic (Gothique méridional) is the austere church architecture of 12th–14th-century Languedoc — fortress-like single-nave preaching halls under wide barrel vaults, deep solid pier buttresses instead of flying buttresses, crenellated parapets, brick laid in geometric patterns, and octagonal tapering bell towers or wall belfries. Its palette is terracotta brick red, ochre and buff stone, and pale whitewash under hard Mediterranean sunlight, with dim amber-lit interiors; ornament is deliberately scarce, an ideological austerity born of the Catholic reconquest after the Albigensian Crusade. Recognize it in fortified church exteriors, vast unadorned naves with rationed light, and brickwork used as the only decoration.

name: Southern_Gothic
description: The haunted American South as visual language — humid, desaturated moss-greens and sepia browns, Spanish moss and cypress swamps, decaying plantation and vernacular architecture, above-ground cemeteries, fear-mongering evangelical billboards, and liminal roadside infrastructure shot in deadpan snapshot or aged-print treatments. Carries moods of isolation, religious guilt and the uncanny, from 19th-century literary decay imagery through the mid-2010s Tumblr "regional gothic" revival to the 2020s dark-country resurgence. Recognize it by wet heat, encroaching vegetation, looming religion, and ruin juxtaposed against the modern; never by urban club Goth trims or pristine period romance.

name: Soviet_Nostalgia
description: Soviet Nostalgia (Sovietcore) is the post-Soviet memory aesthetic of childhood in Khrushchyovka flats: wool carpets hung on walls, lace curtains and oilcloth-covered tables under warm faded film light, set against snowbound panel blocks and blue-hour winters. Its palette runs from cream, dusty rose and oxblood carpet-red to cold grey-blue snow, with signature objects like CRT televisions, enamel pots, faceted tea glasses, kosynka kerchiefs, fur hats and Orthodox icon tapestries. The mood is tender, unheroic domestic melancholy — an amateur family snapshot, never propaganda or pop kitsch.

name: Sovietwave
description: Sovietwave is a 2010s post-Soviet retro-futurist aesthetic born from the synthwave music scene, mourning and glorifying the utopian communist future that never arrived. Its visual DNA fuses earnest Soviet propaganda iconography — hammer and sickle, red stars, CCCP-stencilled rockets, cosmonauts, Cyrillic slogan blocks — with 1980s analog media decay: VHS scanlines, chromatic aberration fringes, dithering, faded print grain. Palette is anchored in red, white and yellow over deep space blue or amber sunset black; typical subjects are space-program hardware, Red Army parade columns, panel-house urbanism and monumental allegorical figures, all rendered with sincere melancholy rather than irony.

name: Space_Age
description: Space Age is the optimistic retrofuturism of the mid-1950s to early 1970s, built from molded plastic, fiberglass, vinyl and chrome in stark white fields punctuated by saturated primaries and orange, shaped into spheres, capsules, parabolas and tail fins. Recognize it by spacecraft iconography (rockets, satellites, flying saucers, starbursts), pod and ball chairs, UFO-like lamps, Googie towers and upswept roofs, finned cars, and couture in metallic fabric and PVC with helmets, bubble visors and go-go boots — all staged clean, glossy and shadowless in a mood of utopian technological wonder.

name: Space_Cowgirl
description: Space Cowgirl is a 2020s TikTok-born hybrid aesthetic that fuses American Western signifiers — cowboy hats, boots, fringe, belt buckles, cow print — with retrofuturist Space Age and Y2K gloss: saturated pinks, holographic silver, neon accents, disco balls, planets and glitter. Recognize it by traditional ranch gear rendered in metallic vinyl, iridescent textiles and rhinestone shine, staged in joyful, maximalist, artificially-lit tableaus, pastel studio sets or scrapbook-style collages. Typical subjects are party groups of friends, glitter-makeup portraits, kitsch roadside-desert scenes, and cosmic collages mixing cacti with Saturn.

name: Space_Western
description: Space Western fuses 19th-century American frontier iconography — wide-brimmed hats, long dusters, holsters, saloon porches, dusty main streets — with interstellar science fiction: starships docked like star-horses, rayguns, droids, and alien skies with twin suns. Its palette leans earthy dust (sandy tan, rust, olive, leather brown) against deep cosmic indigo and violet, punctuated by sparse gunmetal or neon accents, lit by harsh sun or alien twilight. Look for worn utilitarian gear, lived-in frontier outposts, and gunslinger silhouettes posed against vast rocky planetscapes.

name: Spacecore
description: Spacecore (Astrocore) is a 2020s internet aesthetic that treats the cosmos as pure decoration: stylized galaxies, rainbow-banded planets and pink-violet moons glowing against black or deep-indigo voids, dusted with glitter and four-point star flares. Dreamlike floating compositions, meteor trails, star-shaped decor and short existential captions ("who's out there?") signal its escapist, wonder-struck, gently melancholic mood. Recognize it by impossible candy-colored celestial bodies, digital bloom and sparkle grain — never by hard sci-fi realism, aliens, or true-color astronomy.

name: Spainwave
description: Spainwave is a 2020s Spanish localization of Vaporwave/Synthwave born on Reddit's r/spainwave, filtering Iberian iconography — Spanish Golden Age statues and literature, regional landmarks, vintage Spanish TV and advertising, political broadcast stills — through neon-magenta perspective grids, pastel VHS grading and glitch collage. Expect a fuchsia/violet/turquoise palette with sunset-orange accents, chrome or pixel-font Spanish typography, and an ironic, melancholic affection for the mundane Spain of the 1980s–2000s. Load this skill when an image fuses distinctly Spanish cultural subject matter with retro-digital Vaporwave treatment.

name: Spanish_Golden_Age
description: The visual culture of Habsburg Spain and its empire, c. 1492–1681 — tenebrist oil painting of saints, martyrs and courtiers in black velvet and starched white ruffs, bodegón still lifes and mythological scenes carved out of deep shadow by a single raking light. Its palette is soot black, earthy ochre-brown, oxblood red and retablo gold, extended in architecture to honey and rose cantera stone in Plateresque, Herrerian and Churrigueresque façades from Salamanca to Cusco. Load for Counter-Reformation religious drama, Spanish court fashion and portraiture, or Spanish colonial Baroque imagery; it is distinct from Italian Baroque exuberance, Dutch daylight domesticity, Italian Renaissance clarity and Gothic verticality.

name: Sparkledog
description: Sparkledog (sparklefur, sparklecat, sparkleanimal) is a 2000s DeviantArt-born character-design aesthetic of feral animal OCs in oversaturated, unnatural multicolor — rainbow-gradient manes and tails, clashing neon patchwork, star/heart/stripe markings, scene-hair manes, feathered wings — drawn in simplified, amateur anime-inspired digital paint and typically presented as reference sheets, chibi icons or meme layouts. Key colours are rainbow plus a grounding black; the mood is gleefully gaudy, DIY-proud and self-aware, with an emo/scene angst undercurrent that leaks candy pink even at its darkest.

name: Spicers
description: Spicers is a late-2000s Dublin teen subculture aesthetic built around flat-ironed, box-dyed mullets and heavy fringes in neon green, blue, red and magenta over jet-black or bleach-blonde bases, worn with Adidas tracksuits, shutter shades, bandanas and facial piercings. Its imagery is amateur flash-lit compact-camera selfie grammar — bathrooms, bedrooms, suburban interiors — tied to Bebo profile culture, Skins (2007), and jumpstyle/hardstyle/dubstep shuffling. Recognise it by the straightened spiky mullet silhouette with hard-edged colour blocks, tacky-loud sportswear, and a party-like, deliberately tacky exuberance.

name: Sportsbrut
description: Sportsbrut (Sports Brutalism, Corporate Neu-Grunge) is a mid-late 2010s graphic-design aesthetic that fuses high-octane athletic branding with Neubrutalist grid rawness: ultra-condensed stretched slab and grotesque type, bare-bones box grids that hero elements burst out of, ticket-stub/barcode/credential ephemera, and photocopy-halftone grain over a stark black-white-gray base blasted by a single neon accent. Recognize it by loud sports-merch energy — threshold-treated athlete photos, stacked repeat type rows, tour-date lists, logo badges — all conveying speed, action and raw kinetic hype.

name: Sprezzatura
description: Sprezzatura is the Italian art of studied nonchalance — tailored clothing worn with deliberate ease, from Castiglione's 16th-century courtly ideal to the modern menswear street-style canon. Visually it reads as soft-shouldered Italian tailoring in sun-baked earth tones (tobacco, oatmeal, olive, wine, chambray) broken by one or two calculated imperfections: an askew tie knot, an unbuttoned cuff, a jacket or scarf casually draped, a pocket square that deliberately does not match the tie. Recognize it by well-worn matte textures (herringbone, corduroy, flannel, suede), mixed formal-and-casual registers, natural asymmetry, and relaxed body language caught in candid daylight.

name: Spring_Aesthetic
description: Spring Aesthetic codifies the season of first bloom — budding flowers, flowering meadows, baby animals and fresh sunshine — in a palette of pastels, light green and earthy brown, frequently carried by a faded analog-film tonality with blown-out skies. Its imagery centers on renewal: seed rows, nursery pots, cut-flower baskets, blossom-canopied streets, picnics and layered floral fashion, all with a hopeful, tender, feminine-coded but inclusive mood. Recognize it by bloom-led subjects, soft generous daylight, and pink/peach/cream/lilac pastels set against young-leaf green and weathered-wood brown.

name: Spy_Fiction
description: Spy Fiction (Spycore) is the espionage aesthetic fixed by 1960s spy cinema and Cold War tradecraft — a black-dominant palette cut with gunmetal silver and signal-red accents, concealed gadgets and holsters, dossiers, passports and coded maps, black turtlenecks and tan trench coats or tuxedos and ballgowns, ranging from glossy manor-house glamour to grainy clandestine monochrome. Recognize it by the hidden layer: an ordinary object, garment or paper concealing apparatus, identity or intent, plus a tradecraft object-language (micro-cameras, thigh holsters, briefcases, martini glass) rather than crime-scene or drawing-room deduction cues.

name: St_Ives_School
description: British coastal modernism of St Ives, Cornwall (flourished 1940s–1960s, roots in the 1920s), fusing lyrical abstraction with naive maritime painting. A blue-white-grey palette punctuated by ochre, slate and sage; translucent overlapping planes, oval and crescent forms recalling sails, moons, stones and harbour windows, scraped matte grounds with graphite scribble, patchwork fields and flat quay bands. Subjects transpose the Cornish sea, ships, hedges, headlands and coastal light into flat, contemplative painterly structure.

name: Stargirl
description: Stargirl is a 2020s TikTok-born aesthetic that fuses Y2K revival fashion with Cyber Grunge edge and Night-Luxe glamour, built on a cool grey–silver–black palette punctured by sequin sparkle and an omnipresent star motif (star prints, rhinestone stars, star-shaped light). It carries music-devotion objects — vinyl records, cassettes, electric guitars, headphones, tracklist scraps — and splits into two registers: aloof club-night luxe (sequin miniskirts, sheer tops, dim flash photography) and chill teen-diary casual (star graphic tees, flare jeans, scrapbook moodboards). Recognize it by desaturated monochrome greys, metallic glitter textures, scattered stars, grainy low-light or paper-collage presentation, and small disciplined accents of red or gold.

name: Starrflesh
description: Starrflesh (also "Starflesh", formerly "icecore"/"coldcore") is a surreal early-2010s Tumblr/TikTok horror aesthetic of pale, flash-lit photo edits: white snarling animals, multiplied glowing eyes and star-shaped pupils, fangs, claws, scales, translucent jelly, shattered glass and icy water. Its palette is bone-white, glacier blue, mint and black void, punctured by blood red and holographic iridescent sheen, graded cold and grainy. Recognize it by lo-fi uncanny body-and-animal imagery that feels simultaneously calm, empty and raging — never warm, never painterly, never cartoonish.

name: Steampunk
description: Steampunk is a retrofuturistic aesthetic that fuses Victorian and Edwardian elegance with exposed steam-age machinery — brass, copper, polished wood and leather fitted with visible gears, cogs, boilers, pipes, dials and goggles, applied to airships, automatons, workshops and customized period fashion. Its palette runs bronze, brown, copper and gold through sepia cream and gaslit amber, lit by lamplight pools and shafts of light through iron-and-glass roofs. Recognize it by ornate 19th-century silhouettes made mechanically legible and hand-worn: never plastic, never chrome streamlining, never neon or digital screens.

name: Stickerbomb
description: Stickerbomb is a late-1990s to 2000s DIY maximalist aesthetic in which a surface is completely covered with overlapping stickers, decals, and slap tags from JDM car culture, skate graphics, corporate-logo parodies, and vector mascots. Its recognition cues are high-contrast CMYK color, black ink outlines, white sticker borders, Japanese import symbols, and a chaotic all-over pattern that obscures the original object.

name: Stilyagi
description: Soviet youth-subculture aesthetic of the late 1940s to early 1960s — candy-bright, deliberately clashing tailoring (narrow "dudochki" trousers or loud wide pants, padded-shoulder jackets, "jungle fire" or slim ties, thick-soled "manna kasha" shoes) worn against drab grey Soviet streets, with pompadours, ducktails, beehives and "venchik mira" hair crowns. Recognizable by saturated color defiance inside institutional drabness, promenading group poses, jazz/rock-and-roll props (X-ray "bone music" records, trophy lighters, pin-up playing cards), and a parallel satirical-print register of Cyrillic headlines and Krokodil-style caricature.

name: Stonepunk
description: Stonepunk is the retro-futurist aesthetic of a Stone Age pushed to anachronistic complexity — machines, vehicles, dwellings and even "computers" built from knapped flint, rough stone, bone, antler, hide, fur, woven reed and mudbrick, joined with rope lashings and wooden pegs instead of nails. Its palette is earthy ochre and umber, bone parchment, rustic oxide red, charcoal grey, mustard yellow and sparing earthy blue; its signature sights are mammoth cranes, dinosaur haulers, skull-and-tusk totems, rib-bone arches, cliff-carved megastructures and tribal engineer-hunters in fur, war paint and bone armour. Read it as "high concept, low materials": modern function executed in Paleolithic matter.

name: Straight_Edge
description: Visual language of the straight edge (sXe) hardcore subculture, born in early-1980s Washington D.C. punk: the black marker "X" on the back of the hand, tattooed, printed on merch, patches and pins; clean-cut Youth Crew athletic wear (band hoodies, varsity jackets, Vans sneakers, crew cuts and shaved heads) captured in flash-lit club snapshots, xeroxed flyers and flat black/white/red print graphics. Recognition hinges on sobriety slogans ("DRUG FREE", "IT'S OK NOT TO DRINK"), unity gestures (crossed arms, stacked fists, raised marked hand), analog grain and photocopy contrast — and on the pointed absence of alcohol, smoke, studs and mohawks that defines its punk parent.

name: Streamline_Moderne
description: Streamline Moderne (Art Moderne, Style Paquebot) is the 1930s–40s American machine-age style descended from Art Deco: aerodynamic teardrop, bullet and cylinder volumes with rounded corners, long horizontal "speed lines," smooth unadorned stucco or metal skins, glass block, porthole windows and chrome trim. Its palette runs from white, cream and pale earth tones through chrome and steel, punctuated by thin machine-age accents — cobalt, mint, butter yellow, oxblood banding, neon glow. Typical subjects are ocean-liner-like terminals, diners and bus stations, bullet-nose trains and teardrop cars, and hand-size machines such as radios, toasters, refrigerators and club chairs, all rendered with optimistic promotional clarity.

name: Strega
description: Strega (Italian for "witch") is a mid-2010s Tumblr-born gothic fashion aesthetic, an offshoot of Dark Mori and Japanese Mori Kei, defined by layered black-and-earth-tone garments — flowing dresses, brocade, velvet, lace, thigh-high boots — carrying pentacle, moon, sun and feather motifs. Its imagery is darkly dream-like: misty temperate forests, bare trunks and thorns, candle and lantern light, moths, black cats, tea things and stained glass, rendered in desaturated charcoal, umber, moss green and oxblood with soft grain and blur. Recognize it by witch-folklore signifiers worn as fashion, Pre-Raphaelite color, and twilight-forest atmosphere — darker than Mori Kei, fae-romantic rather than domestic-cozy, intimate rather than epic.

name: Studyblr
description: Studyblr is the 2010s Tumblr-born aesthetic of romanticized studying: immaculate handwritten notes with brush-calligraphy headings, color-coded highlighter blocks, boxed bullets, arrows and doodles on white grid or dot paper, photographed top-down in bright diffuse daylight with pastel stationery props. Recognize it by high-key paper-white frames, blush pink / baby blue / mint / lavender information color with mustard-gold or teal marker lettering, sticky notes, washi tape, spiral notebooks and hands writing with brush pens. It celebrates organized, shareable productivity — never old-world scholarship, darkness, or mess.

name: Suburban_Gothic
description: Suburban Gothic is the uncanny of American postwar suburbia — empty cul-de-sacs, strip-mall parking lots, diners, laundromats and highway signs rendered in washed-out whites, grays and cool blues, punctured by a single saturated artificial accent such as amber LED, red neon, fluorescent green or a pink-glowing window. Signature elements include deadpan text (handwritten notes taped to glass, variable-message signs bearing bleak messages), streetlamps and fluorescent light, picket-fence facades concealing dread, 60s–80s technology like box CRT TVs, and absent or lone figures. It reads as Lynchian stillness: realistic but stylized, alienated, quietly wrong.

name: Suburbia
description: Suburbia is the neutral, lived-in aesthetic of American suburban life from the 1970s to the present: single-family ranches, split-levels and neo-eclectic houses on curving cul-de-sac streets, manicured lawns, sprinklers, driveways, inflatable pools, strip malls and backyard rituals. Its palette is lawn green and sky blue anchored by concrete, stucco, brick red and beige siding, lit by cumulus daylight, golden-hour sunset or sodium streetlamp dusk, and captured in a vernacular snapshot or documentary register. Neither idealized nor critical, it reads as ordinary daily life — kids on bikes, sparklers on the Fourth of July, teens loitering at the mall fountain.

name: Subversive_Basics
description: Subversive Basics is a post-pandemic deconstructed-fashion aesthetic that takes ordinary staples — ribbed white tanks, little black dresses, nylon tights, baggy pants — and re-cuts them with asymmetrical straps, sheer mesh panels, keyholes and raw edges so the body's shape becomes part of the garment. Its visual DNA is a mineral palette of black, concrete gray, off-white and forest green, a tight cutout or sheer top set against enormous pooled volume below, and DIY upcycled texture (tights-turned-sleeves, exposed seams, buckled utility straps) photographed deadpan against pebble-dash concrete, in messy bedrooms via mirror selfie, or on flat lookbook backdrops. Load this skill when an image shows familiar basics visibly altered rather than worn intact.

name: Succubus_Chic
description: Succubus Chic is a 2020s TikTok-born fashion microtrend of vampiric, high-fashion darkness: waif-thin, androgynous figures in black leather, lace, velvet and sheer mesh, with center-parted messy black hair, thin or bleached brows, hollowed contoured cheeks, eyebags, smoky siren eyes and bold nude-mauve lips held in a dead-eyed stare. Its palette is near-monochrome black against porcelain (or occasionally tanned) skin, punctuated only by chokers, crosses, spiked metal, fishnets and small white accents, lit by hard paparazzi flash, flat studio light or cold cinematic blue. Recognize it against goth DIY, noir femme fatale and 90s heroin chic by its designer polish, its predatory-yet-fragile glamour and its refusal of any wellness-clean or cheerful register.

name: Sukeban
description: Sukeban is the Japanese delinquent-girl aesthetic of the 1960s–1980s: modified sailor school uniforms with ankle-length skirts, cropped blouses baring the midriff, sneakers instead of loafers, and long tokkō-fuku coats embroidered with vertical columns of kanji slogans and gang crests. Its palette is solid ground cloth — navy, black, off-white, royal blue, or revival pastel pink and lilac — carrying high-contrast vermillion, gold, white or black chain-stitch lettering. Recognize it by the sailor-collar-plus-maxi-skirt silhouette, dense vertical kanji on backs and sleeves, all-female gang framing, and a confrontational, flash-lit snapshot mood of feminist defiance.

name: Summer_Aesthetic
description: Summer_Aesthetic is the sun-drunk visual language of beach, pool and tropical leisure, rendered in analog-snapshot softness: cyan-turquoise water, sun yellow and coral pink over sand cream, filled with swimwear, hibiscus and plumeria flowers, cut fruit, cold drinks, pool floaties and candid sunbathers. Its mood runs from high-energy vacation play to wistful dusk idleness, unified by abundant natural sunlight, film grain and casual off-center framing. Use it to recognize or generate images of effortless seasonal leisure rather than posed glamour, maritime uniformity or liminal pool architecture.

name: Superflat
description: Superflat is a postmodern Japanese art movement founded by Takashi Murakami in the late 1990s that fuses anime/manga flatness, kawaii and otaku consumer iconography with ukiyo-e and Nihonga tradition and a satirical grotesque undercurrent. Recognize it by ultraflat two-dimensional color planes with hard bold outlines, candy-high-contrast palettes or deliberately barren beige grounds, big-eyed cute-creepy mascots and doe-eyed children, all-over flower/skull pattern fields, and glossy vinyl-toy sculpture derivatives. The mood is superficial cheer masking unease — cuteness deployed as consumer critique.

name: Superflat_Pop
description: Superflat Pop is the commercialized, kawaii-first offshoot of Takashi Murakami's Superflat movement that saturated late-2000s to early-2010s animation, video-game box art, designer toys and advertising. Recognize it by rainbow-saturated candy palettes set on white or pale grounds, strong black outlines around chibi mascots, smiling "sweet and sunny" flowers, urban-vinyl toy silhouettes, sticker-bomb density, and rounded bubble typography. Typical subjects are chibi character casts, vinyl figures, candy and fruit, flower all-over patterns, and logo-centric poster or game art.

name: Supergraphic_Ultramodern
description: Supergraphic Ultramodern ("70s Ultra-Modern") is the optimistic futurism of late-1960s to early-1980s set design, product design and environmental graphics: molded white, orange or single-hue rainbow interiors with coved curves, spherical and capsule objects, inflatable and ball furniture, and floor-to-wall flat supergraphics (concentric arcs, stripes, dot grids, silhouette cut-outs) in plastic, fiberglass, plush and shiny metal. Recognize it by shadowless slide-film lighting, rounded geometric sans-serif type, and a palette swinging between bone-white bases with tangerine/harvest/avocado accents and fully monochrome hue rooms; the late-1990s-to-mid-2000s revival replays the same rules on album sleeves and club interiors with cleaner print and colored gel light. Load this skill for sci-fi lounge interiors, expo-pavilion sculpture, sphere radios and pod TVs, and rainbow-concentric poster design.

name: Suprematism
description: Suprematism is the non-objective geometric abstraction launched by Kazimir Malevich in Russia in 1915: flat, hand-painted planes of pure colour — squares, rectangles, circles, crosses and thin bars — floating weightlessly in an unbounded white or cream void with no shadow, no horizon and no recognizable subject. Its palette is deliberately limited (black, white, red, yellow, green, cobalt blue, with occasional pale accents), and its compositions span a single monumental monochrome form to dynamic diagonal scatters of tilted planes. Recognise it by matte geometry adrift in cosmic empty space; it differs from Constructivism's utilitarian typography, De Stijl's orthogonal grid and Minimalism's industrial seriality.

name: Surf_Crush
description: Surf Crush (alias Coconut Girl) is the sun-soaked US teen beach aesthetic of roughly 1999–2008, built on hibiscus/aloha floral prints, surfboards and puka shell jewelry in a citrus-and-ocean palette of yellow, orange and blue. Recognize it by tanned skin in hard sunlight or golden-hour glow, halter tops and board shorts, cowrie shell chokers, ensemble teen casts on sand, and Myspace-era saturated digital gloss or poster/DVD-cover graphic design with brush-script logos. Load this skill for late-1990s/2000s surf-brand casual sport-leisure imagery — not for urban McBling bling, glossy Frutiger Aero tech utopia, or static tropical Coconut Girl still lifes.

name: Surfer
description: Beach-subculture aesthetic crystallized in 1950s–60s California and Hawaii from ancient Polynesian roots: teal-and-turquoise ocean, foam cream, sun yellow, sand earth tones and hibiscus pink, carried by longboards, palm trees, thatch surf shacks, vintage cars loaded with boards and tanned barefoot figures in board shirts and bikinis. Appears as sun-bleached film print, saturated tropical daylight, or clean mid-century commercial illustration; mood is laid-back community, sport dedication and escapism. Use when images or prompts involve waves, surfboards, beach life, tiki/tropical kitsh or retro surf culture.

name: Surreal_Meme
description: Mid-2010s neo-Dada internet aesthetic built from crude low-fidelity 3D renders (gray metallic heads, anthropomorphic oranges, low-poly creatures) and banal stock-photo cutouts adrift in void black, starfields, checkerboard floors or flat gradient fields. Its palette runs gradient orange, void black, deep cosmic blue and digital green across clean, smooth early-CGI surfaces, captioned in plain serif or WordArt-gradient type with deliberately broken grammar. Recognize it by the uncanny fidelity mismatch between collage layers, deadpan bureaucratic captions, and mundane objects (vegetables, cups, cubes, baguettes) treated as sentient cosmic entities.

name: Surrealism
description: Surrealism (Paris, 1920s–1950s, codified by André Breton's 1924 manifesto) renders dream logic with deadpan precision: hyper-real desert plains and interiors where melting clocks, displaced pipes, easels-that-hide-their-own-view, and boiler-bodied machine-elephants sit under even light and consistent shadows, in sun-bleached ochres, slate greys, olive and cream voids punctured by small vermilion or cobalt accents. Two registers coexist: illusionist verist dreamscapes and flat automatist fields of wandering black line with primary-color dots on dusty rose or sand grounds. Recognize by uncanny stillness, rational perspective hosting impossible premises, and authored paradox — never neon saturation, glitch decay, collage scrap, or snapshot accident.

name: Sweet_Lolita
description: Sweet Lolita (ama rori) is the most child-like of the three main Japanese Lolita fashion styles — knee-length, petticoat-poofed "cupcake" bell skirts in baby pink, sax blue, mint, pale yellow and lilac over white, covered in allover prints of sweets, animals, hearts and ribbons. Recognition anchors are a head-width satin hairbow, Peter Pan collars and puffed sleeves, lace wrist cuffs, knee socks with multi-bow Mary Janes, heart- or star-shaped bags, toy-like plastic jewellery, and hime bangs or twin-tail wigs. High-key soft light and doll-like posed or street-snap framing complete an innocent, storybook mood.

name: Swenkas
description: Swenkas is the mid-20th-century Zulu working-class dandy subculture of Johannesburg: migrant-labour men in immaculately tailored European suits (conservative black, brown and ivory or bold pink, red, blue, plum), brimmed fedoras, polished leather shoes and accessories such as braces, cuff links, gloves and zebra-striped socks, caught in held, choreographed competition poses ("swank"). Images pair sartorial glamour with sun-faded township backdrops — corrugated iron, peeling plaster, dust yards, shopfronts — in honest colour-documentary light. Load this skill for formally suited Black South African men posing with statuesque pride against modest urban environments, as distinct from La Sape, Skhothane or the historical European Dandy.

name: Swingjugend
description: Swingjugend (Swing Youth) is the late-1930s to early-1940s German youth counterculture of jazz defiance — long-haired boys in long checked sports jackets, crepe-soled shoes, showy scarves and carried-anyway umbrellas, girls with loose hair, red lipstick and penciled eyebrows, caught mid-lindy-hop or crowded around shellac 78 rpm records. Visually it survives as grainy wartime gelatin-silver snapshots: packed rooms with collage walls of posters and record discs, kicked-up dancing couples, laughing group portraits, in a muted wool-and-cream palette punctuated by lipstick red, deliberately brighter than any uniform. Recognize it by the conjunction of Anglo-American swing props, ironic film-star cool, and monochrome or faintly hand-tinted period print quality.

name: Symbolism
description: Late-19th-century European movement that paints dreams, myths, the occult, eroticism and death as veiled emblems rather than observed reality. Its palette runs from charcoal noir and muted sage-and-cream fresco tones to jewel-box gold, ultramarine and carnelian, lit by twilight, interior gloom, or a single supernatural glow emanating from halos, apparitions and pale flesh. Signature elements include hieratic solitary figures, winged or demon doubles, masks and hollow eyes, veils, cypresses, thrones and idols, and threshold spaces such as shores, towers and sealed interiors.

name: Synthwave
description: Synthwave (also Outrun / Retrowave) is the neon-noir retrofuturism of the mid-2000s French electronic scene, remembering a 1980s that never happened: striped setting suns over glowing perspective grids, wireframe mountains, chrome script typography, and wedge-shaped supercars on night coastal highways. Its palette is deep black, magenta, cyan and violet with a yellow-to-magenta sun ramp, rendered with a polished, high-contrast, cinematic finish. Load this skill for night-drive nostalgia imagery, neon grid landscapes, arcade/soundtrack homage art, or chrome-and-neon cover and poster design.

name: Tacticool
description: Tacticool is a 2010s hobbyist aesthetic built on modern special-forces replica gear — plate carriers, MOLLE webbing, high-cut helmets with night-vision mounts, and over-accessorized prop firearms — in black, olive drab, coyote brown and multicam camouflage, deliberately mixed with civilian clothes like jeans and flannel. Subjects range from airsoft operators and firearms hobbyists to anime "battle maids" and armed schoolgirls, all staged with pristine kit in studio backdrops, concrete interiors or urban night scenes. The look prizes appearance over function: redundant optics, scopes on handguns, and camouflage worn where it conceals nothing are signature tells.

name: Taisho_Roman
description: Taisho Roman (Taisho Romance, Haikara) is the Japanese-Western hybrid aesthetic of 1912–1926 Japan and its nostalgic revivals: moga in cloche hats and geometric-motif kimonos, mobo in bowler hats and Lloyd glasses, girls in serafuku sailor collars, moving through streets of brick Art Deco stations, streetcars, trains and telegraph wires. Its palette sets bright aniline-dye accents — vermilion, mustard, teal, plum — over cream paper, hand-tinted photograph softness, or flat sousaku-hanga print planes. Recognize it by the fusion of Japanese tradition with 1920s machine-age optimism and a romantic, briefly-liberal, faintly elegiac mood.

name: Takenokozoku
description: Takenokozoku ("Bamboo Shoot Tribe") is the mid-1970s–1981 Harajuku street-dance subculture of teenagers in voluminous, vividly saturated synthetic costumes — harem pants and shapeless jumpsuits in magenta, crimson, violet and teal, trimmed with ribbons, bows, sashes and fringe. Recognition hinges on gaudy color-blocked satin or jersey ensembles with wide kimono-like or dolman sleeves, group dance formations on sunlit park promenades and pedestrian crossings, portable radios blaring rock, and a deliberately unrefined, handmade-maximalist finish — captured either as faded 1970s film snapshot or crisp modern revival documentary.

name: Talahon
description: Talahon is the German-speaking TikTok youth aesthetic that went viral in summer 2024: teenage and young-men crews performing gangster posturing — shadowboxing, flying kicks, deadpan stares into the lens — in black tracksuits and glossy puffers accented by bootleg Gucci monogram caps, belts and chest-slung fanny packs, metal chains and chunky white Air Max sneakers. Its palette is red, white, black and gold over monogram beige, captured in vertical phone-video frames or harsh-flash night snapshots in mundane public spaces. Recognize it by the trio of counterfeit-luxury display, sportswear base, and confrontational meme performance.

name: Tanbi_Kei
description: Tanbi Kei is the Visual Kei substyle of elaborate European court costume — Baroque, Victorian and Rococo revival stage wear in wine red, black, ivory and antique gold, loaded with brocade frock coats, jabots, corseted gowns, bonnets and hair ribbons. It is recognized by porcelain white-face makeup with bright lips, teased architectural wigs, androgynous or crossdressed performers, and formal court-portrait tableaus set against damask interiors, gilded furniture or painterly backdrops. Look for maximal lace-and-gold detail density and a theatrical royalty mood; distinguish it from restrained Aristocrat, streetwear Lolita and period-accurate Rococo.

name: Tang_Dynasty
description: Court and Silk-Road aesthetic of Tang China (618–907): plump court ladies and fine horses drawn in smooth, rounded "flowing drapery" line on warm aged-silk grounds; sancai lead-glazed ceramics in green, amber and cream; gold and silver vessels with lobed petal forms and chased floral scrolls; and baoxiang rosettes, pearl roundels and scroll-grass vines set in gold on teal. Recognize by mineral pigment over tan silk, dripping tri-color glaze, radial medallion symmetry, gently sloped broad-eaved halls, and an air of prosperous, cosmopolitan confidence.

name: Tango
description: Argentine dance-born aesthetic (1880s Buenos Aires–Montevideo ports, golden age 1930–1952) built on a red–black–white spine: couples locked in close embrace, bandoneóns, red roses, cobblestones, milonga halls and Buenos Aires icons. Renders as tenebrist oil painting, grainy monochrome photograph, or flat vintage litho poster with worn paper and Art Deco lettering. Mood is tragic romance, contained passion and taboo sexuality — never festive or tropical.

name: Taqwacore
description: Taqwacore is the early-2000s Muslim-punk fusion aesthetic born from Michael Muhammad Knight's novel The Taqwacores: black DIY punk (mohawks, liberty spikes, leather, stitched patches, tartan) deliberately spliced with Islamic and South Asian dress (hijab, burqa, kufi, kurta, keffiyeh) and Arabic-script graphic design. Expect deadpan plain-wall promo portraits, flash-lit basement shows, and screen-printed posters in a palette of black, tartan red, acid lime or violet, and olive or cream grounds. Recognize it by the juxtaposition itself — band patches over a burqa, spikes rising from a hijab, a prayer rug under a band's knees.

name: TechnoNeko2000
description: TechnoNeko2000 is the glossy "cyber-moe" house style of mid-2000s to early-2010s YouTube/Niconico upload culture and Exit Trance-style compilation covers: 2000s moe anime girls fused with consumer hardware — oversized mechanical headphones, communicator headsets, cables and plugs wrapped into the outfit — framed by floating Aero-Glass UI panels, hex code rain, loading bars and speaker-stacked digital voids. Its palette runs from high-key white and periwinkle washes to saturated cyan, lime green and silver on near-black, with hot-pink accents, all rendered in high-gloss vector/airbrush anime finish. Recognize it by tech-optimist glow, hardware personification (OS-tan, VOCALOID-type idols), and rave-energy posing rather than cyberpunk grime or corporate sterility.

name: Technozen
description: Technozen is the mid-late 2000s Japanese consumer-tech aesthetic: high-key white and unstained light-wood minimalism accented with pale cyan and matcha green, populated by small boxy glossy-and-matte gadgets (Wii/DS-era consoles, clamshell handhelds, service robots, PDAs), UI-like rounded panels with thin gothic type, and houseplants or low-poly nature held in tidy balance. It reads simultaneously sterile-professional and cozy-cute. Use this skill when recognizing or generating images of 2000s Japanese tech product art, bright Muji/IKEA-adjacent interiors, casual-game menus and box art, or clean CG still lifes in that lineage.

name: Techwear
description: Techwear is the urban-functional fashion aesthetic born in 1990s Munich and Japan (Acronym, Nike ACG), built on monochrome technical shells — matte Gore-Tex laminate, ripstop, taped waterproof zippers, MOLLE webbing, magnetic buckles — cut into ergonomic silhouettes with high collars, hoods, face masks and tapered articulated trousers. Its figures are masked or collar-hidden "grey man" commuters and ninja-like loners on overcast concrete rooftops, parking decks and brutalist plazas, shot in flat, desaturated light with logo-free restraint. Recognize it by purposeful hardware, baggy-thigh/tight-ankle trousers, and a stealth palette of black, graphite, olive, navy and grey set against urban infrastructure.

name: Tecktonik
description: Tecktonik (TCK / Electro Dance / Milky Way) is the flash-lit French club-and-street subculture of 2006–2008: upright dancers with gel-stiffened mohawks and mullets, skinny jeans, fingerless black-and-white striped gloves, rhinestone or LED belts, and heraldic-eagle-and-pink-star brand prints, all on a black-and-white base pierced by hot pink, neon green and electric cyan. Expect harsh on-camera flash at night, flat daylight on concrete plazas and parking garages, low-res YouTube-era video stills, and Y2K vector flyers with sunburst rays, stars, checkerboard and diagonal wordmarks. Recognize it by the vertical, arm-driven dance pose with planted feet, the dark star makeup at one eye, and logo-wearing teenage bodies treated as both dancer and merchandise.

name: Teddy_Boys
description: British 1950s working-class subculture aesthetic built on the New Edwardian suit — long draped jackets (often with contrast velvet collars), high-waisted tapered drainpipe trousers, waistcoats, bootlace ties, crepe-soled Brothel Creepers and a flash of bright green or pink sock, worn with greased quiff hair. The visual record splits between grainy, overcast black-and-white street photography of loitering gangs among brick walls, iron railings and bomb-site rubble, and saturated early-colour studio portraits against flat pastel paper. Plain, sober cloth colours punctuated by one small saturated accent; thrifted fabric, peacock posture, defiant elegance.

name: Teen_Crush
description: Teen Crush is a late-2010s South Korean K-pop concept aesthetic that fuses Girl Crush attitude with High Teen preppy codes: subverted school uniforms, varsity lettering and sportswear clashed with cargo pants, combat boots and chains, rendered in neon pink, electric blue and acid yellow plaids and graphic prints. Recognize it by bright hair dye, chunky sneakers or Dr. Martens, glitter-eye makeup, sticker-kitch collage graphics, high-key studio or daylight promo lighting, and confident, bratty staging of young performers.

name: Teenpunk
description: Teenpunk is the commercial pop-punk youth aesthetic of the late 1990s to early 2010s: black plus hot pink on white grounds, checkerboard strips and Vans slip-ons, skulls softened with bows or hearts, star and paint-splatter stickers, fishnets and studded belts over band tees. Expect collage-scrapbook layouts, glitter-edit sparkles, angsty handwritten or stencil type, and messy spiky hair with neon pink or green streaks. It reads as mall-bought rebellion — edgy motifs packaged playfully — rather than subcultural punk or emo.

name: Teethcore
description: Teethcore is a mid-2010s Tumblr surreal aesthetic that treats extracted human teeth as isolated art objects — loose teeth arranged in ritual patterns (hearts, circles, pentagrams), capped into necklaces and earrings, or kept in lockets, music boxes and specimen trays. Its palette is muted blush pink, ivory and bone with small antique-gold or silver accents and occasional stark near-black grounds, shot in soft flat-lay or macro still-life with lo-fi Tumblr-era grain. Recognize it by the tooth decontextualized from the mouth and paired with sentimental, delicate staging: uncanny and anxiously tender rather than gory.

name: Tenniscore
description: Tenniscore is a 2020s fashion microtrend built from classic tennis apparel: pleated white skirts, piqué polo shirts and tennis dresses trimmed in court green, lime or navy, accessorized with visors, terry sweatbands, tube socks and diamond tennis bracelets. Its imagery lives on clay, grass and blue hard courts under hard sunlight or faded vintage-film light, mixing country-club leisure with sporty poise. Recognize it by a white-first palette, knife pleats, rackets and nets as props, and a preppy, luxurious, leisurely mood.

name: Teslapunk
description: Teslapunk is a retrofuturist microgenre branched from steampunk, set in a Victorian/Edwardian alternate history in which Nikola Tesla-style wireless electricity powers the world. Its visual DNA is copper-and-brass coil apparatus, exposed screws and glass insulators lit by jagged cyan-white lightning arcs and glowing plasma orbs, set against deep indigo shadow, fog, and warm incandescent amber; figures wear top hats, waistcoats, crinolines and goggles. Typical subjects are tesla coils, coil-fed weapons and vehicles, generator-cathedral interiors, inventor portraits, and characters channeling electric "magic" from their hands.

name: Thai_Modern
