description: Thai Modern (also called Thai Vintage) is the candy-saturated hybrid aesthetic of Thailand from the 1930s to the early 1980s — golden-age Thai cinema's colour logic of teal green, hot pink, crimson and mustard yellow, hand-painted backdrops and brush-script poster logotypes, rural rice-field and lotus-water tableaus, and Western-cut fashion fused with Thai dress. Recognise it by matte aged-film colour with cream-lifted highlights, staged romantic tableaus against painted or flat-colour walls, colonial stucco and painted-wood settings, and a sincere, melodramatic, festive mood.

name: That_Girl
description: Early-2020s TikTok-born wellness-routine aesthetic of aspirational self-improvement: high-key white, cream and nude frames punctuated by sage/matcha green accents and small fruit-colored pops. Signature content is the documented daily routine — healthy breakfast flat-lays, matcha and spa water, matching ribbed workout sets, organized bins and tidy rooms, gym/park/grocery errands — shot as candid phone vlog stills or labeled multi-panel collage grids. Mood is serene, orderly, optimistically productive.

name: Theatre_Academia
description: Theatre Academia is a 2010s academic aesthetic built around the study and practice of dramaturgy: gilded playhouse interiors, crystal chandeliers and red velvet seats under golden candlelight, annotated scripts, sheet music and playbills, costume rails and backstage rigging, dressed in tweed blazers, turtlenecks and period-costume silks in gold, red, black, grey and cream. Recognize it by warm gilt-and-amber light falling on theatrical architecture, rehearsal labor and costume craft — midway between Dark Academia's libraries and Romantic Academia's lace, but always inside the orbit of a stage.

name: Theriancore
description: Theriancore is a 2010s–2020s internet aesthetic from the therian/alterhuman community, recognizable by crude glowing-white "spirit edit" doodles (stars, hearts, swirls, exclamation marks, and the Theta-Delta ΘΔ sigil, typically stamped on the forehead) scratched over realistic wildlife photography, and by DIY paper-mache or felt animal masks with faux-fur tufts worn over ordinary hoodies and tank tops in low-angle, ground-level snapshots. Its palette is muted earth tones — moss green, charcoal, rust, brown, cream — with stark white reserved for the hand-drawn line-art layer. Mood: feral escapism, craftcore sincerity, melancholic autumn liminality, and masked digital anonymity.

name: Thought_Daughter
description: Thought Daughter (c. 2024, Pinterest/TikTok meme culture) is the aesthetic of the melancholy, intellectual young woman: cut-out PNG moodboards on cream and white grounds, serif and italic captions mixing elevated diction with internet slang, prestige book covers and philosophy tomes, cut figs and pomegranates, oysters and martinis, niche perfume bottles, black-and-white 1960s arthouse film stills of tearful women, and librarian-vintage fashion in black, ivory and jewel tones. Recognize it by taxonomic object grids ("top notes / base notes"), photographed poem pages and handwritten ink notes, and soft, unfiltered daylight photography of attainable daily life rather than heightened glamour.

name: Thrash_Metal
description: Thrash Metal is the visual culture of the early-1980s speed-metal scene — sleeveless denim battle vests sewn dense with embroidered band patches, bullet belts, ripped indigo or black jeans, white high-top sneakers and long loose hair, captured with faded analog grain against corrugated shutters, brick alleys and gel-lit stages. Its palette is black and denim blue punctured by small bright, often neon, album-art accents; its graphics are sharp weapon-angular logos and cartoonish-grotesque or politically charged illustration. Recognize it by the patch-collage vest, headbanging energy and DIY snapshot framing; it carries no punk mohawks, no black-metal corpsepaint, no glam gloss.

name: TikTok_4chan_Art_Trend
description: Mid-2020s TikTok aesthetic ("Lottie Clone", "4chancore") that restages mid-2000s imageboard and Flash culture as polished Moe/Cutecore digital art: chibi cat-eared OCs with four-leaf-clover hairclips, a "medical" pink and mint-green palette, maroon 4chan UI screenshots, rainbow WordArt and NEET shirt slogans layered as collage. Flat cel coloring, airbrushed pastel haze, deadpan ironic cuteness, and old-web artifacts rendered with modern fidelity. Recognize it by the clover motif plus pastel kawaii characters plus archival web debris in one frame.

name: Tiki
description: Mid-century American "Polynesian Pop" escapism born in 1930s cocktail lounges: dim amber light over carved wooden idols, bamboo and rattan ceilings, rope nets with glass fishing floats, hibiscus blooms, torches, and rum cocktails in sculptural ceramic mugs. Palette of khaki, olive green, warm wood brown, vermilion-orange flame accents and aqua turquoise, rendered as vintage photograph, mid-century cream-paper print, or flat bamboo-print animation pattern. Recognize by theatrical tropical kitsch — thatch, tiki mugs, hand-lettered luau signage, lagoon glow — never by bright minimalist resort tropicalism.

name: Tokusatsu
description: Japanese practical-effects spectacle aesthetic (1954–present): suited kaiju and masked henshin heroes in glossy molded armor with insectoid compound eyes, color-coded in saturated primaries and chrome sheens, staged against miniature city sets, smoke and pyro explosions. Signature elements include transformation belts, low-angle giant-scale staging, team color lineups, retrofuturistic analog technology and hand-built suit textures. Mood is earnest heroism, handmade wonder and monster pathos, from monochrome 1950s kaiju films to saturated Showa TV color to modern digital suits.

name: Tomato_Girl_Summer
description: Tomato Girl Summer is the 2023 TikTok-born microtrend of romanticized Mediterranean leisure — tomato-red linen, slip sundresses, silk headscarves, straw bags and espadrilles set against cream stucco, cerulean sea and olive green, lit by hard sun-bleached noon light. Recognize it by al fresco tables of pasta and heirloom tomatoes, tiled terraces, cobblestone streets and vintage Vespas, red-white stripes, gingham and majolica florals, and a curated 1950s Riviera escapism that is warm, red-dominant and sensually sun-drunk.

name: Tomboy
description: Tomboy is an identity-first aesthetic of girls and women wearing masculine-coded clothing — oversized shirts, boyfriend jeans, distressed denim, flannel, camo, band tees, sneakers and work boots — captured mid-activity in sports, outdoors, garages or gaming rooms. Its palette is neutral-dominant (black, white, heather grey, denim blue) with sparing saturated accents (red, green, purple, orange), hair is short, undercut, messy bun or ponytail, and a single feminine accent such as a gold hoop earring often punctuates the look. Mood is unbothered, free-spirited and androgynous: comfort, competence and worn-in fabric over ornament.

name: Too_Cool
description: Too Cool (土酷, "tacky cool") is a kitschy 2010s Chinese aesthetic that reclaims rural taste through maximalist digital collage — saturated teal, pink, red and ingot-gold, glossy skeuomorphic rainbow typography, Buddhist and folk iconography (deities, ingots, lotus, temples), waterfall and peony backdrops, and embellished qipao worn in performative, flash-lit poses. Recognize it by cut-and-paste composite logic with mismatched scale and lighting, horror-vacui layering of clip-art orbs, hearts, starbursts and vernacular Chinese text over studio portraits or poster layouts, and an unapologetically garish, ironical-yet-affectionate mood.

name: Torero_Aesthetic
description: The Torero aesthetic (Bullfighter/Matador Style, Tauromaquia) is the ornate ceremonial visual language of Spanish bullfighting, built around the traje de luces — a waist-cut silk and satin suit saturated in hand-sewn gold or silver thread embroidery — with the black velvet montera, the magenta-and-yellow capote and the red muleta as its signature props. Its palette is blood red, fuchsia pink, metallic gold and silver, ink black and albero ochre sand, lit by hard arena sun, votive candlelight or controlled editorial light. Recognize it by all-over metallic arabesque embroidery on a tight high-waisted silhouette, pink stockings, cape arcs in motion, and a mood of solemn pageantry, bravery and tragedy.

name: Touge
description: Touge (also called the Initial D aesthetic or Eurobeat Drifting) is a 2010s internet aesthetic romanticizing 1990s–early-2000s Japanese street racing: boxy JDM tuner cars, iconically the panda-trim Toyota AE86, drifting dark winding mountain passes lit only by hazy headlights. Recognize it by lo-fi VHS grain, scan lines and chromatic aberration, kinetic Japanese typography, and a night palette of deep blues and blacks pierced by white-yellow headlight bloom, with magenta-violet-teal poster/album-cover variants. Distinguish it from Synthwave and Cyberpunk by its rural mountain-road setting, period-correct analog cars, and degraded analog-video texture rather than neon city gloss.

name: Toyism
description: Toyism is a collective Dutch art movement (founded 1992 in Emmen) of figurative storytelling painted in flat, unmixed, high-contrast color fields saturated with hand-placed dots. Recognition hinges on hybrid bird-fish-insect creatures with concentric-ring eyes and striped limbs, crisp contours over split or banded grounds of magenta, yellow, indigo, cyan and red, dense stipple ornament, and a toy-like joy that hides serious contemporary commentary; masked anonymous artists and whole-object murals (gas spheres, water towers, hotel rooms) extend the same language into three dimensions. Load this skill when imagery shows flat saturated narrative figuration with dotwork craftsmanship, as distinct from Pop Art halftones, Memphis geometry, Neo-Pop gloss or painterly Surrealism.

name: Trad_Goth
description: Trad Goth is the original UK goth subculture look (late 1970s–1980s, Batcave-era post-punk): enormous backcombed black hair, matte pale skin with graphic black Egyptian eyeliner and dark lips, and black layers of leather jackets, band tees, fishnets and studs, patched and pinned by hand. The palette is black-dominant with bone-white, oxblood-red or deep-purple accents, typically carried on grainy black-and-white or flash-faded colour film. Recognise it by the teased hair silhouette that dominates the frame, the DIY punk hardware (ankhs, cross beads, mesh gloves, winklepickers), and the aloof, androgynous pose; separate it from Deathrock's bright dyes and veils, Glam Rock's glitter, and Post-Punk's austerity.

name: Tradcath_Coquette
description: Tradcath Coquette (Coquette Catholic, Conventcore) is a mid-2020s internet aesthetic that filters traditional Catholic devotion — rosaries, veils, crucifixes, Virgin Mary and medieval-saint statuary, candlelit cathedral interiors — through hyper-feminine coquette softness: blush pinks, pearls, lace, silk slips, bows woven into braids. Signature images juxtapose girlish sweetness with melancholy or deadpan irony: flash-lit veiled selfies, flat-lays of glitter-resin crosses and pearl rosaries, meme-captioned holy cards, crimson Sacred Hearts on cream grounds. Recognize by the pastel-pink-plus-oxblood palette, faded-film or direct-flash lighting, and the constant tension between reverence and play.

name: Tradwife
description: Tradwife is a late-2010s–2020s internet aesthetic in which a contemporary woman performs an idealized 1950s housewife — modest vintage-style dresses and aprons in soft pastels, floral prints and gingham, captured mid-domestic-task (baking bread, hanging laundry, serving a husband) in immaculate kitchens, gardens and porches. Recognize it by camera-aware women in puff-sleeve, below-knee dresses holding oven mitts, loaves or enamelware; soft warm window light or saturated mid-century ad colorization; and a serene, performed contentment. Two registers coexist: smartphone-era reenactment and mid-century advertisement/photo pastiche.

name: Trailer_Park_Princess
description: Trailer Park Princess is a 2010s Tumblr-born aesthetic that dresses 1950s–70s American poverty in hyperfeminine pink kitsch — trailer parks, run-down motels, truck stops and discount-store lingerie shot in washed-out bubblegum pink, cherry red and sun-bleached cream. Signature elements include vintage pin-up lingerie, plastic tiaras, bisque dolls and mannequins, kitschy religious clutter, guns and true-crime ephemera, all rendered in grainy flash-snapshot or exploitation-film screencap grammar. Typical subjects are young women in unglamorous erotic poses amid worn domestic clutter, deadpan object still-lifes of dolls and kitsch, and faded trailer exteriors, carrying a mood of nostalgia, unease and camp deviancy.

name: Tranquil_Serenity
description: Tranquil Serenity (Frutiger Zen) is a mass-market CGI aesthetic of the c. 2000s–2010s that renders East Asian meditation motifs — floating lotus blooms, stacked zen stones, glossy bamboo culms, mirror-still water — in frictionless early-2000s 3D sheen. Its palette runs from spa neutrals (soft sage, cream, warm beige, bluish gray) to saturated bamboo greens and magenta lotus pinks over cyan water, lit by diffuse high-key light with optional candle-glow accents and soft bokeh discs. Recognize it by perfect specular reflections, waxy translucent petals, polished pebble stacks, gradient skies, and spa-brochure stillness; it is the wellness-app and 3D-wallpaper cousin of Frutiger Aero without any technology.

name: Trap_Metal
description: Trap Metal (also Ragecore, Screamo Trap, Hardcore Trap, Industrial Trap) is the visual language of the late-2010s US SoundCloud rap underground that fused trap with metal and punk: black-dominated frames punched with blood red and at most a slash of neon, faces obscured by painted hockey masks, balaclavas or corpse-paint makeup, illegible blackletter and scratchy graffiti tags, distressed streetwear-techwear hybrid fashion, xerox-grade distortion and harsh on-camera flash grain. Typical subjects are masked or heavily tattooed solo performers, screaming fanged creature cover art, deformed scratchy illustrations, and DIY gore clay figures. Load this skill to recognize or generate nihilistic, shock-value underground rap-metal spectacle.

name: Trashcore_(videogame)
description: Trashcore (videogame) is the deliberately harsh aesthetic of the 2000s-onward itch.io underground: game screenshots and title cards that clash acid neons (lime, magenta, hot red, cyan) against dingy browns, greys and black voids, and cram crude pixel sprites, photobashed photo cutouts, full-bright low-poly geometry and broken repeating tilesets into a single mismatched frame. Recognize it by mixed asset fidelity, overcompressed JPEG damage, monospace HUD boxes and command menus, strobing hue-shifted patterns, and cartoonishly unrealistic gore; it prizes discomfort, absurdism and chaos over any polish. Load this skill when an image reads as an intentionally ugly, garish indie-game artifact rather than retro pixel nostalgia or clean low-poly minimalism.

name: Traumacore
description: Traumacore is a mid-to-late-2010s Tumblr-born edit aesthetic that layers confessional, childlike first-person text and wound-signs (blood red, sticker knives, censor scribbles, drawn-on tears) over faded pastel-pink imagery of childhood innocence — Sanrio-type characters, plush toys, porcelain dolls, angels, birthday cakes, dollhouses and empty childhood rooms. Recognize it by its two-layer structure: a soft, low-resolution, pink-white-cream nostalgic base corrupted by sincere journaling text and red/magenta accents, often inside liminal domestic or institutional spaces. It reads as visual journaling and coping art, never as pure cute decor or pure surreal uncanny.

name: Trillwave
description: Trillwave is the cover-art and collage aesthetic of early-2010s underground internet hip-hop (SoundCloud/Tumblr, c. 2010–2014): xeroxed Memphis-rap lo-fi, chopped-and-screwed purple/magenta grading, Greco-Roman statues and pools, jungle foliage dropped into digital voids, low-poly N64/PS1 renders and anime stills, all capped with Old Web Unicode typography. Signature DNA is a black/white/purple/gold palette, mirrored Rorschach symmetry, dithering and compression grain, and transparent-PNG subjects isolated on white voids. Recognize it by the collision of 90s Southern rap iconography (cash, lean cups, firearms, Pen & Pixel chrome type) with early-internet digital nostalgia and melancholy "holy" mysticism.

name: Trinketcore
description: Trinketcore (aka I-Spy) is a 2000s handcrafted-craft aesthetic built from odd antiques, buttons, charm chains, jarred collections, papercraft maquettes and star-strung bedrooms, lit by yellow lamp light over a muted brown-and-cream palette in which blues and purples replace black. Signature looks include dense seek-and-find arrangements of mismatched trinkets, stop-motion/claymation-style objects, doodled creatures on flat yellow grounds, scrapbook collages, and thrifted layered fashion with fluffy socks, patches and charm-laden bags. The mood is childlike curiosity, cozy nostalgia and gentle, glue-gun magic.

name: Trojan_Skinhead
description: British working-class subculture style of the late 1960s and its revivals, named after Trojan Records: clipper-cropped (grade 2–4) hair, Ben Sherman button-downs and Fred Perry polos, braces over shirts, Harrington jackets and Crombie coats, cuffed blue jeans over smooth leather boots or moccasin loafers, in a tan / forest green / black / white wardrobe palette extended by denim indigo and oxblood leather. Imagery is snapshot-documentary — multiracial crews on brick estates, in doorways, at dancehalls and ska gigs — rendered in faded colour film or grainy black-and-white. Use when recognizing or generating Traditional / "Spirit of '69" skinhead fashion and its Jamaican-music culture.

name: Tropicabana
description: Tropicabana is a late-1990s/early-2000s Y2K sub-aesthetic of spunky "island girl" maximalism: oversaturated sunrise-warm palettes (hot pink, tangerine, turquoise, lime, yellow), Hawaiian hibiscus and patchwork prints, airbrushed citrus and fruit decals, sequins, beads and bandanas over halter tops and sarongs, plus triadic-color tween bedrooms with curved sofas and disc curtains. Recognize it by deliberate pattern-clashing warmth, flash-bright or golden-hour light, tropical fruit and florals used as graphics, and an outgoing, playful feminine energy. It descends from 1960s–70s Flower Power and Disco filtered through Polynesian and Caribbean dress, and resurfaces in 2020s pop revivalism.

name: Tropical
description: Tropical (Island Life, Islandcore) is a warm, sun-bleached island aesthetic built on turquoise lagoon water, pale sand, palm and jungle greens, and fruit-and-flower accents of hibiscus red, banana yellow and sunset peach. Its signature elements are castaway and survival traces (shipwrecks, bamboo rafts, straw huts, hammocks, weathered rope), shell and cowrie jewelry, crochet and lei, Hawaiian shirts and flowing white resort wear, coconuts and cold drinks, and sea life such as turtles and crabs, all shot in candid natural light from blown-out noon to peach golden hour. Typical subjects are beach and underwater scenes, surfing and snorkeling, beachcombing and foraging, hammock naps, palm-framed sunsets and island still lifes.

name: Tropicalcore
description: Tropicalcore is an early-2020s internet aesthetic of hyper-saturated, kawaii summer-vacation photo edits and collages — neon-cyan water, bloom-blown high-key light, and digital sticker clutter (hibiscus and plumeria blossoms, four-point sparkles, bubbles, fruit cross-sections) framing dolphins, palm trees, pool inflatables and Sanrio/Nintendo/anime characters in gyaru-style beachwear. Recognize it by indie-kid saturation filters, glossy Frutiger-Aero water textures, and its moodboard/collage medium: it is a digital editing style, not a fashion or travel photography style.

name: Tropideco
description: Tropideco is the 1990s–2000s aesthetic of the commercialized fake tropics — indoor water parks, themed restaurants, resort gift shops and vacation-kitsch bedrooms rendered in oversaturated lagoon teal, jungle green, sunset red, bamboo tan and neon magenta. Its signature elements are fiberglass palms, tiki and moai statues, airbrushed sunset murals standing in for horizons, synthetic pools and aquariums, tiki-torch fire, and point-and-shoot flash photography with soft halation. Recognize it by enclosed, darkly saturated interiors lit only by themed colored light, glossy faux materials, maximalist prop density, and a nostalgic, uncanny "vacation as product" mood.

name: Truzzo
description: Truzzo is the Italian disco-rave youth aesthetic of the late 1990s–2000s: neon-saturated compact-camera flash photos of gel-hardened spiky or two-tone hair, plastic sunglasses, counterfeit-logo tees, animal prints, fur collars and chunky bracelets, crowned with a Blingee edit layer of star and heart stickers, pixel fonts and hue-shifted magenta gradients. Typical subjects are solo poseurs, bathroom mirror selfies and crew phalanxes in piazzas, bedrooms and discoteche, rendered deliberately low-resolution with Italian-language glitter text. Recognize it by the combination of cheap-flash lighting, neon-on-black palette, loud fake-designer logo-mania and earnest sticker-kitself decoration.

name: Trxsh
description: Trxsh (the Trash Gang aesthetic) is a late-2010s YouTube-born style built from high-contrast anime music video edits: a black-white-red palette, sharp-toothed "shark mask" grins, devil horns, face tattoos, chains, Japanese typography and VHS/glitch degradation laid over shōnen anime characters and masked streetwear figures. Recognize it by a monochrome base pierced by one acid accent, crushed blacks or blown whites, scanlines and chromatic aberration, scratchy blackletter logo tags, and an edgy, melancholic underground-rap mood.

name: Trẻ_trâu
description: Trẻ trâu ("young buffalo") is the Vietnamese Flickr-era street-teen aesthetic of the late 2000s to late 2010s: harsh-flash, low-megapixel mirror and arm-length selfies on tilted frames, bleached-blond or copper swooped fringes, tacky skinny shirts and bandanas, modified underbone Honda motorcycles and techno-party nights. Its palette runs from flash-burnt warm whites and cyan night casts to club violet-magenta and cheap hair-dye accents, frequently stamped with leetspeak teen-code watermarks. Recognize it by the mix of defiant flex posing (peace signs, cheek-to-cheek couples, outfit-against-wall shots), cluttered Vietnamese domestic interiors, and early camera-phone noise.

name: Tsuyome_Gyaru
description: Tsuyome gyaru is the "strong" pole of 2000s Japanese gyaru fashion: deeply tanned skin, bleached high-volume blonde extensions, extreme false-lash makeup with pale nude lips, and leopard print layered over black and gold. Signature hardware includes wide studded chain belts (the D.I.A belt), short shorts, fur or knit leg warmers and slouch boots, captured in flash-lit street snaps, mirror selfies and magazine scans. The mood is flashy, sexy, cool rebellion — loud "ora ora" confidence, never sweet or soft.

name: Tudor
description: Visual culture of Tudor and Elizabethan England (1485–1603): hieratic jewel-toned portraiture in satin, velvet and cloth-of-gold, starched white ruffs, gable and French hoods, pearl-encrusted pointed bodices over wheel farthingales, and emblematic symbolism (Tudor rose, heraldry, pearls, pansies). Recognizable by frontal, evenly lit, status-driven composition; deep crimson, royal blue, emerald and Tyrian purple set against black, oak brown and curtain red with gold thread; and, in architecture, black-and-white half-timbering, red brick, ornate chimney stacks and low four-centred Tudor arches. Use for court portraiture, state ceremony, vernacular Tudor streetscapes and prodigy-house interiors — not for Baroque dynamism or Victorian medievalism.

name: Tumbette
description: Tumbette is a TikTok-born Mexican fashion aesthetic (early 2024) that fuses corridos-tumbado streetwear with hyper-feminine coquette: an oversized motocross, baseball or basketball jersey worn over a lace or pleated miniskirt, with white tights or knee socks, ballet flats or platform boots, hair bows, pearls and pearl-studded trucker hats. Recognize it by vertical phone-snapshot outfit photos in domestic or street settings, a palette split between coquette pastels and saturated jersey team colors, gender-fluid casting, and DIY collage edits on airbrushed pastel gradients. Distinguish from Blokette (soccer jerseys, terrace casual), pure Coquette (no masculine anchor), Tumbado (no feminine pieces) and Buchón (luxury logomania).

name: Tumblr_Coming-of-Age
description: Amateur-flash snapshot aesthetic of Tumblr c. 2012–2018 documenting teenage friendship — group house parties, fence-climbing, late-night parking lots, worn Converse and thrifted fuzzy knits, rendered in faded, lifted-black film grading punctured by glow-stick neon. Splits into a rebellious group-night register and an angsty register of glowing sentimental text over empty rooms, abandoned interiors, and childhood cartoon screenshots. Recognize it by tangles of friends (almost never solo), milky desaturated shadows, instant-camera grain, collage-and-caption presentation, and unironic adolescent sentiment.

name: Tuscan_Rustic
description: Tuscan Rustic (also Tuscan Style, Old-World Luxe, 2000s McMansion) is the warm, earthy interior aesthetic of the mid-2000s American housing boom, modeled on Italian hill-country villas: troweled plaster walls in cream and ochre, terracotta and travertine floors, exposed wood beams, round stone arches, wrought-iron chandeliers and balustrades, and heavy distressed wood furniture. Recognize it by its burnished earth-tone palette (gold, rust, olive, chocolate), arched openings and niches, stone or plaster kitchen hoods, candle-style iron lighting, and its deliberate balance of rustic mass with formal, gilt-framed elegance.

name: Twee
description: Twee is a sweet, deliberately childlike indie aesthetic born from mid-1980s UK/US indie pop (C86, Sarah Records, K Records) and later codified by Wes Anderson's filmography and 2010s Tumblr fashion. Recognize it by unnaturally color-coordinated saturated pastels and bright primaries, dense vintage props (rotary phones, typewriters, record players, taxidermy, dollhouses), modest 1950s–70s silhouettes (Peter Pan collars, A-line skirts, knee socks, Mary Janes, cardigans, berets, cat-eye glasses), clashing polka dots and novelty prints, and flat, symmetrical, tableau-like compositions under soft even light. Mood is earnest, shy, whimsical and nostalgic — sweetness worn as a rejection of "cool."

name: Tweencore
description: Tweencore (also Justicecore or Mall Tween) is the maximalist mall-retail aesthetic marketed to pre-teen girls from the late 1990s to about 2014, built on hot pink, lime green, cyan and violet clashing in unnatural zebra and leopard prints, sequined slogan tees (LOL, BFF, OMG), candy-bead and silly-bandz jewelry, translucent butterfly clips, faux fur and pink flip phones. Recognize it by commercial mascot graphics, teen-idol posters and magazine spreads, "random" humor motifs (mustaches, tacos, cupcakes with faces), and bright, glossy, cluttered mall, bedroom and product-flat-lay scenes.

name: Twilightcore
description: Twilightcore (also Twilight Autumn, 2000s Autumn, Dark Y2K) is a nostalgic cinematic aesthetic built on the desaturated, teal-cyan-and-earth-brown grade of the first Twilight film: fogged conifer forests, rain-slick school parking lots and suburbia, overcast diffuse light, and layered late-2000s teen fashion (flare dark jeans, flannel, light dark jackets, gold lockets, chokers). Recognize it by muted cool color grading, wet reflective surfaces, mist and rain, film grain or soft handheld blur, pale melancholic figures often seen from behind, and a mood of romanticized fall, school-days and implied vampiric yearning.

name: UK_Drill
description: UK Drill is the masked, all-black visual language of the London roadman subculture born in Brixton in the early 2010s — balaclavas and ski masks, puffer jackets, Nike Tech Fleece tracksuits and tech vests, shot on grainy phone cameras under harsh flash or sodium-lit night streets. Recognise it by concealed faces showing only eyes, reflective brand logos glowing out of crushed black shadows, crew rows on concrete estates and train carriages, and a menacing, anonymous mood laced with flash-cash and designer-logo aspiration.

name: UK_Garage
description: UK Garage (UKG / 2-step) is the mid-1990s to early-2000s London club subculture whose look is loud Italian designer dressing — Moschino and Versace all-over print shirts (pound notes, clouds, baroque classical art), metallic lamé and satin with gold and silver accents, baggy designer jeans, bucket hats and tinted shades worn indoors, champagne flutes and fresh white Reebok Classics. Images read as 35mm flash party photography: harsh on-camera flash, saturated colour film, dark club interiors or red walls, glamorous multicultural groups posing confidently with arms locked or hands raised. Recognise by print density plus metallic sheen plus flash-snapshot glamour together, not by any single motif.

name: Uchuu_Kei
description: Uchuu Kei ("Space Style") is a 2000s Harajuku street fashion that retools Fairy Kei's pastel, childlike layering into 1990s-flavored space-age pop: a pastel foundation shot through with neon and cool blues/purples, metallic silver and holographic PVC/vinyl sheen, and literal alien, planet, star and rocket motifs. Signature elements include tutu and flared skirts over knee socks or legwarmers, shoulder rings and disc hardware, futuristic headphones or miniature space helmets, big messy candy-colored hair, and unconventional blue/green/purple lipstick. Recognize it by glossy synthetic shine plus cute cosmic literalism in playful, high-key, theatrical pop imagery.

name: Ugly_Chic
description: Ugly Chic (Kitsch Chic) is an early-2020s fashion aesthetic that turns deliberate ugliness into a high-status statement: clashing prints (argyle, plaid, leopard), awkward oversized proportions, and "sludge" tones of olive, mustard and brown colliding with saturated pops of cherry red, fuchsia, cobalt and purple. Signature elements include texture misdirection (heavy wool against tinsel trim, stiff vinyl, sheer synthetics), subverted footwear such as chunky clogs and tabi boots, and ironic runway-derived layering descended from Miuccia Prada's "good taste in bad taste." Recognize it in full-body outfit documentation — runway walks, street snapshots, mirror selfies — where the collision of patterns, textures and proportions is itself the subject.

name: Ukiyo-e
description: Ukiyo-e ("pictures of the floating world") is the Japanese woodblock-print art of Edo-period (1603–1868) urban pleasure culture: bold sumi-ink keylines enclosing flat, unshaded planes of mineral pigment on warm washi paper, in asymmetrical, obliquely projected compositions. Recognize it by Prussian-blue and beni-red on aged beige paper, bokashi sky gradations, patterned kimono textiles, claw-fingered wave foam, reserved-white snow, and calligraphic title cartouches; subjects rank from beauties and kabuki actors to landscapes, folklore and flora-fauna. Distinguish it from Japonisme, Superflat and Art Nouveau by its carved-print logic, limited block palette and absence of modeled light.

name: Ultras
description: Militant football-fan spectacle aesthetic born in 1960s Italy: monochrome technical sportswear, balaclavas and scarves over faces, concrete terraces and painted railings lit by flare-spark and club-hued smoke bombs. Signature elements are hand-painted giant banners and tifos, flags with snarling mascots and condensed lettering, masked figures straddling railings, drums, and "Against Modern Football" defiance. Recognise by collective anonymity, pyro haze swallowing floodlit stands, bold painted heraldry on creased cloth, and grainy high-contrast documentary night photography.

name: Ulzzang
description: South Korean selfie-native "best face" aesthetic born on early-2000s Cyworld: dewy glass skin, straight brows, puppy-dog eyeliner, aegyo-sal and gradient lips on a pale youthful face, framed by see-through bangs and oversized knits in cream, blush and dusty navy. Shot as soft-light selcas and mirror selfies in cafes, bedrooms and plain streets, it values curated innocence and approachability over glamour. Recognize by face-first intimate cropping, muted pastel-neutral palette, beauty-filter smoothness and effortless casual styling.

name: Unicorn_Trend
description: Unicorn Trend (Unicorncore) is a late-2010s Western consumer-media aesthetic that coats food, beauty, fashion and homeware in pastel rainbow gradients, glitter and holographic sheen, centered on a cartoonish sparkly unicorn with a rainbow mane. Recognize it by sherbet pink/lavender/baby-blue ombre, star sprinkles and edible glitter, iridescent film and faux-fur plush textures, clouds-stars-hearts accompaniment, and high-key dreamy flat-lays or flat vector cuteness. It separates from Fairy Kei's vintage-toy fashion coordinates, Galaxy Print's dark nebulae, Yume Kawaii's hazy dreamscapes, and Pastel Goth's macabre accents.

name: Uptown_Girl
description: Uptown Girl is an early-2020s, New York-born internet aesthetic of classic, tailored femininity — crisp whites, blush pinks and pastels, pearl strands, silk head scarves, plaid pencil skirts, Mary Jane heels and glossy lips. Recognize it by fitted, vintage-polished outfits, bright airy or high-key lighting with a film-like fade, and poised-or-frolicking elegance in city, park and boutique settings; it is the polished, brighter counterpart to Downtown Girl's baggy beige thrift.

name: UrBling
description: UrBling (Urban Grunge / City Grunge) is the mid-2000s street-grunge design language of hip-hop marketing, AAA game covers, TV bumpers and Newgrounds-era web graphics: flame orange, red and yellow over soot black, bone white and sepia, stacked with silhouetted streetlights, power lines, highways and skylines, paint splatters and drips, wings, crests, flames and tribal-tattoo flourishes, and slab, stencil and gothic type. Maximalist like McBling but sootier and masculinized, it fuses Graffiti Pop, Corporate Grunge and Kustom Kulture into one loud urban package.

name: Urban_Fantasy
description: Urban Fantasy places magic, creatures and portals inside present-day cityscapes — concrete towers, neon storefronts, subway cars and cracked sidewalks interrupted by dragons on rooftops, chalk circles in apartments, glowing orbs in dark rooms and fae in streetwear. Its palette runs loud and bold: amber dusk, crimson, neon signage green and electric magic blue set against night-shadow and concrete gray, with the supernatural always legible as a localized light source. Expect hybrid dress (jeans and graphic tees under capes, wings, crowns, fur or armor), crowds, worn infrastructure, and a mood of gritty escapism descended from late-1980s borderlands fiction and cyberpunk-adjacent noir.

name: Urbancore
description: Urbancore is the aesthetic of real, lived-in modern city life and 1990s-born streetwear: concrete architecture, graffiti-tagged rooftops, alleyways, underpasses, parking structures and skyscrapers, captured with snapshot directness. Its palette is neutral — concrete gray, asphalt black, bone beige — punctured by spray-paint brights (yellow, green, magenta, signal red) and night fluorescents, with baggy pants, oversized brand tees, puffer jackets, dad hats, chains and sneakers as the human element. Recognize it by used-city texture (tags, rubble, puddles, wear) combined with youth street-culture styling, in photography or flat/stylized render alike.

name: Utopian_Scholastic
description: Utopian Scholastic (Encartawave) is the edutainment aesthetic of late-1980s-to-mid-2000s children's encyclopedias, CD-ROMs, nature documentaries and museum graphics: bright chromatic daylight skies over airbrushed, surreally combined seascape vistas where monumental books, specimens, classical columns and early-CGI primitives float with gentle metaphorical logic. Its second register is the white-ground editorial collage of cutout artifact photographs under classic serif mastheads, as on DK Eyewitness covers and Microsoft Encarta boxes. Recognize it by sky-blue-and-cloud-white palettes with small saturated accents, museum plinth logic, checkerboard floors, piano keys, rainbows, mannequin heads, and an unironic tone of wonder.

name: VSCO_Girl
description: VSCO Girl is the late-2010s (2019) teen internet aesthetic of curated casualness — oversized T-shirts worn over tiny shorts, scrunchies on the wrist, sticker-covered Hydro Flasks, layered Pura Vida bracelets, puka shell chokers, Kånken backpacks and instant cameras — all rendered through warm, slightly desaturated, film-emulating photo filters. Its palette runs sun-bleached pastels, earthy sand tones and aqua pool/sea water; its scenes are beaches, pools, car interiors, drink-in-hand POV shots and object flat-lays. Recognize it by the branded beach-casual uniform plus eco-motifs (metal straws, turtle stickers) plus a sun-kissed, grainy, candid-looking grade.

name: Vacation_Dadcore
description: Vacation Dadcore is a nostalgic, kitschy leisure aesthetic codified on late-2010s social media out of 1970s–80s American resort culture: moustached dads in loud rayon Hawaiian shirts, aviator sunglasses and tan cargo shorts, lounging poolside, on beaches or at tiki bars with a cocktail in hand. Its palette pairs bright hibiscus red, turquoise, cobalt, sunny yellow and flamingo pink against beige, cream and sun-faded white, delivered through analog snapshot grain, 80s airbrush poster gradients, flat vector illustration or all-over textile prints. Recognition hinges on day-drinking rituals, palm silhouettes, rattan-and-chrome kitsch, and an unbothered "permanent vacation" mood.

name: Vampire
description: Aristocratic horror aesthetic descended from 19th-century Gothic literature, built on pale skin, sharp fangs and blood handled with elegant subtlety against a stark palette of black, oxblood red, ivory and silver. Signature elements are anachronistic formal wear (high-collared capes, velvet frock coats, lace cravats, corsets, silk gowns), candlelit castle and crypt interiors, bats, full moons, coffins, and a mood of tragic, predatory elegance. Recognize it by the fusion of nobility and predation: formal antiquated dress, nocturnal chiaroscuro or porcelain high-key light, desaturated filmic grade, and blood as a measured accent rather than gore.

name: Vanilla_Girl
description: Vanilla Girl is an early-2020s Gen-Z microtrend of soft domestic femininity built on a high-key neutral palette of white, cream, beige and warm brown, descended from Clean Girl minimalism. Its signature visuals are cream ribbed knitwear and wardrobe basics, claw clips and scrunchies, scented candles and vanilla-scented toiletries, rumpled soft bedding, wood and rattan, and baked goods such as cinnamon rolls and croissants, shot in diffused daylight as flat lays, mirror selfies, vanity corners and quiet café moments. Recognize it by matte low-contrast light, texture-over-color styling, faceless or obscured subjects, and a mood of mindful self-care; separate it from Clean Girl's sleek grooming, Danish Pastel's candy colors, Cinnamon Girl's rust autumnalism and That Girl's productivity props.

name: Vaporgoth
description: Vaporgoth (also Deathdream, Spookwave, Blackvapor) is the horror branch of mid-2010s vaporwave: black-dominant monochrome imagery rotted by glitch, scanlines and dither, lit only by phosphor green, CRT cyan or blood-red accents. Signature elements are corrupted digital artifacts, obsolete technology (candlestick telephones, cassette spines, low-poly CGI rooms), uncanny masks and silhouettes, and cryptic Japanese or block-glyph text set in album-cover layouts with vertical spine strips. Typical subjects are haunted transmissions, technological decay, surveillance dread and spectral figures in empty industrial or virtual spaces.

name: Vaporwave
description: Early-2010s internet aesthetic built from the degraded residue of 1980s–90s consumer capitalism — pastel pink and cyan washes, purple neon gradients, glitch and VHS artifacts laid over Greco-Roman busts, palm trees, dolphins, empty malls, Windows 95-era UI, and gratuitous Japanese or full-width type. Reads as soft, faded, collage-like and ironically nostalgic ("a memory of a future that never arrived"), never high-contrast or heroic. Recognize it by lifted milky blacks, dithered gradient skies, tinted classical sculpture, period corporate branding, and an uncanny, deserted-mall stillness.

name: Vector_Minimalism
description: Vector Minimalism (also called Vector-Flat or Neoliberal Vector Minimalism) is a 2010s design aesthetic born from Windows 8's "Flat Metro" UI and carried by Google- and Microsoft-era branding: flat, solid-color vector shapes with sterile mathematical edges, strict grids, generous negative space, geometric sans-serif type (Futura, Avenir, Helvetica), and a firm absence of gradients, textures and shadows. Its range runs from bright multicolor tile mosaics, icon sets and flat illustrated scenes to a warm lifestyle offshoot of fluid hand-drawn shapes, botanicals and line-art faces in terracotta, sand and sage.

name: Vector_Música
description: Vector Música is the late-2000s pastel vector aesthetic of the magical-girl and virtual-idol boom: curved musical staves sweeping across pink, lavender, baby-blue and white gradient fields, strewn with scattering notes, treble clefs, hearts, stars and floral filigree, lit by soft bokeh glow and sparkle glints. It is the soft, feminine branch of Vectordelia — smooth Bézier curves, glossy orbs and solitary headphone-wearing silhouettes instead of jagged ink splatters and stark black crowds — seen on anime idol promo art, back-to-school stationery, karaoke interfaces and rhythm-game backgrounds. Recognize it by the combination of flat vector music notation as compositional spine, high-key pastel palette, and whisper-light whimsy.

name: Vectorbloom
description: Vectorbloom is the early-2000s-to-early-2010s maximalism of digital vector tools: intricate flourishes, stylized flowers and hybrid natural forms "blooming" in layered swirls over dramatic smooth gradients. Its palette runs through saturated pink, red, purple, cyan, green and yellow anchored by black or white contrast grounds, applied to ads, album covers, logos, product decals and seamless interior murals. Recognize it by razor-sharp Bézier edges, flat fills with gradient-only lighting, and dense ornamental growth that wraps whatever surface carries it.

name: Vectordelia
description: Vectordelia (popularly "Frutiger Metro", also vector maximalism or abstract vector art) is the mid-2000s to early-2010s graphic-design aesthetic of crisp Bézier flourishes, ink-splat bursts, halftone dot fields and sunburst rays in a high-contrast CMYK palette (cyan, magenta, lime, orange) set over solid black or white grounds. Its signature content is solid silhouettes of dancers, crowds and DJs amid speakers, headphones, turntables and microphones, plus glossy gradient spheres, striped concentric circles, bokeh glows and arrow clusters, all layered into maximalist "organized chaos". Recognize it by geometrically neat vector outlines with digital sheen and translucency, ranging from a rave-loud dark pole to a pastel, bokeh-soft feminine pole.

name: Vectorheart
description: Vectorheart is the mid-late-1990s-to-2000s graphic-design aesthetic of The Designers Republic and the Wipeout games: flat, high-contrast vector planes cut by 45° and 60° diagonals, futuristic experimental typography, spec-sheet microtext, pictograms and machine silhouettes, plus ironic trademark-laden consumer parody and occasional kanji/katakana or anime references. Recognize it by its maximalist-minimalist poster surface — a huge flat signal-color field or an empty paper-white ground carrying one dense cluster of tiny data — in signal red, traffic orange, warning yellow, hot magenta, racing green or slate teal. Load this skill for album sleeves, game boxart and UI, club posters, pictogram signage and mascot art that read as printed vector systems rather than rendered scenes.

name: Venetian_Carnival
description: Venetian Carnival (Carnevale di Venezia) is a mask-centred festival aesthetic: hand-finished porcelain, leather and papier-mâché masks (full-face white Bauta, gemmed Colombina half-mask, beaked Medico della Peste, cat-muzzled Gnaga) worn with 18th-century Baroque and Rococo costume — corseted brocade ballgowns, doublets, black cloaks, tricorns and cap-and-bells — in deep jewel tones of gold, burgundy, purple, black and ivory. Signature elements are gilded trim, ostrich feathers, gems, lace and craquelure-glazed mask surfaces set against Venetian stone, lagoon water or damask backdrops, with a mood of anonymous elegance and licensed mischief. Recognise it by the concealed face, the period silhouette and the metallic richness; it is not Brazilian Carnival (bare skin, samba plumage) nor Clowncore (modern painted faces).

name: Victorian
description: Victorian (1837–1901, United Kingdom and Empire) is the ornate, morally formal aesthetic of historical revivalism: Gothic Revival arches, Rococo Revival gilt and porcelain, Beaux Arts stone façades, and cluttered velvet-and-fringe parlours lit by gaslight and candle flame. Its palette runs from somber black, umber, taupe and sepia through deep jewel tones (emerald, ruby, sapphire) threaded with gilt, with a permitted lighter register of pastel Rococo-revival dress; signature elements include corseted crinoline-to-bustle silhouettes, top hats and pocket watches, mantel clock garnitures, wrought iron, mourning ritual, and sepia photographic tone. Subjects range from Academic oil paintings and hand-coloured fashion plates to industrial train sheds, scientific paraphernalia, and densely prop-filled domestic interiors.

name: Victorian_Goth
description: Victorian Goth is the Goth subculture's restaging of mid-to-late 19th-century mourning fashion — corseted, bustled floor-length gowns in black velvet and lace, men's tailcoats with cravats and top hats, veils, cameos and jet jewelry — photographed against dull, greyed or misty natural backgrounds. The palette is overwhelmingly black with bounded accents of burgundy, plum and dark green; the mood is somber aristocratic elegance, melancholy as ceremony. Recognize it by structured later-Victorian silhouettes, mourning paraphernalia, matte low-contrast light, and costume-as-subject framing.

name: Viking_Art
description: Viking Art is the material-culture aesthetic of 8th–11th century Norse seafarers from southern Scandinavia: clinker-built longships with carved dragon figureheads and square wool sails, round painted shields along the gunwale, and sinuous beast-interlace carving on wood, bone, bronze and stone. Its palette is weathered timber brown and silver-grey, moss and sea green, tar black and North-Sea blue, with madder, woad and weld dye accents confined to wool, linen and shield boards. The style stages coastlines, fjords and harbours rather than woodlands, and favours documented historical craft over mythic fantasy.

name: Vintage_Americana
description: A 2010s-born nostalgic aesthetic that filters 1950s–60s American life through aged film stock — cherry red, cream white and denim blue over pastel support, sepia-washed or pink-teal split-toned, grainy and sun-bleached. Signature elements are diner chrome and neon, Coca-Cola glassware, cherries and gingham, classic cars on open roads, and pin-up-styled femininity with red lipstick, heart-shaped sunglasses and swing skirts, all carrying a melancholic, escapist longing for an idealized American past. Recognize it when mid-century consumer totems and girl-next-door styling meet faded-print color and dreamlike haze.

name: Vintage_British_Sportsman
description: The visual culture of British estate sport — hunting, shooting, riding, fishing and golf as practised by the nobility and their estate staff, codified between the Victorian era and the 1950s. Earth-bound palette of olive, moss, brown and honey-beige punctured by hunt scarlet and oxblood; tweed, tartan, argyle and houndstooth; waxed cotton, plus fours, turnover-top shooting socks, flat caps, Wellington boots, double-barrelled shotguns; horses, hounds, boot rooms, stone fireplaces and misty patchwork countryside. Recognise it by weathered, functional elegance under overcast light and a stoic, inherited self-possession — never polished newness, never minimalist modernity.

name: Visigothic_Art
description: Visigothic Art is the Pre-Romanesque visual language of the Visigothic Kingdom of Iberia and southern Gaul (418–711 AD): cloisonné goldsmithing set with garnets, sapphires and pearls (votive crowns, eagle fibulae, belt buckles), compact ashlar basilicas with horseshoe arches, bevel-carved stone reliefs, and rare, faded expressive frescoes. Its palette is a triad of gold, garnet red and sapphire blue carried on limestone grey, bone white and verdigris plaster; its grammar is heraldic symmetry, chi-rho monograms, vegetal-zoomorphic interlace and a solemn, votive religious mood.

name: Visual_Kei
description: Visual Kei is the Japanese rock-movement aesthetic of the 1980s onward: androgynous performers with towering spiked or backcombed hair in unnatural dyes, pale or shironuri-white faces with kohl-rimmed eyes and dark lips, and layered elaborate costumes ranging from black leather-and-vinyl harness goth to Rococo brocade princely coats to Harajuku-bright clashing pop. Recognize it in group promo lineups where each member carries a distinct color and costume variant inside one unified palette, platform boots, lace jabots, corset-and-harness hardware, and theatrical posed stillness under hard studio flash, cold monochrome grading, or flat patterned graphic backdrops.

name: Vulture_Culture
description: Vulture Culture is the 2010s Tumblr/Instagram/Reddit subculture of ethically collected animal remains — cleaned skulls, articulated bones, taxidermy pelts, pinned insects and jarred wet specimens — photographed as craft, study and collection. Its visual DNA is bone-white and ivory set against velvet black, bark brown and moss green, with tan fur, chitin sheen, glass jars and tarnished wire, lit in honest diffuse light as palm-up offerings, symmetrical specimen flat-lays, crowded curio shelves, scientific-plate grids or forest-floor finds. Recognition hinges on evidence of preservation practice (wire-wrapping, labels, jars, articulation, dyeing) and on reverence rather than horror staging.

name: Wa_Lolita
description: Wa Lolita (Wa Rori) is a late-1990s Japanese Lolita substyle that fuses kimono structure — wrapped left-over-right crossover collar, wide squared furisode sleeves, obi-style waist sash or bow — with a petticoat-supported bell or A-line skirt at knee length. Recognition hinges on traditional Japanese textiles (sakura, goldfish, fans, cranes, temari balls), kanzashi hair ornaments, geta or zōri footwear, and a palette drawn from Japanese dye vocabulary (beni red, sumi black, gofun white, indigo, gold, plus pastel print grounds). Use this skill when an image or prompt combines the doll-like Lolita silhouette with explicit Japanese garment citations.

name: Waif
description: Waif (also Girlblogger, Female Manipulator) is an early-2020s Tumblr/Whisper/Pinterest aesthetic inside the Coquette sphere: pale, milk-washed pastel photographs — white, blush pink, soft blue, lavender, beige, gray and anchoring black — of thin young women in baby tees, ribbed camisoles, sheer tights and ballet wear, surrounded by cigarettes, Diet Coke, pointe shoes, luxury shopping bags and messy or sterile bedrooms, very often overlaid with confessional, ironic captions in cursive script or plain grotesque type. Its signature is the text-on-image whisper format, collage moodboards, flash-snapshot grain or overexposed haze, and a detached, blasé, self-destructively glamorous girlhood mood. Recognize it by the caption-over-pale-photo construction and internet-repost intimacy; it differs from Heroin Chic editorial by being amateur, pastel and meme-literate.

name: Warcore
description: Warcore is a late-2010s techwear substyle that wears modern military tactical gear — chest rigs, cargo pants, combat boots, face masks — as exaggerated everyday streetwear. Its palette is near-monochrome black with olive drab, khaki and grey, its silhouette is strap- and pouch-laden with the face obscured, and its mood is intimidating, dystopian "aesthetic armor". Recognize it by MOLLE webbing, plate-carrier vests, balaclavas and mundane urban fit-check framing rather than camo, distressing or neon.

name: Wartime_Austerity
description: Wartime Austerity is the 1940s home-front fashion aesthetic of WWII rationing in Britain and the US: narrow wool utility suits and knee-length shirtwaist dresses with squared padded shoulders, small tilted felt or straw hats, sturdy rounded-toe shoes, and gas-mask bags on shoulder straps, all in muted browns, greys, olives and navies. Its imagery lives in government "Make Do and Mend" poster lithography, matte black-and-white press and studio photography, and sepia vernacular snapshots, valuing neatness, ingenuity and efficiency over luxury. Load this skill to recognize or generate rationed-silhouette, minimal-embellishment 1940s civilian dress and its propaganda-print graphics.

name: Webcore
description: Webcore (also Internetcore, Enacore) is a late-2010s/early-2020s internet aesthetic that reconstructs the Old Web of roughly 1995–2005 — Windows 95/98/XP chrome, GeoCities clip art and glitter GIFs, scam pop-ups and error dialogs, low-poly early 3D, pixel dither and CRT scanlines — rearranged into surrealist, dreamlike compositions. Recognize it by bright system primaries (BSOD blue, hyperlink blue, Bliss lawn green) over gray/beige UI chrome, system-font text treated as image content, and naive desktop-interface collage floating in abstract voids.

name: Weeaboo
description: Weeaboo is the visual culture of mid-2000s-to-mid-2016 Western anime fandom: mundane Western bedrooms, malls, lecture halls and convention floors saturated with anime merchandise — graphic tees, pin-crusted messenger bags, figures, plushies, waifu posters — worn and stacked incongruously over everyday clothing, school-uniform kawaii fashion and emo/scene leftovers. Its palette swings between saturated cel-print magenta and cyan, manga-paper black-and-white halftone, lavender plush pastel, and fluorescent-lit concrete grey, captured in candid documentary snapshots or old-web interface frames (CRT glow, forum threads, video thumbnails). Recognize it by clutter over curation, screen-print and halftone texture, and anime imagery existing only as printed, molded or stitched objects inside real Western space.

name: Weimar_Cabaret
description: Weimar Cabaret (Kabarett) is the transgressive nightlife aesthetic of 1920s–early 1930s Berlin and Munich: androgynous performers in tuxedos, monocles and top hats, vamp makeup with pencil-thin arched brows and dark cupid's-bow lips, chorus lines and revue tableaux in smoke-filled clubs. Its palette is black, blood red and metallic sequin over cream poster paper or sepia/silver-gelatin monochrome, lit by harsh spotlight chiaroscuro and footlight glow from below. Recognize it by satirical grotesque typography, Expressionist canted angles, garçonne silhouettes and a mood of hedonistic despair — a dance on the volcano — rather than optimistic Jazz Age glamour.

name: Weirdcore
description: Weirdcore is a surreal Tumblr-born internet aesthetic (mid-2010s onward, referencing late-1990s–mid-2000s web imagery) built from amateur, heavily compressed photography and primitive low-poly digital graphics of mundane liminal places — stairwells, empty blush-pink rooms, backyards, pools, parking lots — disrupted by out-of-place objects, black void rectangles, misapplied sky textures, sparkle stickers and plain system-font captions that ask incomplete questions. Its palette spans faded domestic neutrals and foggy greys against naive saturated reds, dialog-box blues, flat lawn greens and glitter pinks, all degraded by JPEG artifacts. Load this skill to recognize or generate images that feel like a found early-internet snapshot of a place that is almost, but not quite, real.

name: Welwitschia_Goth
description: Welwitschia Goth (aka Welwitschia Emo, Facebook Alt, Whimsical Emo) is the DeviantArt/MySpace-era digital collage and photo-manipulation aesthetic (c. 1999–2015) that fuses emo and mallgoth darkness with corrupted childhood motifs: cracked dolls, stitched plush, butterflies, bows, striped socks and lace set against blood red, magenta pink and deep purple over black-and-bone grunge. Recognize it by heavy Y2K filtering — vignettes, crushed blacks, script and sheet-music texture fragments, swirl flourishes, splatter stamps — and pale, heavy-eyeliner figures or hollow-eyed doll-children in dead forests, nurseries and checkered rooms. Load this skill for early-2000s amateur digital goth art, morbid-innocence imagery, and creepypasta-adjacent visuals.

name: Werewolf
description: A feral alternative-youth aesthetic built on lycanthropy as metaphor — the beast within, and the body changing out of one's control. Neutral-first palette of black, bark brown, wolf grey and fog, punctured by blood red, moonlight blue and rare bruise purple; signature motifs are the full moon, wolves and dogs, fur and animal print, bared fangs, claws, foggy forests and animal bones. Wardrobe is late-1990s/2000s "bad boy" alternative — leather and denim jackets, flannels, distressed dark jeans, combat boots, chokers and bone pendants — rendered in low-key moonlight, fog-flat overcast, or grainy lo-fi blur, with a secondary register of stark silhouette graphics and vintage anatomical transformation plates.

name: Western
description: The Western (Wild West / Old West / Cowboy / Spaghetti Western) aesthetic of the 1860s–1890s American frontier and its cinematic myth — muted earth-tone palette of leather brown, dust tan and sunset orange-red, wide-brimmed cowboy hats, boots with spurs, six-shooters, horses, cacti, tumbleweeds and weathered wooden saloon towns under hard sun or low golden light. It speaks through three registers: sepia cabinet-card photography, grainy filmic stills, and painted poster art, all carrying a mood of solitude, self-reliance, vigilantism and remembrance. Load when imagery combines period frontier gear, semi-arid desert or prairie landscape, cattle-town architecture, or gunfighter mythos.

name: Whimsicraft
description: Whimsicraft is the handmade folk-maximalist aesthetic of mid-1980s to mid-1990s art fairs, children's television sets and outsider-art environments — saturated fuchsia, lapis lazuli, lilac and matte gold layered over patchwork, polka dots and mosaic, with painted suns and crescent moons on hand-built furniture and junk-art assemblages of kitchen metal and scrap wood. Typical subjects are cluttered craft-filled interiors, painted folk facades and roadside art environments, quirky-aunt wardrobes of graphic sweaters and handmade jewelry, and wobbly hand-lettered title cards and shop signs. Recognize it by visible amateur handwork everywhere, pattern-on-pattern density, festive string lights, and childlike wonder played completely straight.

name: Whimsigothic
description: Whimsigothic (Whimsigoth) is a late-1980s–1990s interior, fashion and album-art aesthetic that fuses gothic-revival darkness with playful celestial whimsy — deep blues, plums and jewel tones lit by candle-amber string lights, stained glass and taper flames. Signature elements are moon-and-sun faces, stars, velvet and lace layering, curved Victorian-inspired furniture, wrought iron, trailing plants, and maximalist clutter of mismatched vintage trinkets. Typical subjects: cozy nocturnal rooms and alcoves, witchy layered fashion and kitschy gold jewelry, trinket still lifes, and ornate calligraphic album or poster art featuring supernatural beings.

name: Whimsy_Twee
description: Whimsy Twee (aka Applecore) is a mid-2020s TikTok-born maximalist revival of Twee: clashing swirls, polka dots, stripes, gingham and checkerboard in bright primaries plus purple and green, layered thrifted garments, patterned tights under chunky buckled shoes, Mod doll-eye makeup, and handmade felt, crochet and button crafts. Apples, suns, moons, stars, animals and children's-book creatures recur as prints, props and crafts, presented in snapshot-bright, collage-dense frames. Load this skill when an image pairs vintage craft sincerity and childlike wonder with 2020s maximalist layering rather than muted 2010s Twee quietness.

name: Winter_Aesthetic
description: Winter Aesthetic (also "Romanticized Winter" or "Wintercore") is a 2010s lifestyle and photography trend that curates the cold season into a hygge-derived dialogue between freezing outdoors and warm indoors. Its visual DNA is a cooled, desaturated base of snow white, ice blue, silver and grey, anchored by warm neutrals (cream, beige, aged wood) and small festive accents of deep red or forest green, carrying motifs of falling snow, chunky knits, fireplaces, candles, steaming cocoa, frost-laden pines and fairy lights. Recognize it by matte, grainy, soft-lit photographs with intimate crops — hands around a mug, a lone figure in a quiet snowed street, a glowing window in blue dusk — and a mood of slowness, mindfulness and quiet magic.

name: Winter_Bimbo
description: Winter Bimbo (also Winter Fairy Coquette) is an early-2020s TikTok-born fashion aesthetic that pairs bulky faux-fur winter gear — ushanka hats, plush earmuffs, slouched knit leg warmers, fur coats — with deliberate exposure: corsets, miniskirts and bare thighs set against snow. Its palette is white, cream, beige and ice pastels, photographed in idealized snowy forests or high-key white interiors under soft, overcast snow-glare. Recognize it by the cozy-versus-bare silhouette contrast, ribbon-laced coquette detailing, doll-like glamour and a romanticized, deliberately impractical cold.

name: Wishcore
description: Wishcore is a 2020s fan-born K-pop deco aesthetic derived from NCT Wish branding: whisper-pastel pink, light blue and cream carrying star, crescent-moon, treble-clef and clover charms, plush mascots, cupid wings and holographic glimmer. Recognize it by small customized objects (charm-laden bags, deco phone cases, photocard toploaders, keychains), soft fluffy textures, overexposed hazy snapshot lighting, and sticker or pixel-doodle overlays that voice quiet wishfulness and a desire to be protected rather than bold display.

name: Witch_House
description: Witch House is the late-2000s internet-born occult electronic microgenre aesthetic: grainy, lo-fi, found-footage imagery soaked in black and desaturated cold tones, punctured by dark red, purple and blue, and stamped with triangles, inverted crosses and obfuscated Unicode glyphs. Typical subjects are hooded or all-black streetwear figures in cemeteries, dim churches, playgrounds and glitched digital collages, alongside animal skulls, mirrored symmetry, tapestries and VHS-grade noise. Recognize it by the fusion of DIY deep-web degradation, occult sigils and goth-streetwear fashion; distinguish it from neon Trillwave, cozy Witchcore, aquatic Seapunk and polished Nu-Goth.

name: Witchcore
description: Witchcore is the internet-born aesthetic of modern witchcraft practice (Witchblr, Witch Tok, "Witches of Instagram"): candlelit altars of crystals, tarot cards and leather-bound grimoires, hanging bundles of dried herbs, potion bottles and glass terrariums, wide-brimmed hats, velvet and lace. Its palette anchors in black, deep green and plum purple lit by candle-amber, gold and silver accents, with a secondary pale dried-botanical branch; the mood is intimate, mystical and empowering rather than horrific.

name: Wixa
description: Wixa (Vixa, Wixapol, "Polish Neo-Gabber") is a Polish club subculture — late-1990s hardcore/trance original, 2010s WIXAPOL S.A. revival — whose visual language fuses Dresiarz tracksuits and football-ultras scarves with rave fluorescents and cybersigil thorn prints, on a core palette of black, white and acid yellow with neon magenta, green and blue accents. Recognize it by harsh compact-flash snapshots in clubs and concrete stairwells, deadpan group poses on overcast football pitches, letterboxed video stills with all-caps pixel text, subverted smiley/tribal logos, and a post-shame, ironic, deliberately "bad taste" mood.

name: Wizardcore
description: Wizardcore is a 2010s internet aesthetic of wizardly magic and scholarly discovery — leather-bound grimoires, gnarled staffs, cloaks and pointed hats, crystal balls and glass baubles, candles and weathered maps gathered in dim, candlelit clutter. Its palette grounds black, gray and leather brown in deep purple, navy, forest green and dark red, lit by candle-amber or spectral teal-magenta glow, with silver star-and-moon embroidery on velvet as a recurring ornament. Subjects range from bearded sages, modern practitioners and cartoon animal wizards to curiosity shelves, potion bottles, familiars and handmade glittery figurines, all carrying a mood of wise, whimsical study.

name: Wonderland
description: Wonderland is the surreal Victorian storybook aesthetic descended from Lewis Carroll's Alice books (1865) and their illustration and film legacy: muted sepia, cream and light-brown grounds punctured by cardinal red, alice blue and stark black-and-white checker contrast, populated by pocket watches, playing cards, tea sets, white rabbits, keyholes, mirrors and overgrown hedge mazes. Recognize it by dream-logic scale paradoxes, threshold motifs (locked doors, holes, mirrors, corridors), pinafores, Mary Janes and top hats, and a mood suspended between playful nonsense and quiet uncanny dread.

name: Wonyoungism
description: Wonyoungism is a 2020s TikTok-born, hyper-feminine self-improvement aesthetic built around K-pop idol Jang Wonyoung: pastel pink, white and cream worlds of skincare rituals, pilates, study desks and luxury beauty products (Miu Miu, Dior, Innisfree), trimmed with coquette bows, pearls and tiara headbands. Recognize it by high-key dreamy lighting, glossy K-beauty skin and mirror-shine "glass hair," satin-knit-lace textures, and collage-style motivation posters carrying affirmations like "confidence" or "I was born worthy." It reads as "That Girl" productivity filtered through coquette softness and K-pop fandom gloss.

name: Wuxia
description: Wuxia is the aesthetic of Chinese martial-hero fiction — swordsmen and wanderers in layered cross-collared hanfu robes moving through mist-shrouded bamboo forests, snowy peaks, desert inns and ink-wash riverscapes. Its palette runs through rice-paper white, ink black, cinnabar red, malachite teal and ochre tan, with red-tasseled jian swords, bamboo li hats, flowing sleeves and vertical calligraphy as signature elements. The mood blends chivalric resolve with Daoist effortless wandering, expressed through balletic qing-gong movement and Chinese-painting negative space.

name: XO
description: XO is the blacked-out party-aftermath aesthetic of The Weeknd's early-2010s mixtapes (House of Balloons, Thursday, Echoes of Silence): grainy, scratched, high-contrast black-and-white snapshots of balloons, confetti litter, bathtubs, household furniture and liminal corridors, with faces hidden and highlights blown by harsh flash. Its signature moves are party supplies twisted into funerary debris, cropped arms and legs, amateur mirror and light-leak edits, and plain Helvetica Bold type. The mood is numb detachment, addiction and self-loathing documented coldly, never glamorized.

name: Xpiritualism
description: Xpiritualism is an internet outsider-art aesthetic of dense digital collage (early-2010s origins, codified in the 2020s) that fuses early-2000s web debris — spam-ad gloss, "Unregistered Hypercam" screen captures, bootleg Flash-game and anime visual-novel sprites, medical diagrams, software UI chrome — with New Age esoterica: halos, angels, love-spell and miracle-cure testimonials, numerological sigils like 1616 and 8888. Its palette swings between hot magenta/crimson/electric-blue spam saturation and overexposed pastel halo-glow, all degraded by JPEG compression, glitter clipart and garbled multilingual Unicode text. Recognize it by hard-edged cutout layering with no shared perspective, clashing WordArt-versus-cursive typography, scam-landing-page layouts, and an uncanny, sincerely mystical rather than ironic mood.

name: Y2K_Futurism
description: Y2K Futurism (Cyber Y2K, Kaybug) is the techno-utopian visual language of roughly 1997–2004: cool fields of icy blue, chrome silver, glossy white and black, punctured by lime-green or bright-orange accents; liquid-metal 3D "blobs," translucent tinted plastic hardware, sleek techno typography and futuristic interface framing. Typical subjects are cyber-armor pop performers in spaceship-like sets, early-CGI abstract renders, console and UI menus, broadcast idents, and aerodynamic product design. Load this skill to recognize or generate millennium-optimist chrome-and-blue futurism and to keep it distinct from Bling Era, Bubblegum Dance, Chromecore and 90s Cool.

name: Y3K
description: Y3K ("Year 3000", meta fashion / digital clothing) is a 2020s East-Asian-born, K-pop-propelled futuristic fashion aesthetic built on chrome and holographic "second-skin" bodies, bug-eyed mirrored sunglasses, exoskeleton-like metal hardware coiling around dressed figures, glitch overlays and avatar concepts, staged in cold high-key voids or neon-lit blackness. Recognize it by metallic silver plus glossy black plus iridescent or neon accents, luminous alien-like skin, render-perfect digital finish, and sculptural liquid-metal structures worn by or orbiting the body. It is colder and more refined than Y2K nostalgia, cleaner than cyberpunk grit, and more fashion-bound than flat black cybersigilist tribalism.

name: Yabi
description: Yabi is the maximalist collage aesthetic of China's Gen-Z underground (Shanghai/Beijing club circuits, c. 2019), stacking goth, cybergoth, gyaru, kawaii, punk, Y2K and Chinese kitsch fragments into one deliberately clashing outfit. Recognize it by black-neon-pastel-metallic color collisions, ripped tights and fur leg warmers, chunky platforms, over-ear headphones or vintage handheld consoles, neon or pastel dyed hair, and lo-fi flash photography with blur filters, tilted angles and sticker overlays that radiate spiritual ennui. Load this skill when an image or brief combines extreme mix-and-match layering with Chinese digital-native snapshot degradation.

name: Yabujincore
description: Yabujincore (Jumpstylecore) is a satirical TikTok shitpost aesthetic from 2021 onward that stacks low-res jumpstyle/Roblox dance footage, scrolling Arabic, Cyrillic and Japanese text, cursed 2000s meme faces (Epic Face, Trollface), stretched anime girls and Christian crosses over bit-crushed post-Soviet winter scenery. Its visual DNA is a two-register clash: a degraded, bleached, Matrix-green or winter-blue found-footage base pierced by crisp, flat, saturated overlays — alarm-red type, neon magenta halos, emoji-yellow stickers, MS-Paint line art. Recognize it by the formula of jerky dance motion plus nonsensical multilingual text plus cursed meme faces plus deliberate compression damage.

name: Yakuza_Aesthetic
description: A media-born Japanese organized-crime style built on visual duality — sober tailored suits in black, white and charcoal concealing full-body irezumi tattoos of dragons, tigers, koi and oni in vivid folklore color. Lit by hard shadow, grainy monochrome, or the red-and-magenta neon of Tokyo entertainment districts, with katana, dark sunglasses and gold jewelry as recurring props. Spans Showa-era film grain to glossy neon game renders; mood of intimidating calm, hidden artistry and ritualized honor.

name: Yallternative
description: Yallternative (Y'allternative) is a 2010s US Southern internet-born aesthetic that fuses country-western workwear — cowboy hats, denim in every cut, rodeo buckles, cowboy boots, turquoise and silver — with goth/emo black, winged dark makeup, dyed hair, fishnets and band tees. Recognize it by black-anchored outfits holding rural Western hardware in deliberate tension with alternative grooming, documented as casual vertical snapshots on porches, stairwells, barns, gates and rural yards. Palette: black, denim blue, cool silver, turquoise.

name: Yami_Kawaii
description: Yami Kawaii ("sickly cute," yamikawa) is a 2010s Japanese aesthetic and Harajuku-born fashion mode that fuses shoujo-anime cuteness with explicit mental-anguish iconography: pills, syringes, bandages, eye patches, stylized razors and nooses, and cynical Japanese text over black, deep purple, hot pink and lavender. Recognize it by its duality rule — pastel kawaii accents carrying morbid medical motifs, under-eye blush makeup, and vent-art prints on dark casual clothing — always stylized, never gory.

name: Yandere
description: Yandere (Yanderecore) is a 2000s-born, anime-rooted aesthetic of obsessive love turned menace, built on the juxtaposition of cute and disturbing: bubblegum pink, blood red, black and white; pink or heart-shaped knives, stylized splatter, heart-eyed or shadow-eyed "yandere faces," and handwritten or repeating possessive text ("I love you just a little too much," "you're mine"). Typical subjects are anime screencap edits, pink-tinted manga panels, flat pastel graphics and devotion-note still lifes in which hearts, blades and threats share one frame. Load this skill when an image pairs saccharine pink love-iconography with an undercurrent of violence, surveillance or possession.

name: Yanki
description: Yanki is the Japanese working-class delinquent aesthetic of the 1970s–90s with roots in 1950s rockabilly: bleached blond or orange hair, towering gel-set pompadours and punch perms, shaved eyebrows, and altered school uniforms — long black chouran jackets, embroidered sukajan, kanji-stitched tokku-fuku — worn by squatting groups under harsh camera flash or faded film light. Its palette is black, cloth white and gold-red embroidery, punctuated by kanji banners, cigarettes and old cars or bikes; its mood is loud, loyal rebellion against polite Japanese society. Recognize it by the uniform-plus-hair silhouette and the analog snapshot or anime-cel rendering, not by any single scene.

name: Young_Poland
description: Young Poland (Młoda Polska, 1891–1918) is the Polish Neo-Romantic modernist style — matte tempera, pastel and leaded stained-glass surfaces in earthy browns, gold and deep ultramarine-teal, fusing Vienna Secession ornament (peacock-eye flora, gold stars, flaming halos, stylized script cartouches) with peasant folk motifs and melancholic Symbolist figures. Expect symbolic flowers, mourning or pensive people, madonnas and nursing mothers, snowbound cemeteries with wooden crosses, and muted interiors — elegiac, patriotic, decadent yet tender.

name: Yugo-Nostalgia
description: Yugo-Nostalgia (jugonostalgija) is the post-2000s nostalgia aesthetic for the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia of the 1960s–1980s — faded analog slide photography and period print design anchored in the red-white-blue tricolor with its gold-edged five-pointed star, Tito portraits, pioneer neckerchiefs and caps, modernist and brutalist concrete, Zastava/Yugo cars, and socialist consumer goods (Plazma, Bajadera, travel posters, enamel badges). The mood is sincere, sunlit melancholy: unity, brotherhood and a perceived better quality of life, never war imagery, Soviet iconography or ironic satire.

name: Yume_Kawaii
description: Yume Kawaii ("dream cute," Japan, from 2013) is a pastel dreamworld aesthetic: hazy, high-key images in baby pink, lavender, mint and cream, filled with magical-girl wands and star compacts, strawberry milk, sailor collars, fluffy plush unicorns and bunnies, sheer frills and glitter-scatter overlays, sometimes edged with a pale, sleepy melancholy. Recognize it by desaturated candy pastels under soft bloom, sleep-and-fantasy motifs, dense cute object collections, and rounded Japanese text edits; it differs from Fairy Kei's vintage retro, Babycore's nursery props, and the saturated punch of 2010s Bright Kawaii.

name: Yuppie
description: 1980s American "Young Urban Professional" aesthetic — tailored power suits in navy, charcoal, white and khaki with red power ties, padded shoulders and slicked-back grooming, surrounded by conspicuous status hardware (gold watches, Filofax organizers, brick mobile phones, European luxury sedans). Staged in glass-and-granite Manhattan towers, high-floor restaurants, marble lobbies and cream executive interiors, rendered with the even flash or diffused window light of period magazine ads and 35mm film stock. Mood is ambitious, transactional and glossily self-assured, with an allowable undercurrent of satirical emptiness.

name: Yé-yé
description: Early-1960s French and Southwestern-European pop youth aesthetic: black-and-white studio and TV portraits of teenage singers with architectural fringes, cat-eye eyeliner, Peter Pan collars and go-go boots, alongside flat-color record sleeves and teen-magazine covers in bright pastels and bold primaries with mod geometry and naive florals. Reads as wholesome, cheeky, print-native Sixties optimism; distinguishable from Mod by its girlish Romance-language print culture and from later revivals by its halftone, silver-print materiality.

name: Zakopane_Style
description: The Zakopane Style (Styl zakopiański, Witkiewicz Style) is the Polish national style of c. 1890–1914 born in the Tatra highlands of Podhale: halved-log walls on fieldstone plinths, steep shingled roofs with vertical ridge finials, and carved sunray slats, rosettes, lilies and hearts on honey-toned spruce. Its grammar extends from villas and wooden chapels to carved chairs and stoves, white linen embroidered in red, hand-painted porcelain with heart motifs, and crochet sunburst lace, all in a palette of wood browns, stone grey and spruce green. Recognize it by vernacular wood tectonics plus Goral carving, mountain daylight or warm interior lamplight, and a handcrafted, national-romantic mood.

name: Zazou
description: Zazou is the flamboyant youth style of Occupied Paris (1941–44): knee-length checked or striped jackets with padded shoulders worn over narrow, cropped trousers that flash bright socks and thick-soled shoes, plus furled umbrellas, greased quiffs, blonde curls with dark roots, tartan pleated skirts and scarlet lipstick. It reads as high-contrast wartime monochrome (press photograph, halftone caricature) punctured by defiant checks and one or two hot accents, caught mid-swing in cellar jazz clubs or on café terraces. The mood is ironic, hedonistic and elegantly defiant — pleasure performed as protest.

name: Zef
description: Zef is the 2000s South African counterculture aesthetic born in working-class Cape Town suburbs and globalized by Die Antwoord's rap-rave: a deliberately garish collision of cheap kitsch and borrowed glamour — bleached mullets, white face paint, gold grillz, tracksuits and logo-collage DIY clothing set against cracked plaster, concrete yards and cramped domestic interiors. Recognize it by its crude hand-drawn doodle layer (simple figures, dollar signs, vulgar sayings), its twin lighting registers of harsh flash snapshot and stark black-and-white tableau, and its unapologetic "poor but fancy, poor but sexy" posture that is simultaneously playful and disturbing.

name: Zen-X
description: Zen-X is the 1990s environmentalist-wellness aesthetic: Japanese-inflected minimalism of bamboo, grass blades, moss, water and pale wood set in beige-white negative space, accented by chartreuse green and aqua blue. Signature elements include diffuse high-key or warm lamplight, women in yoga poses and natural-fabric athleisure, brushstroke calligraphy and thin light sans-serif type on catalog, CD-sleeve and spa-ad layouts of roughly 1994–2003. Recognize it by matte natural materials, sparse composition, serene wellness mood and a printed-catalog color cast.

name: Zenitism
description: Zenitism is the Yugoslav interwar avant-garde (1921–1926, Zagreb–Belgrade, ZENIT journal): dynamic letterpress typography in Cyrillic and Latin, monumental black geometric glyphs on aged cream paper, isometric machine-city assemblages floating on black voids, and raw linocut distortion, all in a black–white–red core spiked with ochre and teal accents. Recognize it by the fusion of Constructivist geometry and Cubist fragmentation with Balkan "Barbarogenius" primitivism — structured yet energetic print matter, checkerboard ground planes, diagonal type bands, advertising signage masts, and distorted human figures carrying unease beneath the order. Distinguish it from pure Constructivism by its folklore-tinged rawness and eclectic collage, and from Dada by its programmatic, manifesto-driven geometric discipline.

name: Zombie_Apocalypse
description: Zombie Apocalypse (Zombiecore) is the survival-horror aesthetic of civilization emptied by infectious undead hordes — vacant streets, hand-lettered quarantine signs, chain-link and corrugated barriers, reaching hands at dark windows — rendered in faded earthy blacks, grays, tans, moss greens and browns with sparse alarm accents of red, orange and warning yellow, or graded toward sickly teal, bruised purple and cadaverous pink. Born from 1960s Romero-era cinema and carried by games and TV, it values fatigue, hunger and survival, and signs itself with torn clothes, firearms, scavenged gear and derelict civic buildings. Read this skill when an image shows mundane recent-past infrastructure made empty and threatening rather than stylized gothic or desert-wasteland ruin.
